title: Anger Volcanoes
objective: This workshop aims to give children a safe space to understand how anger can build up inside, through the creation and metaphor of an erupting volcano.
materials:
Optional printable worksheet

  • Play Dough (variety of colors)

  • Baking soda

  • Vinegar

  • Paper plates

  • Plastic spoons

  • Paper towels

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print copies out for your participants beforehand depending on the setting.
setup:
You can set up a table so each child has a paper plate and plastic spoon and easy access to the play dough.

If you wish, you can provide each child with markers, crayons, and/or colored pencils for the optional writing after the creation.

Depending on manufacturer packaging, you may want to break up the play dough so each child has equal amount and access to each color available.

If you see fit, you can provide each child with a small amount of vinegar in a cup, or you can go around and pour it into their volcanoes (see Creation).

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You can do our suggested Get off My Back exercise, or your own.

Get off My Back:
To start, you can invite children who wish to follow along to:

  • Stand in a circle, slightly spread their feet, bend down and gently bounce, dropping their hands down, then say in unison: "It's so difficult."

  • Staying down, they can roll their shoulders and say: "Get off my back."

  • Next, they can straighten up and reach for the ceiling and say: "I want it."

  • Then, they can cross their arms (as if hugging themselves) and rock back and forth and say: "It's mine."

  • Lastly, they can open their arms and say: "I can share."


In addition to, or instead of the above warm-up, you can invite the children to play with the play dough, soften them, and get a feel for it.
creation:
Creating the volcano
 
 
  Adding baking soda to the volcano
 

You can now invite those who wish to create their volcano to begin. Some children may need help with certain elements, so feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
 

Step 1:
Children can begin by choosing a color (or colors) play dough, put it on the paper plate and create their volcano by molding and shaping it. You can encourage them to use as many colors as they like.

In the center of the volcano, they can create a hole, about 2/3 as deep as the height of the volcano.


Step 2:
You can now take the baking soda to each child and let them spoon the soda into their volcano hole, until it's about 1/2 full.

Discussion:
You can ask the children what they think will happen next.


Step 3:
Next, you can invite the children to pour the vinegar into their volcanoes and see them "erupt." For younger children, you can go around and do this yourself.

Discussion:
As they watch their volcanoes erupt, you may share: "The volcanoes got so angry that they exploded to release their anger. Sometimes people can act like this, too. They get so angry that they can't hold it in any longer and they explode."
closing:
If you see fit, you can invite the children to brainstorm the ways that people can explode when they're angry, being mindful of the fact that this conversation may be triggering for children who have experienced domestic violence. The idea is for children to feel that this can be a safe space for them to talk about it.

You can prompt a discussion with a question like: "Have you ever seen anyone get so angry that they explode like an angry volcano?" This discussion may be more effective in a one-on-one setting, where the child may feel more inclined to share, as opposed to a group, but feel free to facilitate this discussion however you see fit.

Alternatively, you can give children (if age appropriate) the option to write about when and where they've seen or experienced anger building up to where someone explodes like a volcano.
description: Allows children to understand the cycle of violence through creation of a volcano and then experience its three stages - the tension-building, the explosion, and the cooling-off period.
tips:
Because of the nature of this workshop, it is important to keep an eye on, and check in with, each child during the workshop to make sure each child is emotionally handling the process.

We recommend that you start anger workshops with a discussion. Don't be afraid to talk to the children about their anger. Anger is nothing to be ashamed of, it is important to look at and talk about it to try to understand it.

Some anger prompts that we like are:

  • What is Anger?

  • What does it look like and what does it sound like?

  • What was the trigger to your anger?

  • What did you think about it?

  • How did it make you feel?

  • How did you act?

  • What effect did it have on you and those around you?
optional_materials:
• Cups for vinegar

For Optional Writing:

  • Markers

  • Crayons

  • Pencils

  • Plain paper
introduction:
"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

"Today, you will all have an opportunity to create a volcano. Does anyone know what a volcano is?"

(You can invite the children to a discussion, and/or share the following. Feel free to facilitate the discussion however you see fit).

"A volcano is a mountain that has a hot lava on the inside of it. Even though it looks quiet on the outside, on the inside it can be rumbling and getting hotter and hotter. There's a lot of pressure that can build up inside a volcano. Does anyone know what happens when the pressure becomes too much?"

"The volcano gets so hot and angry that it will eventually explode (erupt). Then it gets quiet and it feels better. That's how a volcano works."

title: Intuition Dolls
objective: This workshop aims to help children honor their inner voice and create a doll that can serve as a visual reminder to listen to their intuition.
materials:
• Pipe cleaners (1 and a half per participant)

  • Embroidery thread (for the hair)

  • Thin ribbon (for the skin; about 36 inches long per participant)

  • Fabric rectangles (4" x 7"; variety of colors, textures and patterns)

  • Scissors

  • Dress pattern template

  • Intuition Dolls Instructions template
setup:
You are welcome to provide any and as many of the suggested decorative material (beads, feathers, etc) as you like.

You may wish to cut the fabric to rectangles (about 4" x 7") for the children in advance. You may also want to cut half of the pipe cleaners in half with a wire-cutter. Each child gets 1 full-sized, and one half-sized pipe cleaner (Ex: if you have 10 participants, you can provide 10 full-sized and 10 half-sized pipe cleaners).

You can print the dress pattern template, which children can use as a stencil to cut the fabric.

You may also want to print a copy of the Intuition Dolls Instructions handout for each child.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get a feel for the creation process and the measurements (ribbon, fabric, etc.) needed, as well as to show children what the finished doll can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample and using only the material you're providing so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested mediation or your own. We have found that guided meditations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.


"Before we start, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief relaxation exercise. If you prefer to just observe, that’s perfectly okay. Observing is participating.”

“For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get yourself in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. However way you are most comfortable.”

“Now, let’s take a few deep breaths (you can guide participants to breathe in for a count of 5 seconds, hold it for 3 and exhale for 7 seconds)... As you breathe, I'd like you to try to notice the tense parts in your body and visualize your breath going to those areas."

"Now begin to breathe normally. Try not to control it... and as you breathe, try to imagine cool, soothing, healing air going into the tense areas of your body, and releasing all that tension with each breath out. You can continue to breathe and sit in this relaxed state as long as you like... Try to scan all throughout your body for tense areas. Try to allow your mind to be present, and as you are in this relaxed state, imagine, what does your intuition look like?... what colors and images come to mind?... if you look for your intuition in your body where do you find it?... How does your intuition speak to you?"

"Sit with your thought for a moment… and when you are ready, you can come back to this moment and open your eyes."
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create their dolls to begin. You may wish to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create or participate.

Feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
closing: You can give children a chance to volunteer and share their creations, what it means to them, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.
description: Encourages participants to (re)discover and honor their intuition, the inner voices that guide us and tell us what to do if we allow ourselves to become quiet enough to hear them. The dolls are a visual reminder to listen to our intuition.
tips: If working with teens, this workshop can be used to talk about healthy body image.
optional_materials:
• Fishing line

  • Old jewelry

  • Feathers

  • Beads

  • Pin backs

  • Jewelry pliers / wire cutters

  • Paper and pens

  • Your choice of embellishments
introduction:
“There is a Russian folk tale called Vasilisa the Beautiful. It is the story of a girl who receives a doll from her mother, right before her mother passed away. She tells Vasilisa to always keep the doll close to her and to listen to what the doll tells her. She also tells Vasilisa to keep the doll a secret and tell no one. Vasilisa keeps the doll in her pocket. Through the story Vasilisa consults her doll, who always gives her good advice. When Vasilisa comes to a fork in the road, the doll seems to tell her which way to go. When she comes across danger, the doll jumps up and down in Vasilisa's pocket to warn her."

“Vasilisa's doll is like intuition. That voice inside ourselves that tells us which path to take and warns us of danger. So today, you have a chance to create your very own intuition doll. The doll can be a symbol to remind you to listen to your own inner voice."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
The Body: Step 1
 
  The Body: Step 2
 
  The Body: Steps 3 & 4
 
  The Hair: Step 1
 
  The Hair: Steps 2 & 3
 
  The Skin: Step 1
 
  The Dress: Step 1
 
  The Dress: Step 4
 
  Final touches

You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation process with the children. You may find it helpful to share your sample, if you've made one, as well as demonstrate the creation steps as you see fit. Feel free to cater the demonstration and the creation however way it works best for your and the group.


The Body:

  1. Fold the full-sized pipe cleaner in half.

  2. Twist 1/2" - 3/4" of the top into a loop to make the head.

  3. Using the half-pipe cleaner for arms, twist onto the body below the head loop.

  4. For smaller dolls, you can bend the the arms, about half-way down, towards the body. If you wish to create hands, you can twist small loops at the tips.

  5. For larger dolls, you can make the head loop slightly larger, and fold in arms and legs at desired length, or leave at full length.


The Hair:

  1. Wrap embroidery thread around all 4 of your fingers to make loops.

  2. Insert loops through the head.

  3. Tie a knot. You can also clip the loops to secure them, instead of a knot.


The Skin:

  1. Using thin ribbon, you can tie an X over the chest of the doll.

  2. Wrap the ribbon tightly (in a crisscross fashion) around the arms, neck, head and chest area (leaving the hands unwrapped, if you've created them). The ribbon forms the doll's body, so feel free to use as much ribbon as you desire. Legs do not need to be wrapped.

  3. Tie the end of the ribbon into a tight knot. You can save any extra ribbon for the belt.


The Dress:

  1. You can use the dress pattern template as a stencil to cut out the fabric to create the dress. You can choose any color or style fabric you like.

  2. If you like, you can cut fringes.

  3. Fold the fabric in, 1/2 front to back, then fold in 1/2 again side to side. Just barely clip folded corner. This makes the neck-hole. It will stretch, so make sure not to cut it too big.

  4. Slide the dress over the head of the doll until it's in place. You can use a ribbon to tie around the waist and adjust if necessary.


Final Touches:

  1. You can add beads, feathers, and or any other embellishments.

  2. (Optional): You can glue a pin on the back or you can use a little piece of ribbon to tie it on.

  3. When you are done, you can decorate your fabric however way you like. You can write words about your intuition doll and what it means to you, draw symbols, shapes, or anything else that you like.

title: The Monster in Me / Monstro Dentro De Mi
objective: To provide children an opportunity to explore difficult emotions in a safe and playful way, and give voice to the feelings that may be hidden inside, by creating artwork that represents the “monster” within.
materials:
• CrayPas (or oil pastels)

  • Thick white paper (twice as much as the number of participants)

  • Watercolor sets

  • Watercolor brushes

  • Cups for water (2 per participant; one for cleaning brush and one for wetting it)

  • Newspaper / disposable table covers (to cover the table)

  • Paper towels (for drying brushes)

  • Spray bottle (filled with water; one per table will do; you can also use a broad house-painting brush instead)

  • Feeling Target Warm-Up plates

    • (You can click on the above link and use the templates and instructions provided in the Set-Up section to create the "feelings plates" used in this workshop. These should be created in advance)
setup:
Sample space set-up
 

You may consider opening the CrayPas and watercolor sets in advance, and lightly spraying each watercolor set with water. The water helps soften the colors so that they will be easy to use when the children paint.

Depending on the age group and if necessary, you may place the supplies out of reach until creation.

You may wish to cover your workstations with newspaper, or disposable table covers to avoid getting wet paint on them.

Each child should ideally have 2 water cups in front of them; one for cleaning the brush and the other to dip into and wet the brush before dipping it in the color of their choice.

Depending on the space you're working with, you may wish to set up the Feelings Target warm-up plates in advance. You can do the warm-up inside or outside. It's entirely up to you.
warm_up:
Monster Dance

“Before we begin our workshop, I'd like to invite you to join me in a game where we will each have a chance to share about our feelings. When we talk about our feelings, whether they are ones we like or ones that are difficult for us, it gives us the freedom to be ourselves and notice what's alive for us.”

"We each have many different feelings, and even sometimes we feel all of these emotions simultaneously. In one day, we can feel joyful, upset, angry, and proud. Remember that while many of these feelings may seem uncomfortable, strange, challenging, or frustrating, it is important to acknowledge each and every one of them. Of course, this is optional, so if you prefer to observe, or use this time to do something else entirely, that's perfectly okay."

To start this warm-up, you can lay out the "feelings plates" (see set-up section for details) on the floor and invite those who wish to participate to stand a few feet away from the plates and toss a penny/sandbag towards them. If the penny/sandbag lands on a face, the child can share a story about the last time (or any time) they felt that particular feeling. For example, if the penny lands on the “happy” face, the child can share about the last time (or anytime) they felt happy. If the penny/sandbag lands between two feelings, the child can talk about either one of the feelings (moving the penny/sandbag on top of the feeling the child wishes to talking about). The other children can practice listening as each person shares.

If any of the children don't feel comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay. They can simply observe.

You can also incorporate more embodied art into the warm-up by giving children the option to make a statue of the feeling instead of sharing verbally. For example, you might say: "Another option is that instead of speaking, you can show us an image (statue) of that emotion. For example, here's what I look like when I'm nervous (create a statue with your body, perhaps by hiding your face behind your hands and crouching down)."

You might also give children an opportunity to practice making images together by saying, "Let's do a demo. Everyone show what you look like when you're feeling excited in 3-2-1-freeze."

If it’s feasible, you can also do this warm up outside.

 

Monster Dance Warm-up:

Once the children who wished to participate have had a chance to share how they feel, you can invite them to join you in a "Monster Dance."

“Now, I'd like to invite you to join me in doing a Monster Dance. First we can start by moving around in a circle being monsters. Let’s all be scary monsters..."

"Now let’s be happy monsters. Can you be really loud monsters? Can you be really quiet monsters?”

 

Alternative To Monster Dance Warm-up for Teens:
If you are working with a group of teens, the Monster Dance might not be the best way to start. You could try something more theatrical, like walking into the workshop with a scary mask on and asking them what they see. You can talk about how we all have "monsters" inside of us and how it’s important to take a look at those "monsters" and see who they are and what they need.
creation:
Sample Monster creation

“Now it’s your turn. I now invite those of you who like to create, to go ahead and draw your monster using the CrayPas. When you are creating, you can think about what kind of eyes do you want to make? What kind of mouth? Teeth? Ears? Does your monster have hair? If you like to spray the page, when you are done drawing, you can raise your hand, so I can come water your monster."

“When your monster has been sprayed, you get to drop in any colors you like and watch them fill the spaces. You can draw your monster however you like and use any of the colors available to color it. Remember, it doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is that you are creating something in any way that you like."
closing:
Monster in Me Samples

For the closing, you can invite the children to share their monster, if they wish. You can encourage the children to share with questions like:

“What does your monster feel like? What is it thinking?”

You can invite the children to think about and/or share what their monster needs in order to feel better.

"Does it need to be loved? Does it need to be understood? Sometimes monsters have important things to say if you listen to what they need in order to feel better."

You can thank the children for sharing and for being brave by exposing their monsters within.


Alternate Closing:

If you are doing this as an anger management workshop, you also have the option to close by brainstorming a "Safety Plan" with the children to help them process their anger. Some helpful tips to share with them include:

  • Talk to a friend you can trust

  • Count to ten

  • Take out art supplies and draw a picture of your anger

  • Journal about your anger

  • Take deep breaths

  • Listen to music

  • Walk away

  • Dance or exercise


Again, please feel free to alter or adapt any element or portion of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
description: Gives children an opportunity to be playful in exploring some of the more difficult emotions they experience. Offers a process that will look bold and powerful, and be rewarding and satisfying for the children.
notes:
If using this workshop to help the children release or process anger, we suggest beginning by having a discussion on "What is Anger?" Please click here to see the entire Processing Anger Workshop Series.

If you'd like to include journaling in this workshop, here is a journaling handout that you can distribute to the participants.
tips:
We recommend that you start anger workshops with a discussion; don't be afraid to talk to the children about their anger. Anger is nothing to be ashamed of, it is important to look at and talk about it to try to understand it.

Some anger prompts that we like are:

  • What is Anger? What does it look like and what does it sound like?

  • What was the trigger to your anger?

  • What did you think about it?

  • How did it make you feel?

  • How did you act?

  • What effect did it have on you and those around you?
objective_spanish:
Proveer oportunidades a participantes para reflexionar sobre sus experiencias personales con violencia domestica, explorar emociones difíciles de una manera segura y divertida, dando le una voz a los sentimientos que puedan estar escondidos adentro de uno mismo creando una pieza de arte que representa el “mostró” dentro.

Materiales:
Craypas
Papel blanco grueso (doble el número de participantes)
Acuarelas
Brochas
Vasos de agua- 1 por participante
Espejos de mano

Tiempo:
Calentamiento: 15 minutos
Introducción y Demostración: 10 minutos
Creación: 50 minutos
Circulo de clausura: 15 minutos
Tiempo total: 1 hora y 30 minutos

Calentamiento:
Vamos a empezar el taller de hoy día con un calentamiento que nos ayudara a relajar nuestros cuerpos, conectar con nuestros sentimientos y la manera que nos expresamos, preparar y inspirar nos para cuando nos siéntenos a crear.  Vamos a comenzar con crear un círculo.

Empezamos con extender nuestro brazo derecho hacia arriba, hasta donde alcancen.

Ahora su brazo izquierdo hacia arriba, hasta donde alcancen.

Estiren su cara en un bostezo grande y espiren profundamente.

Ahora aprieten su cara fuerte como una pasa y luego suelten lo.

Empiecen a masticar, en visionen que tienen una goma de mascar grande dentro de su boca- mastica de el lado derecho de tu boca, luego muevo lo a el lado izquierdo.

Extiende los dos brazos hacia arriba y luego baja los dejando los caer, doblando en la cintura.
Párense, vertebre por vertebre hasta que su espaldas estén rectas.

Ahora… Todos juntos!

Todos hagan un sonido expresa algo tonto…

Hagan un sonido que expresa enojo.

Hagan un sonido que expresa miedo.

Hagan un sonido que expresa tristeza.

Hagan un sonido que expresa descanso.

Ahora vamos a sentarnos y empezar.

Introducción y Demostración técnica:
Hay una parte de nosotros que no demostramos a los demás, a no ser que siéntanos ciertas emociones, por ejemplo cuando nos sentimos tristes y ponemos una cara feliz, es como tener una persona adentro que no queremos exponer.  Hoy estamos creando un dibujo que expone esa persona que llevamos dentro, el nombre del taller es Mostró dentro de mi.

Vamos a empezar con conocer los materiales que utilizaremos para crear nuestros Monstros.  Voy ha empezar con una demostración creando mi mostró, luego empezaran a crear su propio mostró.  Recuerden sus monstruos no serán igual, porque demostramos nuestras emociones y experiencias de diferente maneras.  Todos sentimos, enojo, tristeza, felicidad, y miedo… pero se manifiesta de diferente manera con deferente gente.

(Caminen mientras dan la demostración, ayuda mantener la atención de la gente)

El primer material es como una crayola, se llama pastel.  Mi mostró tendrá una cara y voy a utilizar el pastel para crear la forma de la cara.  Voy a dibujar una forma … (dibuja la forma).  Pueden usar toda la pagina para crear su mostró.  Pueden utilizar toda la página para dibujar el cuerpo, o su cara, o pueden incluir un ambiente.  Hay muchas maneras en que sus monstros pueden tomar forma.

Ahora voy a utilizar acuarelas… Primero voy a mojar la brocha y escogeré mi color.  (Demuestra como los pasteles mantienen el color dentro de la forma.  Agrega otra forma con el pastel y demuestra como limpiar la brocha y como resiste el color cuando agregas la acuarela sobre el pastel.)

Que ven en la mesa que no se haiga explicado?

Espejos.  Levanten el espejo y mírense.  Noten como cambia su cara cuando hacen diferentes expresiones, cuando sonríes, miren sus dientes y cuando arrugas las cejas.

Ahora quiero que miren en el espejo, quiero que miren dentro de ustedes y vean si pueden ver el mostró adentro.  Como se siente tu  mostró?  Como se ve?  Tu mostró se ve feliz, triste, enojado, asustado?

No tienen que contestar estas preguntas con palabras, vamos a exponer estos monstros en el papel dejen que se expresen solos.  Cuando estén listos, bajen su espejo y empiecen a crear.

Creación:
Recuerden mientras que trabajan, este es un lugar seguro para ustedes.  No tienen que saber quien es su mostró ni como se ve cuando comiencen , se aparecerán y tomaran su propia forma mientras que van creando.

Circulo de Clausura:
Da le una oportunidad a cada mujer para compartir su mostró.  Pueden compartir en parejas o como grupo (dependiendo de lo que sea mejor para el grupo).  Cuando comparten en parejas una persona compartirá primero mientras que la otra practica a escuchar, compartiendo una por una 3 minutos cada una.  Avisa cuando es tiempo de cambiar.

Puedes animar a las mujeres que compartan con preguntas como:  “Como se siente tu mostró?  Que esta pensando?”  Pregúntales a las mujeres que necesitan sus monstros, para sentirse mejor.  Necesita amor? Necesita que lo entiendan?  A veces monstros tienen cosas importantes que decir si escuchan lo que necesitan para sentirse mejor.

Da gracias a las mujeres por compartir y por ser valientes en exponer a sus monstros que llevan dentro.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • The Monster in Me Worksheet

 
The Monster in Me Worksheet
introduction:
"There is a side of us we don't show to other people unless we feel certain emotions. For example, when we feel sad, sometimes we try to put on a happy face, and it's like we have another person inside that we don't want to show. Today, you will have an opportunity to create a drawing that exposes that person inside in a fun and creative way."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
Step 1
 
 
  Step 2
 
 
  Step 3

You can show the children how to create and use the watercolors, CrayPas (or oil pastels) by doing a quick demonstration. You may invite them to get involved in the demonstration by asking them to guide you as you go through the three steps, so you’re creating the monster they are telling you to make. You can demonstrate how the watercolor can be used on the paper and how the oil pastels hold the color inside the shape. The idea is that children get a sense of how to create using watercolors.
 

Step 1: Drawing the Monster
You can use the CrayPas (or oil pastels) to draw the monster. If you wish to invite the children to contribute with ideas, you can prompt them with the following questions:

“What kind of nose should I put on this monster? What kind of eyes? What kind of ears? How about big teeth? Anything else I should add? How about a neck for the monster... Notice that I’m pressing really hard to make the lines. This is important because it makes the lines strong enough for when we put the paint on.” 
 

Step 2: Watering the Monster
“Now we get to make the monster all wet (You can spray the entire page with a spray bottle). Did I get the whole monster wet? Is there anywhere I missed? (Keep spraying until the whole surface is wet. You could call the water 'Monster Juice').” 
 

Step 3: Coloring the Monster
“Now we get to add the colors. What colors should we use? We can just drop the colors into each space and see them spread (You can demonstrate how the watercolors spread in the water) Isn’t that cool? What color should I make the eyes? How about the mouth? How about the space around the monster?”

 

We suggest creating a simple sample so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges, but one that demonstrates how the oil pastels and watercolors work with each other to create a cool effect.

title: My Home
objective: This workshop aims to help children identify and express what "home" means to them and create a symbolic house that represents what they want to include in their ideal home.
materials:
• House template

  • Construction paper

  • Scissors

  • Glue sticks

  • Magazines (Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Markers

  • Pens
setup:
You can print a house template for each child to decorate.

Ideally, the size of the construction paper would be larger than the house. You can provide a single color or variety of colors.

For younger children, you may want to do steps 1 and/or 2 of the creation process in advance (see Demonstration). It's entirely up to you.

You may also want to cut a variety of images and words or phrases out of magazines that are appropriate for your specific group in advance, to preclude the children from handling scissors. Or, you can just invite the children to tear the images out of magazines by hand, which can create a cool, jagged-edge effect.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show the children what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested warm-up or one of your own. For this warm-up, you can invite the children to gather in a circle, leaving ample space around them to move freely.

Feel free to adapt this warm-up however it best suits your group.


Growing As A Tree:
"Before we start, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief warm-up. If you prefer to just observe, that's perfectly okay. Observing is participating."

"For those of you who want to follow along, let's form a circle and give ourselves space to grow like a tree."

"Let's start by being a small tree, with our feet as roots. We have strong roots that will help us grow. Let's all hunker down close to the ground so we can be small trees."

"Now, we're growing, little by little. First, let's put our arms up above our head. Our fingers are like little leaves... wiggle them about and then little by little, we are growing bigger and bigger (you can slowly stand upright, while wiggling arms and fingers)."

"Now, we are strong, wise trees, upright and ready for anything."

"Now let's image that a wind sweeps across the land... not too big a wind, but big enough that it makes us move around and about (you can sway arms, fingers, and upper body while keeping feet aground)."

"Can anyone show how the wind in the trees sounds like (you can guide them in making wind sounds)?"

"Great! Notice that the wind can move our branches and leaves, but because we have strong roots, it can't shake us out of our roots."
creation:
You can now invite the children to create their home. You may wish to remind them that this is their window of time and if they choose to observe or use the art supplies to create something else, that's perfectly okay.

Those who want to create their home, can add any images they like, and use any of the supplies available to create their home any way they like. There is no right or wrong way to create. Images could include a dog, a cat, a family, a swing-set, a car, a heart shape, a Christmas tree, a bed, and/or anything that represents the things they want in their ideal home. They can add images behind the windows in each room and behind the door, on the outside of the house, or anywhere they choose.

Some children may need help with certain creation elements (cutting images, applying glue, etc.), so feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.


 

    
"Laughter and Smiles"    "Unity and Acceptance"
closing:
You can invite volunteers to share their home creations, what the images represent, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.

Of course, this is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
description: Helps children identify and verbalize what "Home" means to them individually. Provides a forum where the children can express their hopes and dreams for their future "Homes."
introduction:
"Today, you will have a chance to think about what 'home' means to you and create your dream home however you envision it."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
My Home creation
 
 
  Closed window
 
 
  Open window

You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation process with them. You can demonstrate any creation elements that you see fit. For example, you can show them how to use scissors, or their hands to cut images out of magazines and use the glue sticks to glue the image onto the house template. Or, how they can use the markers to draw any images or symbols, or just to color the house, create a roof by drawing tiles or bricks, etc.

If you've done any of the following steps in advance, feel free to jump to the appropriate creation step.


Step 1: (If not done in advance)
To start, children can cut the house template out, and cut along the dashed lines to "open" the windows and door.


Step 2: (If not done in advance)
Next, using a glue stick, they can apply glue along the back edges of the house, avoiding glue behind the the windows and door (to allow them to open and close). They can then glue the house onto the construction paper.
 

Step 3:
Once they have the backdrop (construction paper), children can collage images or words that symbolize the things they want to include in their ideal home.

They can also use any of the material (markers, etc.) available and add drawings, colors, symbols, etc. and decorate the house however they like.

title: Intuition Dolls
objective: This workshop aims to help participants honor their inner voice and create a doll that can serve as a visual reminder to listen to their intuition.
materials:
• Pipe cleaners (1 and a half per participant)

  • Embroidery thread (for the hair)

  • Thin ribbon (for the skin; about 36 inches long per participant)

  • Fabric rectangles (4" x 7"; variety of colors, textures and patterns)

  • Scissors

  • Dress pattern template

  • Intuition Dolls Instructions template
setup:
You are welcome to provide any and as many of the suggested decorative material (beads, feathers, etc) as you like.

You may wish to cut the fabric to rectangles (about 4" x 7") for the participants in advance. You may also want to cut half of the pipe cleaners in half with a wire-cutter. Each participants gets 1 full-sized, and one half-sized pipe cleaner (Ex: if you have 10 participants, you can provide 10 full-sized and 10 half-sized pipe cleaners).

You can print the dress pattern template, which participants can use as a stencil to cut the fabric.

You may also want to print a copy of the Intuition Dolls Instructions handout for each participant.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get a feel for the creation process and the measurements (ribbon, fabric, etc.) needed, as well as to show participants what the finished doll can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample and using only the material you're providing so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested mediation or your own. We have found that guided meditations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.


"Before we start, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief relaxation exercise. If you prefer to just observe, that’s perfectly okay. Observing is participating.”

“For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get yourself in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. However way you are most comfortable.”

“Now, let’s take a few deep breaths (you can guide participants to breathe in for a count of 5 seconds, hold it for 3 and exhale for 7 seconds)... As you breathe, I'd like you to try to notice the tense parts in your body and visualize your breath going to those areas."

"Now begin to breathe normally. Try not to control it... and as you breathe, try to imagine cool, soothing, healing air going into the tense areas of your body, and releasing all that tension with each breath out. You can continue to breathe and sit in this relaxed state as long as you like... Try to scan all throughout your body for tense areas. Try to allow your mind to be present, and as you are in this relaxed state, imagine, what does your intuition look like?... what colors and images come to mind?... if you look for your intuition in your body where do you find it?... How does your intuition speak to you?"

"Sit with your thought for a moment… and when you are ready, you can come back to this moment and open your eyes."
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create their dolls to begin. You may wish to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create or participate.

Feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
closing: You can give participants a chance to volunteer and share their creations, what it means to them, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.
description: Allows time for the rediscovery and honoring of the inner voices that can guide us if we allow ourselves to become quiet enough to hear them. The dolls are a visual reminder to listen to our intuition.
tips: If working with teens, this workshop can be used to talk about healthy body image.
optional_materials:
• Fishing line

  • Old jewelry

  • Feathers

  • Beads

  • Pin backs

  • Jewelry pliers / wire cutters

  • Paper and pens

  • Your choice of embellishments
introduction:
“There is a Russian folk tale called Vasilisa the Beautiful. It is the story of a girl who receives a doll from her mother, right before her mother passed away. She tells Vasilisa to always keep the doll close to her and to listen to what the doll tells her. She also tells Vasilisa to keep the doll a secret and tell no one. Vasilisa keeps the doll in her pocket. Through the story Vasilisa consults her doll, who always gives her good advice. When Vasilisa comes to a fork in the road, the doll seems to tell her which way to go. When she comes across danger, the doll jumps up and down in Vasilisa's pocket to warn her."

“Vasilisa's doll is like intuition. That voice inside ourselves that tells us which path to take and warns us of danger. So today, you have a chance to create your very own intuition doll. The doll can be a symbol to remind you to listen to your own inner voice."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
The Body: Step 1
 
  The Body: Step 2
 
  The Body: Steps 3 & 4
 
  The Hair: Step 1
 
  The Hair: Steps 2 & 3
 
  The Skin: Step 1
 
  The Dress: Step 1
 
  The Dress: Step 4
 
  Final touches

You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation process with the participants. You may find it helpful to share your sample, if you've made one, as well as demonstrate the creation steps as you see fit. Feel free to cater the demonstration and the creation however way it works best for your and the group.


The Body:

  1. Fold the full-sized pipe cleaner in half.

  2. Twist 1/2" - 3/4" of the top into a loop to make the head.

  3. Using the half-pipe cleaner for arms, twist onto the body below the head loop.

  4. For smaller dolls, you can bend the the arms, about half-way down, towards the body. If you wish to create hands, you can twist small loops at the tips.

  5. For larger dolls, you can make the head loop slightly larger, and fold in arms and legs at desired length, or leave at full length.


The Hair:

  1. Wrap embroidery thread around all 4 of your fingers to make loops.

  2. Insert loops through the head.

  3. Tie a knot. You can also clip the loops to secure them, instead of a knot.


The Skin:

  1. Using thin ribbon, you can tie an X over the chest of the doll.

  2. Wrap the ribbon tightly (in a crisscross fashion) around the arms, neck, head and chest area (leaving the hands unwrapped, if you've created them). The ribbon forms the doll's body, so feel free to use as much ribbon as you desire. Legs do not need to be wrapped.

  3. Tie the end of the ribbon into a tight knot. You can save any extra ribbon for the belt.


The Dress:

  1. You can use the dress pattern template as a stencil to cut out the fabric to create the dress. You can choose any color or style fabric you like.

  2. If you like, you can cut fringes.

  3. Fold the fabric in, 1/2 front to back, then fold in 1/2 again side to side. Just barely clip folded corner. This makes the neck-hole. It will stretch, so make sure not to cut it too big.

  4. Slide the dress over the head of the doll until it's in place. You can use a ribbon to tie around the waist and adjust if necessary.


Final Touches:

  1. You can add beads, feathers, and or any other embellishments.

  2. (Optional): You can glue a pin on the back or you can use a little piece of ribbon to tie it on.

  3. When you are done, you can decorate your fabric however way you like. You can write words about your intuition doll and what it means to you, draw symbols, shapes, or anything else that you like.

title: Meditation Focus Painting
objective: This workshop gives participants a chance to experience how art and spirituality can go hand in hand, through the creation of a meditation focus painting art piece.
materials:
• Cardstock (variety of colors)

  • Scissors

  • Glue sticks

  • Oil pastels (CrayPas)

  • Acrylic paints

  • Brushes

  • Paint palettes (plates)

  • Writing paper

  • Pens
setup:
The participants may not use all these mediums, but it's nice to have different supplies available so they can make their focus art in a way that's comfortable for them. For example, some participants would rather make a collage with the various papers than use paint, so feel free to provide any and as many of the supplies and materials as you like and cater the creation however it best works for you and your group.

You can print copies of the I Am Light poem to share with participants, if it suits your objective

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample using only the material you're providing, so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested meditation, or your own. We have found that guided meditations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.

"Before we start, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief relaxation exercise. If you prefer to just observe, that’s perfectly okay. Observing is participating.”

“For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get yourself in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. However way you are most comfortable.”

"Now take a deep breath, and try to imagine a calm place where your heart is... Try to concentrate on your heart... take another deep breath for your heart. Now try to think about the other people in this room... imagine that you wish them the best, and they wish you the best... Imagine light comes down into the room... this light is from a higher power... that may mean 'God' for some, or it could be light from mother nature, or your your higher self. Whatever you envision a higher power being, is just right."

"Breathe in this light... with it, you feel calm and protected... imagine the colors that make you feel calm and peaceful... look at these colors and what shapes they are... try to notice and honor anything that comes to your mind."

"Think about what colors make you feel happy, light hearted, comfortable and protected... think about any other quality you want for yourself... notice their shapes and colors... think about these colors and beams of light coming down from above... they wash over you and you can breathe them in... take all the time you want to imagine these colors, and what they stand for."

"Sit in this relaxed state and with your thoughts for as long as you like... and when you are ready, you can bring yourself back to this moment, open your eyes, and begin creating your focus painting as you just envisioned it."
creation:
Heart meditation focus painting

You may want to remind participants that there is no right or wrong way to create. They are free to use the art supplies however they like to create their meditation focus painting.

Feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
closing: You can invite participants to volunteer and share their creations, what qualities they represent in their art piece, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during the workshop, or anything else they may wish to share.
description: Gives participants an experience of how art and spirituality can go hand in hand and time to think about uplifting qualities that we want to become more in tune with. The end product acts as a visual focus for meditation.
notes:
From the author:
I'm a painter, and a survivor of domestic violence. I've been running weekly workshops in a shelter in Columbus Ohio. The workshops I facilitate usually have a spiritual overtone. I believe art can be a spiritual endeavor, and that painting, drawing, writing, and other creative forms can bring us closer to God, or a higher power. I've introduced this meditation focus workshop to the women in Columbus a few times, and it's been well accepted, so I wanted to share it with you also.
optional_materials:
I Am Light poem handout
 

Other Collaging Options:

  • Scrapbook cutouts

  • Tissue paper (variety of colors)
introduction:
Sun and window meditation focus painting
 

"Today, you will have an opportunity to make meditation focus art. You'll get to create an image using colors and shapes that make you feel peaceful, free, protected, happy or any other quality or feeling that you wish to strive toward."

"A focus is a reminder of something. One of the most famous examples of this type of art is the Statue of Liberty, which is meant to be a focus, or symbol, of freedom and liberty. There are so many ways to make a type of focus art and the possibilities are endless. Today, you'll have an opportunity to explore those possibilities and create something that is expressive and meaningful to you."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
Leaf Mandala meditation focus painting



 

You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation process with the participants. You may want to demonstrate any techniques and/or creation elements that you see fit.


"There are so many ways to go about creating your meditation focus painting. You are invited to use any of the supplies available and make your art piece however way you want. Here are some suggested way to create:"


Collaging Method:
"You can start by thinking of a quality that you want for yourself. Let's use 'wholeness' as an example. You can try to imagine what color represents wholeness to you. What shape is it? Let's say it's a green circle, so you can start with a green circle and glue it onto the cardstock."

"If you wish to add more qualities, you can repeat and add them onto the cardstock however way you wish to arrange them."


Oil Pastel Method:
"You can also layer oil pastels and draw the shapes in the colors that you choose. You can scratch into them, write into the pastels with pencil to make dark lines, or scratch out images or shapes of your choosing."


Paint Options:
"You also have the option to use paints and draw the shape and explore colors through paint, or you can use a combination of all three methods. Again, the possibilities are endless and you are invited to use the art supplies however way you like."

"You are welcome to explore your thoughts and write them down on paper before you start creating. However you wish to do it will be perfectly okay."
opening_circle:
You can facilitate a discussion around "qualities" that participants may wish to have in their lives. You can open by sharing examples of qualities, such as: security; prosperity; freedom; calmness; wisdom; ability to make wise choices in life; be protected; peaceful; centered; assertive; patient; abundance; happy; light-hearted, etc. and invite participants to share their own and create a list.

Participants may or may not wish to use some of the qualities shared during this discussion, on which to base their creations.

Feel free to cater the discussion around a specific focus relevant to your group.

title: Gratitude Journals
objective: This workshop offers participants a chance to reflect on the good and positive aspects of their life and create a personalized journal as an expression of those positive aspects and to have a place to record the things, people, and personal strengths, for which they are grateful.
materials:
•     
      Composition book

    Composition theme books (hardcovers)

  • Magazines (Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Scissors

  • Glue sticks

  • Pens

  • Clear packing tape
setup: You can precut words and images out of magazines to provide for the participants, if you wish. It's entirely up to you. As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested visualization, or your own. Guided visualization are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.
 

“Before we begin, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief visualization exercise. If you prefer to observe, or use this time to do something else, that's perfectly okay."

"For those of you who wish to participate, try to get in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. However you are most comfortable."

"Now try to notice your hands. Are they relaxed and loose? If not, take a moment to relax your hands... Now focus your attention on your face, is it relaxed? Take a moment and simply send the message to your entire body to relax. Focus your attention on your breath, not seeking to change it in any way but simply become aware of your in-breath and your out-breath. Now using your imagination, try to picture yourself in your favorite kind of place. This is a place you know to be safe, nurturing and uplifting. This is your special space, where you are at peace, empowered and centered. It is a place of beauty... one that sets your soul free to soar. See it very clearly taking in every detail that makes this place special to you... Take a look around you and take in the beauty of your surroundings... What is the weather like? Is there a breeze? What are the sounds and smells?... Try to become aware of your surrounding in this place with your whole being... Now notice in front of you a gentle pathway... You begin to walk along the path... feeling content and at ease... completely enjoying this time... soon you come to a small garden... and in the garden you find a bench... you find yourself drawn to this little garden and choose to rest here for awhile... as you sit there among the flowers and trees on the little bench, I invite you to reflect on your life... looking for the good that is there... the things that bring you joy and happiness... it could be your child's smile... or a hug from a friend... or the sunshine warm on your face... or the smell of violets growing in the garden... look for the things that you are thankful for in your life... maybe it is your courage and strength... or your willingness to make changes in your life... perhaps it is a special person... someone you deeply love and appreciate... someone who supports and honors you... as you remember the blessings in your life, you begin to feel a greater sense of joy and connection to all life... a sense of peace settles over you, as you remember what you are grateful for... Take a few deep breaths... and when you are ready, feel yourself in your body... back here in this room."


After the guided relaxation, you can invite the participants to take a few moments to write down some of the thoughts that came to them during the relaxation. They can date this as their first journal entry if they wish.
creation:
Sample Gratitude Journal cover

You can now invite the participants to begin creating their gratitude journals. As they begin to cut images for their collages, you may encourage them to focus on gratitude and the images that best represent their personal response to the visualization.

You may also wish to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to honor their thoughts and feelings of gratitude and creating something that is meaningful to them.
closing:
For the closing, you can give participants a chance to share their Gratitude Journals. If any participants have not fully completed the collages, you may encourage them to continue on their own after the workshop.

You may remind them that their journal is a place they can record their accomplishments and daily reflections. They could also use the journal to record uplifting poetry and quotes and refer to it when they need some encouragement.
description: Gives participants time to reflect on the good and positive aspects of her life. The end products are individualized, personalized journals, expressions of those positive aspects and a place to record daily gratitude lists and strengths.
notes: Hello! My name is Kelly Carter and I have been volunteering with the AWBW program at the Shasta County Women's Refuge in Redding, California. The idea for the Gratitude Journal workshop came from watching my two daughters make collages on everything from folders to binders. I used their idea to start making collages on hardcover composition books and sealing them with clear packing tape to preserve the collage. My youngest daughter had been keeping a gratitude journal for about five years. After a trip home from college, she had left her journal at my house. When she arrived back at school and discovered her journal was missing, she immediately called and asked me to send it to her as soon as possible. I realized what a powerful process keeping the journal had become for her and decided to introduce the concept of the Gratitude Journal at our monthly AWBW meeting. The next month we took the workshop into the shelter. The women at the shelter loved the process and appreciated creating something that they could use daily. By focusing on the positive aspects of our lives, we can lift our awareness and create a more positive life experience as well. Keeping a gratitude journal is something we can all benefit from.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

"The workshop is called Gratitude Journals. You'll have a chance to spend some time in a relaxation and guided visualization, followed by a few minutes of journal writing. You will then get to create your personal journals in any way that is meaningful to you. You can use your journals as a daily reflection tool to record your blessings, draw, sketch, write letters, poems, anything you like. Focusing on our strengths and blessings can go a long way in keeping us centered and grounded."

What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. “I am strong and wise...”

“I now invite you to join me in a color relaxation exercise. If you prefer to just observe, or do something else during this time that is perfectly okay."

"For those of you who wish to participate, I invite you to get in a comfortable position. If you are sitting, you can sit with your feet flat, your back straight and your hands just lying loosely in your lap. If it feels safe for you, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. Now try to picture the colors that come to your mind."

“Take a deep breath... and as you slowly let it out, see yourself surrounded by peaceful sky blue ribbons drifting through the air. Feel yourself calmly breathing in and out. Feel the tension in your body softening and melting away with every breath."

“Picture yourself floating on a soft pink fluffy cloud, feel the music surrounding and caressing you. As you relax your body, notice that you feel very light, almost like cotton candy. Your breathing intuitively is deeper as you begin to feel more and more relaxed."

“Visualize fresh yellow sunshine gently warming your body. You notice all your muscles relaxing and all their knots untying. Notice feeling free. Take a deep breath, fill your lungs... and as you let all the air out, feel any last tension you have totally leave your body."

“Breathe in... and imagine you can smell the wonderful scent of fresh cut green grass and feel a slight breeze clearing your mind."

“Take another deep breath and go to that deep place inside of you and remember how strong you are... Remember how absolutely wonderful you are...  And remember how beautiful you are... just soak these positive thoughts up holding onto them...  knowing that they are all true..."

“When you are ready, you can bring yourself gently back to the room and begin to create your affirmation hearts."
creation:
“You don’t have to study to become
an angel -- just wing it!”

You may wish to remind participants that if they feel comfortable doing so, to create two affirmation hearts for themselves and three to share with the group. You may also with to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create. They have complete freedom to use any of the material available and design their affirmation hearts however they like. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is that they are taking this time to honor their thoughts and feelings and create something that is meaningful to them.
closing:
“Always be an angel-on-call for a friend”

For the closing, you can invite those who created multiple Affirmation Hearts to choose which two hearts they wish to keep for themselves, and then put the other three in a basket or bag. Of course, this is optional. Some may have created one, some may have created multiple and wish to keep them all for themselves. That's perfectly okay.

Once you've collected the Affirmation Hearts participants wished to share, you can pass the basket or bag around the room again and invite each participant to pick one at a time until they are all gone. If they pick their own, they, of course, have a choice to keep it or put it back in the basket and pick again. It might just so happen that if they pick your own, they must really need that affirmation. The participants might feel that there are no coincidences.

If you wish to give participants the option, and if time permits, participants can string the affirmation hearts together to create a heart garland with knots keeping the hearts spaced on their ribbon, yarn or string. Or they can tie a ribbon on each heart separately like you would an ornament or a bookmark.

You can also invite participants to share their favorite affirmation, their creations, anything they may have felt, or experienced, or anything else they may wish to share. Of course, sharing is optional and if no one wishes to share, that's perfectly okay.
description: Provides a space in which participants can notice that healing from emotional abuse is a difficult task and reflect on words they find to be affirming and encouraging and can create hearts to use as a fun and beautiful support in the days ahead.
objective_spanish: Este taller ofrece a los participantes una oportunidad de reflexionar sobre las palabras que son afirmativas y alentadoras, y con ellas crear corazones que pueden ser utilizados como apoyo durante los tiempos difíciles.
materials_spanish:
• Papel de construcción o cartulina (varios colores)
  • Marcadores Bolígrafos de gel Cinta, cuerda o hilo
  • Perforadora para hacer agujeros
  • Palillos de pegamento
  • Tijeras
  • Música relajante
  • Plantillas de corazón

Introducción: 5 min

Demostración: 5 min

Apertura: 10 min

Calentamiento: 5 min

Total: 01:35 (Una Hora y treinta y cinco minutos)
warm_up_spanish:
Usted puede utilizar nuestra relajación sugerida, o el suyo propio. Cuando guíe a los participantes, le recomendamos que hable en un tono suave y calmado,Haga una pausa donde se sienta bien hacerla. "Ahora les invito a unirse a mí en un ejercicio de relajación de color. Si prefieres simplemente observar, o hacer algo más durante este tiempo, está perfectamente bien."

"Para aquellos de ustedes que deseen participar, les invito a ponerse en una posición cómoda. Si usted está sentado, puede sentarse con los pies planos, la espalda recta y sus manos simplemente acostadas libremente en su regazo. Si se siente seguro para usted, puede cerrar los ojos, o mantenerlos abiertos. Ahora trate de imaginar los colores que vienen a su mente."

"Respira profundo... y a medida que sale la respiración,, te ves rodeado de tranquilas cintas de color azul que se deslizan por el aire. Siénta calmadamente respirando y exhalando. Sienta como la tensión en su cuerpo se va ablandando y derritiendo  con cada respiración." "Imagínase que estas flotando en una nube suave, esponjosa y de color rosa esponjoso, siente la música que le rodea y acaricia. A medida que relaja su cuerpo, observe que se siente muy ligero, casi como un  algodón de azúcar. Su respiración intuitivamente es más profunda a medida que comienza a sentirse más y más relajado."

Usted nota que todos sus músculos estan relajándose y todos sus nudos se desatan, detras de su cuello y su espalda. Note que empieza a sentirse libre. Respira profundo, llene sus pulmones... y a medida que deja salir todo el aire, sienta la ultima tension final que haya dejado tu cuerpo.”

"Respira... e imagina que puedes oler el maravilloso aroma de la hierba verde fresca recién  cortada y siente la brisa ligera despejando su mente." "Toma otra respiración profunda  y lo invite a  ir a ese lugar profundo dentro de si mismo y recordar lo fuerte que es... Recuerde lo Hermosa/o que eres… simplemente  manténgase en estos pensamientos positivos hasta aferrarse a ellos...  sabiendo que todos son verdaderos...  "

"Cuando esté listo, para regresar a la habitación y abrir sus ojos y comienze a crear sus corazones de afirmación. "
creation_spanish:
Tal vez desee recordarle a los participantes que si se sienten cómodos al hacerlo, creen dos corazones de afirmación para sí mismos y tres para compartir con el grupo. También puedes recordarle que no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de crear.

Mencione que ellos tienen total libertad para usar cualquiera de los materiales disponibles y diseñar sus corazones de afirmación de la manera que a ellos les gusta.

No importa como se vean. Lo que importa es que están tomando este tiempo para honrar sus pensamientos y sentimientos y crear algo que sea significativo para ellos.
closing_spanish: Para el cierre, puedes invitar a aquellos que crearon múltiples corazones de afirmación para elegir los dos corazones qué desean conservar para sí mismos, y luego poner los otros tres en una canasta. Por supuesto, esto es opcional. Algunos pueden haber creado uno, algunos pueden haber creado múltiples y desean mantenerlos todos para sí mismos. Eso está perfectamente bien. Una vez que hayas recogido los corazones de afirmación que los participantes desearon compartir, puedes pasar la canasta alrededor de la habitación de nuevo e invita a cada participante a escoger uno a la vez hasta que todos se hayan ido. Si recogen los suyos, por supuesto, tienen la opción de guardarlo o ponerlo en la cesta y elige de nuevo. Podría suceder que si escojen la suya, deben realmente necesitar esa afirmación. Los participantes podrían sentir que no hay coincidencias. Si desea dar a los participantes la opción, y si el tiempo lo permite, los participantes pueden encadenar los corazones juntos para crear una guirnalda de corazones con nudos manteniendo los corazones espaciados en su cinta, hilo o cuerda. O pueden atar una cinta en cada corazón por separado como lo haría un ornamento o un marcador. También puede invitar a los participantes a compartir su afirmación favorita, sus creaciones, cualquier cosa que puedan haber sentido o experimentado, o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir. Por supuesto, compartir es opcional y si nadie desea compartir, eso está perfectamente bien.
notes_spanish:
El taller está ordenado debido al hecho de que me inspiro y a su vez puedo inspirar a alguien más ó que podemos recibir  empoderamiento. -Participante

Creo que este programa me ayudó a ser más positivo en mi perspectiva de la vida y de mí mismo. -Participante

Yo estaba enojado cuando llegué-no quería hacer ningún corazón. Pero lo hice. Me encanta el arte, siempre lo he tenido. El collage fue realmente relajante, revelador y curativo. -Participante
