introduction:
“Shout your joy, shout your sadness, shout that you are here and alive...”

"This workshop is window into loving yourself and others more everyday. Today, you'll have an opportunity to create two affirmation hearts for yourself, and three hearts to share with the group via a grab basket. That means you will walk away with a total of five hearts of love with which you can affirm yourself every day. Any kind of trauma can be very difficult to heal from. These hearts with positive affirmations on them are a fun and beautiful way to begin the process of healing.” 

“Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your Window of Time. It's a time for you to notice your thoughts, needs and feelings. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your Window of time, you get to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please ask for what you need. Any questions before I begin?"
introduction_spanish:
Puede imprimir la plantilla de corazón en varias tarjetas de colores o papel de construcción. Es posible que desee cortar los corazones (5 por participante, más algunos extra) por adelantado, ya que esto puede ahorrar tiempo en el taller. O puede incorporar eso en su taller y darles a los participantes la oportunidad de cortar sus propios corazones.

Podría ser útil hacer algunos corazones con anticipación para que usted disfrute y comparta con su grupo. Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos que cree muestras sencillas para que los participantes no se sientan intimidados por ningún desafío "artístico".

Como facilitador-a, usted tiene total libertad de alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento de este taller para satisfacer las necesidades específicas de su grupo.

"Este taller es una ventana para amarte a ti mismo y a los demas cada día. Hoy, tendrás la oportunidad de crear dos corazones de afirmación para ti, y tres corazones para compartir con el grupo. Eso significa que al salir del taller, llevará un total de cinco corazones de amor con los que podrás afirmarse cada día. cualquier tipo de trauma puede ser muy difícil de curar. Estos corazones con afirmaciones positivas sobre ellos son una forma divertida y hermosa de comenzar el proceso de sanación ". Antes de empezar, quiero que sepas que esta es tu ventana de tiempo. Es un momento para que identifique y anote sus pensamientos, necesidades y sentimientos. Durante este tiempo, no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de participar o crear. Voy a compartir algunas instrucciones, pero puede elegir cómo quieres participar. Usted puede seguirme  completamente, o es posible que desee hacer algo diferente, la decisión es completamente suya. Durante su ventana de tiempo, usted elige. Estoy aquí para apoyarlo a usted de cualquier manera que pueda, así que por favor pregunte por lo que necesita. ¿Alguna pregunta antes de empezar?"
demonstration:
You can introduce the participants to the material and give a quick demonstration on how to create the affirmation hearts. If you've made samples in advance, you may wish to pass them out as you explain the steps.

Step 1:
First, you can cut out hearts out of the template (if this hasn't been done in advance). Five hearts per participant is recommended for this workshop, but you are free to invite participants to create as many as you see fit.

Step 2:
Next, you can collage the hearts to create a background with scraps of paper and/or draw designs with the markers or gel rollers on either or both sides of the heart.

Step 3:
You can write an affirmation on each heart. Affirmations can be anything positive and empowering (see images for examples).

Step 4:
For those who wish to hang their affirmation hearts, you can invite them to hole punch the top of each heart and put a ribbon or yarn through and tie up the ends.
demonstration_spanish:
Usted puede introducir a los participantes  el material y dar una demostración rápida sobre cómo crear los corazones de la afirmación. Si has hecho muestras por adelantado, es posible que desees pasarlas a medida que expliques los pasos.

Paso 1: En primer lugar, puede recortar los corazones de la plantilla (si esto no se ha hecho de antemano). se recomiendan para este taller, cinco corazones por participante, pero usted es libre de invitar a los participantes a crear los que deseen.

Paso 2: A continuación, puede hacer un collage con  los corazones para crear un fondo con trozos de papel y/o dibujar diseños con los marcadores o plumas de gel en cualquiera o ambos lados del corazón.

Paso 3: Puedes escribir una afirmación en cada corazón. Las afirmaciones pueden ser cualquier cosa positiva y empoderadora (ver imágenes para ejemplos).

Paso 4: Para aquellos que deseen colgar sus corazones de afirmación, puede invitarlos a perforar la parte superior de cada corazón y poner una cinta o listón a través y atar los extremos.
opening_circle:
You can begin by inviting participants to share what words they find encouraging or anything that they like to hear when they are having a hard day. You might also include a “check-in” so they can share how they are feeling right now; good or bad.

If no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
opening_circle_spanish:
Puede comenzar invitando a los participantes a compartir las palabras que ellos encuentren alentadoras o cualquier cosa que les gusten escuchar cuando estén teniendo un día difícil.

También pueden incluir un "check-in" para que puedan compartir cómo se sienten en este momento; bueno o malo. Si nadie se siente cómodo compartiendo, eso está perfectamente bien.

title: Skeleton Woman
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to explore issues of life, death, love and relationships through the creation of a movable skeleton marionette.
materials:
• Skeleton Woman pattern

  • Cardstock

  • Scissors

  • Paper fasteners (12 per participant)

  • Hole puncher

  • Color pencils
setup:
You are welcome to provide any and as many of the decorative material and mediums as you wish.

You can print a copy of Skeleton Woman pattern for each participant. Feel free to print as large a pattern as you like. If possible, you can print them on heavy cardstock (and skip step 1 of the creation).

You can print a copy of the Women Who Run With the Wolves excerpt to share with the participants for the opening circle.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get a feel for the creation process, as well as to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample and using only the material you are providing, so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Sample Skeleton woman creation

 
 
  Using feathers to decorate the hat

You can now invite those who wish to create to the following creation process. You may want to remind participants that they are free to use the material and supplies however they like. There is no right or wrong way to create or participate.

Feel free to modify the complexity of the creation however you see fit.


Creation:

  1. You can start by gluing a copy of the Skeleton Woman template onto a piece of cardstock (if not printed on cardstock).

  2. You can now use any of the material available and decorate/paint the skeleton however way that you like.

  3. Next, you can cut out all the individual parts.

  4. If you wish, you can add any embellishments to the pieces. You can make a "dress" using fabric (if available), you can decorate the hat with any of the embellishments, etc.

  5. You can then use a hole puncher to punch out holes at every circle (and "X"). These are the joints.

  6. Finally, you can connect the arms, legs, hands and feet to the body with paper fasteners.
closing: You can give participants a chance to volunteer and share their Skeleton Woman creations, what the decorations may represent, anything they discovered, felt, learned or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.
description: Participants create a movable (and/or dancing) Skeleton Woman marionette as a way of exploring issues of life, death, love and relationships. Uses the "Skeleton Woman" story in the book "Women Who Run With the Wolves" to spark the creative process.
notes: If you are doing this workshop in October or November, you can make this a Dia De Los Muertos theme, a Mexican celebration where the dead members of the family are remembered, honored and their lives celebrated by a big party. An alter is made with pictures, flowers, food, and articles of the person that passed away. The celebration is also a way to teach that death is a natural process and that you should enjoy life, of which, death is also a part.
optional_materials:
• Paint

  • Brushes

  • Markers


Your choice of embellishments:

  • Pieces of cloth (with thread and needles)

  • Feathers

  • Beads

  • Sparklers / glitter / sequins

  • Women Who Run With the Wolves excerpt
introduction:
Skeleton Woman sample
 

"Today, you will have an opportunity to explore issues of life, death, love and relationships through the creation of a movable skeleton marionette."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration: You can introduce the art supplies and demonstrate any creation application and/or techniques that you see fit.
opening_circle:
Group photo of Skeleton Woman creations

For the opening circle, you give participants a brief overview of the Skeleton Woman myth from the Women Who Run With the Wolves excerpt. You can then facilitate a discussion around the topics of life, death, love, relationships, and or any topic that is more relevant to your group.

If anyone prefers to just observe, that's okay too. Observing is participating.

title: My Butterfly / Mi Mariposa
objective: This workshop aims to help participants notice their resilience and see their pain and challenges transform through the process of creating a butterfly that symbolizes their ability to move on from trauma and come out stronger and more whole.
materials:
• Paper towels

  • Cardstock (construction paper)

  • Scissors

  • Hole punchers

  • Puffy paints

  • Oil pastels (CrayPas)

  • Toothpicks (for scratching)

  • Pipe cleaners (variety of colors; to create the antenna)

  • The Butterfly story
setup:
You can lay out the art supplies so each participant has easy access to them.

You may want to cover the tables with newspaper to protect from the paint.

If you wish, you can print a copy of The Butterfly Story handout for each participant.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get the feel for the creation process, as well as to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample and using only the material you're providing so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

If you see fit, you may consider cutting out a butterfly in advance for each participant to use as a template to trace (see step 1 of template). This is up to you.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Colorful My Butterfly creations

You can now invite those who wish to create to begin doing so. You may wish to remind the participants that there is no right or wrong way to create and it doesn't matter what their butterfly looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to honor their resilience, courage and strength and creating something that is expressive and meaningful to them.
closing:
You can give participants a chance to share their butterfly, what it represents, anything they learned, felt or experienced during the creation process, or anything else they may wish to share.

Of course, this is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
description: To offer participants a 'window of time' to notice their beautiful resilience. To give participants an opportunity to see their pain and challenges transform through a process of noticing their strengths, resources and wholeness. The end product is a reminder of how we can move through our trauma and come out stronger and more whole.
objective_spanish: Este taller tiene como objetivo ayudar a las y los participantes a darse cuenta de su capacidad de recuperación y poder ver cómo se transforman sus desafíos y su dolor a través del proceso de la creación de una mariposa que simboliza su capacidad para atravesar una situación traumática y salir más fuerte y más entera y entero.

setup_spanish:
Puede acomodar los materiales de arte para que cada participante tenga fácil acceso a ellos.

Es posible que desee cubrir las mesas con papel periódico o un mantel desechable para protegerlas de la pintura.

Si lo desea, puede imprimir una copia del folleto “La historia de la mariposa” para cada participante.

Puede ser útil crear una muestra antes del taller para familiarizarse con el proceso de creación, también para mostrar a las y los participantes cómo puede verse la pieza de arte terminada. Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos que cree una muestra simple y use solo el material que está proporcionando para que las y los participantes no se sientan abrumados por los desafíos "artísticos".

Si lo considera conveniente, puede considerar cortar una mariposa por adelantado para que cada participante la use como plantilla para trazar su propia mariposa (vea el paso 1 de la plantilla). Esto depende completamente de usted.

Siéntase con la libertad de alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento de este taller para poder servir las necesidades específicas del grupo.
creation_spanish: Ahora puede invitar a comenzar a aquellas y aquellos que deseen crear la mariposa. Tal vez desee recordarles a las y los participantes que no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de crear y que no importa cómo se vea su mariposa. Lo importante es que se tomen este tiempo para honrar su capacidad de recuperación, coraje y fuerza y creen algo que sea expresivo y significativo para ellas y ellos.
closing_spanish:
Puede darles a las y los participantes la oportunidad de compartir su mariposa, lo que representa, todo lo que aprendieron, sintieron o experimentaron durante el proceso de creación, o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir.

Por supuesto, esto es opcional y si nadie se siente cómoda o cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.

introduction:
"All butterflies go through a period of transformation to become the awesome creatures that they are. You may know that they start off as caterpillars before they become butterflies. I have a story to share with you about how a butterfly becomes beautiful and strong."

You can read The Butterfly story to the participants, or pass out copies of the handout and invite the participants to read either on their own or a paragraph each, etc.

After reading the story:

"Like a butterfly, we all go through life overcoming challenges and learning lessons through our experience. Getting through the hard times can help us see how we are powerful, strong and uniquely beautiful. Today, you’ll get a chance to notice your beautiful resilience and create a butterfly of your own."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
introduction_spanish:
"Todas las mariposas pasan por un período de transformación para convertirse en las maravillosas criaturas que son. Quizás sepan que éstas comienzan como orugas antes convertirse en mariposas. Les voy a compartir una historia sobre cómo una mariposa se vuelve bella y fuerte".

Puede leer la historia en el folleto “La historia de la mariposa” a las y los participantes, o repartir copias del folleto e invitar a las y los participantes a leer por su cuenta o un párrafo cada participante, etc.

Después de leer la historia:

"Como la mariposa, todas y todos pasamos por la vida superando desafíos y aprendiendo lecciones a través de nuestra experiencia. Superar los momentos difíciles puede ayudarnos a ver cómo somos poderosas y poderosos, fuertes y especialmente hermosas y hermosos. Hoy, tendrán la oportunidad de notar su bella resiliencia y crear su propia mariposa."

“Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que esta es su ventana de tiempo. Esto significa que este tiempo puede ser un lugar seguro para que noten sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que decidan hacer o decir es voluntario. Durante este tiempo, no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta para participar o crear. Voy a compartir con ustedes unas instrucciones básicas, sin embargo, ustedes deciden cómo quieren participar. Pueden seguir las instrucciones por completo o tal vez quieran hacer algo diferente, depende completamente de ustedes. Durante su ventana de tiempo, tienen completa libertad de decidir. Como decidan pasar este tiempo está perfectamente bien. Yo estoy aquí para apoyarles de cualquier forma que pueda, así que siéntanse libres de pedirme lo que necesiten.”
demonstration:
You can take a few minutes to introduce the art supplies and materials and share the following creation steps with the participants. If you've made a sample, you may want to pass it around at this time. Feel free to demonstrate any of the elements as you see fit.
 

    
  My Butterfly creation
 
 
  coloring with oil pastels
 
 
  Mother and child creating

 

Step 1: (If you haven't created a template in advance)
"To begin, you can fold any color piece of cardstock in half, and cut to create a half of a butterfly shape. Open the fold to reveal your butterfly."


Step 2: (Antenna)
"If you want to have antenna on your butterfly, you can punch a holes at the top and thread a wire (pipe cleaner) through it after you've painted your butterfly."

Note, it’s easier to do this before the paint is added.


Step 3: (Adding Oil Pastels)
"Next, you can use the oil pastels to cover your butterfly with any color that you like. You can use one color, or as many colors as there are. You can layer colors and create new ones. However you choose to decorate your butterfly will be perfect."


Step 4: (Adding Puffy Paint)
"After adding the oil pastels, you can add any color, and as many colors puffy paints to your butterfly any way you like. If you like, you can choose oil pastel colors that represent the difficulties and challenges you've faced in your life in the previous step, and choose puffy paint colors to represent your resilience, strength and courage that helped you overcome those challenges and made you the amazing person you are today. You can add the paint on top of the oil pastels in any shape or fashion that you like."


Step 5:  (Folding the Butterfly)
"Once you're done with the coloring, you can fold your butterfly in half with the paint inside and press so that some of the paint squeezes out of the edges, then gently open it back up to reveal the amazing shapes and colors that your butterfly has formed."


Step 6: (Adding Embellishments)
"If you like, you can use a toothpick to scratch through the paint and add lines, shapes, symbols, or words. You can also add glitter, sequins (if available) to your butterfly and let it dry."


Step 7: (Adding the Antenna)
"Finally, if you like, you can now use any color pipe cleaner and put it through the punched hole, fold it in half and bend the ends to create the butterfly antenna."
demonstration_spanish:
Puede tomar unos minutos para presentar los materiales de arte y compartir los siguientes pasos creativos con las y los participantes. Si ha creado una muestra, es posible que desee mostrarla en este momento. Siéntase libre de mostrar cualquiera de los elementos que considere oportunos.

Paso 1: (Si no ha creado una plantilla de antemano)

"Para comenzar, pueden doblar cualquier cartulina (o papel de construcción) de color por la mitad y cortar en forma de la mitad de una mariposa. Abra el pliegue para revelar tu mariposa".

Paso 2: (Antena)

"Si quieren que su mariposa tenga antenas, antes de pintar pueden hacerle un agujero en la parte superior y pasar un tallo de chenilla (limpiador de tuberías) a través de él cuando su mariposa esté pintada".

Tengan en cuenta que es más fácil hacer el agujero antes de agregar la pintura.

"A continuación, pueden usar los pasteles al óleo para cubrir su mariposa con el color que deseen. Pueden usar únicamente un color, o todos los colores que deseen. Pueden combinar colores y crear nuevos. De cualquier forma, está perfecto cómo ustedes decidan decorar sus mariposas."

Paso 4: (Añadiendo pintura de relieve)

"Después de agregar los pasteles al óleo, pueden agregar a sus mariposas cualquier color o colores de pintura de relieve como decidan. Si lo desean, en el paso anterior, al agregar los colores de pastel al óleo pueden elegir colores que representen las dificultades y los desafíos que han enfrentado en sus vidas. Ahora al agregar la pintura de relieve, pueden elegir colores que representen su resiliencia, fuerza y coraje que les ayudaron a superar esos desafíos y les convirtió en las increíbles personas que son hoy. Pueden agregar la pintura de relieve sobre la pintura de pastel al óleo en cualquier forma que gusten."

Paso 5: (Doblando la mariposa)

"Una vez que hayan terminado con el color, puede doblar su mariposa por la mitad con la pintura interior y presionar de manera que parte de la pintura de relieve se esparza fuera de los bordes, luego abrirla de nuevo suavemente para revelar las asombrosas formas y colores que sus mariposas han formado ".

Paso 6: (Añadiendo los adornos)

"Si lo desean, pueden usar un palillo para raspar la pintura y agregar líneas, formas, símbolos o palabras. También pueden agregar diamantina, lentejuelas (si tienen disponibles) a sus mariposas y dejar que se sequen".

Paso 7: (Añadiendo la antena)

"Finalmente, si lo desean, ahora puede usar cualquier color de los tallos de chenilla (limpiador de tuberías) y colocarlo a través del orificio perforado, doblar el tallo de chenilla por la mitad y doblar los extremos del mismo para crear las antenas de sus mariposas."
opening_circle: You can open by giving participants who wish to do so, the option to share any challenges they've overcome in their life and what lesson they learned from that experience.
opening_circle_spanish: Puede comenzar dando a las y los participantes que lo deseen, la opción de compartir cualquier desafío que hayan superado en su vida y qué lección aprendieron de esa experiencia.

title: Eagles in a Storm
objective: To give each participant an opportunity to identify the “storms” they are facing in their life, choose the perspective they want to hold through it, and create a beautiful visual reminder to carry with them as they rise above these “storms.”
materials:
• Plain white paper

  • Clear plastic wrap

  • Aluminum foil

  • Scotch tape

  • Feather pattern template (1 per participant)

  • Permanent markers (Sharpies; variety of colors)

  • Scissors

  • Glue sticks
setup:
You may consider creating a sample eagle feather for yourself in advance to get the feel for the creation process as well as to show participants what the art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest making a simple sample so that participants aren't intimidated by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
If you're using relaxing music, you may play it in the background while guiding the relaxation. You are welcome to use our suggested guided relaxation, or your own. It's entirely up to you. We recommend speaking in a soft, calming tone and pausing where it feels right.

“I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief relaxation. You are welcome to participate, observe, or use this time to do something else. It's entirely up to you. For those of you who wish to participate, I'd like to invite you to get in a comfortable position. You can rest your feet on the floor and your arms are comfortably in your lap, or if you prefer, you can lie down. You can closer your eyes, or keep them open. However you are most comfortable."

"Now take a deep breath in, and hold it for a moment... and as you let it out, imagine releasing any tension you are carrying from the day. Take another deep breath in, and again release with it any tension you may be carrying. Try to notice your body becoming more relaxed as you take another breath in...  and release...  As you take another deep breath and release it, imagine you are releasing any storms and turmoil you’ve been facing and feeling. Imagine that with each breath you take you are finding calm and clarity, and with each breath you release, you are rising higher above any storms, able to find more strength... and that strength gives you peace and serenity. Take as many breaths as you wish. And whenever you are ready, you can open your eyes and come back to this moment.”
creation:
You can now invite the participants to begin creating their Eagle Feathers. You may wish to remind them that they are free to create however they wish and use any of the material provided. They can write words on their feathers, draw symbols, color them or anything else they wish. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is that they are taking this moment to notice and honor the courage and strength they hold within to create something that is meaningful to them.

 

Step 1: You can start by taping the feather pattern onto the table.

 

Step 2: Next, you can tape a piece of plastic wrap over the feather pattern.

 

Step 3: Using permanent markers, you can trace and color the feather onto the plastic wrap. You can use any color and design your feather however way you like.

 

Step 4: Next, you can either crumble a piece of square tin foil, then flatten it back out again to create a textured surface, or keep the foil smooth. It's entirely up to you.

 

Step 5: Once your foil is ready, you can apply glue on the back of the plastic wrap. We suggest gluing the entire back side.

 

Step 6: You can place the plastic wrap onto the tin foil and gently press so the glue holds it together.

 

Step 7: You can cut out the feather. You may wish to pay careful attention when cutting the quill of the feather (the narrow end). Once cut, the feather can be bend, cut or molded further.

 

Step 8: On the back of the feather, you can add words, draw symbols, color, or anything else you like to go with your feather. You can date it, if you like. You can smooth out parts of the foil you wish to write on.
closing:
For the closing, you may give the participants an opportunity to share their eagle feathers, what it means to them, anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

You may wish to congratulate and validate the participants for their courage to be part of the workshop today.
description: Gives participants an opportunity to identify the "storms" faced in their lives, and choose the perspective they would like to hold through them. End product is a beautiful visual reminder to rise above the "storms."
notes:
About this Workshop:
This workshop was adapted from an e-mail story we received via Denise Nyby who coordinates the Windows Programs in Redding, CA. As with many internet inspirational thoughts, the message was anonymous. We thank Denise for sending it to us and hope you and your groups will enjoy it.
optional_materials: • Relaxing music (for relaxation)
introduction:
“Today, you will have an opportunity to create your own special eagle’s feather. This workshop provides you with a chance to notice any storms you may be facing in your life and to connect with the strength you hold within, to help you use the winds of the storm to lift you high above it. These beliefs and strengths are part of your eagle’s feather.”

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
You may wish to do a quick demonstration of the creation process (see Creation) before the relaxation. You can also show your sample eagle's feather if you've made one.

If possible, you may wish to show participants images of various eagles' feathers.

We suggest distributing the supplies before you start the relaxation. That way, once the relaxation ends, participants can begin creating.
opening_circle:
If you see fit, you can share the following Eagles In A Storm story with the participants and invite them to a discussion.

"Did you know that an eagle knows that a storm is approaching long before the storm breaks? The eagle will fly to a spot high in the sky and wait for the winds to come. When the storm hits, the eagle sets its wings so that the wind can pick it up and lift it above the storm. While the storm rages below, the eagle is soaring above it."

"The eagle does not escape the storm. It simply uses the storm to lift it higher. It rises on the winds that bring the storm. When the storm of life come upon us, and all of us experience them, we can rise above it by setting our mind and our beliefs toward that which is deepest in our hearts: our sources of clarity and strength. The storms do not have to overcome us. We can focus on that which lifts us above them."

"We can find the clarity and strength to ride the winds of the storm that bring sickness, tragedy, failure, and disappointment in our lives. We can soar above them."

"Remember, it is not the burdens of life that weigh us down, it's how we handle them."

~Unknown source

title: My Butterfly
objective: This workshop aims to help children notice their resilience and see their pain and challenges transform through the process of creating a butterfly that symbolizes their ability to move on from trauma and come out stronger and more whole.
materials:
• Paper towels

  • Cardstock (construction paper)

  • Scissors

  • Hole punchers

  • Puffy paints

  • Oil pastels (CrayPas)

  • Toothpicks (for scratching)

  • Pipe cleaners (variety of colors; to create the antenna)

  • The Butterfly story
setup:
You can lay out the art supplies so each participant has easy access to them.

You may want to cover the tables with newspaper to protect from the paint.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get the feel for the creation process, as well as to show the children what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample and using only the material you're providing so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

If you see fit, you may consider cutting out a butterfly in advance for each child to use as a template to trace (see step 1 of template). This is up to you.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
“Before we start, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief warm-up exercise. If you prefer to observe, that's perfectly okay. Observing is participating."

"For those of you who wish to follow along, let’s pretend we are baby butterflies. Do you remember how a butterfly starts out when it’s a baby? That’s right. It’s a cocoon. So let’s start as cocoons (you can curl up on the floor or squat)."

"Can you get curled up really tight? There you go. And now you’re growing, starting to wiggle, and you think maybe it’s time to start making your way out of your cocoon. Can you make a little hole? And wiggle, wiggle wiggle."

"I think I see some butterflies coming out (you can wiggle your way out of the cocoon and into becoming butterflies). Beautiful! Can you enjoy all the air and all the space around you as you stretch your new wings? And let’s stretch and fly until every little cocoon has turned into a beautiful butterfly.”

You can playfully pretend-fly around the room with the children, then invite them back to their seats.
creation:
Proud participant showing her butterflies

You can now invite those who wish to create to begin doing so. You may wish to remind the children that there is no right or wrong way to create and it doesn't matter what their butterfly looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to honor their resilience, courage and strength and creating something that is expressive and meaningful to them.

Some children may need help with certain elements of the creation process, so feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
closing:
You can give the children a chance to share their butterfly, what it represents, anything they learned, felt or experienced during the creation process, or anything else they may wish to share.

Of course, this is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

This is a good opportunity for you to validate the children's courage and resilience and empower them to continue to use their strength to overcome any challenges that may lay ahead.
description: To offer participants a 'window of time' to notice their beautiful resilience. To give participants an opportunity to see their pain and challenges transform through a process of noticing their strengths, resources and wholeness. The end product is a reminder of how we can move through our trauma and come out stronger and more whole.
optional_materials:
• My Butterfly Template 1

  • My Butterfly Template 2

  • My Butterfly Template 3

  • Glitter

  • Sequins

  • Newspaper (or disposable table cover)

“I'd like to share a story with you. It’s a sad story, but it’s an important story with a lesson. This is a story about a butterfly coming out of a cocoon. Does anybody know what a cocoon is?"

(Feel free to engage the children in a discussion if you see fit and they feel comfortable).

"A cocoon is how a butterfly starts out when it’s a baby. And then when it is ready, the butterfly comes out of the cocoon and spreads its wings to fly."

You can now read The Butterfly story to the children.

After sharing the story:

"Today, you'll have a chance to create your very own butterfly and decorate it however way that you like. Your butterfly can be a reminder that hard things that happen to us can make us stronger, smarter and even more beautiful."

Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
You can take a few minutes to introduce the art supplies and materials and share the following creation steps with the participants. If you've made a sample, you may want to pass it around at this time. Depending on the age group, some children may need help with certain elements of creation. Feel free to demonstrate any of the elements as you see fit.

     
  Participant applying paint to her butterfly
 
 
  Mother and child creating
 
 
  Finished butterflies waiting to dry
 
 
  Finished butterflies


Step 1: (If you haven't created a template in advance)
"To begin, you can fold any color piece of cardstock in half, and cut to create a half of a butterfly shape. Open the fold to reveal your butterfly."


Step 2: (Antenna)
"If you want to have antenna on your butterfly, you can punch a holes at the top and thread a wire (pipe cleaner) through it after you've painted your butterfly."

Note, it’s easier to do this before the paint is added.


Step 3: (Adding Oil Pastels)
"Next, you can use the oil pastels to cover your butterfly with any color that you like. You can use one color, or as many colors as there are. You can layer colors and create new ones. However you choose to decorate your butterfly will be perfect."


Step 4: (Adding Puffy Paint)
"After adding the oil pastels, you can add any color, and as many colors puffy paints to your butterfly any way you like. If you like, you can choose oil pastel colors that represent the difficulties and challenges you've faced in your life in the previous step, and choose puffy paint colors to represent your resilience, strength and courage that helped you overcome those challenges and made you the amazing person you are today. You can add the paint on top of the oil pastels in any shape or fashion that you like."


Step 5:  (Folding the Butterfly)
"Once you're done with the coloring, you can fold your butterfly in half with the paint inside and press so that some of the paint squeezes out of the edges, then gently open it back up to reveal the amazing shapes and colors that your butterfly has formed."


Step 6: (Adding Embellishments)
"If you like, you can use a toothpick to scratch through the paint and add lines, shapes, symbols, or words. You can also add glitter, sequins (if available) to your butterfly and let it dry."


Step 7: (Adding the Antenna)
"Finally, if you like, you can now use any color pipe cleaner and put it through the punched hole, fold it in half and bend the ends to create the butterfly antenna."
opening_circle: You can invite the children, if any feel comfortable doing so, to share if they’ve ever been through something difficult, but found out that it helped them to grow. Examples could be doing homework, practicing a sport, a musical instrument, a dance move, learning to share with their brothers and sisters, or any other example that may be relevant to your specific group.

title: Scared/Safe Quilt
objective: This workshop aims to create a safe space for participants to express their feelings about a time they felt scared and a time they felt safe.
materials:
• 8” X 8” fabric—two per participant

  • Fabric markers

  • Fabric crayons/pastels

  • Writing utensil and paper for Warm-up
setup: You may choose to lay the art supplies on the table for easier access to the participants. It is also encouraged to create a sample of the Scared/Safe Quilt in order for the participants to see what it can look like. However, we suggest creating a simple sample, so that participants are not overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges. It's also important to note that being scared can be sad and serious, therefore we recommend doing the "scared" square part of the creation first, then the "safe" square second, in order to leave the participants on a positive note.
warm_up:
During this part, each participant should have a separate sheet of paper that they can write and/or draw on. If they like they can fold the paper vertically (hot dog style) in order to separate their scared and safe feelings and experiences. 

Journaling Prompt:

"In this time, I encourage you to think about a time you were scared. What did you feel? Where were you? Was anyone with you? What colors, smell, sounds were present? Go ahead and draw/write it all on your paper."

Allow some time for the participants to draw and/or write. 

"Now think of a time when you felt safe and protected: What was it like? Where were you? Was anyone with you? What colors, smells, sounds were present?"

"When you are done you may pick up your 'scared' and 'safe' squares and draw your feelings and thoughts regarding a time you felt scared on one square and your thoughts and feelings regarding a time you felt safe on the other. You may use what was written/drawn in your journal as a guide to decide what to create on your 'scared' and 'safe' square."
creation: Feel free to offer assistance if needed and remind participants that there is no right or wrong way to create their artwork. You may also provide time reminders for the participants in order to avoid them from feeling rushed towards the end.
closing:
During the closing, allow participants time to share what they learned, thought, and felt during the workshop/creation process. Remember, sharing is voluntary and observation and/or listening is participation. If there is not enough time, you may also encourage participants to have a "sitting exhibit" where they hold up their art work and they get to see other's work while also sharing their own. 

Last, thank the participants for joining in creating this safe/brave space.

Completed Scared/Safe Quilt from
Humboldt Women for Shelter
 
  Completed Workshop Worksheet
description: Creates a safe space for children to express their feelings about a time they felt scared and a time they felt safe. Honors their experiences and expressions by putting them into a quilt which can help raise awareness about domestic violence in the community.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Scared/Safe Quilt Worksheet

  • Cardstock (to glue paper quilt if sewing is not possible)

  • Puffy paints are also good to use with fabric.

 

 
Scared/Safe Quilt Worksheet
introduction: "Before we begin I would like to mention that this time and space is a window of time for you. In this time, participation is voluntary and can look differently for each of you. In this time I encourage you to focus on your thoughts, feelings, and needs. I will be here to guide you in the creation process, however, you are free to create however you like. There is no right or wrong way to create."
demonstration:
During this time you may walk the participants through each of the supplies, creation steps, and then share the example that you created. 

1. First start with the 'scared' square and you can use your thoughts, writing, and/or drawing from the warm-up for guidance in this creation. Participants can use words, shapes, drawings, or a combination of both.  


2.  Participants can follow the same process from step 1 to create their 'safe' square. 


3. If sewing is not possible, have the participants glue their fabric to cardstock in order to have a sturdy background. Participants may also choose to decorate the background.
opening_circle:
“Today, we are going to make squares for a quilt together. This is going to be a Scared/Safe quilt, meaning we each get to think of a time where we felt scared and a time where we felt safe." 

You may hold up the two squares to demonstrate to the participants. 

"One square is for your scared feelings and one square is for your safe feelings. We will first start with the 'scared' square then move on to the 'safe' square."

title: Inside/Outside / Adentro/Afuera
objective:
Helps create awareness and a stronger sense of self by exploring the self that we allow others to see and the self that is on the inside. In this workshop, participants use creative paper folding, symbolism and journaling to represent their inside and outside selves.

This project was brought to us by Karen Akamine who was trained at the Armory Center for the Arts in Pasadena. The concept was adapted into this workshop by the AWBW staff.
materials:
• Colored construction paper

  • Copy paper

  • Cray-Pas

  • Colored pencils

  • Pens
setup:
Table Set-Up

We recommend that you prepare the supplies and set up in advance to help things go smoothly. You might want to create an example of the journaling page with copy paper as well as different types of folds (see figures below) with construction paper.
warm_up:
"To help jog our thinking and get us ready to create, we are going to do a quick journaling exercise. You can choose a piece of copy paper and fold it in half, long ways, dividing it into two columns.

On one side, you can write ‘Inside’ and on the other side, you can write ‘Outside.’ You can choose to write on either side of the paper, the top and bottom, in a circle and around it, or whatever way you choose to represent "inside" and "outside."

  • Inside: On the "inside" part of the paper, you can write words or phrases that describe how you feel and look like on the inside. How would you describe or tell about the you that you or only a few people may know about?

  • Outside: On the "outside" part of the paper, you can write words or phrases that describe how you feel and look like on the outside. How would you describe or tell about the you that you show to the world?
creation:
"Next, I invite you to choose a piece of construction paper and fold it so it has an inside and an outside. You can also feel free to get creative with your folds and show your expression through unique folds (refer to the different folding options below). I will demonstrate some different folds that you can try out on your creations to represent the inner and outer you.

Door Fold Triangle Fold Diamond Fold (open and closed)  Double Door Fold
       

"Think about the outside you, and when you are ready, you can start with the outside of your paper. On the outside are you bright or dark? Are you sharp or soft? Are you foggy or clear? Think about the words that you wrote down on your journaling page. What colors come to mind when you think of those words? Can you add any shapes or symbols that go along with those words?

"With the Cray-Pas, use shapes and colors to draw how you are on the outside. When you are ready, you can move to the inside. Open up your paper and think about how you are on the inside. Are you bright or dark? Are you one color or many colors? Are you soft or rough? Use Cray-Pas to draw shapes and colors that show the inside ‘you’ on the inside of your paper. When you are finished, you can write any words that go with your creation."

Note: Welcome participants to start on any part of their creation as desired. Some participants might find it easier to start on a specific part of their creation first. As you notice participants finishing up, encourage them to think about how they might want to take care of themselves, inside and outside. What are some of the things they can do?

 "Outside" with symbols and images  "Inside" with words and images
 "Outside" with words and images  "Inside" with words and images
closing:
Give each participant an opportunity to share their creation and how it felt to create it. You can also ask how they plan to take care of themselves, inside and outside.

Validate their courage for opening themselves up to their own creativity and respecting whatever came out.
description: Helps create awareness and a stronger sense of self by exploring the self that we allow others to see and the self that is on the inside. In this workshop, participants use creative paper folding, symbolism and journaling to represent their inside and outside selves.
objective_spanish:
Explorar y conocer la persona que dejas que los demás conozcan, y la persona que llevas dentro o debajo.

Materiales:

  • 9”X12” papel de color

  • Pasteles de tiza

  • Toalla de papel

  • Plumas y papel para escribir

  • (Opción: mujeres pueden utilizar sus agendas)

  • Hoja informativa (para taller individual)

  • Variaciones alternativas:  Este taller puede utilizar collage envés de pasteles.  Utilizando collage se puede utilizar cajas o bolsas en vez de papel de color.


Tiempo:

  • Tiempo total:  1 hora

  • Intro: 5 minutos

  • Circulo de abertura:  10 minutos

  • Escribir en Agenda:  10 minutos

  • Creación:  30 minutos

  • Circulo de clausura:  10 minutos


Organizar:
Ayuda bastante cuando los materiales están preparados antes del taller.  Intenta varias maneras de doblar el papel, para mostrar a las mujeres.  Usa los pastels para hacer un ejemplo. Podrás notar si hay material que hace falta.

Introducción:
“Este tiempo es especial es ‘una ventana en tiempo’ para cada una de ustedes.  El taller que vamos hacer se llama Dentro/Fuera.  Es una oportunidad para explorar el “tu” que la gente ve afuera y el “tu” que solo tu conoces por dentro.  Vamos a utilizar papel doblado y pastels para crear el afuera y adentro que tenemos, usando diferentes formas y colores.  

Circulo de abertura:
Toma el tiempo para dar la bienvenida a todos, dejándole saber que son apreciados.  “Antes de empezar el arte,  vamos a tener un circulo para compartir nuestros nombres, como se sienten hoy, y sus sentimientos hacia el arte.”  Es buen tiempo para asegurar les que esta bien si tienen miedo y esta bien si lo “odian.”  Recuérdales que no tienen que hacer el taller.  Pueden observar si no quieren participar.  Dando la libertad para participar motiva a la gente que solo piensa observar.  Si no quieren compartir, deja les saber que esta bien.

Agenda Calentamiento:
“Vamos ha empezar escribiendo en nuestras agendas.  Dividan una hoja de papel en dos.  De un lado escriban “Adentro” del otro lado escriban “Afuera.”  Llenen el lado que dice adentro con palabras que describen como se sienten adentro al otro lado escriban palabras que describan lo que la gente ve afuera.  Traten de no pensar tanto cuando escriben.  Permitan que las palabras salgan naturalmente.  Si no pueden pensar en más palabras vallan a la próxima columna y regresen a la primera después.  Después de que terminen tomen un momento para observar las palabras que han escrito sin juzgar.  Simplemente reconózcanlas y acéptenlas como parte de ustedes.  Las palabras servirán como guía durante su creación.”

Creación:
“Ahora escoge una pieza de papel y dobla la para que tenga un porción adentro y una afuera.  Empieza a crear la parte de afuera mientras que piensas en colores, texturas, y formas, cosas que te describen por fuera.  Siempre puedes leer las cosas que has escrito en tu papel.  Eres brillante, oscura, fuerte, o clara?

Cuando estés lista abre tu papel y piensa como eres por dentro.  Eres brillante, oscura, suave o dura?  Eres varios colores o uno?  Usa los pastels o collaging para decorar la parte de adentre y de afuera de tu papel.

Cuando termines toma unos minutos para anotar unas palabras que vallan con tu creación.  (Puedes tomar un minuto para animar a las mujeres en pensar de diferentes maneras que se pueden cuidar por dentro y por fuera)

Circulo de Clausura:
Da a cada mujer una oportunidad para compartir lo que ha creado, lo que quiere decir y lo que siente.  Valida el valor que tuvieron en abrirse con su propia creatividad y por respetar lo que salio.

You may also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

introduction:
When possible, try to individually welcome each participant and let them know you are glad they are there. One-on-one contact can help them get connected and feel safe and comfortable enough to truly use their Windows time for themselves.

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you do or say is voluntary. I will offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create. Just because I choose to demonstrate a certain way though does not mean there is a right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. Please ask for what you need, and know that I am here to support you. If you are having trouble thinking or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just play with the materials."
opening_circle:
"The workshop we are doing today is called Inside/Outside. It is a chance to explore the ‘you’ that people see on the outside, and the ‘you’ that you know is on the inside. We will be using folded paper, Cray-Pas, and colored pencils to create our inside and outside selves with words, shapes, and symbols.

"Before we start, I invite you to share your name and two words and/or body movements if you would like:

  • The first thing is a word and/or body movement that describes/shows how you feel on the inside.

  • The second is a word and/or body movement that describes/shows how your feel on the outside. I will give you a moment to think about what you would like to share or if you would like to share at all. 

Again, this is your window of time and everything is voluntary. As long as you are honoring your needs, you are just fine."

title: Angel Workshop
objective: This workshop gives children an opportunity to create angels out of paper plates.
materials:
• Angel template

  • Paper plates (the template is designed for 9" diameter plates)

  • Angel Words template

  • Scissors

  • Stapler

  • Hat / basket / bowl (for Opening circle)
setup:
Paper plate angel template


 

To save time during the workshop and simplify the creation process for the children, you may want to precut the angel templates in advance and make a blank paper plate angel for each child in advance. To do this, you can print a copy of the Angel template, cut it out and use it as a stencil to trace onto the back of a paper plate (9" diameter). Most of the template should line up with the outline of the plate. You can then cut out the parts that form the angel's head and neck as well as the two slits out of the plate (see image on the right).

It may take a couple of tries to align the template onto the plate, so feel free to experiment the best method for you.

You can make one for each child and a few spare extras.

A simpler alternative would be to print the template onto heavy card stock paper and use the paper as opposed to paper plates. It's entirely up to you.

You can also print a copy of the Angel Words template and cutting out each individual word, and placing them all in a hat or basket for the opening circle.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get a feel for the creation process, as well as to show children what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample and using only the decorative material you're providing, so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You may find this How To Make Paper Angels video helpful. The creation process is almost the same.

You are welcome to provide any and as many of the decorative material (paint, markers, etc.) that you see fit.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Precut angel
 
  Step 1
 
  Step 2
 
  Step 3
 
  Step 4

You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation steps with the children. You may want to demonstrate any creation elements and/or techniques that you see fit. For example, if you're providing the painting option, you can show them how they can mix different colors paint to come up with a new color, how to rinse their brush in the water, etc.



Step 1:
Children can take a pre-cut angel plate and bend the sides of the plate backwards.


Step 2:
Bend the left wing upside down and tuck slit A into slit B so the wings cross in the back. It helps if you pull the two slits into each other as far as they can so the end of the slits touch.


Step 3:
Gently expand the skirt of the angel to make it circular.


Step 4:
To secure the wings in their position, you can staple the back.


Step 5:
You can pull and adjust neck and head position, and you have your assembled angel.

 

Children can then use any of the decorative material (markers, paint, etc.) and decorate their angel however they like.
closing: You can give children a chance to volunteer and share their angel creations, anything they discovered, learned or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.
description: Encourages children to explore non-violent words and ideas. Helps them cope with past crisis and trauma and foster their sense of safety and security by creating their own angel.
notes:
It is important not to assume that everyone celebrates Christmas. You many want to have an alternative project planned for children who choose not to make a paper plate angel.

You can also compare and angel to a guardian, or a source of positivity and strength for younger children, or those whose religious/spiritual background do not incorporate angels or any variations thereof.
