Sample Angel Workshop creations with feathers, ribbons and paint

 

"Today, you have an opportunity to create your own guardian angel."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
opening_circle:
Angel Workshop creation
 

For the opening, you can invite those who want to follow along, to pick a word out of the basket at random and share what it means to them. If you see fit, you can go around more than once and give children a chance to pick more than one word.

You can then facilitate a discussion about angels by asking them: "What are angels?" and inviting them to share their ideas.

title: My Footprints
objective: To allow the children to validate and express feelings about their unique journey through the creation of a special footprint.
materials:
• Poster board

  • Markers

  • Footprint template

  • Glue sticks

  • Scissors

  • Magazines and/or stickers

  • "Footprints in the Sand" poem
setup: Some children may not feel comfortable taking off their shoes in order to trace their feet. You may wish to have some footprints cut out in advance. You can trace your own foot or invite another child during the workshop to volunteer, if they feel comfortable doing so, to have their foot traced as a generic print for others to use. It's entirely up to you.
warm_up:
To get the children to focus on their journey and get comfortable in creating, you may read the "Footprints In the Sand" poem.

Or you may wish to incorporate a feet warm-up exercise. We have used this exercise in the past, but you are welcome to adapt, alter or use your own warm-up exercise.

“Before we get started, I'd like to invite you to join me in a feet warm-up exercise. Again, this is completely optional, so if you wish to observe instead or follow along in your seat, you are welcome do to that. For those of you who wish to participate, I'd like to invite you to stand in a circle. Now, try to pretend that your feet are glued to the ground. Get them glued down so you can’t lift them up. And now, slowly, try to pull them out of the glue. If you feel comfortable, let’s now walk around in a circle slowly...slowly, like there’s gum on the bottom of your shoes (you can invite them to hold hands while they walk in a circle, if you see fit). And now the gum is wearing off and we can walk more easily. And now you're free to walk around outside of the circle, inside of the circle, you can walk wherever you want to go. And let’s see how your feet look when you are walking happily and freely. Can anybody skip? Does anyone like to run? Wonderful! And now try to see how they look when you are starting to get tired. Let go slower and slower, and come back towards the circle. If you can, try to go around in the circle again, slower and slower, getting tired. And when your feet are really sleepy you might wish to sit down and rest. Or you may like to lay down, that's perfectly okay too. Now I'd like to invite you to take a moment to relax and rest your feet however way you like."
creation:
Rethink, Rebuild, Rebirth

For those who wish to participate in the footprint creation, you can guide them through the following steps. Depending on the age group, you may see the need to assist them in tracing their feet.

Depending on your time constraints, you may wish to give the children an opportunity to create two feet, one to show where they’ve been and one to show where they’re going to. This is perfectly okay.

Step 1: Tracing
To start, you may trace the outline of each child's foot onto a poster board and invite them to cut it out. If you have younger children, you may wish to cut out the footprint for them.

Step 2: Creation
Once the footprints have been cut out, you can now invite the children to use markers, stickers, and collage materials to illustrate their journey. You can encourage them to get as creative as possible and remind them that there is no wrong way to create. However way they choose to design their footprints will be perfect.

Step 3: Words
As the children finish their footprints you can encourage them to think of words that go with their footprint. It could be any word that symbolizes where they've been and where they wish to go in life. If possible, you can work with each child one-on-one as they are done. They have the option to write the words they come up with on the back along with today's date. It can be meaningful as time goes by and the journey continues on. 

Step 4: (optional) Lamination
If possible, you may laminate the footprints. They look great and last longer. After laminating, small pieces of magnetic tape (adhesive backed) can be added to the back of the collages so they can be hung on a metal surface. Again, this is purely optional if time, space and resources allow.
closing: For the closing, you may give the children an opportunity to share their footprints, share some words about where they're from, where they wish to go and what each element of their footprint design represents. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.
description: Allows children to validate and express feelings about their unique journey, what they are learning and where they want to go in their lives, by creating drawings or collages using outlines of their own feet.
notes:
Background:
This workshop was adapted from a Women’s Windows Workshop written by Lucy Tschachtli. Lucy is a Women’s Windows facilitator at Haven House in Buffalo, New York. A special “thanks” to Silvia Gutierrez for helping to adapt this project for children. The footprint collages throughout this update were created during Lucy’s workshops.
tips:
Note about Introducing Embodied Art:

You may wish to consider sharing with the youth the benefits of moving their bodies in playful and safe ways. By sharing this information with them, you can empower them to feel a sense of ownership over their bodies and their expression. For more about embodied art workshops and how to introduce them in your groups, see Introduction to Embodied Art Workshops.
optional_materials:
•  
      Printable self-led worksheet
       

    Laminator

  • Laminating sheets

  • Relaxing music

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable self-led worksheet. If you are utilizing this sheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out beforehand for your participants depending on the setting.

Optional materials for self-led worksheet:

  • Self-led worksheet

  • Pencils

  • Pens

  • Colored pencils

  • Markers

  • Erasers
introduction:
“Our workshop today is called My Footprints. Our whole life is a journey and it is often our feet that carry us along. And sometimes it’s the feet of people we love when they are carrying us."

“Today you'll have the opportunity to create an amazing picture in the shape of your own feet. For those of you who wish to participate, I'd like to encourage you to think about your feet .... where have they carried you? What images, words, colors come to mind? Where would you like your feet to carry you in the future? Every journey goes through hard times and good times. Along the way, it can help to notice where you’ve been and where you want to go next."

“You'll have a chance to trace your own foot and cut it out, then draw on it, collage on it, and decorate it however way you like, using any and of the material available, that represents your journey. You can put anything on it. I'd like to encourage you to try to include something about where you have been, and something about where you hope to go next. It could be anything. It could be words, images, symbols, anything you like."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."

title: Flowers With Vase
objective: This workshop provides an opportunity to show children that they can create beautiful things by expressing themselves through the creation of flowers and a vase.
materials:
• Coffee filters - 3 per participants

  • Markers

  • Watercolors

  • Pipe cleaners

  • Bottles (e.g., plastic water bottles, soda bottles)

  • Tissue paper cut into squares of varying sizes

  • Glue

  • Water

  • Medium Bowl

  • Paint brushes
setup:
We encourage you to have all the materials and supplies set up or close to the participants for easy accessibility. If possible, we suggest that a sample is created, in order for the participants to see what the creation can look like at the end. However, it's important to create a simple sample, so that participants are not overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

For this workshop, we will need to prepare a glue-water mixture, which we suggest doing in advance. Pour glue into a medium bowl then slowly add water and stir until the glue is like heavy cream. 1/2 glue and 1/2 water is a good ratio for this mixture. 

For the warm up, we will be doing some body movement, therefore, it's important to have space for participants to feel comfortable moving around and stretching.
warm_up:
Body Movement

"Before we jump into our creation, I'll invite you to use your body for this next activity, which is called "Flower Warm-up". I invite you all to stand in a circle and stretch your arms. Make sure you have enough room for yourself and others. Great! To do our Flower Warm-up, let’s take a minute to think together. How do flowers start out? What are they before they bloom? What are they before they even have stems or leaves? That’s right! They start out as seeds! So that’s how we’re going to start out: as seeds. Can you make yourself into a seed? Would you be a small round seed, like a poppy seed? Would you be big like a sunflower seed? Would you be a long stretched out seed, like a green bean? As you rest on the ground being a seed, I’m going to walk around the room and sprinkle some magic water on you so you can begin to grow."

Walk around the circle rubbing your hands together over each special seed to make the magic water sound.

"As I sprinkle the magic water on you, you may begin to grow. Can you make a stem? Can you make a leaf? How tall can you grow? And is your flower ready to open? Let's see all of the flowers opening! Beautiful!”

 

Open discussion

"Before we begin, I would like for us to think about this question “If you were a flower today, what would you look like and why? This can include the color that you would be, big or small, short or tall. Would your flower be happy? Shy? Angry? Wise? For those who would like to share, we will go in a circle and share what flower you would like to be."
creation: As the group creates, feel free to offer assistance if needed. Providing time reminders may also be helpful to participants, in order to avoid participants feeling rushed or overwhelmed towards the end of the workshop.
closing: As the workshop comes to a close, offer the opportunity to have a "heart talk" in which participants have the opportunity to demonstrate or share their creation, or any thoughts/feelings they experienced during the workshop. If time is running out, you may choose to do an "art exhibit" in which participants hold up their creations so everyone can see. Thank everyone for joining and being a part of this safe/brave space with you and each other.
description: A great way to show kids that using ordinary kitchen items can create beautiful things.
notes: It is important to note that many feelings and emotions can come out when the child shares about their flower, therefore, it is important to validate each child's experience. Also, the colors that participants use to create their flowers and vase can mean different things for different individuals. For example, the color black could mean strength, anger, danger, and much more.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Flowers With Vase Worksheet

 
Flowers With Vase Worksheet
introduction: "For our workshop today, we each get to make flowers and a vase. However, before we begin I want you to know that this is a Window of Time for you. During this time, I encourage you to honor any thoughts, feelings, and needs you may have. I will be sharing some instructions regarding today's workshop; however, you have the power and freedom to create however you like. There is no wrong or right way to create. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please ask for what you need."
demonstration:
Step 1: Decorate three filters
   
 
  Step 2: Stack on top of each other
   
 
  Step 3: Dig finger in center to
close and tie on pipe cleaner
   
 
  Step 4: Spread filters to open flower

Flower Making Process

1. First, each participant will receive three coffee filters. Each participant can color in each filter with watercolors and/or markers. Participants may also use as little or as many colors as they like, they may write words, symbols, and shapes.

2. Next, when all three filters are done and dried, put all three filters together, one on top of the other in any order. Then dig your finger in the middle of the filter to create a closed-like flower. Keep the flower closed by pinching the bottom of the filters and twisting a small piece of all three filters.

3. Next, grab your pipe cleaner and tie a small part of the pipe cleaner onto the small twisted piece of the filter. You can just wrap the pipe cleaner around.

4. Spread out the filters to create a bloomed flower.

 

Vase Making Process

5. Cut out tissue paper into small square pieces, all of different sizes and colors. 

6. Grab an empty bottle (e.g., water bottle, soda can) and using a paint brush, paint the bottle with the water-glue mixture created earlier.

7. Place the tissue squares onto the bottle and add another coat of the glue-water mixture

8. Let dry and place your flowers in the vase.

title: Stories of the Heart
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to listen to their hearts and tell their heart stories through the process of journaling, meditation and creation of a watercolor art piece.
materials:
• Watercolor paper (up to 3 pieces per participant)

  • Masking tape

  • Watercolor sets

  • Brushes

  • Cups of water (1 per participant; to rinse the brush)

  • Paper towels

  • "What Is Your Heart Story?"  journaling template

  • Pens
setup:
Sample table setup

You can print a copy of the "What Is Your Heart Story" journaling template for each participant.

You can lay out the supplies for each participant to have easy access to them.

If you see fit, you can cut the watercolor papers down to smaller squares for each participant in advance. You can provide any size paper that you like, and you can give participants the option to create however many Heart Stories that you see fit. In the past, we've given participants an opportunity to create three.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get a feel for the watercolor techniques, as well as to show participants what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges. You may also want to leave the tape on the sample and show how a border can be created by removing it during the demonstration (see Demonstration).

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested meditation, or your own. We have found that guided meditations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.
 

"Before we start, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief meditation. This is an opportunity to look inward, to connect with our hearts, and ourselves exactly where we are. If you prefer to just observe, that’s perfectly okay. Observing is participating.”

“For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get yourself in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. If you like, you can place both hands over your heart. However way you are most comfortable.”

"Now take a moment to relax and release some of the tension your body carries. Take a deep breath in, and as you let it go, picture letting go of any more tension in your body... and take another nice deep breath in... and let it go. As you breathe deeply, bring your attention to your hands resting on your heart."

"Notice that this is a special time to care for your heart. All the good things, all the challenging things, all that your heart carries inside. If you remain still, can you hear any special message your heart has?... As you listen to your heart you might hear difficult things, and you might also hear wonderful things."

"Begin to breathe in love and compassion for yourself... if expectations or doubts come up, listen to the strength in the beats of your heart and breathe. You might hear strength, hope, courage, or pain... you may hear words, songs or see shapes and colors in your minds eye. Trust your heart and take a moment to listen... Is it something personal? Is it a change you want to make in the world?"

"No story is too big or too small. You are welcome to sit in this moment for as long as you like, and whenever you are ready, you can open your eyes and begin to create what your heart tells you."
creation:
Participant journaling

Each participant is invited to create their shapes in water on the pages and then begin to add color as they wish. You may want to remind them that there's no right or wrong way to create or participate. They are free to create whatever they like.

If participants finish early, you can invite them to start the journaling process.

When participants are finished, you suggest for them to leave the papers taped down until the closing. This will give the water washes a chance to dry.


Journaling:
After participants have created their heart stories, you can give them 5 minutes or so to journal or reflect on what they've created. You can offer the following prompt, "What is the story you see in front of you?" Or, they are free to write whatever feels right or good to them in this moment.
closing:
You can give everyone an opportunity to share with the group about their heart story, any discoveries they made, anything they felt or experienced through the process, or anything else they may wish to share.

You also have the option to invite participants to choose a partner, or pair them up, and give each person 2 minutes or so to share about their heart story, the process, or anything else that is coming up for them.


"Thank you for taking this time to connect and listen to your hearts, to honor yourselves and your stories exactly where you are. You are worth it. Each of your hearts are beautiful and unique in their own way, and each heart has an important story that deserves to be heard."

After the circle, participants can go ahead and carefully take the tape off their art. If the paint is still wet, they may want to wait longer.
description: This workshop offers participants an opportunity to listen to their hearts, and express their heart story. Using a simple watercolor technique, along with meditation and journaling, participants will connect and honor themselves exactly where they are.
optional_materials: • Relaxing, instrumental music
introduction:
Heart Stories creation in progress


 

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

"Today, I invite you to share your Heart Story. Each of us has a story to tell. Sometimes we think 'our' story is the narrative of what is happening all around us, or to us. But actually, our heart stories are something different. Our heart stories are created in our hearts; they are the feelings, experiences, hopes and colors that live inside of each of us. If we listen, we can notice the learning, the wisdom and value that guides and shapes our lives and who we are, and inspires our life stories. Today, you'll have a chance to listen to our hearts and tell their stories."

"Our stories can be expressed in many different ways, though voice, movement and many art forms.Today, you'll get to use watercolors. I'll guide you through a process that lets your story emerge by listening to your heart and expressing it through colors, shapes and flowing imagination."
demonstration:
Fig. 1: Taping the edges
 
 
  Fig. 2: Defining your shape with water
 
 
  Fig. 3: Dropping color into the water
 
 
  Fig. 4: Filling the shape with color
 
 
  Fig. 5: Leaving an edge of dry paper between the shape and the background
 
 
  Fig. 6: Bridging the dry edge where they desire

You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation process with the participants. You may want to demonstrate the steps for them.


"I'll show you a simple watercolor 'wash' technique. Or feel free to play and explore if that is what feels right to you. Remember this is your window of time, to honor your thoughts, feelings, visions and needs. What you choose to do is completely up to you. If you want to just sit quietly with your hand on your heart, that's okay. There is no right or wrong way to create or participate."

"The way the watercolors move and blend can express so much. You can choose a simple shape to tell your story. It can be as simple as a circle or line or triangle. You don't have to think of the shape right now. We'll be doing a relaxation, and you can just let it come to you."

"You can use one, two, three, or more pages to tell your story. The page(s) can represent whatever you want them to represent. They can represent how you feel on the inside, and how the world feels around you. They can represent your transformation and healing. They can represent your past, your present and your future. Or moving from 'I can't,' to 'I can'.”


Step 1:
You can demonstrate to the participants how to tape down the paper if you haven't taped it prior to the workshop (Fig.1) and let them know the reasons for taping the paper down is so when the tape is removed, after the watercolor is dry, there will be a frame around the art like a window, and also the tape helps to contain the water so it stays on the page.


Step 2:
You can paint a shape with pure water on the paper (Fig. 2). You may want to use plenty of water so that the shape remains wet like a lake on the page.


Step 3:
You can then begin to drop color into the shapes (Fig. 3). Notice how the beauty of watercolor comes from what the color does by itself as it is carried through the water. When the paint is dropped into it, the magic begins effortlessly.


Step 4:
You can show what it's like to drop the color near the edge and what it's like as the color spreads and runs into other colors (Fig. 4).


Step 5:
You can show what it's like to paint the area outside the shape with color, leaving a space of dry paper between the shape and the background (Fig. 5).


Step 6:
You can show what it's like if you join the two wet spaces (Fig. 6).

You can invite participants to volunteer and share a word about how their heart is feeling today (Ex: light, heavy, foggy, clear, full, strong, happy, weak, sad, etc).

title: Stories of the Heart for Teens
objective: This workshop gives teens an opportunity to listen to their hearts and tell their heart stories through the process of journaling, meditation and creation of a watercolor art piece.
materials:
• Watercolor paper (up to 3 pieces per participant)

  • Masking tape

  • Watercolor sets

  • Brushes

  • Cups of water (1 per participant; to rinse the brush)

  • Paper towels

  • "What Is Your Heart Story?" journaling template

  • Pens
setup:
Sample table setup

You can print a copy of the "What Is Your Heart Story" journaling template for each participant.

You can lay out the supplies for each participant to have easy access to them.

If you see fit, you can cut the watercolor papers down to smaller squares for each participant in advance. You can provide any size paper that you like, and you can give teens the option to create however many Heart Stories that you see fit. In the past, we've given participants an opportunity to create three.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get a feel for the watercolor techniques, as well as to show participants what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges. You may also want to leave the tape on the sample and show how a border can be created by removing it during the demonstration (see Demonstration).

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested meditation, or your own. We have found that guided meditations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.
 

"Before we start, I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief meditation. This is an opportunity to look inward, to connect with our hearts, and ourselves exactly where we are. If you prefer to just observe, that’s perfectly okay. Observing is participating.”

“For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get yourself in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. If you like, you can place both hands over your heart. However way you are most comfortable.”

"Now take a moment to relax and release some of the tension your body carries. Take a deep breath in, and as you let it go, picture letting go of any more tension in your body... and take another nice deep breath in... and let it go. As you breathe deeply, bring your attention to your hands resting on your heart."

"Notice that this is a special time to care for your heart. All the good things, all the challenging things, all that your heart carries inside. If you remain still, can you hear any special message your heart has?... As you listen to your heart you might hear difficult things, and you might also hear wonderful things."

"Begin to breathe in love and compassion for yourself... if expectations or doubts come up, listen to the strength in the beats of your heart and breathe. You might hear strength, hope, courage, or pain... you may hear words, songs or see shapes and colors in your minds eye. Trust your heart and take a moment to listen... Is it something personal? Is it a change you want to make in the world?"

"No story is too big or too small. You are welcome to sit in this moment for as long as you like, and whenever you are ready, you can open your eyes and begin to create what your heart tells you."
creation:
Participant journaling
 
  Stories Of the Heart creation

Each teen is invited to create their shapes in water on the pages and then begin to add color as they wish. You may want to remind them that there's no right or wrong way to create or participate. They are free to create whatever they like.

If the teens finish early, you can invite them to start the journaling process.

When they are finished, you can suggest for them to leave the papers taped down until the closing. This will give the water washes a chance to dry.


Journaling:
After participants have created their heart stories, you can give them 5 minutes or so to journal or reflect on what they've created. You can offer the following prompt, "What is the story you see in front of you?" Or, they are free to write whatever feels right or good to them in this moment.
closing:
You can give everyone an opportunity to share with the group about their heart story, any discoveries they made, anything they felt or experienced through the process, or anything else they may wish to share.

You also have the option to invite the teen to choose a partner, or pair them up, and give each person 2 minutes or so to share about their heart story, the process, or anything else that is coming up for them.


"Thank you for taking this time to connect and listen to your hearts, to honor yourselves and your stories exactly where you are. You are worth it. Each of your hearts are beautiful and unique in their own way, and each heart has an important story that deserves to be heard."

After the circle, participants can go ahead and carefully take the tape off their art. If the paint is still wet, they may want to wait longer.
description: This workshop offers teens an opportunity to listen to their hearts, and express their heart story. Using a simple watercolor technique, along with meditation and journaling, participants will connect and honor themselves exactly where they are.

introduction:
Heart Stories creation in progress


 

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

"Today, I invite you to share your Heart Story. Each of us has a story to tell. Sometimes we think 'our' story is the narrative of what is happening all around us, or to us. But actually, our heart stories are something different. Our heart stories are created in our hearts; they are the feelings, experiences, hopes and colors that live inside of each of us. If we listen, we can notice the learning, the wisdom and value that guides and shapes our lives and who we are, and inspires our life stories. Today, you'll have a chance to listen to our hearts and tell their stories."

"Our stories can be expressed in many different ways, though voice, movement and many art forms.Today, you'll get to use watercolors. I'll guide you through a process that lets your story emerge by listening to your heart and expressing it through colors, shapes and flowing imagination."

title: Expressing Feelings with Watercolor / Expresando Sentimientos conen  Acuarela (Pinturas de aguawatercolor)
author_location: Antelope Valley Domestic Violence Council, Lancaster, California
objective: This workshop gives children the opportunity to express their feelings without criticism or judgment, and experience the magic and beauty of seeing something invisible become visible.
materials:
• Supplies: paper, white crayons, and watercolors

    White construction paper or watercolor paper

  • Watercolor sets w/ brushes

  • Cups of water (2 per participant - 1 for wetting brush, 1 for cleaning brush)

  • Paper towels

  • White crayons (or oil pastels)

  • Children’s music

  • Feelings chart (click to download)
setup:
You may wish to create a sample to show the children. If you choose to do so, we recommend a simple sample using only the material you'll be providing, so children won't feel overwhelmed with any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any element or portion of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
"Happy" feeling creation using watercolor
on top of white crayon writing.

 		  

You can now invite the children to write, draw, or color how they feel. One suggestion is to use white crayons for this step, but you may wish to remind the children that their creation is their own. It doesn't matter what it looks like, and there's no right or wrong way to do this.

If they're using the white crayons, you can let them know that it works best if they press hard to make their crayon lines. The harder they press, the more the crayon will show up when painted over with watercolor, the softer, the less it will show. Because both the paper and crayon are white, it is sometimes hard to see exactly where you left off. You can let the children know that that’s part of the creation and it’s okay.

If they are unable to write, they might dictate the words and have you write for them. Or, they can draw or use symbols, or one of the Feelings Emojis as inspiration. However they do this, will be just perfect.

Once the children are done with the crayon writing, you can invite them to paint over the crayon with the watercolors.

If they wish to see more of the colors mixing together, you can spray the paper lightly with a spray bottle (set on light mist). When the color appears, a white outline will appear where the crayon is. The writing or drawing will stand out.

You can let the children know even if their creation is not exactly what they expected, it’s perfectly okay. What matters is that they have taken time to acknowledge, honor and express their feelings.
closing:
"Sad" feelings painting    

For the closing, you may give the children an opportunity to share their creations and anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

You may wish to remind everyone about respecting all the art and all the different feelings.
description: Allows the children time to express their feelings without criticism. Gives the opportunity to experience the magic and beauty of seeing something invisible become visible.

Ahora puede invitar a los niños a escribir, dibujar o colorear sus sentimientos.  Una sugerencia es que usen el crayón blanco para este paso, pero usted puede desear recordarle  a los niños que esta creación es de ellos.  No importa cómo se vea, y no hay forma manera correcta o errónea incorrecta de hacer esta actividad.

Si ellos usan el crayón blanco, puede decirles que sirve mejor cuando lo presionan fuerte para hacer líneas. Lo más fuerte que sea presionado, hará que el crayón se note más cuando pinten sobre él.   Por qué el papel y el crayón son blancos, puede ser más difícil de ver donde terminaste.  Puede hacerle saber a los niños que esa es la parte de la creación y que está bien.

Expressing Feeling sample: Mad

You can open by inviting the children to introduce themselves and share how they feel at this time, if any feel comfortable doing so. If they don't feel comfortable sharing, they can simply take a moment to notice how they are feeling. There is no wrong feeling, whatever they're feeling is okay.

Puede abrir el taller invitando a los niños a que se introduzcan y compartir como se sienten en este tiempo, s.  Si alguno se siente cómodo para hacerlo.  Si no se sienten cómodos compartiendo, pueden simplemente tomar un momento para notar como se sienten.  No hay sentimientos erróneos, como se sientan estará bien.

title: You're a Shining Star
objective:
This workshop aims to help build participants self-esteem and confidence by creating a shining star.

 
Shining Stars
materials:
Materials:

  • Star Templates
  • Polaroid camera (if not available, see optional materials)
  • Markers
  • Colored Pencils
  • Glue
  • Glitter
  • Writing utensils
  • Scissors

Small Stars   Big Star w/ Picture goes here   Big Star
setup:
Table Setup

It may be helpful to have your materials and supplies set up prior to starting the workshop. A sample may also be created to help participants see the final project and for the demonstration portion. Remember to create a simple sample in order to avoid participants feeling overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges. You can also provide pre-cut stars for participants who are too young or don't have the ability to use scissors.

If you would like to recycle the glitter being used, you may want to put one piece of construction paper/newspaper paper at each workstation. This allows for easy funneling of the glitter back into the containers.
warm_up:
Body Movement

"I invite everyone to stand up for a quick stretch if you'd like. If standing does not work for you, I invite you to participate in your chair or wherever you feel comfortable. First, I want you to look up and reach high, high at the sky!" (Mime reaching for the sky)

"Now look down low, low to the ground and stretch you arms down." (Mime reaching down to the ground)

"Then look up and reach high, high at the sky again. See the stars all around? Reach for the stars! Grab them, touch them, reach for them.”

“Do you have them? Bring them down. Put them in your palm. Pack them tight. Did any get away?” (Mime packing them into the palms of your hands.)

“Okay now everyone put them into your pocket or away for safekeeping until later.”
creation:
During this time you may offer assistance to the participants if needed. Time reminders may also be helpful to participants, in order to avoid participants feeling rushed or overwhelmed towards the end of the workshop.

 

 
Star side w/ picture    Star Side- w/ words, drawings, etc.
closing: As the workshop comes to a close, offer the opportunity to have a "heart talk" in which participants have the chance to demonstrate or share their creation, or any thoughts/feelings they experienced during the workshop. Participants may also share their favorite thing they wrote about themselves or that someone wrote about them. If time is running out, you may choose to do an "art exhibit" in which participants hold up their stars high in the sky so everyone can see. Thank everyone for joining and being a part of this safe/brave space with you and each other.
description: Aids in building self-esteem/self-concept and confidence. After all, who wouldn't want their face on a star?
notes:
We invite you to create a mobile prior to the participants arriving. This can be created using three wired hangers tied together with pipe cleaners. The participants have the opportunity to choose if they would like to leave their stars to hang on the mobile of if they would like to take it with them.

 
Completed Shining Star   Three hangers tied together with pipe cleaners to hang stars from.
optional_materials:
Camera Options:

  • Polaroid Camera: Polaroid cameras are best because they are instant. In the cases of new participants, this can be especially useful.

  • Digital Camera: Pictures can be downloaded into the computer and printed out on paper.

  • Camera & Scanner: Pictures can be taken and then scanned into computers & printed out on card stock/paper.

  • No Camera Available: Have the participant draw a picture of themselves.

Note: Due to confidentiality, it is important that photos are not duplicated or used without the permission of the participant and their parents and/or caregivers. If photos are uploaded onto computers, phones etc. it's important that it gets deleted immediately after the workshop.
introduction: "Welcome everyone. Before we begin today's workshop I would like to take a moment to let you know that this is a window of time for you. In this moment, I encourage you to focus on your thoughts, feelings, and needs. You have all the power and control to decide how you will participate today. I will be providing some instructions regarding the workshop; however, you are welcome and encouraged to create however you like."
demonstration:
1. Each participant should have two stars that they can cut out from the Star Templates. If possible the stars should be printed out on card stock paper or construction paper. Participants may also choose to create their own stars and cut those out.

  2. Once participants have cut out their stars, they may start decorating them. One side of the star will have their photo and the other can be positive words, symbols, drawings that they have about themselves.

  3. During the creation process, if you have a Polaroid camera this would be the time to take each participant one by one to take their photo and give it to them. If photos will not be taken, allow some time for the young participants to draw themselves on one side of the star.

  4. You may then glue the photo taken on the side that does not have words, symbols, etc.

  5. Grab about 8 inches of yarn and tie a knot at the ends to make a circle.

  6. After the two stars have been decorated, glue the backs of the two stars together (the side that is not decorated) and make it one star; however, add the yarn in the middle so it can hang.

Optional:

  1. For step 2, you may also have the participants write their names on their stars and have everyone pass their stars around the table. Once a star gets to you, look at who it belongs to. Write something you like or admire about that person onto the star with a writing utensil and continue until your star gets back around to you.

Note: If the group is really small, you yourself may want to write something positive about the participant on their stars! You may want to do this in a large group too.

I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation steps with the children. Feel free to demonstrate any creation elements that you deem necessary. For example, you can show them how to apply glue to the construction paper (Step 2), or how to glue yarn on the cardstock (Step 3), or any decorative elements in Step 4.

 

     
  Step 2

 
 
  Step 3

 
 
  Step 4: variety of garden creation techniques
 
   

Step 1: (If not done in advance)
To start, children can cut a piece of construction paper, any color, down to a strip (about 2" wide) to represent the soil/earth, etc.


Step 2:
Next, children can glue the strip onto their cardstock, gluing only the sides and bottom so as to create a pocket.


Step 3:
Children can then glue yarn for stems. They can tuck the bottom of the stems into the envelop. They can add as many stems as they like. Each stem/flower can represent one important person or thing in the child's life.


Step 4:
Next, children can draw flowers for each stem. They can draw any type of flower and as many as they like. They can decorate the cardstock however they like. They can draw a sun, or use tissue paper cut-out and yarn and glue it to the cardstock to represent the sun. They can draw clouds, or anything else they like to include in their garden drawing.

They can also use construction paper and/or tissue paper to create flowers instead of draw them. Or use a combination of both mediums.

Here are some flower creation techniques you can share with the children. Feel free to demonstrate as needed:

  • They can draw daisies (open flowers).

  • They can draw rose buds or other closed, fragile flowers.

  • They can make cones out of tissue or construction paper and glue them to the stems to represent closed flowers.

  • They can cut daisy petals out of tissue paper.

  • They can use a hole punch (if available) and make dots out of different color construction paper and glue them onto the flowers.


Feel free to suggest and demonstrate any other flower creation techniques that you like.
opening_circle:
You can facilitate a discussion around what different types of flowers could possibly mean or represent and invite children to share their thoughts, ideas and suggestions. You can invite them to share what the different flower colors mean to them, who they wish to represent in their garden, etc.

Of course, flowers, colors, symbols can have different meaning to different people, so it's important to honor and validate every idea that's shared.

title: Releasing the Feelings Bubble Paints
objective:
Bubble paintings mounted with bubble-shaped cut-outs
make a beautiful display.		  

The goal of this workshop is to give participants the opportunity to express the more difficult things they are feeling and experiencing in order to help them discover a non-critical way to release any sense of negativity they carry and break through to joy and laughter.
materials:
• Bubble solution and wands

  • Plastic cups

  • Colored tempera paints

  • Paper towels

  • White construction paper
setup:
If possible, prior to doing this workshop, remind parents and participants that paint may splatter when the bubbles pop; therefore, invite participants to wear an outfit they do not mind getting paint on.

It may also be helpful to have the materials and supplies set up prior to the participants arriving. You may have the table covered with paper towels to protect it from the splattering paint. We also recommend having the bubble-paint mixture created beforehand. Have several plastic cups with a mixture of the bubble-paint solution and a bubble wand; different colors in each cup. There should be two parts bubble solution and one part paint per cup.
warm_up:
"If you wish, I invite you all to join me in a relaxation exercise. If you would like to join, we will begin by getting comfortable in our chairs. If you like, you may close your eyes and let your body relax into the chair. I would like us to take a deep breath together, in through your nose and out through your mouth. Now imagine a beam of light shining down from above. Imagine that light shimmering and falling to your feet. The light is warming. It starts to slowly make its way up your entire body, slowly warming you up and relaxing your muscles, first from your toes all the way up to the top of your head. Breathe into any area of your body that feels tense, releasing the tension into the air. Now imagine a bubble floating down. What color is it? Is it big? Small?"

 

"Now imagine stuffing that bubble with any concerns, problems, feelings of sadness, anger, and pain and blow it away into the air, letting it go. Imagine your bubble floating away with all those feelings. As you watch your bubble float away, you begin to feel lighter and your body lifts into the air. Imagine yourself releasing other bubbles with concerns in them and as each bubble is released, your bodies feel lighter, more peaceful and free, and your body lifts up higher and higher, surrounded by hundreds of beautiful bubbles."

 

"Now imagine yourself slowly floating down. When you feel comfortable and ready, you may open your eyes and begin creating."
creation:
Releasing the Feelings Bubble Painting artwork.

During this time, allow the participants time to explore the materials and supplies and allow for support when needed. If you choose to, you may also play calming music while the participants create. Time reminders may also be a great way to inform the participants of when the creation time may be over in order to decrease feelings of being rushed.
closing: As the workshop comes to a close, offer the opportunity to have a "heart talk" in which participants have the opportunity to demonstrate or share their creation, or any thoughts/feelings they experienced during the workshop. If time is running out, you may choose to do an "art exhibit" in which participants hold up their creations so everyone can see. Thank everyone for joining and being a part of this safe/brave space with you and each other.
description: Gives children an opportunity to express the more difficult things they are feeling and experiencing. Helps them discover a non-critical way to release negativity and break through to joy and laughter.
notes:
Introducing Embodied Art

Consider sharing with the young participants the benefits of moving their bodies in playful and safe ways. By sharing this information with them, you empower them to feel a sense of ownership over their bodies and their expression. For more about embodied art workshops and how to introduce them in your groups, see Introduction to Embodied Art Workshops.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Releasing the Feelings Bubble Paints
introduction: "For today's workshop we will be creating art using bubbles. However, before we get started I wanted to highlight that this space together is a window of time for you. In this time together, I encourage you to honor and focus on your thoughts, feelings, and needs. I will be giving you instructions on how to create your artwork; however, know that this is just a suggestion and I encourage you to follow whatever creation process you have. There is no wrong or right way to create. If you start to feel stuck or are unsure of what to do; no worries, take as much time as you need and if you just want to blow bubbles that is completely okay. Participation can look different for everyone. Any questions before we get started?"
demonstration:
1. Each participant should have white paper in front of them, with different colored bubble solution-paint mixtures.

2. Using the wands, participants can dip their wands into the solution and blow bubbles towards the paper, allowing them to pop. It's easier when participants move their heads around the paper to cover the area, as opposed to them moving the paper. Participants may also stand and blow their bubbles downward towards the paper, if they like.

3. Allow the paper to dry.

 

Optional: 

4. Feel free to be creative—cut the white paper out into different sized circular shapes and mount them onto a black background to make the paintings stand out even more!

 

 
1. Bubble colors mixed with paint.   2. Blowing bubbles.
opening_circle:
"Have you ever felt angry or sad? What does it feel like?  Where do you feel it? What are some things that make you angry or sad? What are some things that you do when you are feeling sad or angry? Do you maybe use your words? Maybe you use your body to release your emotions?"

Allow the participants some time to answer each question if they choose.

"There are many healthy and unhealthy ways to release our anger, sadness, and pain. Therefore, today we will be creating art using bubbles as a way to release your feelings of anger and pain in a healthy way and to begin the healing process."
extra_field:
Carolyn Isbrandt, Buffalo, New York.

About this Workshop:
I want to begin by stating that this has been one of my favorite projects. The kids and I all enjoyed this activity from beginning to end, and I hope that you will too! A lot of the children that come into shelter have grown up in an environment that focuses on negativity—negative behavior, negative words and negative treatment between people who should care for one another. This project was designed to help children heal and overcome that negativity that they have been exposed to. In my experience, it does not help a child to make them feel as if they are wrong for feeling anger or resentment. This project helps them to accept their feelings and release them. It’s meant to validate the child’s feelings and help begin a process by which they can express the more difficult things they are feeling and experiencing in a positive manner and begin the healing process. Starting with the meditation, the children are instructed to think of their problems and release them into the air, causing them to feel lighter. When the children and I worked together on this project, they were encouraged to make the project their own, using colors that made them feel good and covering the paper to their own liking

title: My Music Box
objective:
Completed Music Box

This workshop aims to help participants explore their emotions through sound and music, and to find a safe outlet for their expression through rhythm and movement.
materials:
• Shoe box (1-per participant)
  • Glue (Stick and Liquid)
  • Colored construction paper
  • Magazines
  • Large Rubber bands
  • Craft Sticks
  • Scissors
  • Markers
  • Colored Pencils
  • Oil Pastels
  • Music
setup:
We encourage you to have all the materials and supplies set up or close to the participants for easy accessibility. If possible, we suggest that a sample is created, in order for the participants to see what the creation can look like at the end. However, it's important to create a simple sample, so that participants are not overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

For the warm-up, there will also be a music component added, in which you may choose three types of music, or you may choose to just use your voice.
warm_up:
“I invite you all to join me in a sound and feelings warm-up, if you like. If you would like to participate, we will start by standing in a circle and taking a nice deep breath and then letting it out."

"We are going to explore sounds and feelings. Different feelings can sound different ways. Can you make a sad sound? (Make sad sounds together.) And now can you make an angry sound? (Make angry sounds together.) And now can you make a happy sound? (Make happy sounds together.) Wonderful! You guys are making wonderful sounds!"

“Now let’s try putting the sounds together with movements. Let’s try sad again. Can you make your sad sound again? And this time let’s all move around the room in a sad way. And can you make sad faces too? Good! What about an angry face? Let’s hear those angry sounds and make angry movements and faces! Wonderful! And now how about happy faces? Let’s hear the happy sounds and make happy movements around the room! Look at all those happy faces! Beautiful!”

 

Optional:

You could also try playing three different songs (fast, slow and in-between) and ask the participants how they would move to these sounds. “What parts of your body can you move?” Invite participants to join in and share, if they like.

 

Note: It’s important to remember that each participant may interpret each song differently and display something very different and unique from one another. Remind them that there is no right or wrong way. The important part is to allow the participant to feel safe within the immediate environment and free to express themselves.
creation:
As the group creates, feel free to offer assistance if needed. Providing time reminders may also be helpful to participants, in order to avoid participants feeling rushed or overwhelmed towards the end of the workshop.

You are also welcome to play some relaxing music while participants create.
closing:
As the workshop comes to a close, offer the opportunity to have a "heart talk" in which participants have the opportunity to demonstrate or share their creation, or any thoughts/feelings they experienced during the workshop. You may also ask the participants if they would like to share their sounds or their music boxes together.

If time is running out, you may choose to do a concert in which participants may play their instruments together. Thank everyone for joining and being a part of this safe/brave space with you and each other.
description: In this workshop children create their own guitar-like instruments, explore their emotions through sound and music, and find a safe outlet of expression through their own rhythm and movement.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

introduction:
Many different Music Boxes made during  
  one Haven House workshop.

For today's workshop we will be creating a guitar that will allow us to explore our feelings through sound and music. However, before we begin I want you to know that this is a window of time for you. During this time, I encourage you to honor any thoughts, feelings, and needs you may have. I will be sharing some instructions regarding today's workshop; however, you have the power and freedom to create however you like. There is no wrong or right way to create. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please ask for what you need."
demonstration:
1. Begin by inviting the participants to trace a circle on the top of their shoe box lid and on a piece of construction paper. Participants may then cut both circles out. It may be helpful to the participants to trace a circle with a cup or any circular object.

2. Next participants may choose a color of construction paper, to cover the outside of their box. Use a glue stick to apply the paper to the shoe box lid. Remember not to cover the circle made in the show box.

3. Repeat the covering process with the bottom of the shoe box. Once participants have covered the entire box they may put the pieces together, closing the box.

4. Participants may then begin to decorate the box using the materials in front of them. They can also collage or use oil pastels.

5. When participants are finished decorating their Music Box you may pass out the craft sticks and rubber bands. You may need to assist the participants with the rubber bands, they may need to be stretched before they are placed around the box. Once the bands are in place, slide the craft sticks underneath the bands and stand them on their sides so the grooves are holding the rubber bands apart (the sticks may need to be adjusted for sound).

extra_field:
About this Workshop:

At Haven House, the children really seem to respond to the music boxes. Each child was eager for us all to hear their own music boxes. They took turns and shared as a group. The sounds were amazing and so beautiful. They all worked so hard, each box displayed a very different and unique look and sound. When we returned the children to their cottages they couldn’t wait to show their moms their works of art. Music is a part of us all in some way or another and their response to this activity, was evidence of that. I enjoyed sharing this activity with the children at Haven House very much. It brought much laughter into a room that is sometimes very quiet, especially when there's a lot of pain.

title: Persona Dolls
author_location: Women's and Children's Crisis Shelter, California
objective:
Persona Dolls: Batman and Farmer Girl

Participants will have the opportunity to explore and gain a sense of identity in themselves by creating a character or a person doll.
materials:
• Persona Dolls Pattern (Various brown hues of construction paper)

  • Colorful Felt or fabric

  • Colorful Yarn

  • Googly eyes, Buttons, sequins (for facial features)

  • Scissors

  • Markers

  • Glue

  • Craft sticks

  • Tape

  • Paper

  • Writing utensils

  • Paint
setup: Before the workshop, you may need to cut out dolls of various brown hues on construction paper if young participants are unable to use scissors or for safety concerns. Setting up the materials can also help participants gain accessibility to all the supplies during the workshop. We also recommend making a sample of a completed doll before leading the group so you understand the steps in creating. Having a simple sample also gives the participants a visual to work with as they begin and can spark their imagination.
warm_up:
For today's warm-up, I invite you to journal or think about your persona dolls. I encourage those who would like to participate to write and/or think about who they are planning to create? How does your persona doll look? What color is their hair? What color is their eyes? Do they have a happy expression? Sad expression? Have you seen them on T.V. or in real life? What traits do you like about this person? What is their personality like? What strengths does this person have? How does this person treat others? What is this person's occupation? What does this person mean to you?"

"Once you are done thinking and/or writing about your persona dolls you may go ahead and create them".
creation: During this time you may offer assistance to the participants if needed. Give time reminders along the way. If possible, you can reassure participants that they can finish their dolls later or even take extra materials home to work on there.
closing: As the workshop comes to a close, invite participants to introduce their dolls to the group and explain why they created it. Participants may also share any thoughts/feelings they experienced during the workshop. If time is running out, you may choose to do an "art exhibit" in which participants hold up their dolls high in the sky so everyone can see. Thank everyone for joining and being a part of this safe space with you and each other.
description: Provides an arena where children have the opportunity to make a character or a 'persona' of any kind. Children make up a new character of their choice, superhero, cartoon character, family member, or even themselves!
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Persona Dolls Worksheet

  • Persona Dolls Pattern

 

 
Persona Dolls Worksheet   Persona Dolls Pattern
introduction:
Completed Persona Dolls

"Before we begin today's workshop, I want to take a moment to express that this is a window of time for you. During this time I encourage you to take note of your feelings, thoughts, and needs. You have the power and choice to decide how you will participate today. I will give some basic instructions regarding the workshop creation; however, these are just suggestions and I invite you to be as creative as you like. There is no wrong or right way to create art. Any questions before we begin?"
demonstration:
1. Invite each participant to choose a persona doll pattern and have them cut it out. Have some pre-cut persona dolls if young participants cannot use scissors or may potentially get hurt if using scissors. 

  2. Next, participants can dress the persona doll using all the different kinds of material. The participants can trace the doll onto the fabric and draw what type of clothing they would like their persona dolls to have.

  3. Participants may then make the doll’s face using markers. Small objects can also be used for personal attire such as buttons or designs.

  4. Yarn may then be used for the doll's hair. You can make spiky hair by cutting the yarn pieces about 1/2 an inch and lining them up, placing them on top of the head like a fence. Pigtails or braids can be made: just make sure you have fairly long pieces. Tie up the middle with a separate yarn piece and then braid each side, closing it with another yarn piece.

  5. Last, participants can glue craft sticks on the back of the doll so they can hold them up like a puppet. You will need two craft sticks for each doll. Be sure to overlap the two sticks about 1/4 together, and tape together to give it some sturdiness.

 

 
Yarn can be braided and tied at both ends to make this hairdo. Bangs are added.  
Yarn can be cut short and lined up to make this spiky hairdo.

when held by the stick.
opening_circle: "Today you are invited to make a persona doll. These dolls can be inspired by a favorite character, someone special in your life, or even you! You will have the power to choose and create this doll however you like. There is no wrong or right way to create this doll. As long as you are creating the doll the way you like, that is all that matters."

title: Show Me your Tail Feathers
objective: This workshop gives children a chance to explore things about themselves that they are proud of and express them in a fun and festive way. This workshop offers both individual and group creation options.
materials:
• Construction paper (variety of colors)

  • Markers

  • Bulletin Board

  • Scissors

  • Turkey template

  • Feathers template
setup:
You have two options for the creation process. You can invite each participant to create a turkey and feather individually, or you can print one turkey for the group and invite each child to create the feathers and collectively glue the feathers onto the turkey (see creation).


For individual creation:
You may wish to print one turkey template on construction paper for each participant in advance. You can print as many feathers as you like. For younger children, you may want to cut the templates out in advance so children won't have to handle scissors.

For younger children you can use the Turkey and Feathers template so children won't have to handle scissors.


For group creation:
You can print one turkey (without feathers) on construction paper for the whole group, and 2 feathers for each child. Again, you can precut the templates if you see fit.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You can start with a warm-up that is a variation of the Wiggle Down. It’s called the “I Feel Good!” Wiggle Down. You are welcome to use our suggested warm-up or your own.

“Before we help make the turkey feel proud, I'd like to invite you all to take a moment to feel good about ourselves, all the way from head to toe. Feel free to follow along, or if you prefer to observe, that's perfectly okay too. Observing is participating."

"For those who want to follow along, I invite you to join me in a circle. Make sure you have an arm’s length distance around you. Good! Now let’s start with our toes. Can you notice how they feel today? Let’s get our toes feeling good. Can you give them an 'I feel good!' wiggle? Wonderful! And how about our legs? Can we wiggle our legs too? And how about all of our bottoms? Let’s give them an 'I feel good!' wiggle. What about our shoulders? Let's give our shoulder a good wiggle. Good! And now the whole length of our arms. Good! And now our heads? Let's wiggle that too. And how does your body move when you feel really good? Can you do an 'I feel good!' dance? (jumping, wiggling, etc.) Wonderful. And now let’s take all our wiggles and wiggle them down, down, down (begin to crouch down so your hands are touching the floor)."

"Let all our extra wiggles go down into the floor, and let's all take a nice deep breath... And you can sit down on the floor (if possible) in our circle and take another deep breath. Wonderful! Now as you sit there (or remain standing), I encourage you to think of some things you feel proud of yourself. Do you feel proud of how you are a good friend? Or how you draw well? Or how you run fast? Anything that you are proud of will be perfect. When you are ready, go to the art table and make two feathers representing what you are proud of about yourself.”

Note, that for group activity, it might be helpful to invite each child to create a limited number of feathers, as there is limited space on the turkey for every feather created. For individual activity, you can invite the children to create as many feathers as they like, since they each will have their own turkey they can add feathers to. Feel free to adapt the warm-up verbiage according to which option you choose.
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to do so, to begin creating. 

For group creation, you can invite each child to write their name on one side of each feather, if they wish to do so, and on the other side, they can write one thing they are proud of themselves. Once each child has created their feathers, you can invite them to attach them to the turkey during the closing.

For individual creation, children are free to write on thing they are proud of on as many feathers as they wish, and glue each onto their turkey.
closing: For group creation, you can invite each child to bring their feathers and glue it to the group turkey. Feel free to offer assistance where you see the need. For individual creation, you can give children the chance to share their feathers and what they are proud of themselves, if any wish to do so. Of course, this is optional, so if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
description: Two workshops that provide a wonderful way to take the themes of the Fall season and use them to explore emotions; what we are proud of as well as letting go of bad feelings.
notes: This workshop has a complimentary workshop called "Let the Bad Feelings Fall Away," which is part of our fall workshop series.
tips:
Note about introducing embodied art:
You may wish to share with the youth the benefits of moving their bodies in playful and safe ways. By sharing this information with them, you can empower them to feel a sense of ownership over their bodies and their expression. For more information about embodied art workshops and how to introduce them in your groups, please see Introduction to Embodied Art Workshops.
optional_materials: • Turkey and feather template (for a simplified individual workshop that doesn't require cutting)
introduction:
As an introduction, you can ask the children what is wrong with the turkey. The answer is that it doesn't have any feathers. You can adapt the introduction according to whether you wish to do individual, or group creation process.

Example of “Show Me Your Tail Feathers”"Great. Today, we will have an opportunity to make feathers for the turkey. The feathers are special because on each feather, you'll get to write things about yourself that you are proud of. This way, we can make the turkey feel proud of itself with the feathers you will give it."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

title: Inner Gifts
objective:
Inner Gifts creation.

To give participants a chance to explore their inner gift and understand their value.
materials:
Inner Gift Template

  • Inner Gift Template (printed on colored construction paper)

  • Markers

  • Scissors 

  • Glue

  • Glitter

  • Feathers
setup: If possible, create a simple sample in advance in order for participants to see how the creation can look like and get ideas for their own. We also invite you to set up the supplies prior to the participants arriving.
warm_up:
"For today's warmup, I invite you to join me in a short meditation. You may sit or stand, whichever feels most comfortable to you. I invite you to begin by placing your hand on your heart and if you feel comfortable, you may close your eyes. You may then take a nice deep breath in and then out. 

"Now I want you to know that each one of you has a very, very, special present inside of you. I can see it on the inside of each one of you! I can see your heart —and that’s where the most special gifts of all lives. Your heart is where I can see your kindness. If I look really, really close, I see your laughter and smiles! All these things live inside your special heart. With your hand resting on your heart, think about what is in your heart. Do you see the kindness? Do you see caring? Do you see smiles?"

"Now picture something that makes you feel happy inside your heart, or something you are thankful for. It could be the face of someone you love or whatever you love to think of. Notice what makes your heart feel happy. Now, imagine it filling up your heart. Feel that happiness filling your heart so full it’s overflowing. And now picture it filling your whole body – all your joy and happiness. And now picture it filling up the whole room! All your happiness, filling the room so full it’s going to burst! It’s shining out of your heart like sunshine, filling the whole room! And now picture it shining out from the room to the whole world. Shining all the way from inside your heart out to the whole world around you."

“I invite you to take one more deep breath, in through your nose and out through your mouth. When you feel ready, you may open your eyes and begin creating."
creation: During this time, you may play some calming music, and offer assistance when needed and/or asked. Time reminders during the creation process may also help participants keep track of their progress.
closing: As the workshop comes to an end, provide an opportunity for the participants to share what they learned, experienced, or felt during the workshop. You may also invite participants to share their inner gift that makes them feel special. Thank the group for coming and being in community with everyone.
description: Gives the children a chance to explore the gifts they have on the inside, and notice that they are their best gifts--better than anything money can buy.
optional_materials: If printing is unavailable, invite the participants to hand-draw a gingerbread outline on various colors of construction paper.

During this time we invite you to listen to your thoughts, feelings, and needs. I will be providing us with instructions regarding the creation process, however, you are welcome to create however you like. There is no wrong or right way to create."

  3. Participants may then decorate their person and include what makes them special inside using colors, words, symbols and much more.
