title: I am Strong Because...
objective: This workshop aims to help children and teens build a sense of pride in their strength to overcome difficulties, and create an art piece that can serve as a pride badge as well as a reminder to never give up.
materials:
• Construction paper

  • Markers

  • Rulers

  • Butcher paper (or large paper)

  • Poems handout
setup:
You are welcome to provide any and as many decorative material that you see fit.

If you'd like to do a group project, you can provide a large piece of butcher or craft paper and tape it on a board or a wall. The size would depend on the number of children in your group. You can write "We Are Strong Because..." somewhere on the top of the paper.

For older teens, you can print copies of the Poems handout. For younger age groups, you can just print one copy and read it to them. You are also welcome to use your own choice of poem that may be more relevant to your group.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show the children what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
 

     
Sample I Am Strong Because... creations
creation:
You can invite those who wish to create their puzzle art piece to use any of the art supplies available and decorate their puzzles however they wish. Each individual puzzle piece can represent one reason they feel they are strong (or one thing they feel they're good at). They can write words, draw symbols, shapes and/or use colors. The puzzle can be in any shape (a heart, a square, etc.). They can have as many pieces as they wish. There is no right or wrong way to create, but you may want to encourage them to think of all the ways they have shown resiliency (or demonstrated accomplishment in something) in the past and are strong.

Ex: One puzzle piece can say: "I am willing to learn." Another piece can say: "Smart." They can color and/or decorate each piece however they choose.

Children can use rulers in case they want to draw straight edges. If you like, you can invite them to write "I Am Strong Because..." at the top of their sheet.

If you see fit, you can provide writing paper and give children the option to write down/brainstorm their thoughts and ideas before creating their puzzles.


Group Project:
If you're choosing to do a group project, you can invite children at any point to come up to the large poster board (butcher paper) and write one or more reasons why they are strong.
 

     
I Am Strong Because... puzzle creation   Heart-shaped puzzle
closing:
You can give children a chance to volunteer and share their art creation, one or more of the reasons they are strong, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.


Group Project:
For the group project, you can point out similar points made by what was shared and add those commonalities to the "We Are Strong Because..." board.

If possible, you also have the option to format the common elements they share as to why they feel they are strong into a poem. Here's an example from a past workshop:


We are Strong Because - The Poetry Club

"We are patient (sometimes).
We all have experienced good times and bad times.
We are strong because we come from strong cultures.
We help each other even when we don’t all get along.
We’ve had similar experiences.
We’ve had similar pasts.
We come together to help each other through hard times.
If we weren’t, we wouldn’t be here today.
We are all loved and we need each other."


Feel free to close out the workshop however way that best works for your and your group.
description: Offers the chance to build a sense of pride in oneself as well as a sense of cohesion within the group about the obstacles and hard times that they have been through. The finished artwork serves as a pride badge and reminder to not give up.
tips:
For younger children, it may be more helpful to focus the workshop on things they're good at (art, studying, doing chores, listening to parents, being a good friend, being on time to class, etc.).

The theme behind this workshop also works well with journaling and poetry projects.
optional_materials:
• Crayons

  • Colored pencils

  • Glue

  • Scissors

  • Writing paper

  • Your choice of embellishments
introduction:
I Am Strong Because... puzzle creation

"Today, you'll have a chance to create a puzzle made up of individual pieces that represent a reason why you are strong. You'll get a chance to use any of the art supplies and design and decorate it any way you like."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
opening_circle:
6-piece I Am Strong Because... puzzle creation

For the opening circle, you can read one or more of the poems from the handout to the children and then invite them to a discussion. You can prompt a discussion by asking what they feel that the overall message of the poem is.

Based on the discussion that's been generated, you can then make a transition statement such as: "We all have been through good times and bad times and everything we've experienced has made us who we are today... strong. If we were not strong, we wouldn't make a commitment to be here today."

Feel free to cater the discussion however way it best suits your group.

title: Children United Throughout The World
objective:
Completed Mural at Women Shelter of Long Beach (WSLB).  

This workshop aims to provide space for participants to share their feelings about being in a family with domestic violence and to bring awareness that they are not alone.
materials:
• World Template

  • Person Outline Template

  • Colorful Construction paper

  • Colorful Yarn

  • Oil Pastels

  • Markers

  • Glue

  • Scissors

 

   
World Template     Person Outline Template
setup: If possible, having the materials and supplies set up prior to the participants arriving can be beneficial for group accessibility. If younger participants will be joining the group, it may be helpful to have the templates pre-cut.
warm_up:
Discussion:

"Before we get started on our creation, I want to invite you to a conversation regarding domestic violence. Do you know what domestic violence is? What about abuse?"

Allow some time for the participants to answer, if they like. After, inform the participants about what domestic violence and abuse is.

"Do you know that domestic violence can happen to anyone around the world? Do you know any countries around the world? How do you think other children may feel in homes with domestic violence?

Validate the responses the participants provide and thank them for joining you in this important conversation. 

 

Grounding Technique:

"I know discussing domestic violence can be hard sometimes, so I would like to invite you to join me in a grounding exercise, called the Five Senses Grounding Technique. This technique can be used when we are feeling anxious, overwhelmed, or even scared. First, I invite you to look around the room and name five things you see. Perfect! Next, I invite you to list four things you can touch. (e.g., table, art materials) Great. Now what are three things you can hear? Two things you can smell. Lastly, what is one thing you can taste? Fabulous! Thank you for joining me in that grounding technique and remember you can use this whenever you like."

Note: For each question allow some time for participants to answer.
creation:
Paper Dolls made at WSLB
   

During this time, you may play music if you like and offer assistance if needed. Time reminders may also be helpful in order to help participants track their progress.
closing:
Before ending the workshop, invite participants to share any experiences, feelings, or thoughts they had throughout the workshop. Participants are also welcome to pair share, in which they can discuss a time they felt united with others regarding a certain situation.

If time is running out, invite participants to have a sitting exhibit, in which they all hold up their artwork and show their creation to the group. Thank the group for joining you in this safe/brave space.
description: Offers a chance to educate, discuss and have children share their feelings about being in a family with domestic violence. While doing the workshop, children learn that children all over the world have experienced domestic violence issues.
notes: We did this project during a whole week, taking about an hour each day to work on it. Once it was up, we decided to leave it up (it’s been 6 months now) and make it an on-going project adding new dolls when new children come to the shelter. They really like it, and when they leave the shelter, we give them their doll to take with them. This makes space for new dolls to be welcomed as new families come to the shelter.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

title: New Year's Garden
objective:
Completed New Year's Garden

The goal of this workshop is to reflect on and explore your thoughts about your past, present, and future by creating a New Year's Garden.
materials:
• Card-stock Paper

  • Construction Paper

  • Tissue Paper

  • Oil Pastels

  • Glue

  • Scissors

  • Colorful Yarn

  • Paper

  • Writing Utensils
setup:
Setup of materials and supplies  

We encourage that materials and supplies be set up for better access before participants arrive. If possible, we also invite you to create your own New Year's Garden in order to illustrate to the participants how the final creation can look like.
warm_up:
"To get us started, I invite you to take a moment to think or write about what you want your garden to look like or represent. For instance...

  • Is each flower a separate time period in your life?

  • Do the flowers represent different people?

  • Does the way a flower looks symbolize something?

  • What does each color mean?

  • Does each flower represent yourself at different times—in the past, presently and in the future?

  • Are there flowers in the garden? If not, what is in the garden?”

"If you prefer to just think or draw, instead of writing please feel free to do so."
creation:
Flowers and Sun

During this time, you may play calming music if you like and offer assistance if needed. Time reminders may also be helpful in order to pace participants throughout their creation process.
closing: Before closing the workshop, invite participants to share one word that best represents each flower. If time is running out, you may also have a "sitting exhibit" in which participants have the opportunity to hold up their creation to show others, while also seeing the artwork of others. Thank the participants for being in community with you and each other.
description: Offers participants the opportunity to think about and explore their past, present, and future by creating a New Year's Garden.
optional_materials:
New Year's Garden Worksheet

opening_circle:
New Year's Garden daisy

"Today you will have the opportunity to reflect on your past, present, and future by creating a garden. Your garden can represent many things, for example, growth from past experiences or opportunities to plant seeds for growth in the future. Your New Year's Garden can include many things, such as your family, events, memories, and much more. Your garden will be unique to you, and there is no right or wrong way to create it."
extra_field:
Suzy Karcher Rogers

About This Workshop:

While making this I found myself dividing my life into time periods—each flower in my garden represented me at a different time of my life. I thought about what were really good times for me and what I was like during those times. I made flowers for my difficult periods also and I found myself looking for what I had learned during these times and how I had been strengthened during these periods. As I represented my future, I was pleased that I had ended up making the flower very similar to my present flower.  It wasn’t some distant dream, which made me realize I was heading in the right direction.  

I hope the individuals who participate in this workshop are able to gain some valuable perspective about the different periods of their lives. Sometimes the future seems a bit intimidating. This workshop is helpful in lightening up our thoughts about the future.

title: Dream Pillows
objective:
Completed Dream Pillows

The objective of this workshop is to honor our wishes and dreams through the creation of a special pillow.
materials:
• Colorful fabric

  • Stuffing Material

  • Ribbons

  • Fabric Glue

  • Colorful paper

  • Writing utensils
setup: If possible, we encourage you to have the supplies and materials set up prior to the participants arriving in order to increase accessibility. We also invite you to create your own dream pillows, in order for participants to see what the final product can look like.
warm_up:
Journaling Prompt:

"To get us started, I invite you to engage in a short journaling warm-up. If you would like to join, I encourage you to think about your dreams."

  • How often do you allow yourself time to dream?

  • How did your dreams come about?

  • Can you think of a special dream or wish you have for yourself?

  • If you could have one wish come true in your lifetime, what would it be?

"If you prefer to think or draw instead of writing, that is completely okay! You decide how you would like to participate today."

Guided Meditation:

“Before we begin our Dream Pillows, I invite you to take a moment to relax. If you feel comfortable, I welcome you to close your eyes and imagine a beautiful, warm, safe flame in the middle of the room. This fire represents the flame deep inside your hearts. No matter how difficult things get, that flame is still there, deep inside of you. It is the flame of your wishes… It is the light of your dreams. As you notice the warmth and beauty of the flame, you are welcome to take a deep breath in and let it out. If you prefer to roll your neck or stand, instead of doing deep breaths, you are encouraged to do so. Do whatever feels most comfortable for your mind and body. I invite you to take another wonderful, deep breath in… And let it go… As you watch the flame, and breathe deeply, notice this is your time, just for yourself. It is a time to honor your deepest dreams and wishes. You can take as long as you like just to relax and notice your thoughts. And whenever you’re ready, you can start to create your dream pillow.”
creation: During this time, you may play soft calming music and offer assistance if needed. Time reminders may also be helpful in order to help participants become aware of their creation process.
closing:
Completed Dream Pillow with a dream inside

Before closing the workshop, invite participants to share a dream they wish to accomplish and what significance does accomplishing this dream have? Last, thank the participants for being in community with you and everyone in the group.
description: Participants create a special pillow with a pocket that can hold messages - a place to honor their wishes and affirmations.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

There is no wrong or right way to be present or create, as long as you are doing what is best for you, that is all that matters.

1. Participants are invited to choose whatever fabric they like. These colors can reflect your dreams and wishes.

  2. Participants can then cut the fabric to whatever shape they would like their pillows. Note: Squares and rectangles are the easiest to make.

  5. Participants may then turn it right side out and stuff it completely with stuffing and glue the last edge together.

  6. Write your dreams and wishes to store inside the pocket.

opening_circle: "Today I will invite you to create a dream pillow. A dream pillow is a special pillow that has a place to hold messages, dreams, or wishes for yourself. Sometimes you might think your dreams are silly, but they are not. There are no right or wrong wishes or dreams. Whatever is most dear to your heart is very important. If your thoughts feel silly or impossible, they are especially important. Together today, let’s create a special space where it is safe for your dreams to come out, be supported, and find a home in our Dream Pillows.”
extra_field: I have had this idea for a long time. As part of my self-growth, I like to write about my dreams for the future or positive wishes for myself. I shared the idea of Dream Pillows at the Fall 2002 training and Cathy encouraged me to share it with you.

title: Money Jar
objective:
Money Jars and other variations  

This workshop aims to make finances a joyous and sacred process, by giving intention and importance to the practice of saving money and nurturing yourself.
materials:
• Jars

  • Puffy paint

  • Glitter
setup: Prior to participants arriving, we encourage you to set up the materials to increase accessibility. It may also be helpful for you to create a simple sample of the "Money Jar" in order for participants to visualize what the jar can look like.
warm_up:
Journaling

"For today's warmup, you are invited to journal about your money jar.

  • What will you be saving for?

  • How much would you want to put into it?

  • Are you saving for something big or small or maybe something long-term or short-term? For example a vacation, flowers for a garden, a spa day, going out with friends and much more.

"You are also encouraged to give your Money Jar a name that represents your intentions. For example, if you're saving for a down payment on a car, it could be your Car Jar. It may be important for your jar to know why you're saving it. Once you are done, you are invited to create their money jars, however you like."
creation: As participants are creating their Money Jar, you may play some calming music and offer assistance when needed. Time reminders may also be extremely helpful to participants, in order for them to pace themselves throughout the creation process.
closing:
As the workshop comes to a close, allow some time for participants to share what they will be saving up for. Participants are also welcome to share how they felt throughout the workshop.

You may also share that "the money jar is something to be honored and respected. It’s a jar where you consciously build toward your dreams. It’s a way of honoring yourself, celebrating yourself, and loving the life you’re living.”
description: Participants create a tracking system to help them observe where they spend their money each and every day--a way of becoming conscious of that which might be overlooked and causes the 'holes' in our 'money buckets'. End product are helpful and empowering reminders of what they have learned and hope to accomplish.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Money Jar Worksheet

 

 
Money Jar Worksheet
introduction: "Before we get started, I would like to take this moment, to highlight that this is a window of time for you. During this time, you are encouraged to focus on your thoughts, needs, and feelings. There is also no wrong or right way, to participate. I will be giving some basic instructions, however, you are welcome to create however you like. Is there any questions before we get started?"
demonstration: 1. Participants are invited to decorate their jars however they like, using the provided materials.
opening_circle:
Money Jar decorated with the words 'Family' and 'My Style'  

"In this workshop, you will be invited to think about treating yourself. The concept of paying yourself is normally foreign, especially when juggling other financial responsibilities. You may also often share with others—but do you share with yourself? If you were with your best friend and had three cookies, you'd probably offer one of them to your friend. In this workshop, you are invited to decide what percentage of your paycheck goes to you. It doesn’t matter what percentage you begin with, as long as you are able to treat yourself, as your own best friend."
extra_field: This is a four-session workshop that can be used as individual workshops or together.  Each session shares a different “tool” — a creative process leading us to awareness about our wealth through observing, respecting, honoring and tracking.  They say “the rich get richer” and that’s no accident.  There is a focus and attention involved.  These projects are about finding creative, simple ways to build that focus and attention.

title: Personal Needs Flower / Flor de Necesidades Personales
objective: This workshop aims to help participants focus on and honor their physical, emotional and spiritual needs, through the creation of a flower with each petal representing one of those needs.
materials:
• Colored journaling paper

  • Pens

  • Colored construction paper (cardstock)

  • CrayPas (crayons, or oil pastels)

  • Sharpies

  • Glue sticks
setup:
Sample table set up

You can lay out all the supplies where they are easily accessible.

You may wish to prepare a sample in advance so that your demonstration can go quickly and leave plenty of time for creating. If you wish to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
Journal page, showing flower construction
 
Journal page, showing flower construction
 
Journal page, showing flower construction
 

"You are welcome to follow along with this warm-up exercise, or if you prefer, you can just observe. Observing is participating."

"For those of you who wish to participate, first, I invite you to pick a color paper that speaks to you or makes you feel strong and hopeful."

"If you choose to, you can journal about three different types of needs that we all have: the needs of our body, our mind, and our spirit. You can fold that paper into thirds lengthwise (show example; see images for reference). On the top of the first column, I invite you to write the word 'Physical,' on the second, 'Emotional,' and on the third, 'Spiritual'."

"I'm going to talk a little bit about each of these three needs then give you a few minutes (you can time this, if you like) after each one to reflect on, and write about this need for yourself. There is no right or wrong way to do this journaling exercise. You can write sentences, words, lists, draw symbols, shapes, or anything else you like. I'd like to encourage you to just allow your thoughts to flow onto your paper without judgment. This is your space and your time."

"What you write does not have to make sense to anyone but you. It is also fine to just sit quietly and notice what comes up. Remember this is your window of time to connect with yourself and what's meaningful for you."

(You can play soft, background music if you choose to provide it at this time).

"Physical needs are what we usually think about first. What are your physical needs in order to feel safe, happy, and healthy?"

"For example, we need to be free from harm. We need shelter and a safe place to live. We need good nutrition: healthy food and clean water. We need exercise. Keeping our bodies healthy and strong. We need rest, giving us energy to do what we need to do, like succeeding at work or going to school."

"In the first column, I invite you now to write words, sentences, symbols or shapes to represent your physical needs."

(You can give participants are much time as you see fit to write; about 2-5 minutes usually suffices).

"Another need that may be a little harder to think about is our emotional needs. What are your emotional needs in order to feel safe, happy, and healthy?"

"For example, feeling understood, accepted, and heard. Knowing that we are loved and appreciated also gives us the feeling of having emotional support. Relaxation, fun, and friendship help us to find emotional balance. Having boundaries, realistic expectations, and a positive attitude are other ways of supporting our emotional health."

"Now in the second column, I invite you to begin journaling about your emotional needs."

(Pause to allow them to write).

"Finally, we will address our spiritual needs. What does your spirit need to give you peace?"

"For example, the ability to forgive, have patience or acceptance of others? Do you need quiet time to reflect, meditate, or pray? Do you need to do good deeds or help others feel uplifted? Do you need 'me' time to care for your soul?"

"In the third column, I invite you to journal about your spiritual needs."

(Pause to allow them to write).

"Thank you for taking the time to reflect on and honor your own personal needs. Remember that you are worth it and representing your needs shows that they are, too."
creation:
"Now I invite you to begin creating."

As the participants create their flowers, you can remind them that there is no right or wrong way. The only important thing to keep noticing and honoring their own needs. You can encourage them to keep asking the question, "What are my needs?"

You can also encourage each participant to decide how they want to finish their flower. Do they want to glue it together? Do they want to create any extra petals to carry with them to add more needs as they are discovered? Or do they wish to keep the pedals separate and keep them in an envelop (if provided).
 

Keep your petals in a pile to carry with you Or glue your flower together
closing:
Personal Needs Flower creation

For the closing, you can give participants who feel comfortable doing so an opportunity to share about their Personal Needs Flower, and any discoveries they made as they took time to notice their needs. Of course, this is optional, and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

You can remind participants: "This process does not end today. You can reflect back on it anytime, however it best serves you. Noticing what you need to feel safe, happy and healthy in your life is one of the most important jobs you will ever have, and one job that no one else can do for you."

You can encourage participants to continue the journaling exercise at home and to keep identifying more of their physical, emotional and spiritual needs.
description: This workshop provides an opportunity for participants to notice their personal needs by creating a flower where each petal represents one need. They will begin to see the many layers of needs—physical, emotional and spiritual—and to honor all these layers.
notes:
Note About Conflicting Needs:
Sometimes a person might notice that their different needs seem to be in conflict with each other. For example, the need to have more quiet alone time and the need to spend more playful, fun time with her children. This is okay.

The purpose of this workshop is to reveal the many needs that can be seen as part of our entire makeup. It is okay not to be problem-solving at this time, but rather supporting participants as they reveal and learn to accept themselves at this creative stage, seeing not only the needs that can be fulfilled, but also those that seem far from resolution.

By putting all the needs around a single circle, we allow our conscious mind to see how they all can coexist and intersect, and how we can begin to find safer and more creative ways to embrace and move through any conflicts.

"Le invitamos a seguir este ejercicio de calentamiento, o si lo prefiere, puede observar. Observar es participar". "Para aquellos de ustedes que desean participar, primero, los invito a elegir un papel de color que le habla o le hace sentir fuerte y con esperanza".

"Si lo desea, puede registrar tres tipos diferentes de necesidades que todos tenemos: las necesidades de nuestro cuerpo, nuestra mente y nuestro espíritu. Puede doblar ese papel en tercios a lo largo (muestre un ejemplo; vea las imágenes como referencia) En la parte superior de la primera columna, te invito a escribir la palabra "Físico", en la segunda, "Emocional" y en la tercera, "Espiritual".

"Voy a hablar un poco sobre cada una de estas tres necesidades y luego te daré unos minutos (puedes cronometrar esto, si quieres) después de cada una para reflexionar, y escribe sobre esta necesidad por ti mismo. No hay Una forma correcta o incorrecta de hacer este ejercicio diario. Puede escribir oraciones, palabras, listas, dibujar símbolos, formas o cualquier otra cosa que desee. Me gustaría animarle a que simplemente permita que sus pensamientos fluyan en su papel sin juzgarlo. Este es tu espacio y tu tiempo.”

"Lo que escribes no tiene que tener sentido para nadie más que para ti. También está bien simplemente sentarte en silencio y notar lo que ocurre. Recuerda que esta es tu ventana de tiempo para conectarte contigo mismo y lo que es significativo para ti". (Puede reproducir música de fondo suave si elige proporcionarla en este momento).

"Las necesidades físicas son lo que generalmente pensamos primero. ¿Cuáles son sus necesidades físicas para sentirse seguro, feliz y saludable?"

"Por ejemplo, debemos estar libres de daños. Necesitamos refugio y un lugar seguro para vivir. Necesitamos una buena nutrición: alimentos saludables y agua limpia. Necesitamos ejercicio. Mantener nuestros cuerpos sanos y fuertes. Necesitamos descansar, darnos energía para hacer lo que necesitamos hacer, como tener éxito en el trabajo o ir a la escuela ".

"En la primera columna, los invito a escribir palabras, oraciones, símbolos o formas para representar sus necesidades físicas". (Puede darles a los participantes mucho tiempo como le parezca adecuado para escribir; por lo general, son suficientes entre 2 y 5 minutos). "Otra necesidad que puede ser un poco más difícil de pensar son nuestras necesidades emocionales. ¿Cuáles son sus necesidades emocionales para sentirse seguros, felices y saludables?"

"Por ejemplo, sentirse comprendido, aceptado y escuchado. Saber que somos amados y apreciados también nos da la sensación de tener apoyo emocional. La relajación, la diversión y la amistad nos ayudan a encontrar el equilibrio emocional. Tener límites, expectativas realistas y actitud positiva son otras formas de apoyar nuestra salud emocional ".

"Ahora, en la segunda columna, los invito a comenzar a escribir un diario sobre sus necesidades emocionales". (Pausa para permitir que escriban).

"Finalmente, abordaremos nuestras necesidades espirituales. ¿Qué necesita tu espíritu para darte paz?"

"Por ejemplo, ¿la capacidad de perdonar, tener paciencia o la aceptación de los demás? ¿Necesita un momento de tranquilidad para reflexionar, meditar u orar? ¿Necesita hacer buenas acciones o ayudar a otros a sentirse motivados? ¿Necesita que 'yo' tenga tiempo para cuidar tu alma? "

"En la tercera columna, te invito a un diario sobre tus necesidades espirituales". (Pausa para permitir que escriban). "Gracias por tomarse el tiempo para reflexionar y honrar sus necesidades personales. Recuerde que vale la pena y que representa sus necesidades demuestra que también lo son".
creation_spanish:
"Ahora te invito a que comiences a crear".

A medida que los participantes crean sus flores, puede recordarles que no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta. Lo único importante para seguir notando y honrando sus propias necesidades.

Puede alentarlos a que sigan haciendo la pregunta: "¿Cuáles son mis necesidades?"

También puede animar a cada participante a decidir cómo quieren terminar su flor. ¿Quieren pegarlos juntos? ¿Quieren crear pétalos adicionales para llevar con ellos y agregar más necesidades a medida que se descubren? ¿O desean mantener los pedales separados y guardarlos en un sobre (si se proporciona)?
closing_spanish:
Para el cierre, puede darles a los participantes que se sientan cómodos al hacerlo la oportunidad de compartir acerca de su Flor de Necesidades Personales, y cualquier descubrimiento que hayan hecho al tomarse el tiempo para notar sus necesidades. Por supuesto, esto es opcional, y si nadie se siente cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.

Puede recordar a los participantes: "Este proceso no termina hoy. Puede reflexionar sobre él en cualquier momento, sin embargo, le es más útil.

Notar lo que necesita para sentirse seguro, feliz y saludable en su vida es uno de los trabajos más importantes que tendrá. alguna vez, y un trabajo que nadie más puede hacer por ti ".

Puede alentar a los participantes a que continúen con el ejercicio de registro en el hogar en casa y que sigan identificando más sus necesidades físicas, emocionales y espirituales.
notes_spanish:
Nota sobre necesidades conflictivas:

A veces, una persona puede notar que sus diferentes necesidades parecen estar en conflicto entre sí. Por ejemplo, la necesidad de tener más tiempo a solas y la necesidad de pasar más tiempo lúdico y divertido con sus hijos. Esto está bien. El propósito de este taller es revelar las muchas necesidades que se pueden ver como parte de todo nuestro maquillaje.

Está bien no resolver problemas en este momento, sino apoyar a los participantes a medida que se revelan y aprenden a aceptarse a sí mismos en esta etapa creativa, viendo no solo las necesidades que se pueden satisfacer, sino también aquellas que parecen estar lejos de resolverse.

Al poner todas las necesidades en torno a un solo círculo, permitimos que nuestra mente consciente vea cómo todos pueden coexistir e intersectarse, y cómo podemos comenzar a encontrar formas más seguras y creativas de aceptar y avanzar a través de cualquier conflicto.

introduction:
"Many of us are willing to give ourselves to our families, our friends, our coworkers, etc. We're often willing to sacrifice so much for others, that we forget to acknowledge and honor our own needs. Sometimes we don't even take time to breathe. It can be such a blind spot for us and we are often not even aware of it."

"This workshop is called Personal Needs Flower. Today, you will have an opportunity to take a window of time to notice and honor your physical, emotional, and spiritual needs; what you want more of in your life, or what might be out of balance and needs your attention. Tending to your needs is a vital part of self-care and one of the most important jobs you have. It is not only important, it is necessary for each of you to respect and honor your needs so you can recharge your batteries and be there in greater ways for yourself and others. You will then get a chance to create a flower, where each petal represents one of those needs."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
introduction_spanish:
"Muchos de nosotros estamos dispuestos a entregarnos a nuestras familias, nuestros amigos, nuestros compañeros de trabajo, etc. A menudo estamos dispuestos a sacrificar tanto por los demás, que nos olvidamos de reconocer y honrar nuestras propias necesidades. A veces ni siquiera nos tomamos el tiempo para respirar. Puede ser un punto tan ciego para nosotros y a menudo ni siquiera somos conscientes de ello".

"Este taller se llama Flor de Necesidades Personales. Hoy tendrá la oportunidad de tomar un tiempo para observar y honrar sus necesidades físicas, emocionales y espirituales; lo que desee más en su vida o lo que podría estar fuera de su vida. Equilibrio y necesita tu atención. Muchas veces ni siquiera somos conscientes de ello ". Atender sus necesidades es una parte vital del cuidado personal y uno de los trabajos más importantes que tiene. No solo es importante, es necesario que cada uno de ustedes respete y honre sus necesidades para que pueda recargar sus baterías y estar allí de una manera mayor para usted y para los demás. Luego tendrás la oportunidad de crear una flor, donde cada pétalo representa una de esas necesidades ".

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepas que este taller es una ventana de tiempo para ti. Esto significa que este puede ser un espacio seguro para notar tus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es tu ventana de tiempo, todo lo que digas o hagas es voluntario. Ofreceré una idea sugerida para el taller, compartiré los materiales que tenemos disponibles e invitarte a crear, pero no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de hacerlo. No importa lo que parece. Lo que importa es tomarse este tiempo para honrar verdaderamente sus pensamientos y sentimientos, sin embargo, surgen. Si no puedes pensar en nada o dejar en blanco qué crear o escribir, siéntete libre de solo observar. Sin embargo usted elige pasar este tiempo estará perfectamente bien. Este es tu tiempo. Solicite lo que necesita y sepa que estoy aquí para ayudarlo."
demonstration:
Step 1: Tearing the center circle
 
Adding a face to represent the peaceful, nurturing part of you
 
Step 2: Drawing/writing on the petals
 

If you've made a sample, you may wish to pass it around at this time.

“First, I'll invite you to start with a journaling exercise to help you notice your needs. I’ll demonstrate the materials and creation process now, so that at the end of the journaling process, if you choose to, you can dive right into creating."

"As I demonstrate the steps, remember that more than anything else, this is your special time to listen to and trust your own needs. There is no right or wrong to what you create. Just listen to the voice inside of you as you go. Whatever emerges in your creative process is fine. You are the expert of your own experience."

"I am going to be demonstrating a flower, but your creation can be anything you like. It does not even have to look like a flower. For example, you could create a deck of cards, where each card represents a specific need."


Step 1: Creating the Center
"The first step is creating the center of your flower."

"With the colored paper, you can tear a circle as small or as large as you like. You can create this center to represent you. You might want to draw a face that represents the peaceful, nurturing, supportive part of yourself that is here to help you. Whatever you choose, is up to you. I'd like to encourage you to feel free to 'tear' the paper. This is an opportunity to let go and enjoy the freedom that tearing allows. Allowing ourselves to be curious and playful can help us discover needs we might not even be aware of."


Step 2: Creating the Petals
"The next step is creating the petals, each one representing one of your needs."

"To make each petal, you can choose any color paper and tear it into whatever shape or size you want. You may want to vary the size of the petals to illustrate the importance of each need. For example, one of your greatest needs might be 'peace,' so you can choose to tear a large piece to represent that, and a smaller need of yours might be 'entertainment' so you can use a smaller petal for that. These are only suggestions. You are free to design it however way it has meaning to you."

"Then, if you like, you can draw symbols or use words to represent each need. Feel free to use your imagination to create colorful representations of all that you discover. You can place each petal, adding layer upon layer to the flower-like shape.


Step 3: Completing Your Flower
"The final step is deciding how you want to finish your flower. Using a glue stick, you can attach your petals together or glue them onto a larger piece of construction paper, or collect them into a pile that can travel with you. If you are going to keep your petals loose, you might want to decorate an envelope to keep them in (if envelop is provided)."

"You can finish your flower whichever way will best support you in being reminded of the needs you noticed today, but also in the ongoing process of discovering more of your needs. You could even make some extra petals without anything on them yet so you can add more needs as you discover them."

"Puedes terminar tu flor de cualquier manera que te ayude mejor a que te recuerden las necesidades que has notado hoy, pero también en el proceso continuo de descubrir más de tus necesidades. Incluso puedes hacer algunos pétalos adicionales sin nada sobre ellos para que puedas Añade más necesidades a medida que las descubras ".

title: I Am Strong Because... / Yo soy Fuerte porque…
objective: This workshop aims to help participants build a sense of pride in their strength to overcome difficulties, and create an art piece that can serve as a pride badge as well as a reminder to never give up.
materials:
• Construction paper

  • Markers

  • Rulers

  • Butcher paper (or large paper)

  • Poems handout
setup:
You are welcome to provide any and as many decorative material that you see fit.

If you'd like to do a group project, you can provide a large piece of butcher or craft paper and tape it on a board or a wall. The size would depend on the number of participants in your group. You can write "We Are Strong Because..." somewhere on the top of the paper.

You can print copies of the Poems handout for your participants, if it suits your group. You are also welcome to use your own choice of poem that may be more relevant to your group.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
 

     
Sample I Am Strong Because... creations
creation:
You can invite those who wish to create their puzzle art piece to use any of the art supplies available and decorate their puzzles however they wish. Each individual puzzle piece can represent one reason they feel they are strong. They can write words, draw symbols, shapes and/or use colors. The puzzle can be in any shape (a heart, a square, etc.). They can have as many pieces as they wish. There is no right or wrong way to create, but you may want to encourage them to think of all the ways they have shown resiliency in the past and are strong.

Ex: One puzzle piece can say: "I am willing to learn." Another piece can say: "Smart." They can color and/or decorate each piece however they choose.

Participants can use rulers in case they want to draw straight edges. If you like, you can invite them to write "I Am Strong Because..." at the top of their sheet.

If you see fit, you can provide writing paper and give participants the option to write down/brainstorm their thoughts and ideas before creating their puzzles.


Group Project:
If you're choosing to do a group project, you can invite participants at any point to come up to the large poster board (butcher paper) and write one or more reasons why they are strong.
 

     
I Am Strong Because... puzzle creation   Heart-shaped puzzle
closing:
You can give participants a chance to volunteer and share their art creation, one or more of the reasons they are strong, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.


Group Project:
For the group project, you can point out similar points made by what was shared and add those commonalities to the "We Are Strong Because..." board.

If possible, you also have the option to format the common elements they share as to why they feel they are strong into a poem. Here's an example from a past workshop:


We are Strong Because - The Poetry Club

"We are patient (sometimes).
We all have experienced good times and bad times.
We are strong because we come from strong cultures.
We help each other even when we don’t all get along.
We’ve had similar experiences.
We’ve had similar pasts.
We come together to help each other through hard times.
If we weren’t, we wouldn’t be here today.
We are all loved and we need each other."


Feel free to close out the workshop however way that best works for your and your group.
description: Offers the chance to build a sense of pride in oneself as well as a sense of cohesion within the group about the obstacles and hard times that they have been through. The finished artwork serves as a pride badge and reminder to not give up.
objective_spanish: Este taller tiene como objetivo ayudar a las y los participantes a construir un sentido de orgullo sobre su fortaleza para superar las dificultades, y crear una pieza de arte que pueda servir como una insignia, así como un recordatorio para nunca rendirse.
materials_spanish:
• Papel de construcción
  • Marcadores Regla
  • Papel de carnicero (o papel grande)
  • Folleto de poemas
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 5 min
Apertura: 15 min
Creación: 40 min
Cierre: 10 min
Total: 1:15 hora
setup_spanish:
Le invitamos que proporcione cualquier material decorativo que considere oportuno. Si desea hacer un proyecto grupal, puede proporcionar un trozo grande de papel de carnicero y pegarlo en una mesa o en una pared. El tamaño dependerá de la cantidad de participantes en su grupo.

Puedes escribir "Somos fuertes porque ..." en algún lugar en la parte superior del papel. Puede imprimir copias del folleto de Poemas para sus participantes, si se adapta a su grupo. También le invitamos a utilizar su propia elección de poemas que puedan ser más relevantes para su grupo.

Puede ser útil crear una muestra por adelantado para enseñar a las y los participantes cómo puede verse la pieza de arte terminada. Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos que cree un ejemplo de demostración muy básica para que las y los participantes no se sientan abrumadas o abrumados por ningún desafío "artístico".

Tiene total libertad para alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento de este taller para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo específico.
creation_spanish:
Puede invitar a las personas del grupo que deseen crear su pieza de arte de rompecabezas a utilizar cualquiera de los materiales de arte disponibles y decorar sus rompecabezas como lo deseen. Cada pieza individual del rompecabezas puede representar una razón por la que sienten que son fuertes.

Pueden escribir palabras, dibujar símbolos, formas y/o usar colores. El rompecabezas puede ser de cualquier forma (un corazón, un cuadrado, etc.). Pueden tener tantas piezas como deseen. No hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de crear, pero es posible que desee animarles a pensar en todas las formas en que han demostrado resistencia en el pasado y en todas las formas en las que son fuertes. Ej.: Una pieza del rompecabezas puede decir: "Tengo la disposición de aprender".

Otra pieza puede decir: "Inteligente". Pueden colorear y/o decorar cada pieza como elijan. Las y los participantes pueden usar reglas en caso de que quieran dibujar bordes rectos. Si lo desea, puede invitarles a escribir "Soy fuerte porque ..." en la parte superior de su hoja. Si lo considera oportuno, puede proporcionar papel de escritura y dar a las y los participantes la opción de escribir / hacer una lluvia de ideas sobre sus pensamientos e ideas antes de crear sus rompecabezas.

Proyecto de grupo: Si elige hacer un proyecto grupal, puede invitar a las y los participantes en cualquier momento a acercarse al cartel grande (papel de carnicero) y escribir una o más razones por las que son fuertes.
closing_spanish:
Puede darle al grupo la oportunidad de compartir de manera voluntaria su creación artística, una o más de las razones por las que son fuertes, todo lo que descubrieron, sintieron o experimentaron durante la creación, o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir.

Proyecto de grupo: Para el proyecto grupal, puede señalar puntos similares hechos que se compartieron y agregar esos puntos en común al tablero "Somos fuertes porque ...".

Si es posible, también tiene la opción de dar formato a los elementos que comparten en común en cuanto a por qué sienten que son fuertes y hacerlo un poema. Aquí hay un ejemplo de un taller que se ha hecho en el pasado: Somos fuertes porque - El Club de Poesía "Somos pacientes (a veces).

Todas y todos hemos experimentado buenos y malos momentos. Somos fuertes porque venimos de culturas fuertes. Nos ayudamos mutuamente incluso cuando no nos llevamos bien.

Hemos tenido experiencias similares. Hemos tenido pasados similares. Nos reunimos para ayudarnos entre nosotras y nosotros en tiempos difíciles. Si no lo fuéramos, no estaríamos aquí hoy.

Todas y todos somos amadas y amados y nos necesitamos entre nosotras y nosotros ". Siéntase libre de cerrar el taller de la manera que mejor funcione para usted y su grupo.
