For the opening circle, you can read one or more of the poems from the handout to the participants and then invite them to a discussion. You can prompt a discussion by asking what they feel that the overall message of the poem is.

Based on the discussion that's been generated, you can then make a transition statement such as: "We all have been through good times and bad times and everything we've experienced has made us who we are today... strong. If we were not strong, we wouldn't make a commitment to be here today."

Feel free to cater the discussion however way it best suits your group.
opening_circle_spanish:
Para el círculo de apertura, puede leer uno o más de los poemas del folleto al grupo y luego invitar al grupo a discutirlos. Puede iniciar una discusión preguntando qué es lo que creen las y los participantes que es el mensaje general del poema.

De acuerdo con la discusión que se ha generado, puede hacer una declaración de transición como: "Todas y todos hemos pasado por momentos buenos y malos y todo lo que hemos experimentado nos ha hecho quienes somos hoy ... fuertes. Si no fuéramos fuertes, no nos comprometeríamos a estar aquí hoy."

Siéntase libre de atender la discusión de la manera que mejor se adapte a su grupo.

title: Journey Footprints / Huellas de Viaje
objective: This workshop aims to validate participants' unique life journeys through the creation of a two feet representing their past and future.
materials:
•  
      Feet template
       

    Poster board

  • Glue sticks

  • Scissors

  • Magazines

  • Markers

  • Construction paper

  • Feet template

  • Relaxing music
setup:
If possible, we recommend that the participants have the opportunity to trace their own feet as template for their footprint journey. But you may wish to consider printing copies of the Feet Template on colored cardstock beforehand for participants who don't feel comfortable revealing and/or tracing their own feet.

If time permits, you also have the option to give participants the opportunity to create two footprints, one representing their past, and the other focused on their future. This is entirely up to you, but it will require more time for your workshop.
warm_up:
If you choose to incorporate relaxation/mediation into your workshop, you can use our suggested exercise, or your own. It's entirely up to you. You have complete freedom to adapt or alter any part of this workshop to cater to your group's needs. You may wish to play soft, relaxing music in the background to create a calming atmosphere.

You can begin by guiding those who wish to participate through a simple breathing exercise.

Let’s get comfortable in our seats, you are welcome to close your eyes or gently affix your gaze to an area in the room.  Now, as you sit breathing deeply and slowly, I want to remind you that this is a window of time for you.  

Take a deep deep breath all the way down to your feet. Feel a relaxing sensation come over you and take another deep breath all the way down to your toes.

Think about your feet... where have they carried you in your journey through life?  Where are some of the places they have taken you? What are some of the things you have seen along the way? What are some of the things you have felt or thought while on your journey? What has led you to this point in your life? What has led you to today?  What images, words, and colors come to mind?  Hold those thoughts in you mind and take another breath.

 Take another deep breath and think about your feet…where they can carry you in your future?  Where are some of the places you would like to go? What are some of the things you would like to do? Notice if any specific images, words or colors come to mind ... and take another deep breath….And when you are ready…I invite you to open your eyes if they were closed and begin to create your journey footprint.
creation:
Step 1:
To begin, you can invite those who wish to participate to trace the outline of their own foot onto a poster board and then cut it out. For those who don't feel comfortable using their own feet, you can invite them to select their preferred color footprint (if you have printed them from the template in advance).

Step 2:
Now, you may invite the participants to use any and as much of the collage materials as they like to create their journey footprints. You may wish to encourage them to include their whole journey; past, present, and future hopes and dreams. It doesn't matter what it looks like and there is no wrong way to create. However way they choose to collage their art piece will be perfect. Ideally, they would collage on only one side of the foot.

You may play soft music in the background during this step to create a relaxing atmosphere as participants create.

Step 3:
When participants have had ample time to create their collages, you can encourage them write some words on the back of the collage regarding what the collage may mean to them, if they wish, or anything else they may want to write. Some may want to sign and date their collage. Anything they would like to write, or if they wish to not write anything at all would be just fine.

If you have chosen to give them the opportunity to create two separate journey footprints (one for past and one for the future), you may repeat steps 1 and 2.

Step 4 (Optional):
If possible, you can now give participants an opportunity to laminate their collages. To laminate, you can cover the entire footprint using self-laminating sheets or contact paper on both sides, then cut off any excess laminating material and voila... they look great and will last longer! 

If you are using a laminator, you may need to do the laminating, as lamination sheets can be tricky and unforgiving when you make a mistake. After laminating, small pieces of magnetic tape (adhesive backed) can be added to the back of the collages so they can be hung on a metal surface.

                            
Cutting the foot out     Gluing words and images   Creation with foot templates Creation on printable worksheet
closing:
For the closing, you may give the participants an opportunity to share their amazing footprint journeys, what it means to them, and anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating and seeing their whole journey on their own foot, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

You may wish to close out by affirming each participant's experiences and thanking them for their courage.
description: Participants create collages that validate their unique journey through domestic violence using the outline of their own feet as the template of the collage.
objective_spanish: Este taller tiene como objetivo permitir a las y los participantes validar su viaje único y personal de la vida, a través de la creación de un collage utilizando el contorno de su propio pie como plantilla.
materials_spanish:
• Cartulina
• Pegamento en barra
• Tijeras
• Revistas
• Marcadores
• Papel de construcción
• Plantilla de pies
• Música relajante
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 10 min
Calentamiento: 5 min
Creación: 45 min
Cierre: 10 min
Total: 1:10 hora
setup_spanish:
Si es posible, recomendamos que las y los participantes tengan la oportunidad de trazar sus propios pies como plantilla para su huella de viaje. Pero es posible que desee considerar la posibilidad de imprimir copias de la Plantilla de Pies en cartulina de colores de antemano para las y los participantes que no se sientan con la comodidad de revelar y / o trazar sus propios pies.

Si el tiempo lo permite, también tiene la opción de darles a las y los participantes la oportunidad de crear dos huellas, una que represente su pasado y la otra enfocada en su futuro. Esto depende completamente de usted, pero requerirá más tiempo para su taller.
warm_up_spanish:
Si elige incorporar la relajación / mediación en su taller, puede utilizar nuestro ejercicio sugerido, o uno suyo. Depende totalmente de usted. Tiene total libertad para adaptar o alterar cualquier parte de este taller para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo. Es posible que desee reproducir música suave y relajante en el fondo para crear un ambiente relajante.

Puede comenzar guiando a las y los integrantes que desean participar a través de un simple ejercicio de respiración.

Una vez que las y los participantes hayan tenido la oportunidad de notar su respiración y concentrarse en el momento presente, puede terminar con: "Ahora, mientras se sientan y respiran profunda y lentamente, me gustaría que recuerden que este es un momento para que se den cuenta y honren su viaje de la vida a través del bien, así como los momentos difíciles. Todos los lugares en los que han estado en su vida han jugado un papel importante en la formación de la hermosa persona que son hoy. Me gustaría animarles a que ahora se concentren en sus pies... ¿a dónde les han llevado en el viaje de su vida? Traten de notar qué imágenes, palabras o colores vienen a su mente. Traten de imaginar a dónde les gustaría que les llevaran sus pies ahora y en el futuro. ¿Cómo sería su vida ideal? no hay respuesta incorrecta. Cualquier imagen, palabra o color que venga a su mente será perfecta, porque eso es lo que les está hablando en este momento... Cuando estén listas o listos, pueden abrir los ojos y comenzar el collage de su viaje."
creation_spanish:
Paso 1:
Para comenzar, puede invitar a las y los integrantes que deseen participar a trazar el contorno de sus propios pies en una cartulina y luego recortarlos. Para aquellas o aquellos que no se sienten cómodas o cómodos usando sus propios pies, puede invitarles a seleccionar su huella de papel cartulina del color que prefieran (si ha impreso la plantilla con anticipación).

Paso 2:
Ahora, puede invitar a las y los participantes a utilizar el cualquier tipo y cantidad del material para hacer su collage como gusten, para poder crear sus huellas de viaje. Si lo desea, puede animarles a incluir todo su viaje; Sueños y esperanzas pasadas, presentes y futuras. No importa cómo se vea ya que no hay una forma incorrecta de crear. Cómo sea que decidan crear su arte será perfecto. Lo ideal sería que hagan el collage en un solo lado del pie.

Puede poner música suave de fondo durante este paso para crear un ambiente relajante mientras las y los participantes crean.

Paso 3:
Cuando las y los participantes hayan tenido tiempo suficiente para crear sus collages, puede animarles a escribir algunas palabras en la parte posterior del collage referentes a lo que su collage puede significar para cada quien, si así lo desean, o cualquier otra cosa que quieran escribir. Algunos querrán firmar y poner la fecha en su collage. Cualquier cosa que les gustaría escribir, o si no desean escribir nada en absoluto, está perfecto.

Si ha elegido darles la oportunidad de crear dos huellas de viaje separadas (una para el pasado y otra para el futuro), puede repetir los pasos 1 y 2.

Paso 4 (Opcional):
Si es posible, ahora puede darles a las y los participantes la oportunidad de laminar sus collages. Para laminar, puede cubrir toda la huella con hojas de laminación automática o 

papel de contacto en ambos lados, luego cortar cualquier exceso de material de laminación y listo ... ¡se ven muy bien y durarán más!

Si está utilizando un laminador, es posible que deba hacer el laminado, ya que las hojas de laminación pueden ser difíciles e castigadoras cuando cometen un error. Después de la laminación, pueden agregar pequeños trozos de cinta magnética (adhesivo con respaldo) a la parte posterior de los collages para que puedan colgarse en una superficie metálica.
closing_spanish:
Para el cierre, puede darles a las los participantes la oportunidad de compartir los increíbles recorridos que han hecho sus huellas, lo que significa para cada quien, todo lo que aprendieron, sintieron o experimentaron en el proceso de creación y cómo fue ver todo el viaje que han tenido sus propios pies o cualquier otra cosa que quieran compartir. Por supuesto, esto es puramente opcional y si nadie se siente cómoda o cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.

Si lo desea, puede cerrar validando las experiencias de cada participante y agradeciéndoles su valentía.
optional_materials:
Printable self-led worksheet  

These materials can be used with the materials list above:

  • Laminating sheets

  • Contact paper or laminator

  • "Footprints in the Sand" poem (click here for handout)

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable self-led worksheet. If you are utilizing this sheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out beforehand for your participants depending on the setting. You can also offer this journaling page if you like.

Optional materials for self-led worksheet:

  • Self-led worksheet

  • Journey Footprints journal

  • Pencils

  • Pens

  • Colored pencils

  • Markers

  • Erasers
optional_materials_spanish:
• Hojas de laminación
• Papel de contacto o laminador.
• Poema "Huellas en la arena"
introduction:
You can open by taking a brief moment to explain the Journey Footprints workshop and what it symbolizes. You can show a sample if you have created one in advance. You may also invite the participants to introduce themselves and give one word describing how they are feeling today, if they feel comfortable doing so. If you choose, you may also read the "Footprints in the Sand" poem for the participants and/or print copies for them to take home.

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
introduction_spanish:
Puede comenzar tomando un breve momento para explicar el taller “Huellas de Viaje” y lo que simboliza. Si ha creado una pieza por adelantado, puede mostrarla. También puede invitar a cada integrante del grupo a presentarse y describir cómo se sienten hoy, en una palabra, si se sienten cómodas o cómodos de hacerlo. Si lo desea, también puede leer el poema "Huellas en la arena" para el grupo y / o imprimir copias para que se las lleven a casa.

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que este taller es una ventana de tiempo para ustedes. Esto significa que este es un espacio seguro para notar sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que digan o hagan es voluntario.

Ofreceré una sugerencia de cómo hacer el taller, compartiré los materiales que tenemos disponibles y les invitaré a crear, pero no hay una forma incorrecta de hacerlo. No importa cómo se vea. Lo importante es tomar este tiempo para honrar verdaderamente sus pensamientos y sentimientos, sin importar cómo surjan. Si no pueden pensar en nada qué crear o escribir, siéntanse libres de solo observar.

Como decidan pasar este tiempo está perfectamente bien. Este es su momento. Por favor, pídanme lo que necesiten y sepan que estoy aquí para ayudarles."

title: Brick Wall
author_location: Sexual Assault Crisis Agency, Long Beach, California
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to explore their feelings and issues and create a brick wall drawing that symbolizes the emotional walls they've built in order to survive.
materials:
• Construction paper

  • Markers
setup:
If appropriate for your group, you can print a copy of The Wall poem handout for each participant, or just one copy for yourself to read to the participants during the opening.

You can provide any and as many drawing utensils as you like.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create to begin. Participants can use markers (or pencils, oil pastels, if available) to draw a brick wall. On each brick, participants can draw any images, shapes, symbols, just use colors, or write word(s) that represent the elements of the emotional wall they've built.

The bottom brick can symbolize the things they hide from the outside world, and the brick on top can symbolize what the outside world sees. They have complete freedom to draw as many bricks as they like and decorate each brick however way they like.

You may wish to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create and it doesn't matter what it looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to honor their thoughts and feelings and creating something that is meaningful and expressive.
closing:
You can invite participants to volunteer and share their drawings, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.

You can also give participants the option to "tear down" their wall, if they so choose. They can tear it up, crumple it and throw it in the trash, or however way they like to symbolize their readiness to break down their wall.
description: Clients are given the opportunity to explore feelings and issues and gain self-awareness by creating a brick wall to represent the emotional walls they have built in order to survive.
optional_materials:
• The Wall: Freedom In Three Parts poem Click here for handout in Spanish

  • Oil pastels

  • Colored pencils
introduction:
"Today, you have an opportunity to explore issues and feelings that may have compelled you to build an emotional wall in order to survive. You'll get to notice what you show the outside world and what you keep inside, and explore the positive and negative aspects of having the wall, and consider what it may be like to take it down."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
opening_circle: If relevant to your group, you can share The Wall: Freedom In Three Parts poem with the participants. You can also facilitate a discussion around the proverbial building an emotional wall as a way to protect oneself.

title: Protective Shields
objective: This workshop aims to give children an opportunity to explore what it means to feel protected and create a shield decorated with representations of the people and elements of their lives they wish to protect.
materials:
• Blank DIY shields

  • Magazines (Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Scissors

  • Glue sticks

  • Aluminum foil
setup:
You are welcome to use either the blank shields which you can purchase from Amazon, or use one of our templates for smaller, less expensive version.

You can print one template for each child and invite them to decorate it on the printed sheet, or you can print them, cut them out and invite children to use them as a stencil to trace the shield onto a sheet of construction paper (or cardstock), the size of your choice.

You can lay out the supplies so that each child has easy access to them.

For younger children, you may consider cutting a diverse variety of images and words out of magazines in advance, as this can help save time, and preclude the children from handling scissors.

You may find it helpful to create a sample in advance to show the children what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample and using only the material you're providing so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges. You may, however, use one of the templates to create a small sample, even if you're providing the larger shields.

If possible, you can invite the children in advance to bring photos of people and/or things they wish to protect into the workshop (Ex: picture of siblings, pet, home, etc).

For younger children who may be less inclined to collage, you can give them the option to decorate their shield with markers, oil pastels, or any other supplies (without the aluminum foil). It's entirely up to you.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation: You can now invite those who wish to create their protective shield to begin doing so. Depending on the options you're providing, some children may need help with certain elements. Feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
closing:
You can invite children to share their creations, whom and what they've chosen to protect, anything they discovered or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.

Of course, this is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
description: This workshop gives the children the opportunity to visually express valuable aspects in their life they wish to protect when they feel a sense of danger. To explore what it means to feel protected or safe and create something tangible that helps them feel secure.
optional_materials:
• Blank shield template (instead of the large ones)

  • Shield template (with quadrants)

  • Construction paper (or cardstock; variety of colors)

  • Markers

  • Oil pastels (CrayPas)
introduction:
"Shields were once used as a main source for personal protection in war during the early ages. They were carried in one hand or on the arm to ward off enemy shots. Shields were not only for protection in battle, but also to identify its owner. The shields varied in size, shapes, and design."

"Today, you'll get a chance to create your very own personal protective shield and you get to decorate it with images and/or words that represent the people and things you wish to protect."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
Protective Shield that includes "Family, Friends, Myself and Music"

 

You can take a few minutes to introduce the art supplies and share the following creation steps with the children. Feel free to demonstrate any element that you see fit. If you've made a sample, it may be a good time to pass it around for reference.
 

Step 1:
"First, you can wrap the front side of your shield with aluminum foil, as smoothly as possible. An easy way to do is is to put glue on the shield, then lay the aluminum foil on top, smooth out any wrinkles, and either fold or cut the edges out."


Step 2:
"Next, you can divide your shield into 4 parts. Each section can be as big or little as you like. In each section, you can represent a valuable aspect of your life that you want to protect. It could be your siblings, pets, toys, yourself, nature, or anything you wish to protect. You can choose a title for each section, then look through the magazines (or pre-cut images) and cut images and/or words that represent those people or things and glue them on the shield."


If you're providing markers, oil pastels, etc. you can invite children to use any of the supplies available in addition to collaging images to decorate their shield in any manner they like.

For younger children, you can also invite them to tear images out with their hands, which can create a cool effect.
opening_circle:
You can invite the children to think about and share, if any feel comfortable doing so, what things or people they wish to protect in their life. Feel free to share examples of your own to help break the ice.

If no one feels comfortable sharing, they can just write it down, or just think about it.

title: Heart Stories
objective: This workshop gives children and teens an opportunity to listen to their hearts, value the stories within them, and recognize that others want to hear their stories, by creating a Heart Stories art piece.
materials:
• Oil pastels (Cray-Pas preferred)

  • Thick white paper or watercolor paper

  • Brushes

  • Watercolors

  • Cups with water (2 per person; one for rinsing the brush, the other to wet it for the paint)

  • Paper towels
warm_up:
"My heart feels glad because I am thankful. There is no wrong way to do art."
 
 
  "Tomorrow we’re leaving, so my heart is sad and crying. It is drying its eyes with a towel."

For the warm-up you have the option to utilize any of the following suggested exercises, or incorporate your own exercise. Feel free to alter or adapt any element of this workshop to cater to your group's needs. You may wish to consider your age group and other relevant factors to determine which exercise, if any, you wish to include in your workshop.

Option 1: Heart Talk Warm-up:
This is a discussion-style warm-up that children can do in pairs. You can invite the children to select 1-3 questions from the list below or create your own, and give them the opportunity to discuss with a partner.

Option 2: Confetti Heart Questions:
You can print several copies of the questions you have selected for your group on colored paper and cut out each question separately. You can then scatter the questions in the center of the table, and encourage the children to pick a question at random or to pick one that they like, and share their thoughts with the group.

Possible Heart Talk Questions:

  • What is something that made your heart happy this week?

  • If your heart was a color today, what color would it be and why?

  • What makes your heart laugh?

  • If your heart could do something fun, what would it do?

  • If your heart could do something it’s never done before, what would it do?

  • What’s something your heart is proud of about you or your family?

  • What makes your heart feel safe?

  • What makes your heart feel scared?

  • What makes your heart strong?

  • What makes your heart beat faster?

  • What makes your heart happy?

  • How do you look when your heart is sad?

  • How do you look when your heart is happy?
     

Option 3: Embodied Warm-up — Happy Hearts/Sad Hearts:

This embodied warm-up can work well with younger children. This can also be a stand alone workshop, meaning you can choose to only embody the heart stories and omit the visual art portion.

“During this exercise, I'm going to ask you some questions, if you feel comfortable following along, that's great. If you feel more comfortable just listening and watching, that's great too."

"Today you have an opportunity to listen to your heart and notice what helps your heart feel safe and happy. Does anyone know where your heart is? Can you show me (You can guide everyone to put their hands on their hearts)?"

"Good. What does your heart do (Ex: Pump your blood around your body, bring oxygen to your whole self, tell you how you’re feeling, beat fast when you’re excited or nervous, etc.)?"

"Can you feel it beating? Your heart is right in the center of you. Sometimes you can feel feelings in your heart. Has anyone ever felt happiness in their heart? Or sadness, like your heart is breaking? Sometimes when our hearts are feeling different ways, our whole body knows it."

"When you have a sad heart what does your body do (Ex: Does it curl up? Look down? Cry? Does your body react at all?)? If at any point you don't feel comfortable, feel free to stop and observe. It's perfectly okay. If you wish to continue, try to become a sad heart with your whole body, and notice how it feels in your whole body when you are sad. It’s okay to be sad sometimes and let it out with our whole bodies. Remember that sadness can look and feel different for each person. However sadness looks for you is perfectly okay. Now, I'd like to invite you to take a deep breath in and breathe all the sadness out. Good!"

"Now I'd like to invite you to think about when you have happy hearts. What does your body do then (Ex: Does it smile? Jump up and down? Dance?)? Now try to become a happy heart with your whole body. Wonderful! Take a deep breath in and feel your heart filling up with happiness. Hearts need a lot of love. And they need to be taken care of and listened to. Today you have a chance to listen to your hearts and take care of it.”
creation:
For the creation process, you may wish to participate along with the children. By modeling your enthusiasm and willingness to participate, you can help build trust, bonding, and make it safer for the children to play and share vulnerable experiences. Again, this is entirely up to you.

Step One: Draw Your Heart
"For those of you who wish to participate, I'd like to invite you to begin by using oil pastels to draw your heart. Your heart doesn't have to look like other hearts you see. It can look like anything you want. You are free to use any shape or color. You can use as many colors as you like. You can color the inside or just draw an outline. Remember, this is your time to create and there is no right or wrong way to do it."

Step Two: Add Color
"Now, you are welcome to add paint on top of the oil pastels. Again, you are free to choose any and as many colors as you like. The more water you use to blend with your preferred color, the more the Cray-Pas show through. The less water, the 'thicker' the paint will be and the less the Cray-Pas will show."

Step Three: Add Words
"Now, you can notice if there are any words, or even symbols that go with your heart. You have the choice to write down the story that your heart wants to share, just words, draw symbols, or you may leave it as is. Remember, it doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is that you recognize your amazing heart, the feelings and stories you hold inside it, and know that you have the opportunity to express it however way you like."
closing:
For the closing, you may give the children an opportunity to share their amazing Heart Stories and anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

If you notice the group seems sad by the end, you may leave things on a positive note by inviting the children to share something positive. For example, they may wish to share a way they want to take good care of their heart. Or, they could say something they like about the person on their left, in order to put a nice feeling into everyone’s heart. This is entirely up to you and you are free to close out the workshop however way you see fit.
description: This workshop supports children and teens in sharing their hearts and stories through art. The workshop gives them an opportunity to listen to their hearts, value the stories within them, and know that others want to hear them too.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Heart Stories Worksheet (English)

  • Heart Stories Worksheet (Spanish)

   
Heart Stories Worksheet     Heart Stories Worksheet 
(English)     (Spanish)
introduction:
"Today, you will have a chance to notice what’s in your heart and what your heart would say if it could talk. You will have the opportunity to create Heart Stories paintings to express the different feelings you have in your heart. You will have the chance to think about what color your heart would be inside and outside. Remember, it is perfectly okay if it doesn't look like anyone else's, we are all unique and we all feel are feelings different."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."

title: Journey Butterflies
objective: To provide children a creative opportunity to explore their journey toward growth and transformation by using the butterfly as a powerful symbol for their hopes, dreams and freedom.
materials:
Optional printable worksheet

  • Shrinky-Dink paper (Ruff-N-Ready type)

  • Colored pencils

  • Pencil sharpeners

  • Permanent markers

  • Scissors

  • Hole punchers

  • Craft wire

  • Wire cutters/pliers

  • Assorted beads

  • Assorted findings (fishhook earrings, key chains, jump rings)

  • Assorted ribbon

  • Toaster oven

  • Brown paper bag (only need 1 to use as a tray handle; see creation for details)

  • Relaxing music

  • Butterfly templates (3 pages) click here

  • The Butterfly story  click here

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print copies out for your participants beforehand depending on the setting.
setup:
Sample table set-up

You may consider printing enough photocopies of the various templates for all the participants. To save time, you can pre-cut the Shrinky Dinks into 3 1/2" x 4" squares and 2" x 2" squares (for earring-sized butterflies) to fit the size of our template. It's always helpful to have all the materials set up prior to beginning the workshop.

You may also consider at some point during the workshop, to preheat your oven to 300°F at some point so that when children are done with coloring their Shrinky Dinks, they can immediately be placed in the oven.

You may wish to create a sample Shrinky Dink in advance so children can see what the final piece can look like. If you have never used the Shrinky Dink materials, you will also want to get a feel for how the Shrinky Dinks cook. It’s very exciting to watch. If you choose to create a sample, we suggest creating a simple one so children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
"Dare to Dream" Journey Butterfly

For the warm-up, you can read The Very Hungry Caterpillar by Eric Carle. If possible, you can invite the children to act out the 4 stages of a butterfly's life as you read through the story. Young children typically enjoy being a part of the workshop in a dramatic way. You can also read them The Butterfly in conjunction with the book. It's entirely up to you.

You can stand up and physically go through the 4 stages of a butterfly's life: First, a tiny egg, so very small. Second, a hungry caterpillar searching for food; Third, finding a dry safe place to build a comfortable cocoon, and lastly, emerging as a beautiful butterfly, spreading its wings and flying for the first time. You can encourage those who wish to participate to fly around the room, fluttering their arms, then invite them to fly back to their seats.

We recommend reading the story in a fun, animated and engaging voice.
creation:
For the creation, you are welcome to guide the children through the following steps. Depending on the age group, you can guide them through each step at a time, or give them all the instructions at once and then invite them to create. Please feel free to offer your assistance where you see fit, especially in using scissors to cut out their butterflies.

 

    
  Drawing the Butterfly

Step 1: Designing the Shrinky Dinks
"For those of you who wish to participate, I'd like to invite you to choose a butterfly templates. You can start by tracing the template on the Shrinky Dink. Pencils will only work on the rough side, and markers can be used on either side. Once you've traced the template, you can begin to color and create the design that will fill in the shape of your butterfly. You are free to design and color it however you wish. If you like, you can write words, draw shapes, or symbols, or just color in."


Step 2: Cutting the Shrinky Dinks
"Once you're done coloring, you can use scissors to cut out your Shrinky Dink."

 

    
  Baked Butterflies ready for beading

Step 3: Optional Hole Punch
"If you wish to wear your butterfly as a necklace or hang it on your wall, you can use a hole punch to punch a hole near the top, leaving some room at the top. Remember, once Shrinky Dinks are baked, they cannot be altered."


Step 4: Preparing the Shrinky Dinks for Baking
Now the Shrinky Dinks are ready for baking. Your oven should be pre-heated at 300°F. You can place the Shrinky Dink pieces, shiny side up, on a small cut-out piece of a brown paper bag and place it on a tray or cookie sheet. You can use a piece of a brown grocery bag and bend on corner. This paper can serve as a handle for you to remove the Shrinky Dinks without touching the hot cookie sheet.

You may consider leaving some space between each piece to prevent them from sticking together.

 

    
  Beading the Journey Butterfly

Step 5: Baking the Shrinky Dinks
You can now place the Shrinky Dinks in the oven at 300°F for 1-3 minutes and watch the Shrinky Dinks shrink. Children generally enjoy watching this process, so feel free to invite them to stand and watch. Once pieces have shrunk and flattened, you can allow an additional 15 seconds or so to complete the process. If you pull them out prematurely, you can put them right back in the oven. Once they're done and you remove them out of the oven, you can allow a couple of minutes for them to cool.

Please be mindful of the fact that a toaster oven can get very hot even on its outer surfaces.


Step 6: Optional Creating a Loop
For those who punched a hole and want to hang their Shrinky Dinks, you can now invite them to use ribbon, wire, thread, or any of the hanging material you've provided to loop through the hole. They can add beads to the wire or ribbon, if available, and if they wish to do so.
closing: For the closing, you may give the children an opportunity to share their Journey Butterflies, what it means to them, anything felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.
description: This workshop provides participants a creative opportunity to explore their journey toward growth and transformation by using the butterfly as a powerful symbol for our hopes, dreams, and freedom.
tips: If you like, and if time permits, you can make wonderful flowers out of watercolored coffee filters for Mothers' Day or spring. These flowers can be good additional creations to go along with their butterflies. You can click this link for further details.
introduction:
"Change" Journey Butterfly

“Welcome. Butterflies are very special and beautiful creatures, even though they don't start out that way. Like each one of us, they grow and change. In fact, butterflies go through four stages during their lifetime. Their whole life is about transformation. Butterflies are sometimes used in art as a symbol for this. Traditionally, they represent new life, hopes, dreams and freedom. I feel that butterflies are symbolic of the inside of our soul, ready to take flight. So today, you'll have an opportunity to create your very own journey butterflies. You can make more than one and decorate it with beads and wire to hang on your wall, or as key chains, or earrings. Each butterfly will be as unique and special as each one of you. I invite you to relax and enjoy your special creative journey during this art workshop to explore and express your colorful soul.”

"But before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

title: Self-Love Maps / Mapas de amor propio
author_location: Women’s Windows Leader, Haven House Pasadena
objective: This workshop aims to reinforce self-love by giving participants an opportunity to notice where they are now and where they want to go, and create a map that represents their journey to self-love.
materials:
Optional printable worksheet

  • Self-love map template (Map 1, Map 2, Map 3, Map 4)

  • Lists of Characteristics & Traits of Self-Love (English; Spanish)

  • Blank strips of paper

  • Magazines (Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Scissors

  • Glue

  • Fine-point markers

  • Pen and paper (for the warm-up exercise)

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print copies out for your participants beforehand depending on the setting.
setup:
You are welcome to use one or all of the map templates. You can print them so that each participant has one.

You may lay out the art supplies including magazines so that each participant has easy access.

To save time, you may want to cut out strips of paper to (1" x 3") which they will use to write down "street names" on their maps. This could be any color paper.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show participants what the finished art piece can looks like. If you choose to do so we suggest creating a simple map so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You can invite participants to a discussion and prompt them with the following questions. You can create a list of responses to each question on a board, if available, or you can invite the participants to write their responses individually if they don't feel comfortable sharing.

  • "What are the childhood experiences that lead to low-self esteem?" 

  • "What are the childhood experiences that lead to high self-esteem?"

You can then take the "high self-esteem" list and invite the participants to recall what each of these things felt like. That feeling is the feeling of nurturing. You can reinforce that we learn how to treat ourselves from the way our parents/caretakers treated us. The difference is that now we are our own caretakers. Self-love is the result of all the good things on the list being done to us.

Next, you can pass out the list of characteristics and invite participants to read them and if anyone feels comfortable doing so, share ones that resonate with them. Feel free to add your own characteristics, or encourage participants to come up with their own.
creation:
Self-Love Map with "Compassion, Boundaries, Creativity, Economic Security" as street names
 
 
  Road to Self-Love involving "Wisdom" and "Contentment"

You can now invite those who wish to create to begin by choosing a map and going through the magazines and cutting out two images; one that symbolizes where they are now, and one that symbolizes where they want to go. Then, they get to choose a "You are Here" location on the map and glue the respective image on that spot.

Next, they can choose a spot on the map to represent their destination of "Self-Love" and glue the respective image on that spot.

Then, they get to map out their route from the first image (where they are now) to the second image (self-love) by drawing a line on those streets. It could be a direct route (line), or it could be jagged. They get to choose however they wish to create the route to self-love.

Finally, participants can use any and as many characteristics of self-love that resonated with them (either from the list or ones they came up with) and write each on a strips of paper and use them as street names. The map is now a tangible reminder of what they need in order to get from where they are now to their destination of self-love.
closing: You can give participants who wish to do so, a chance to share their maps, what steps they envision they need to take on their journey to self-love, or anything else they may wish to share.
description: This workshop lets participants think in definite terms about where they are on the journey to Self-Love.
objective_spanish:
Para que las participantes puedan pensar en términos definitivos sobre su

lugar en la jornada a “Auto amor” o sea self-love.

Introducción:
“Auto amor o self love crea la posibilidad de cultivar nosotras mismas y sentirnos bien sobre establecer y lograr nuestras metas. Muchas veces, no sabemos cómo cultivar nosotras mismas. Para cultivarnos, es necesario que sea el resultado de amor hacia nosotras mismas. Este taller provee una oportunidad de explorar donde estamos en la jornada a auto amor o self-love.

Caracteristicas del Amor Propio:

  • Compasiòn

  • Sensatez

  • Intuiciòn

  • Paz

  • Seguridad Econòmica

  • Valor de si mismo

  • Bellesa

  • Creatividad

  • Alegria

  • Lealtad Propia

  • Gratitud

  • Autosuficiencia

  • Satisfacciòn

  • Libertad interna

  • Confianza en sì mismo

  • Ingenio

  • Autoestima

  • Amor

  • Reconocimiento proprio

  • Alegrìa

  • Independencia

  • Serenidad

  • Bienestar

  • Cuidado Propio

  • Lìmites


Círculo de abertura:
Pregúntales compartir nombres y un comportamiento de auto cuidar o auto cultivar. También, pregúntales compartir de un acto de cuidar para otra persona. Típicamente hay una diferencia en el tiempo que tarda una persona pensar en un acto de cuidar para si misma y otra persona. Después de hacer esto, cada participante necesita afirmarse por decir: “Cultivaré mi misma con lo mismo amor que tengo para otras personas.”

Presentación:
En la pizarra….

¿Cuáles son las experiencias de la niñez que causan el autoestima bajarse?

Pregúntales escribir sus respuestas en la pizarra

¿Cuáles son las experiencias de la niñez que causan el autoestima estar alto?

También pregúntales escribir sus respuestas en la pizarra

Necesita concentrase en la lista de las buenas experiencias y pregúntales hablar del sentimiento de sus buenas experiencias. Este sentimiento es el sentimiento de cuidarnos. Aprendemos como tratarnos a parte de la manera en la que nuestros padres nos trataron. Auto-amor es el resultado de todas las cosas buenas las cuales que están el lista que hemos recibido.

Creación:
Distribuye la lista de características que necesita leerlas al grupo.

Muestra el mapa de “auto amor” y decirles que tienen la opción de cambiar el dicho “estás aquí” en el mapa. Puede ser en cualquier lugar pero están en el mapa. Auto amor es su destinación. Usando las características como los nombres de las calles. ¿Cuáles son las calles en las que necesita cruzar todavía? Pregúntales dibujar una línea entre el lugar en el que están y Auto-amor. No tiene que ser una línea recta. Entonces utilizando palabras para crear un camino desde el lugar en el que están hasta el final.

Utilizando fotos de una revista, necesitan cortar dos fotos – una para “estoy aquí” demostrando como se ven en este momento. Usa la otra para mostrar el auto amor cuando lleguen a su destino. Si a ellas les sobra tiempo, pueden utilizar una tercera foto para un punto en el medio.
introduction:
“Self-Love makes it possible to nurture ourselves and to feel good about setting and reaching goals. Yet often we just don’t know how to nurture ourselves. The journey to self-love begins with nurturing ourselves and nurturing starts with being loving and kind to ourselves."

"Today, you'll have an opportunity to explore where you are on your journey to self-love and create a special map that symbolizes your journey."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
opening_circle:
You can open by inviting participants, who feel comfortable doing so, to share their name and one act of self-nurturing they can think of. It could be something they’d like to do for themselves, or something they already do. Then, you can invite those who wish to do so, to share one act of nurturing they would do for someone else. 

Usually it's easier to think of how you can nurture someone else than how you can nurture yourself. If applicable, you can then encourage the participants to affirm "I will nurture myself with the same love I nurture others.”

description: This workshop provides participants a creative opportunity to explore their journey toward growth and transformation by using the butterfly as a powerful symbol for our hopes, dreams, and freedom.
objective_spanish: Proporcionar a los participantes una oportunidad creativa para explorar su camino hacia el crecimiento y la transformación mediante el uso de la mariposa como un símbolo poderoso para sus esperanzas, sueños y libertad.
materials_spanish:
• Papel de Shrinky-Dink (tipo de Ruff-N-Ready)

  • Lápices

  • Sacapuntas

  • Marcadores permanentes

  • Tijeras Perforadora para hacer agujeros

  • Alambre del arte Pinzas Cortadores de alambre/(alicates)

  • Perlas surtidas

  • Tiras de elastico surtido (elastico transparente, Argollas para llaveros)

  • Cinta surtida Horno tostador Bolsa de papel marrón (sólo necesita 1 para usar como manija de la bandeja; vea la creación para más detalles)

  • Música relajante

  • Plantillas de mariposa
setup_spanish:
Usted puede considerar la impresión de suficientes fotocopias de las diferentes plantillas con las mariposas, para todos los participantes. 

Para ahorrar tiempo, usted puede pre-cortar los Shrinky Dinks en " rectangulos 3 1/2  "x 4 y en " cuadrados “ 2 "x 2 (para las mariposas) para ajustarse al tamaño de nuestra plantilla. Siempre es útil tener todos los materiales configurados antes de comenzar el taller. También puede considerar en algún momento durante el taller,  precalentar su horno a 300°f , para que en cuanto los participantes han terminado de trazar  y  colorear sus Shrinky Dinks, puedan colocarlas inmediatamente en el horno.

Es posible que desee crear una muestra de Shrinky Dink de antemano para que los participantes puedan ver cómo puede ser la pieza final. Si usted nunca ha utilizado los materiales de Shrinky Dink, usted también querrá tener una idea de cómo se cocinan los Shrinky Dinks. 

La sensación es muy emocionante ver. Si decides crear una muestra, te sugerimos crear una sencilla para que los participantes no se abrumen por ningún desafío "artístico". Como facilitador, usted tiene total libertad para alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento de este taller para satisfacer las necesidades específicas de su grupo.
warm_up_spanish:
Al pasar el folleto de ejercicios de escritura e invitar a los participantes a completarlo. Recuerdeles  que hacer el ejercicio de calentamiento es opcional. Como facilitador del taller usted tiene la opción de también entregar la historia de la mariposa, o simplemente leerlo a los participantes antes de que comiencen su escritura, si lo considera pertinente. Una vez que lo hayan completado, puede invitarlos a compartir algunas de sus respuestas si alguien se siente cómodo haciéndolo. 

Por supuesto, esto es opcional y si nadie se siente cómodo compartiendo, eso está perfectamente bien.
creation_spanish:
Para la creación, le invitamos a guiar a los participantes a través de los siguientes pasos. Puede guiarlos a través de cada paso a la vez, o darles todas las instrucciones a la vez y luego invitarlos a crear. Por favor, siéntase libre de ofrecer su ayuda a los participantes donde usted ve que la necesitan.

Paso 1: 
Diseñando las mariposas en los rectangulos de plastico (Shrinky Dinks) "Para aquellos de ustedes que deseen participar, me gustaría invitarlos a elegir una plantilla de mariposa. Puede comenzar trazando la plantilla en el plastico(Shrinky Dink). Los lápices de color sólo funcionarán en el lado áspero, y los marcadores se pueden utilizar en cualquier lado. Una vez que hayas trazado la mariposa sobre la plantilla, puedes empezar a colorear y crear el diseño que llenará la forma de tu mariposa. Usted es libre de diseñar y colorearlo de la manera que usted desea. Si lo desea, puede escribir palabras, dibujar formas o símbolos, o simplemente colorear."

Paso 2: 
Cortando los plasticos Shrinky Dinks "Una vez que haya terminado de colorear, puede utilizar tijeras para cortar su  dibujo (Shrinky Dink). "

Paso 3: 
Use la perforadora para hacer los agujeros (opcional) "Si usted desea llevar su mariposa como un collar o colgarla en su pared, se puede utilizar una perforadora de un hoyo, para perforar un agujero cerca de la parte superior, dejando un poco de espacio en la parte superior. Recuerde, una vez que los Shrinky Dinks se hornean, no pueden ser alterados."

Paso 4: 
Preparando los Dinks Shrinky para hornear Ahora los Dinks Shrinky están listos para hornear. El horno debe precalentarse a 300 ° f. Usted puede colocar las piezas de Shrinky Dink,el lado brillante hacia arriba, coloquelo en un pedazo de papel (bolsa de papel marron) y colocarlo en una bandeja de metal (en las que hornea galletas). Al usar el papel de la bolsa, haga un doblez en la esquina. Este papel puede servir como manija para que usted quite los Shrinky Dinks sin tocar la bandeja de metal, (tener cuidado, esta muy caliente). Usted puede considerar dejar un poco de espacio entre cada pieza para evitar que se peguen juntos.

Paso 5: 
Hornear los Shrinky Dinks Ahora puede colocar los Shrinky Dinks en el horno a 300°f durante 1-3 minutos y ver el encogimiento de los Shrinky Dinks. Los participantes generalmente disfrutan viendo este proceso, así que siéntase libre de invitarlos a pararse y ver. Una vez que las piezas se han encogido y aplanado, puede permitir un 15 segundos adicionales más o menos para completar el proceso. Si los saca prematuramente, puede volver a ponerlos en el horno. Una vez que hayan terminado y los saque del horno, puede dejar que se enfríen un par de minutos. title: Power and Control Wheel
author_location: Women’s Windows Liaison at Laurel House, PA
objective: This workshop aims to help participants understand the cycle of violence by giving them a creative opportunity to tell their own unique story on a power and control wheel.
materials:
• Blank Power & Control Wheel template

  • Equality Wheel handout

  • Power and Control Wheel handout

  • Wheel Of Intimate Partner Power and Control in the African American/Black Community

  • Construction paper (large; variety of colors)

  • Markers

  • Colored pencils
setup:
You can print one copy of each template per participant. They will be using the blank one to create, and the other two as a reference for the opening discussion.

It may be helpful to read the templates so that you can have a discussion around the meaning of the power and control wheel.

You may want to lay out the art supplies so that each participant has easy access to them. You have the choice to provide any and as many of the decorative materials (paint, collage, etc.) as you like. Generally, the more options participants have, the more they can feel a sense of freedom to create and express.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Completed Power and Control Wheel

You can now invite those who wish to create their Power and Control wheel to begin doing so.

You may want to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to honor their experiences, thoughts and feelings and creating something that is expressive and meaningful to them.

For some participants, it may take some time to open up and begin writing. Feel free to give participants as much time as you see needed to complete their projects.
closing:
You can give anyone who wishes to share their Power and Control Wheel, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share. Of course, this is optional so if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

If you see fit, you can also invite participants to share how they plan to stay safe and take care of themselves, and encourage them to think about and/or share what they think a healthy relationship means. You can also refer to the Equality handout to discuss healthy relationship topics.

You may want to validate each participant's courage and strength and thank them for being here today.
description: The workshop was created to help each woman understand the cycle of violence and the dynamics of the power and control wheel. To give each person an opportunity to tell their own story of abuse by writing, drawing and collaging into a blank power and control wheel.
notes: This workshop is based on the Duluth Power and Control Wheel. It is the second in the “Creative Scrapbook” series created by Carolyn Coleman Manns of Laurel House in Pennsylvania.
tips: You also have the option to invite the participants to create a Power and Control Wheel as a group, in addition to creating one individually. This is great for cohesion building. It can then be hung anywhere that is suitable and bring a great sense of accomplishment to the participants.
optional_materials:
Painting option:

  • Paint

  • Brushes

  • Water cups (to rinse the brush)


Collage option:

  • Magazines (Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Scissors

  • Glue sticks

  • Glitter
introduction:
Power and Control Wheel using glitter words

"Today, we'll have a chance to discuss the cycle of violence and the dynamics of power and control. You will also have an opportunity to tell your own unique story through the creation of a Power and Control wheel."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
Simple Power and Control Wheel using colors
 

If you see the need, you can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation steps with the participants.
 

Step 1:
Participants get to write their own personal story and experience by filling out each sections of the wheel that applies to them. They are free to write in any form they like, i.e., poem, letter, bullet-point list, or any other expression of their thoughts and feelings.


Step 2:
Next, participants get to glue their wheel onto a large piece of construction paper (any color paper they choose) and use any of the art supplies available to decorate their art piece. They can write words, draw images, symbols, or simply use colors to express their thoughts and feelings in any manner they choose. They can use the blank space on the construction paper, and/or the wheel as a canvas. However they choose to decorate it, will be perfectly okay.

Feel free to demonstrate any creation element that you see fit. For instance, if you're providing collaging option, you can demonstrate how participants can cut images and words out of magazines using scissors for precision cutting, or just use their hands and tear the images out to create a cool effect.
opening_circle:
You can open with a discussion around the phases in the cycle of violence. You can also refer to the Power and Control wheel and discuss the tendencies of an abuser in a relationship. You can invite participants to share their story through one section of the wheel. Sharing experiences can give participants a chance to think about what they've gone through as well see how others have dealt with their issues.

This is a good opportunity to validate each participant's experience and note any similarities in their experiences.

This discussion can be triggering for some. Feel free to gauge the participants and structure the discussion however you see fit.

title: What is Love?
objective: This workshop gives children an opportunity to sort out the complex feelings of love, explore what love means to them, and how sharing love can help to spread love around the world.
materials:
• Multicultural people shapes

  • Oil pastels (CrayPas)

  • Googly eyes

  • Construction paper (variety of colors)

  • Tissue paper (variety of colors)

  • Foam heart shapes

  • Glitter glue

  • Glue sticks

  • Yarn (for hair)

  • Scissors

  • Stickers (to decorate the Earth)

  • Large sheet of butcher paper (about 36 inches in diameter, but it can be as big as you want for your earth)

  • Scotch tape
setup:
Drawing a large circle

 

Feel free to provide any decorative supplies (tissue paper, yarn, etc.) that you see fit.

You can draw or cut out a large circle out of butcher paper to represent the Earth. To create an accurate large circle, you can tie a pencil to a string and hold the end of the string where the center of the circle will be and draw with the other end (pencil attached end), stretching the string tightly as you go around in a circle (see image).

You may want to determine a spot to hang it in the room (on a wall, board, etc), ideally with ample space around the earth for children to attach their creations.

You can lay out some Earth decoration supplies near where you hang the Earth so that children can decorate the Earth without having to go back and forth to their tables.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show the children what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use one or both of our suggested warm-up options or one of your own.

Option 1:
You can read a part of the book "What is Love?" out loud to the group. We recommend reading pages that start with: "Love is like a rainbow...," or "But sometimes you may feel angry..." But you are welcome to read any part of it that you may find more suitable and relevant to your group.


Option 2:
In addition to, or instead of reading, you can prompt a discussion and write the children's responses (or invite them to come up and write it themselves) on the earth, leaving room for the Love Doll creations.

Some prompts we like include:

  • "What do you love?" - Ex: "my Mom," or "ice cream."

  • "How do you show love?" - Ex: "I smile," or "I say please and thank you."

  • "How do you give love?" - Ex: "I help with chores," or "I share my toys," or "I say I love you."

  • "How can my love help the world?" - Ex: "I don't waste supplies," or "I help recycle."


This may be a good opportunity to validate each child's response, if any feel comfortable sharing. If children don't feel comfortable sharing their ideas of love, you can share examples with them.

You can also talk about the way their love might touch another person and the ways their love can make a difference in the world.
creation:
Adding a heart to the Love Doll
 
 
  Completed Love Doll with black tissue paper skirt

You can now invite those who wish to create to choose a cut-out person that best represents them and a heart to decorate it with.

On the heart, they get to write words, draw shapes, images or symbols to express their feelings about love, then glue it onto the doll. If they like, they can glue googly eyes onto the dolls. They can use card stock or tissue paper as clothes or any garments or accessory they wish to add to their doll.

Their dolls can be simple or elaborate. There is a lot of flexibility in how they create, so you may want to encourage the children to get as creative as they like.

You may wish to remind them that it doesn't matter what it looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to reflect on love and create something that is expressive and meaningful to them.

As they finish, you can invite anyone who wishes to do so, to go to the Earth circle and help decorate "the world" with any of the supplies available (oil pastels, markers, stickers, etc). They can write loving words, draw symbols shapes or anything they like.

Some children may need help with certain elements such as writing, so feel free to offer your assistance where you see the need.
closing:
Love Dolls around the "World"

For the closing, you can invite children to share their Love Doll, what words they wrote on their heart, anything they learned, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share. You can also give them the option to go up to the Earth circle and tape their person to or around the Earth.

You can thank the children at the end for sharing their love and helping to make it a better place.
description: By creating a paper wall mural of the earth, this workshop gives participants an opportunity to sort out the complex feelings of love, begin to define what love means to them, and explore how sharing love can help to spread love around the world.
notes: This workshop is based on the children’s book "What is Love?" by Etan Boritzer.
optional_materials:

"I'd like to invite you to join me in a warm-up exercise. If you prefer to just observe, that's perfectly okay. Observing is participating."

"For those of you who wish to take part, I invite you to put your name into this basket and we will go around and you will each get to draw a name at random and take a few minutes and write that person an anonymous letter filled with kind thoughts and loving feelings.
