Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
Cutting the Polaroid

 

You can take a few minutes to introduce the art supplies and share the following creation steps with the participants.


Step 1:
Those who wish to participate can come up to the photo station and have their Polaroid profile photo taken (after the demonstration is over).

Ideally, the picture would be their profile from their waist up to their head. They can make a hand gesture or position their head in a way that best shows their pride and courage. But they are welcome to have any framing of their portrait taken that they feel comfortable with.


Step 2:
Next, participants get to cut the outline of their portrait out using scissors.

If you've taken a Polaroid photo in advance (of you or someone else), you can demonstrate cutting out the outline of the portrait (see image), then turning it over to reveal the black silhouette that is created.


Step 3:
Next, they can choose any color card stock and glue the silhouette anywhere they like onto the card stock. The back-side of the portrait (black side) should be facing up.


Step 4:
Finally, participants can use any and as many of the art supplies available and decorate their portrait. They can draw images, symbols, write words, a poem, collage words and/or images, or anything else they like in any manner that best expresses their courage.

You may wish to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to decorate or create. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to honor their strength and courage and creating something that is expressive and meaningful to them.

title: Treasure Boxes / Caja de Tesoros
objective: In this workshop, children get an opportunity to create a treasure box in which they can keep things that are valuable to them. These can be actual items, notes, or symbolic reminders.
materials:
• Boxes (shoe, pencil, paper mache, etc.)

  • Glue

  • Scissors

  • Color pencils

  • Permanent Markers (if using with any liquid including glue)
setup:
Feel free to provide any and as many design and decorative material from our optional list as you like, and even add your own. If you wish to incorporate collage into your workshop, you can bring magazines, or cut out images and words that are suitable for your group.

You may wish to create a sample in advance to show children what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest a simple design, using only the material you are providing, so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

If possible, you can invite the children to bring photographs of special people and/or things in their lives that they find valuable in advance.

Feel free to provide material that are suitable to your age group.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to participate to begin creating.

Depending on the age group, you can give them as much time as you see fit to decorate their treasure boxes. Children can get absorbed in the creation process and lose track of time. Feel free to give them reminders of how much time is left, if you see the need.

You may wish to remind the children that each treasure box is meant to reflect their own special and important treasures and that there is no right or wrong way to create this project. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What is most important is that they fill it with whatever reminders they may need of what is most important to them, and they want to keep safe.

You may also want to remind them that creation is voluntary and if they wish to do something else, that's perfectly okay.
closing:
For the closing, you can give children the opportunity to write or to share about the ways their treasures boxes are significant to them and how they felt creating a safe and private place of their own. If they choose, they can share how they intend to use their treasure boxes, or how they feel after having time to create.

Of course, if no one wishes to share, that's perfectly okay.
description: The purpose of this workshop is for children to create a treasure box of their own in which they can store things that are valuable to them in order to keep them safe. These can be actual items, notes, or symbolic reminders.
objective_spanish: En este taller, las niñas y niños tendrán la oportunidad de crear una caja de tesoros en la que pueden guardar cosas que son valiosas para ellas y ellos. Estos pueden ser objetos reales, notas o recordatorios simbólicos.
materials_spanish:
Cajas (zapato, lápiz, papel maché, etc.)
Pegamento
Tijeras
Lápices de colores
Marcadores permanentes (si se utiliza cualquier líquido, incluido el pegamento)
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 5 min
Demostración: 5 min
Apertura: 10 min
Creación: 45 min
Cierre: 10 min
Total: 1:15 hora
setup_spanish:
Siéntase libre de proporcionar cualquier diseño y material decorativo de nuestra lista opcional que desee, e incluso puede proporcionar cualquier otra idea suya. Si desea incorporar el collage a su taller, puede traer revistas o recortar imágenes y palabras que sean adecuadas para su grupo.

Es posible que desee crear una muestra por adelantado para mostrar a las niñas y niños cómo puede verse. Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos haga un diseño simple, utilizando solo el material que está proporcionando, para que las niñas y niños no se sientan abrumadas o abrumados por los desafíos "artísticos".

Si es posible, puede invitar a las y los participantes a traer de antemano fotografías de personas especiales y / o cosas de sus vidas que les parezcan valiosas.

Siéntase libre de proporcionar material que sea adecuado para la edad de su grupo.

Como la persona que facilita el taller, usted tiene total libertad para alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento del mismo para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo específico.
creation_spanish:
Ahora puede invitar a las personas que deseen participar para comenzar a crear.

Dependiendo de la edad del grupo, puede darles todo el tiempo que considere oportuno para decorar sus cajas de tesoros. Las niñas y niños pueden ser absorbidos en el proceso de creación y perder la noción del tiempo. Siéntase libre de darles recordatorios de cuánto tiempo queda, si ve la necesidad.

Si lo desea, puede recordad a las niñas y niños que cada caja de tesoro debe reflejar sus propios tesoros especiales e importantes y que no existe una forma correcta o incorrecta de crear este proyecto. No importa cómo se mire. Lo más importante es que llenen sus cajas con los recordatorios de lo que es más importante para ellos y lo que quieran mantener a salvo.

También puede recordarles que la creación es voluntaria y que, si desean hacer algo más, está perfectamente bien.
closing_spanish:
Para el cierre, puede darles a las niñas y niños la oportunidad de escribir o compartir de qué forma sus cajas de tesoros son importantes para ellas y ellos y cómo se sintieron al crear un lugar seguro y privado. Si lo desean, pueden compartir cómo planean usar sus cajas de tesoros o cómo se sienten después de tener este tiempo para crear.

Por supuesto, si nadie desea compartir, está perfectamente bien.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Treasure Boxes Worksheet (English and Spanish)

  • Magazines (for collage option; Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive imagery)

  • Tissue paper (variety of colors; to cover boxes)

  • Found objects (to create symbolic reminders of people, places or things that are meaningful or important, including drawings, notes, letters, etc.)

  • Jewelry pieces, sequins, glitter

  • Paint

  • Photographs (personal and/or family)

   
Treasure Boxes Worksheet     Treasure Boxes Worksheet
(English)     (Spanish)
optional_materials_spanish:
Revistas (para la opción de collage; Oprah, Nat Geo y las revistas de viajes tienden a tener imágenes más inclusivas)
Papel crepé (variedad de colores; para cubrir cajas)
Objetos encontrados (para crear recordatorios simbólicos de personas, lugares o cosas que son significativas o importantes, incluyendo dibujos, notas, cartas, etc.)
Joyas, lentejuelas, purpurina.
Pintura
Fotografías (personales y / o familiares)
introduction:
"When we hear treasure, we may imagine pirates, precious gems or gold. Our treasures are simply what is important, valuable, or meaningful to each of us that we want to keep safe and protected. They could be pictures, toys, letter or notes that you wrote for yourself or someone else, or ones someone special gave to you. It could be anything that you find valuable and want to keep safe."

"Today, you'll have a chance to create a special private box where you can keep whatever you find to be important to you. You get to decorate your box in any way that you wish."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
introduction_spanish:
"Cuando escuchamos la palabra “tesoro”, podemos imaginar piratas, piedras preciosas u oro. Nuestros tesoros son simplemente lo que es importante, valioso o significativo para cada una y uno de nosotros y lo que queremos mantener seguro y protegido. Podrían ser fotos, juguetes, cartas o notas que escribieron para ustedes o para otra persona, o tal vez que alguien especial les dio. Podría ser cualquier cosa que consideren valiosa y quieran mantener a salvo."

"Hoy, tendrán la oportunidad de crear una caja especial para ustedes donde pueden guardar todo lo que consideren valioso. Pueden decorar su caja de la forma que deseen."

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que este taller es una ventana de tiempo para ustedes. Esto significa que este puede ser un espacio seguro para notar sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que digan o hagan es voluntario. Ofreceré una idea como sugerencia de cómo hacer el taller, les compartiré los materiales que tenemos disponibles y les invitaré a crear, pero no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de hacerlo. No importa cómo se vea. Lo que importa es tomarse este tiempo para honrar verdaderamente sus pensamientos y sentimientos, sin importar cómo surjan. Háganme saber si necesitan algo y sepan que estoy aquí para apoyarles en lo que pueda. Si no se les ocurre qué escribir o crear, siéntanse libres de jugar con los materiales.”
demonstration:
You can take a few minutes to explain the material and basic creation steps. The demonstration will vary depending on the material you are providing. For instance, if you are incorporating collage, you can explain how they can cut out words and images that have meaning to them (if not pre-cut) and glue them in any way they like onto the box. They can collage background images and layer other images on top to create a cool effect, etc.

If you've created a sample, you can pass it around at this time.
demonstration_spanish:
Puede tomar unos minutos para explicar el material y los pasos básicos de creación. La demostración variará dependiendo del material que proporcione. Por ejemplo, si está incorporando un collage, puede explicar cómo pueden recortar palabras e imágenes que tengan significado para ellas o ellos (si aún no están recortadas) y pegarlas de la forma que más les guste en la caja. Pueden hacer un collage de imágenes de fondo y colocar otras imágenes encima para crear un efecto genial, etc.

Si ha creado una muestra, puede pasarla entre las y los participantes en este momento.
opening_circle:
For the opening, you can invite the children to share one thing that they find valuable, and wish to protect. It could be a dream they have, it could be a special relationship, or person in their life, or a found object.

If no one feels comfortable sharing, that's okay. You can either give them examples of things you find valuable, or simply skip to creation.
opening_circle_spanish:
Para la apertura, puede invitar a las niñas y niños a compartir una cosa que encuentren valiosa y que deseen proteger. Podría ser un sueño que tengan, podría ser una relación especial, una persona en su vida, o un objeto encontrado.

Si nadie se siente cómoda o cómodo compartiendo, está bien. Puede darles ejemplos de cosas que consideren valiosas, o simplemente saltar a la creación.

title: Good Parent
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to express what they feel and believe makes a good parent, through the process of creating a "parent" template decorated with helpful and inspiring tips and messages.
materials:
• Large construction paper (variety of colors)

  • Markers (Sharpies work great)

  • Glue sticks

  • Scissors

  • Parent template (female and male)
setup:
You may want to print the parent template on heavy construction paper or cardstock, cut out the shapes and invite participants to use them as stencils to outline or use them to decorate their art piece (see Creation).

You may also want to precut pieces of multiple colors construction paper into various shapes such as hearts, squares, stars, etc. (2" - 4" should be enough). Participants will use each one of these pieces to write messages on them.

You can lay out the supplies so that each participant has easy access to all the material.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You can invite the participants to join in a brief relaxation exercise. You can guide those who wish to follow along through deep breathing, focusing on releasing tension from the body and clutter from the mind.

In between each breath, you can encourage participants to notice their vision for a better life. You can invite them to notice what they're proud of as parents, what their goals are, etc.

Feel free to adapt the relaxation however it best suits your group.
creation:
Adding cut-out shapes to drawing
 
 
  Example of Good Parent messages
 
  Completed Good Parent creation

You can now invite those who wish to create to the three-step creation process. You may wish to remind participants that this is their window of time and they have complete freedom to observe, or use the material to create something else. It's entirely up to them.


Step 1:
Participants can choose any color construction paper and either use the stencil or hand-draw themselves on it. If they like, they can write: "A Good Parent Is..." somewhere along the edge of the paper.

They can use any and as many color(s) marker they like and decorate the "parent" template in any manner they like. They can add hair, glasses, decorate the clothing, etc.


Step 2:
Next, participants can write down the qualities that describe a good parent on the small pieces of paper (if pre-cut). They can be messages and/or tips to themselves, their goals as a parent, or tips to inspire others. Whatever they wish to write will be perfect.

If you've not pre-cut the shapes, you can invite the participants to cut them as they like, keeping in mind that can add significant time to your workshop.


Step 3:
Lastly, participants can glue the messages and helpful parenting tips anywhere on the paper they like.
closing:
You can invite volunteers to share their Good Parent creations, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during the workshop, or anything else they may wish to share.

Of course, this is optional, and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
description: This workshop gives women the opportunity to express what they feel and believe is a "good mother." The goal is for each woman to see themselves in their creation and help inspire themselves and others to become a better parent.
notes:
Group creation

You can also facilitate this as a group creation workshop. To do that, you can draw a large template of a person on a large poster board and invite participants to write their messages on the small pieces of paper and use them to decorate the poster board as a group instead of individually.
introduction:
Good Parent creation
 

"Today, we will have an opportunity to discuss parenting and what it means to be a good parent, and create a symbolic "parent" decorated with inspiring and helpful messages."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
opening_circle:
You can invite participants to a discussion around parenting, and what being a good parent means to the participants. You can prompt a discussion by asking questions about what our society's ideas and standards of being a parent are like today, compared to the participants' parent's generation. What lessons they learned from how they were raised, good and bad, etc. If applicable, you can also discuss the challenges of being a good parent in a domestic violence shelter.

The idea is to get the participants to reflect on and notice what it means to them to be a good parent. They can think of things they wish they would or wouldn't do, goals they plan on implementing in their parenting style, things they can do to overcome the challenges their specific life circumstances present, etc. If you see the need, you can break the ice by sharing your own personal examples and ideas.

Feel free to cater the discussion however it best suits your specific group's needs.

title: Inside/Outside / Adentro/Afuera
full_name: Karen Akamine of Armory Center for the Arts in Pasadena, Adapted by AWBW Staff
objective: This workshop aims to help participants explore and notice the self that you let people see on the outside and the self that is on the inside or underneath.
materials:
Inside/Outside sample with pocket holder

  • Colored construction paper

  • Paper

  • Writing Utensil

  • Cray-Pas

  • Colored pencils
setup:
Table Setup

We recommend that you prepare the supplies and set up in advance to help things go smoothly. You may want to create an example of the final creation as well as different types of folds (see figures below) with construction paper.
warm_up:
"To help us get ready to create, I invite you to begin with a journaling exercise. You can choose a piece of paper and fold it in half, long ways, dividing it into two columns. 

On one side, you can write 'Inside' and on the other side, you can write 'Outside'. You can choose to write on either side of the paper, the top and bottom, in a circle and around it, or whatever way you choose to represent "inside" and "outside."

  • Inside: On the "inside" section of the paper, you can write words or phrases that describe how you feel and/or look on the inside. How would you describe or tell about the 'you' that you or only a few people may know about?

  • Outside: On the "outside" part of the paper, you can write words or phrases that describe how you feel and/or look on the outside. How would you describe or tell about the 'you' that you show to the world?

I encourage you to allow the words to flow naturally without judgment. If you get stuck in one column, try moving on to the next and return to the first one later. Remember there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. Just follow what feels best for you at this moment in time."
creation:
“Now I invite those of you who would like to create, to go ahead and create the 'inside' and 'outside' you using CrayPas and colored pencils." 

As the participants create, you can remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create their artwork. The only important thing is that they keep noticing and honoring their own needs, thoughts, and feelings. Feel free to offer assistance if needed and it may be helpful to provide time reminders for the participants in order to avoid them from feeling rushed towards the end.
closing:
Give each participant an opportunity to share their creation and how it felt to create it. You can also ask how they plan to take care of themselves, inside and outside.

Validate their courage for opening themselves up to their own creativity and respecting whatever came out.
description: To explore and notice the self that you let people see on the outside and the self that is on the inside or underneath.
objective_spanish: Explorar y conocer la persona que dejas que los demás conozcan, y la persona que llevas dentro o debajo.
materials_spanish:
• Muestra interior/exterior con soporte de bolsillo
    Papel de construcción de colores
  • Papel
  • Utensilio de escritura
  • Cray-Pas
  • Lápices de colores
setup_spanish: Le recomendamos que prepare los materiales están preparados antes del taller. Es posible que desee crear un ejemplo de la creación final, y intenta varias maneras de doblar el papel, para mostrar a los participantes (puedes ver las figuras a continuación).
warm_up_spanish:
"Para ayudarnos a prepararnos para crear, lo invito a comenzar con un ejercicio de diario. Puede elegir una hoja de papel y doblarla por la mitad, a lo largo, dividiéndola en dos columnas.

En un lado, puede escribir 'Interior' y en el otro lado, puede escribir 'Exterior'. Puede elegir escribir en cualquiera de los lados del papel, arriba y abajo, en un círculo y alrededor, o de cualquier forma que elija para representar "adentro" y "afuera".

  • Adentro: En la sección "adentro" del papel, puede escribir palabras o frases que describan cómo se siente o se ve por dentro. ¿Cómo describiría o hablaría sobre el 'usted' que usted o solo unas pocas personas pueden conocer?

  • Afuera: en la parte "afuera" del papel, puede escribir palabras o frases que describan cómo se siente y/o se ve por fuera. ¿Cómo describirías o contarías sobre el 'tú' que muestras al mundo?

Te animo a que permitas que las palabras fluyan naturalmente sin juzgar. Si te quedas atascado en una columna, intenta pasar a la siguiente y vuelve a la primera más tarde. Recuerda que no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de participar o crear. Solo sigue lo que te parezca mejor en este momento".
creation_spanish:
"Ahora invito a aquellos de ustedes a quienes les gustaría crear, a seguir adelante y crear el 'adentro' y el 'afuera' de ustedes usando CrayPas y lápices de colores".

Mientras los participantes crean, puede recordarles que no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de crear su obra de arte. Lo único importante es que sigan notando y honrando sus propias necesidades, pensamientos y sentimientos. Siéntase libre de ofrecer ayuda si es necesario y puede ser útil brindar recordatorios de tiempo a los participantes para evitar que se sientan apurados hacia el final.
closing_spanish:
Dé a cada participante la oportunidad de compartir su creación y cómo se sintió al crearla. También puede preguntar cómo planean cuidar de sí mismos, por dentro y por fuera.

Validar su valentía por abrirse a su propia creatividad y respetar lo que surja.
optional_materials:
You may also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Inside/Outside Worksheet (English)

  • Inside/Outside Worksheet (Spanish)

  • If this workshop is done with a single participant this Independent Project Handout can be used.

   
Inside/Outside Worksheet    Inside/Outside Worksheet   Independent Project Handout
(English)   (Spanish)
optional_materials_spanish:
También puede facilitar este taller utilizando hojas de trabajo imprimibles. Si está utilizando las hojas de trabajo en lugar de los materiales regulares del taller, asegúrese de enviar una copia digital o imprímala para sus participantes si se reúne en persona.

  • Inside/Outside Worksheet
  • Si este taller se realiza con un solo participante, se puede utilizar este Independent Project Handout

 

 
Inside/Outside Worksheet   Independent Project Handout
introduction:
When possible, try to individually welcome each participant and let them know you are glad they are there. One-on-one contact can help them get connected and feel safe and comfortable enough to truly use their windows time for themselves.

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, needs and feelings. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some instructions, but you get to choose how you want to create and participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you get to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please ask for what you need. Any questions before we begin?"
introduction_spanish:
Cuando sea posible, trate de dar la bienvenida individualmente a cada participante y hágales saber que está contento de que estén allí. El contacto uno a uno puede ayudarlos a conectarse y sentirse lo suficientemente seguros y cómodos como para realmente usar su tiempo de ventanas para ellos mismos.

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepas que esta es tu ventana de tiempo. Esto significa que este es un espacio seguro para notar tus pensamientos, necesidades y sentimientos. Durante este tiempo, no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de participar o crear". . Voy a compartir algunas instrucciones, pero puedes elegir cómo quieres crear y participar. Puedes seguir las instrucciones completamente, o puedes querer hacer algo diferente, depende completamente de ti. Durante tu ventana de tiempo, puedes elegir. Estoy aquí para apoyarte en todo lo que pueda, así que pregunta lo que necesites. ¿Alguna pregunta antes de comenzar?"
demonstration:
During this time you may go over the art supplies and the creation steps with the participants. You may also show the participants a sample of the creation.  

1. Participants will first pick a piece of construction paper and fold it so it has an inside and an outside. Feel free to get creative with your folds and show your expression through unique folds (refer to the different folding options below).

     


2. Next you may begin to create the outside of your paper as you think about colors, shapes and textures that might describe you on the outside. You can always refer back to your journaling. Are you bright or dark, sharp or soft, foggy or clear?

3. When you are ready, open up your paper and begin to think about how you are on the inside. Are you bright or dark, soft or rough? Are you one or many colors? 

4. With the Cray-Pas and colored pencils, use shapes and colors to draw how you are on the 'outside' and 'inside'. 

5. When you are finished, take some time to write any words that go with your drawing. 

Note: Welcome participants to start on any part of their creation as desired. Some participants might find it easier to start on a specific part of their creation first. As you notice participants finishing up, encourage them to think about how they might want to take care of themselves, inside and outside. What are some of the things they can do?
demonstration_spanish:
Durante este tiempo, puede repasar los materiales de arte y los pasos de creación con los participantes. También puede mostrar a los participantes una muestra de la creación.

1. Los participantes primero elegirán un pedazo de papel de construcción y lo doblarán para que tenga un interior y un exterior. Siéntase libre de ser creativo con sus doblados y muestre su expresión únicos (consulte las diferentes opciones de doblar a continuación).

 

     

 

2. A continuación, puede comenzar a crear el exterior de su papel mientras piensa en colores, formas y texturas que podrían describirlo en el exterior. Siempre puede consultar su diario. ¿Eres brillante u oscuro, nítido o suave, brumoso o claro?

3. Cuando estés listo, abre tu papel y comienza a pensar en cómo eres por dentro. ¿Eres brillante u oscuro, suave o áspero? ¿Eres de uno o de muchos colores?

4. Con los Cray-Pas y lápices de colores, usa formas y colores para dibujar cómo eres por 'afuera' y 'adentro'.

5. Cuando termines, tómate un tiempo para escribir cualquier palabra que vaya con tu dibujo.

Nota: Dé la bienvenida a los participantes para que comiencen con cualquier parte de su creación según lo deseen. A algunos participantes les puede resultar más fácil comenzar primero con una parte específica de su creación. A medida que observe que los participantes terminan, anímelos a pensar en cómo les gustaría cuidar de sí mismos, por dentro y por fuera. ¿Cuáles son algunas de las cosas que pueden hacer?
opening_circle:
"The workshop we are doing today is called Inside/Outside. title: Story Trees
objective: To give children an opportunity to explore their strength and growth, using the tree as a symbol of life and courage. Participants are free to play and allow their imagination to run wild as they discover what kind of tree they want to be.
materials:
•    
      Sample material set-up

    Scratch paper for writing or pre-sketching

  • Pens

  • Pencils

  • Markers

  • CrayPas

  • Paint  (Acrylic or BioColors)

  • Card stock paper or white construction paper

  • Paintbrushes

  • Sample photos of trees
setup:
Sample set up

You may consider hanging some of the following questions around the room to get the children thinking about their tree. You can write these on poster boards or chalk boards. You may also use these questions as prompts while children are creating. You have complete freedom to adapt or alter any element of this workshop to suit your group's needs.
 

  • If you were a tree, what would you be? 

  • If you were a tree, would you be tall or small? 

  • If you were a tree, would you have colorful fruits? 

  • If you were a tree, would you have big roots? 

  • If you were a tree, would you be smiling in the sun? Would you be having fun? 

  • If you were a tree, would you have a swing to play? Would your tree have something

  • If you were a tree, would you have something special to say?
warm_up:
You an invite the children to stand up, take a deep breath and stretch their "tree limbs" way up to the sky as they reach higher and higher. You may encourage them to spread all their fingers as far as they can and take another deep breath in, and out, as they shake their "leaves" and flutter in the breeze. Children can then walk around the room as trees that sway and stretch as they move.

You may wish to remind them that participation is optional and if they don't feel comfortable participating, it's perfectly okay.
creation:
Story Tree created with color pencil

You can now invite those who wish to participate to begin creating the tree they think they would be. If you see fit, you may wish to re-prompt them to think about what kind of tree they would be and what story their tree would tell if it could talk.

"I'd like to encourage you to think about what helps your tree grow, what your trunk looks like, what kind of leaves do you have, what is growing from your tree... is it fruit or maybe flowers? Try to picture the tree in your mind and when you're ready, paint it or draw it on the paper."

You may consider encouraging the children to use any and as much of the material they like, and create their tree however they wish. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is the process. There is no right or wrong way to create.
closing:
For the closing, you may give the children an opportunity to share their amazing Story Trees and anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

If they do not feel comfortable sharing out loud, you can also invite the children to journal their reflections using the Story Tree Reflections questions.
description: The Story Tree workshop gives children an opportunity to explore their strength and growth. Using the tree as a symbol of life and courage, participants are free to play and let their imaginations run wild as they discover what kind of tree they want to be.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Story Tree (English)

  • Story Tree (Spanish)

  • Story Tree Reflections questions

  • Feathers

  • Glitter

  • Foam Shapes

       
Story Tree (English)     Story Tree (Spanish)
introduction:
"Did you know there are over 20,000 types of trees growing around the world and that they live anywhere from a few years to thousands of years, but they never stop growing? Most trees are strong and have deep sturdy roots. Trees can give shelter and protection with the shade they provide. They also nourish us with the fruits they grow. Notice how trees look different in the summer from what they look like in the winter and even though many trees live through extremely cold winters and very hot summers they still grow stronger and bigger each year. Today you will have an opportunity to create a painting of yourself as a tree."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
opening_circle:
Story Tree created with paint and glitter

For the opening, you have the option to invite the children to think about what type of tree they would be. You also have the option to open up the floor for children to share their thoughts if anyone wishes to share, or give them the opportunity to just think about it on their own. If you have sample tree images, you may wish to display them. 

"If you were a tree, would you be palm tree on a deserted island, a fruit tree in a farm, a big strong tree that others could climb or maybe a pine tree in a forest? Maybe your tree is an imaginary tree where hearts or candy come from?"

"If you were a tree what kind of a tree would you be, and why?"

title: Story Trees
objective: This workshop provides participants a creative opportunity to explore, uncover and express their stories of change and growth, using the tree as a symbol of life and strength.
materials:
• Sample material set-up

    Scratch paper or journal

  • Heavy white cardstock

  • Basic writing/coloring utensils of choice

 

Please feel free to use some or all of the suggested materials. This workshop works well with simple materials or mixed-media. It can be done with any size paper.
setup:
Sample inspiration question posted

You may consider hanging some or all of the following inspirational questions around the room to get the participants thinking about their tree. This can also be a great reference for participants during the creation process. You can write these on poster boards or chalk boards. You may also print these questions in advance and hand them out to participants. These questions are some suggested prompts to inspire participants to think about how they wish to go about creating their trees. You have complete freedom to adapt or alter any element of this workshop to suit your group's needs.
 

  • What kind of tree are you, or what kind of tree do you want to be?

  • What nurtures your tree?

  • How does your tree adapt to changes?

  • What kind of seeds is your tree holding?

  • Who or what provides your tree with light, water, nutrients, and caring?

  • How would you describe the fruit you offer?

  • Where do your roots extend?

  • Where or what is the core of your tree?

  • What is your tree made of?

  • What is your trees story?

  • What kind of transformations has your tree gone or will go through?

  • How does your tree find strength?

  • What is the texture of your roots, trunk, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits?

  • What colors fill the individual shapes of your trees?

  • Does your tree talk? What does it tell you?
warm_up:
Sample Story Tree  

You also have the option to do a brief warm-up or relaxation exercise before participants begin creating. You may also incorporate your own exercise if you see fit.


"For those who wish to participate, try to get comfortable, take off your shoes if you like, or keep them on. You can close your eyes, or keep them open. However you feel comfortable. See if you can feel your feet touching the floor. Breathe in and as you release your breath, try to spread out your toes. Feel that your toes are breathing and expanding onto the floor like roots reaching down, grounding you. Try to focus all your attention on your feet and allow them to sense the floor as if they were your hands. Continue to breathe deeper and deeper, and try to feel your breath reaching your feet. As you breathe out, I'd like to encourage you to imagine that your toes are releasing all tension in your body, letting it flow down into the floor, into the earth as you continue to breathe and relax. Remember, that our feet have traveled far and need some loving too. Repeat the breathing and expanding your toes as many times as you feel necessary."
creation:
Sample Story Tree in watercolor

"Before we begin to create, I'd like to invite you take a little time to sketch. For those of you who wish to participate, I'd like to encourage you to try, without much thinking, to play with your materials, then begin sketching whatever comes to your mind. This is an optional warm-up exercise to allow you to have a stream of consciousness. You could sketch shapes, colors, symbols, words, or even trees. Whatever comes to your mind will work. You are free to use scratch paper with the different kinds of paints or drawing materials. It doesn't matter if the lines, colors or shapes don't 'look' like anything at all. These initial images are meant to allow you to explore the ideas and colors that come to your mind, so I encourage you to feel free to use the material in any way you wish and allow your sketches to flow naturally."

You have the option to read the following story to the participants as they're sketching. It's meant to inspire participants and facilitate a focused atmosphere. Or, you may wish to read this before sketching or during the actual creation step, or not read it at all. It's entirely up to you.


"In the uncertainty of a thunderstorm, I feel the rain falling over my head.
I see a young person standing in a puddle of water.
Something draws me to this person and makes me want to protect them.
I notice a lightning approaching them in slow motion.
I extend my arms and push this person to the side.
I fall on the water and become this young person.
I know the lightning will reach me soon.
I try to stand, but I can’t.
Unexpectedly, I see a hand.
A tree extends its arm and draws me close to its trunk.
With one arm it picks me up, with the other it takes in the full force of the lightning.
As the tree holds me close to its core, I feel the urge to caress its contours.
I can perceive its texture and the energy that flows within its being.
All my senses are awakened.
My arms feel the intensity of the tree as it battles the lightning.
My body connects to it deeply.
The feeling is so vivid.
At that moment I realize that the young person, the tree and I are only one being.
I am the tree that rescues me."

   
  Sample Story Tree sketch

Once participants have had a chance to sketch and connect with images in their minds, you may then invite them to begin creating their Story Tree.

"Just like trees, we gather nutrients from our environment but also must withstand different seasons and their unpredictability. For those of you who wish to participate, I'd like to encourage you to try to notice how your personal story relates to this process. Think about what your tree would like to tell you or tell others and begin to sketch what comes to mind. You are welcome to use these sketches as part of your artwork, or to take a moment to reflect. Maybe during the warm up exercise you were surprised by certain images or feelings. Feel free to allow yourself to be present in your thoughts and honor what you are feeling. Whether you draw a single seed in a field or a 4,000 year old oak, let your tree come to life as you envision your own possibilities. Feel free to allow your hands be free as you continue to create. Remember, it doesn't matter what it looks like, or even if it looks like a tree. What matters is the process of you noticing, honoring and expressing your journey and your feelings."

Feel free to give participants as much time as you see fit to complete their Story Trees.
closing:
As the workshop comes to an end, you can invite the participant to acknowledge the different feelings and thoughts that were present throughout the creative process. You may wish to give the participants an opportunity to share their amazing Story Trees and anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

If they do not feel comfortable sharing out loud, you can also invite them to journal their reflections using the Story Tree Reflections questions.

title: Our Safe Home
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to explore what a safe home means to them and what elements go inside and around it to make it feel safe through the creation of a "safe home" book.
materials:
•  
    Our Safe Home material and sample set-up  

    Construction paper

  • Markers

  • Pens

  • White Elmer's Glue

  • Glue sticks

  • Glitter glue

  • Puffy paint

  • Assorted ribbon, yarn, pipe cleaners (either or all of these work for binding)

  • Assorted flowers

  • Foam shapes

  • Scissors

  • Hole punchers
setup:
Depending on your time constraints, you can save time by cutting out the house templates and even writing the questions on them (see creation) beforehand. Ideally, however, the participants would do this as it's part of the creation process. This is up to you.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance for participants to see what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Once participants have had a chance to reflect on their thoughts about what a happy and safe home means to them, you can then invite them to create. You can share the following creation steps with them and pass around your sample at this time and invite them to create. You may also choose to create along with them. Whatever works best for you and your group.

      
  Step 2: Cutting the folded lines

 

Step 1: Creating the House Template
"You can begin by folding a sheet of construction paper, length-wise, in half. You can use any color paper you like. You get to create six of these, each acting as a page for your "safe home" book. You can use same color for all pages, or different colors. It's entirely up to you. Once you have folded the paper in half vertically, you can fold two corners over to the centerfold and cut along these corner fold lines. Now, you have a template to create the rest of the pages in your safe home book."


Step 2: Cutting Out All the Pages
"You can use the template you just created to trace and cut 5 more home shapes, or pages for your book. Again, you are free to use any color paper you like for each of your pages."
 

      
  Step 3: Writing Safe Home Questions

Step 3: Writing the Safe Home Questions
"Next, you may write down the following questions, one on each page, at the top of each house shape and leave one house page blank. The blank page will be the front of your book, it can be the house you get to decorate shortly. Take as much time as you need to reflect on these questions and write them down. Remember, there are no right or wrong answers. Only what is right for you."

(You can write these questions on a board for everyone to see, and invite them to write them, or you can read them to the participants. Ideally, this is the step participants spend the most time on).

  • "Page 1 - Leave blank to decorate later."

  • "Page 2 - What does a safe home look like?"

  • "Page 3 - What does a safe home feel like?"

  • "Page 4 - What does a safe home sound like?"

  • "Page 5 - How do we treat each other inside our home?"

  • "Page 6 - How are we going to work together to create our Safe Home?"
     

      
  Step 4: Binding the pages

Step 4: Binding the Pages
"When you have your pages written out, you can align these pages with one another and punch holes along the left-hand side. Remember to put your blank page at the front as the cover of your book. Once you've done that, you can lace a ribbon, yarn, pipe cleaner (or any other binding material you've provided) through the holes and tie them to create binding. If you prefer, you can simply staple the pages papers together. It's entirely up to you."


Step 5: Decorating the Cover
"Next, you get a chance to decorate your cover page. If you choose to do so, I'd like to encourage you to have fun. You can use any shapes, images, words, symbols, and design materials that you imagine your safe home to have on the outside. I'd like to remind you that it doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is that you've taken this time to honor your thoughts and feelings."
closing:
Our beautiful Safe Home!  

For the closing, you may give the participants an opportunity to share their creations and some of the ways they can make their home safe. They can also share anything they felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

If you're working with families, you may wish to remind them that if they work together, they can create this safe home in the future. You can also thank participants for being here today.
description: Participants will be provided with an opportunity to discuss the meaning of a safe home and what goes inside and around it to make it feel that way. They will be invited to make specific commitments to creating that safety in their own homes.
notes: You might consider calling this workshop "Happy Home" if you feel this will allow the children and/or families to focus in that way. It's entirely up to you.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Large pieces of felt

Safe Home Worksheet (English)     Safe Home Worksheet (Spanish)
introduction:
"Today, you will have an opportunity to think about what safety and a safe home mean to you, and then create a book that represents your ideal safe home, and you'll get to decorate it however way you like. You'll also get a chance to make specific commitments and decisions about how to create that safe and happy home for yourself."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
opening_circle:
You can invite the participants to a discussion if anyone wishes to participate, or you can just present them with the following prompt questions and invite them to reflect on them.

"To get started I'd like to invite you to think about what having a safe home might mean."

"For those of you who wish to participate, think about what a safe home looks like to you. Maybe it is full of pictures from the good and happy times? Maybe it is full of smiling faces? Maybe it is full of people or it just has the people you want there? Maybe it's just you there."

"What does a safe home feel like? Maybe it is a place you are happy to return to at the end of the day. Maybe it is warm and cozy. Maybe you can freely share your feelings, hopes and dreams there. Maybe it is a place where you feel happy, loved, and relaxed."

"What does a safe home sound like? Maybe there are no loud voices or bad words. Maybe people are happy and laughing. Maybe it is quiet and peaceful or maybe music is playing and everyone is singing."

"Something else to ask yourself is, how do you want to be treated and treat others in your home? How can your family work together to make it a safe home? Remember, there are no right or wrong answers. Whatever comes to your mind as you reflect on these questions is just right."

title: Native American Mistake Wheels
objective: This workshop implements a Native American tradition which aims to help participants think about "mistakes" and how they can learn and grow from them, through the creation of a Mistake Wheel.
materials:
• Native American Wheels handout

  • Solid colored fabrics (preferably canvas, muslin or suede-like materials)

  • Yarn (or ribbons or suede laces)

  • Feathers (various colors)

  • Beads

  • Round hoops or rings (embroidery hoops and or heavy cardboard rounds work just as well)

  • Hole punchers

  • Scissors

  • Pens (and/or puffy paints)

  • Markers (various colors; extra fine tips work well)

  • A circular object (smaller than the embroidery hoop)*

  • Rulers

 

* Depending on the size of the rings or embroidery hoop you provide, you can provide a smaller sized ring or circular objects which participants can use to trace the inner circle onto the center.
setup:
You can lay out the supplies (beads, markers, fabrics, feathers, etc.) so that each participant has easy access to them.

You may want to print a copy of the Native American Wheels handout for each participant, or you can write it on a board.

In spirit of the Native American tradition, you may want to keep some of the decorative art supplies in an assortment of natural colors.

You may also want to cut out the fabric, or whatever material you are providing in advance, 1 per participant. The size of the fabric should be slightly larger than the circumference of the embroidery hoop you are providing, so that the edges can be hole punched and wrapped around the ring to secure it. If you like, you can also punch holes around the edges of the fabric in advance, as evenly spaced apart as possible.

It may be helpful to create a sample mistake wheel in advance to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simply sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
Feel free to use our suggested relaxation exercise, or your own. We have found that guided relaxations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.


"I now invite you to join me in a brief relaxation exercise. You can follow along, or if you prefer, you can simply observe."

"For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get yourself in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. However you are most comfortable."

"Now begin to take a few deep breaths (you can guide them to breathe in for a count of 5 seconds, hold it for 3 and exhale for 7 seconds)... As you breathe, I'd like you to try to notice any tense parts in your body and visualize your breath going to those areas."

"With each breath in, imagine cool, soothing, healing air going into the tense areas of your body, and releasing all that tension with each breath out..."

"Continue to breathe slowly, cleansing your body, soul and spirit from any tension, stress, or judgment..."

"As you continue to relax, notice that just as all Native American wheels are sacred, the work that you will be doing for themselves today is sacred as well..."

"When you are ready, you can come back to this moment, and begin creating your mistake wheel."
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create to begin doing so. It may be helpful to use a timer for each portion of the creation section. Feel free to allocate as much time as you see fit for each section.
 

    
  The North section
 
 
  The East section
 
 
  The South section
 
 
  The West section
 
 
  Center circle with lines to section off North, East, South, West

Step 1: Selecting the Fabric
To begin, participants can pick out the embroidery hoop (or ring) and/or the fabric to be the foundation of their wheel.


Step 2: The Foundation
Next, they can wrap the fabric around the embroidery hoop, punch holes around the edges of the fabric as evenly spaced apart as possible, then fastening the fabric onto the hoop by threading pieces of lace, ribbon or yarn and tying them tightly.


Step 3: The Template
Once you have the foundation of the mistake wheel in place, you can then use a smaller ring (than the embroider hoop), and trace a circle onto the center of the wheel. Then, you can use a ruler to draw 4 lines extending out from the center ring toward the edge of the wheel to section off "North, South, East and West."


Step 4: The North Section
Now that the center ring and the quadrants are drawn, you can invite participants to begin decorating the "North" section of the wheel. You can invite participants to refer to the handout, if you see fit.

In the North section of the wheel, the message reads: "Learning from our own mistakes"

You can invite participants to share as a group, or in pairs what they have learned from their own mistakes for about 2 minutes each. Or, you may generate a larger timed discussion on this with the group as a whole. Feel free to do whichever you think may be more appropriate for your group.

After they have discussed, you can give participants about 10-15 minutes to decorate the North part of their wheel with words and images that have to do with this message; they can even write the very message itself in this section. You may want to remind them that they are free to use colors, shapes, symbols or words to decorate their wheels any way that has meaning to them. There is no right or wrong way to create.


Step 5: The East Section
In the East section, the message reads: "Learning from the mistakes of our teachers"

Again, you can invite participants to discuss, in any manner you see fit, what 'learning from the mistakes of our teachers' means to them, then take 10-15 minutes to decorate the East section of their wheel to represent their thoughts and feelings about it.


Step 6: The South Section
In the South section, the message reads: "Being willing to make as many mistakes as it takes"

You can repeat previous step and invite participants to decorate the South section of their wheel.


Step 7: The West Section
In the West section, the message reads: "Learning from the mistakes of others"

You can repeat previous step and invite participants to decorate the West section of their wheel.


Step 8: The Center Ring
The Center of the ring represents the essence of the teaching, and the message reads: "Learning that there is no such thing as a mistake"

You can repeat previous step and invite participants to decorate the Center ring however they like.


Step 9: Finishing Touches
Finally, you can invite participants to add finishing touches such as beads, feathers, or any other decorative supplies available to their wheels, if they wish to do so.
closing:
You can give participants a chance to share their art piece with the group, anything they learned, felt or experienced during the creation process, or anything else they may wish to share. Of course, this is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

You can share with them that if we open ourselves to the possibilities that all that we encounter, good and bad, are opportunities for joy and learning, and we can make all circumstances useful and fruitful. What we have experienced and what we have learned from our so called "mistakes" can become this wise medicine that we have to share. This wheel can become a reminder of this for them.
description: Teaching everything in terms of circles or wheels is a Native American spiritual tradition. The "mistake wheel" is a new perspective on the medicine wheel and shares the keys to self-acceptance and acceptance of the universe. The five sections of the disk hold five messages about "mistakes," leading us to reflect on what we can learn from them and how we can accept them.
optional_materials: • Timer
introduction:
Mistake Wheel creation with yarn and feather decorations

"Today we'll have an opportunity to explore the concept of mistakes and self-acceptance. Teaching everything in terms of circles or wheels is a Native American spiritual tradition. The 'mistake wheel' shares the keys to self-acceptance and acceptance of the universe. The five sections of the disk, or wheel, hold five messages about 'mistakes,' which allow us to reflect on what we can learn from them and how we can accept them as part of our growth."

"You will get a chance to create a Native American Mistake Wheel, with the goal of learning a different perspective regarding mistakes. Your art piece can serve as a reminder that you can perceive all circumstances and mistakes fruitfully and as part of your natural learning process and growth."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."

If you see fit, you can briefly discuss each of the meanings of each of the messages.

title: Native American Mistake Wheels
objective: This workshop implements a Native American tradition which aims to help children think about "mistakes" and how they can learn and grow from them, through the creation of a Mistake Wheel.
materials:
• Native American Wheels handout

  • Solid colored fabrics (preferably canvas, muslin or suede-like materials)

  • Yarn (or ribbons or suede laces)

  • Feathers (various colors)

  • Beads

  • Round hoops or rings (embroidery hoops and or heavy cardboard rounds work just as well)

  • Hole punchers

  • Scissors

  • Pens (and/or puffy paints)

  • Markers (various colors; extra fine tips work well)

  • A circular object (smaller than the embroidery hoop)*

  • Rulers

 

* Depending on the size of the rings or embroidery hoop you provide, you can provide a smaller sized ring or circular objects which children can use to trace the inner circle onto the center.
setup:
You can lay out the supplies (beads, markers, fabrics, feathers, etc.) so that each participant has easy access to them.

You may want to print a copy of the Native American Wheels handout for each participant, or you can write it on a board.

In spirit of the Native American tradition, you may want to keep some of the decorative art supplies in an assortment of natural colors.

You may also want to cut out the fabric, or whatever material you are providing in advance, 1 per participant. The size of the fabric should be slightly larger than the circumference of the embroidery hoop you are providing, so that the edges can be hole punched and wrapped around the ring to secure it. If you like, you can also punch holes around the edges of the fabric in advance, as evenly spaced apart as possible.

It may be helpful to create a sample mistake wheel in advance to show the children what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simply sample so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
Feel free to use our suggested relaxation exercise, or your own. We have found that guided relaxations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.


"I now invite you to join me in a brief relaxation exercise. You can follow along, or if you prefer, you can simply observe."

"For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get yourself in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. However you are most comfortable."

"Now begin to take a few deep breaths (you can guide them to breathe in for a count of 5 seconds, hold it for 3 and exhale for 7 seconds)... As you breathe, I'd like you to try to notice any tense parts in your body and visualize your breath going to those areas."

"With each breath in, imagine cool, soothing, healing air going into the tense areas of your body, and releasing all that tension with each breath out..."

"Continue to breathe slowly, cleansing your body, soul and spirit from any tension, stress, or judgment..."

"As you continue to relax, notice that just as all Native American wheels are sacred, the work that you will be doing for themselves today is sacred as well..."

"When you are ready, you can come back to this moment, and begin creating your mistake wheel."
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create to begin doing so. It may be helpful to use a timer for each portion of the creation section. Feel free to allocate as much time as you see fit for each section.

Some children may need help with certain elements of creation, such as looping the yarn, securing the fabric, and writing. Feel free to offer your assistance where you see the need.
 

    
  The North section
 
 
  The East section
 
 
  The South section
 
 
  The West section
 
 
  Center circle with lines to section off North, East, South, West

Step 1: Selecting the Fabric
To begin, children can pick out the embroidery hoop (or ring) and/or the fabric to be the foundation of their wheel.


Step 2: The Foundation
Next, they can wrap the fabric around the embroidery hoop, punch holes around the edges of the fabric as evenly spaced apart as possible, then fastening the fabric onto the hoop by threading pieces of lace, ribbon or yarn and tying them tightly.


Step 3: The Template
Once you have the foundation of the mistake wheel in place, you can then use a smaller ring (than the embroider hoop), and trace a circle onto the center of the wheel. Then, you can use a ruler to draw 4 lines extending out from the center ring toward the edge of the wheel to section off "North, South, East and West."


Step 4: The North Section
Now that the center ring and the quadrants are drawn, you can invite children to begin decorating the "North" section of the wheel. You can invite children to refer to the handout, if you see fit.

In the North section of the wheel, the message reads: "Learning from our own mistakes"

You can invite children to share as a group, or in pairs what they have learned from their own mistakes for about 2 minutes each. Or, you may generate a larger timed discussion on this with the group as a whole. Feel free to do whichever you think may be more appropriate for your group.

After they have discussed, you can give children about 10-15 minutes to decorate the North part of their wheel with words and images that have to do with this message; they can even write the very message itself in this section. You may want to remind them that they are free to use colors, shapes, symbols or words to decorate their wheels any way that has meaning to them. There is no right or wrong way to create.


Step 5: The East Section
In the East section, the message reads: "Learning from the mistakes of our teachers"

Again, you can invite children to discuss, in any manner you see fit, what 'learning from the mistakes of our teachers' means to them, then take 10-15 minutes to decorate the East section of their wheel to represent their thoughts and feelings about it.


Step 6: The South Section
In the South section, the message reads: "Being willing to make as many mistakes as it takes"

You can repeat previous step and invite children to decorate the South section of their wheel.


Step 7: The West Section
In the West section, the message reads: "Learning from the mistakes of others"

You can repeat previous step and invite children to decorate the West section of their wheel.


Step 8: The Center Ring
The Center of the ring represents the essence of the teaching, and the message reads: "Learning that there is no such thing as a mistake"

You can repeat previous step and invite children to decorate the Center ring however they like.


Step 9: Finishing Touches
Finally, you can invite children to add finishing touches such as beads, feathers, or any other decorative supplies available to their wheels, if they wish to do so.
closing:
You can give children a chance to share their art piece with the group, anything they learned, felt or experienced during the creation process, or anything else they may wish to share. Of course, this is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

You can share with them that if we open ourselves to the possibilities that all that we encounter, good and bad, are opportunities for joy and learning, and we can make all circumstances useful and fruitful. What we have experienced and what we have learned from our so called "mistakes" can become this wise medicine that we have to share. This wheel can become a reminder of this for them.
