What do you want to keep just for yourself? Now using your Scratch Art Board reveal your relationship boundaries. Scratch words, shapes, symbols or even pictures onto your Scratch Art Board to represent what you will and will not allow in your relationship to maintain healthy boundaries.  

Share examples such as:
-Write the name of a friend or family member to remind you not to lose touch with people who are close to you (other than your partner).
-Draw a mouth to remind you to be open, and honest, and that you have a voice and the right to speak up for yourself.
-Draw two shapes that are the same size to symbolize how you and your partner are equal and have mutual respect for one another.

Keep in mind that what you create doesn't have to make sense to anyone but you. Try not to censor yourself when you create; your project should serve as a reminder of what you want in your intimate/dating relationships. If you are open and honest with yourself about what you want and don't want in your relationship, you will be able to talk to your partner about it and work together to make it happen!  

 

Closing
Ask each participant to share anything they want about their creation, and what knowledge they will take with them from today. You may also ask participants what steps they will take to implement these boundaries in their current or future relationships, or where they will display or keep their project and why. Thank the participants for jumping into this complex, yet very important topic of relationship boundaries, and encourage them to keep their project as a reminder to make sure they feel safe, comfortable and happy in their relationships.
description: This workshop introduces participants to the concept of boundaries and having healthy levels of independence in their intimate relationships.
tips:
Note About Introducing Embodied Art
Consider sharing with the youth the benefits of moving their bodies in playful and safe ways. By sharing this information with them, you empower them to feel a sense of ownership over their bodies and their expression. For more about embodied art workshops and how to introduce them in your groups, see Introduction to Embodied Art Workshops.

title: Do Enter Door Hanger
objective: To encourage participants to think about what they want in their lives, and where their personal boundaries lie, by creating a scratch art door hanger, which can serve as a reminder of what they wish to allow into their life, home, and heart.
materials:
Set up example
  • Scratch Art materials (can be purchased at Discount School Supply or Oriental Trading Company )
  • Toothpicks, pencils, or any object that can be used to scratch off the black layer of the art board
  • Tablecloth or newspaper (to cover the table as the Scratch Art Boards can be very messy)
  • Paper for journaling
  • Pens (variety of colors)
     
  • You can also find a paper template of the door hangers here.
setup: For most efficient workflow, we suggest having all the materials laid out for each participant beforehand. Please note that the black scrapes that come off the art board when you scratch through are very messy and stain easily, so you may want to lay out newspaper or any other covering on top of the table the participants will use when they create.
warm_up:
The journaling exercise gives participants the opportunity to first look at the thoughts, feelings or experiences they do not want in their lives, and then "flip" them around so they can gain understanding of what they do want, and where their personal boundaries lie. 

As a facilitator, you have the option to create along with your participants as you guide them, or do a demonstration before inviting them to start. It's entirely up to you.

   Participant transforming her journaling into a door hanger

"For those of you who wish to participate, you may begin with a piece of paper and fold it in half vertically."

"On the left column of your paper, I encourage you to make a list using words, pictures or symbols of the things you don't want in your life. If you like, you can write, 'What I Don't Want' at the top left hand side of your paper."  

To alleviate the stress of being perfect and "correct," it may be helpful to remind them from time to time that they don't need to worry about spelling, grammar, and they don't even need to write complete sentences or words. The most important thing is that they have the opportunity and freedom to think freely and focus on their thoughts and feelings.

Once the participants have had the chance to complete their list on the left column, you may then invite them to share what they've written/drawn if they so wish. Of course, as with any part of this workshop, this is optional. 

Next, you can invite them to start on the right column.

"Now, I would like to encourage you to write all the things you do want in your life on the right hand column. You can write 'What I Do Want' at the top if you like."

Once they're done, you may again invite them to share if they wish, or proceed with the creation.

We have found that playing soft, instrumental music in the background can create a safer, more relaxing and focused atmosphere for participants as they do the warm-up exercise. But again, this is entirely up to you. 

We have also found that participants tend to take a little longer creating the second column as it may require deeper level thinking and emotions, so feel free to set your time limits accordingly, if needed.
creation:
Revealing reminders of what we want to enter our  

Before starting, you may invite the participants to cut or tear off the "What I Don't Want" list and crumple it up. You could even walk around the room with a wastebasket or even paper shredder to let them dispose of it. You have the freedom to do this now, after the creation, or incorporate a different method as you see fit. The idea is that the crumbling and discarding of that list can represent the letting go of negative things in their life.

If you choose to incorporate music into your workshop, this may also be a good time to have it playing in the background.

Next, you can invite them to think about what their life will look like and feel like if they don't have any of those negative things they just discarded. Using their scratch-through boards, they may now begin to write down a letter, words, shapes, pictures, doodles or symbols that reflect and remind them of the positive thoughts, feelings, or experiences they do want in their life. You may consider reminding them that this is purely optional and if they choose to participate, they have complete freedom to choose any color, design, word, anything they wish and it will be perfectly okay.
closing:
For the closing, you may give the participants an opportunity to share what they created on their door hanger, or what they discovered during the journaling, what they want to remember and keep in their hearts from today, or whatever else they may wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay. 

You may also wish to close by sharing some encouraging and empowering words with your participants. You may ask them to close their eyes if it feels safe, and wrap their arms as if they're giving themselves a hug, and repeat (in their head or out loud): "I am worthy of having the life I want. Going forward, I will decide what thoughts, feelings and experiences I will invite into my life." 

Again, you have complete freedom to adjust and adapt any part of this workshop as you see fit.
description: This workshop helps participants think about what they want in their lives, and where their personal boundaries lie. The Scratch Art Door Hanger will serve as a reminder of what they expect, and will allow into their life, home, and hearts.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Do Enter Door Hanger Worksheet

  • Soft instrumental music (to create a relaxed atmosphere)

 
Do Enter Door Hanger  
Worksheet
introduction:
"Today, I'd like to invite you to join me in creating a door hanger. What is the purpose of a door hanger? Sometimes door hangers say: 'Do Not Enter,' and allow us to protect our worlds and keep us private. For those who wish to participate, I encourage you to focus on what you want, and the experiences you wish to invite into your life. You all get to decide what your personal boundaries are and how you want to be treated. The scratch art door hanger can serve as a positive reminder that you can control what you invite into your life and what you keep out. It's really saying: 'if you enter here, you will treat me the way I expect to be treated; you will respect my values, my principles and what is important to me.'" 

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. It's a time for you to focus on your thoughts, needs and feelings. During this time, there is no way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

title: Stepping Stones / Sendero de Piedras
objective: This workshop provides participants an opportunity to reflect on what they are leaving in the past, and what they'd like to move towards in their future by creating a personal stepping stone.
materials:
• Super Sculpey
  • Polymer Clay
  • Toaster Oven
  • Sharpie markers (variety of colors; metallic Sharpies work best)
setup:
For the most efficient workshop, you may consider preparing the Sculpey Clay by breaking up the blocks into various colored balls of clay. Ideally, there will be enough clay for each person to make two stones.  

If you only have a short amount of time to do the workshop, you have the option to use real rocks or pre-baked Sculpey rocks.

You may find it useful to write the basic creation steps below on a board or large piece of paper for your participants' reference beforehand, which may cut down on the number of questions they may have during the creation process.

Lastly, you may consider preheating your oven to 275° so you can start baking right away. But how you decide to set up is entirely up to you.
creation:
To start, you can invite each participant to make two rocks, one to represent what they would like to leave behind in life, and the other to represent what they wish to move towards. You may wish to remind them that they have complete freedom to choose any colors, as many colors as they like, and if they wish to not participate and just observe, or do something entirely different, that's perfectly okay too. 

Baking:
Once each participant has had the opportunity to create their stones (still in clay form), you may invite them now to bake them. To start, you can lay out all the rocks on a cookie sheet.

For best results, you can bake the Sculpey clay at 275 degrees. Generally, you need 15 minutes for each 1/4 inch of thickness. If you are baking multiple rocks at a time, you may want to make sure that they are all about the same thickness. For participants who have created ticker or maybe rounder rocks, you can bake those with like-sized ones in a separate batch. 

Once the rocks are baked, we recommend allowing the clay to cool completely before handling it. They will be hot out of the oven!

Writing on the Rocks:
Once all the rocks have cooled down, you may invite the participants to write on them. Again, this is optional. If you wish to incorporate music into your workshop, this may be a good opportunity for it.

"Now I'd like to invite you to relax, and take a moment to consider what you are walking away from. You can close your eyes or keep them open. However you feel comfortable. I'd like to encourage you to think about one thing you'd like to leave behind... it could be stress, worries, self-consciousness, anything you want to let go of. If nothing comes to mind, that is okay too. This is for you, so anything you choose will be perfect. Feel free to take a moment and whenever you are ready, I'd like to invite you to choose your "walk away from" stone and use a Sharpie to write what you came up with on it. You can write a word, a shape or symbol, anything that represents what you'd like to leave behind." 

    
    Finished Stepping Stones  

You have the freedom to set a time limit or not, it's entirely up to you. We have found that participants may take some time to dig deep and think of something that may be painful to them. Please feel free to cater to your group's needs.  

"Now, I want to encourage you to think about something you wish to move towards in life. What would you like to learn? How would you like to grow? What area of you life do you want to see positive change? What would you like to find or discover? Feel free to take a moment to think of a word, shape or symbol to represent what you want to go toward and write it on your remaining stone."
closing:
For the closing, you may give the participants an opportunity to share what they wrote on their stepping stones, anything they learned in the process of creating them, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

You may also wish to thank them for being so creative and for sharing about what they made. You can also encourage them to get rid of the stone that represents their past if they so choose. It can be a healing exercise. If you choose to, you may suggest burying their past stone in a garden, putting it in the trash, or throwing it into the ocean. 

"As you walk through life, you might keep these with you, in your pocket, in your purse. They are yours to carry with you as a reminder of where you are going."
description: Participants write words, shapes, symbols on stones to remind them of what they are walking away from and walking toward in their lives.
objective_spanish: Este taller les brinda a las y los participantes la oportunidad de reflexionar sobre lo que están dejando en el pasado y hacía dónde les gustaría avanzar en su futuro, mediante la creación las piedras de su sendero personal.
materials_spanish:
• Arcilla marca “Super Sculpey”
• Arcilla polimérica (arcilla para hornear)
• Horno tostador
• Marcadores Sharpie (variedad de colores; los Sharpies metálicos funcionan mejor)
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 5 min
Demostración: 10 min
Creación: 60 min
Cierre: 10 min
Total: 1:25 hora
setup_spanish:
Para que el taller sea más eficiente, puede considerar preparar la arcilla “Super Sculpey” dividiéndola en varios bloques de colores. Idealmente, habrá suficiente arcilla para que cada persona haga dos piedras.

Si solo cuenta con un corto período de tiempo para hacer el taller, también tiene la opción de utilizar rocas reales o rocas Sculpey precocidas. Puede que le resulte útil escribir de antemano los pasos creativos básicos (explicados más adelante) en una pizarra o en una hoja grande de papel para la referencia de sus participantes, esto puede reducir la cantidad de preguntas que puedan tener durante el proceso de creación.

Por último, puede considerar precalentar su horno a 275 ° grados para que pueda comenzar a hornear de inmediato. Pero la forma en que decida hacer la preparación del taller depende totalmente de usted.
creation_spanish:
Para comenzar, puede invitar a cada participante a hacer dos rocas, una para representar lo que les gustaría dejar atrás en la vida y la otra para representar a lo que desean avanzar. Tal vez desee recordarles que tienen total libertad para elegir cualquier color, o tantos colores como deseen, y si desean no participar y simplemente observar, o hacer algo completamente diferente, eso también está bien.

Al momento de hornear: Una vez que cada participante haya tenido la oportunidad de crear sus piedras (aún en forma de arcilla), puede invitarles a hornearlas. Para empezar, puede colocar todas las rocas en una bandeja para galletas. Para obtener los mejores resultados, puede hornear la arcilla Sculpey a 275 grados.

En general, se necesita 15 minutos por cada 1/4 de pulgada de grosor. Si está horneando varias piedras a la vez, puede asegurarse de que todas tengan el mismo grosor. Para las y los participantes que han creado piedras más gruesas o quizás piedras más redondas, puede hornearlas con las piedras de tamaños similares en un lote separado.

Una vez que las rocas están cocidas, recomendamos que la arcilla se enfríe completamente antes de manipularla. ¡Saldrán muy calientes del horno! Al momento de escribir en las piedras: Una vez que todas las piedras se hayan enfriado, puede invitar a las y los participantes a escribir sobre ellas.

De nuevo, esto es opcional. Si desea incorporar música en su taller, este momento puede ser una buena oportunidad para ello. "Ahora me gustaría invitarles a relajarse y tomarse un momento para considerar de lo que están decidiendo dejar atrás en su camino.

Pueden cerrar los ojos o mantenerlos abiertos. Lo que les haga sentirse más cómodas o cómodos. Me gustaría hacerles una invitación a que piensen una cosa que les gustaría dejar atrás ... podría ser el estrés, las preocupaciones, o cualquier cosa que quieran dejar atrás.

Si no se les viene nada a la mente, eso también está bien. Esto es para ustedes, así que todo lo que elijan será perfecto. Siéntanse libres de tomar un momento y cuando estén listas y listos, me gustaría invitarles a elegir su piedra que represente lo que están dejando atrás y usar un Sharpie para escribir lo que se les vino a la mente. Pueden escribir una palabra, una forma o símbolo, cualquier cosa que represente lo que les gustaría dejar atrás ".

Usted tiene la libertad de establecer un límite de tiempo para cada paso o simplemente no hacerlo, depende totalmente de usted. Nos hemos dado cuenta que las y los participantes pueden demorar un tiempo en profundizar y pensar en algo que les puede ser doloroso. Por favor siéntase libre de atender las necesidades de su grupo.

"Ahora, quiero animarles a que piensen en algo a lo que desean avanzar en la vida. ¿Qué les gustaría aprender? ¿Cómo les gustaría crecer? ¿En qué área de su vida quieren ver un cambio positivo? ¿Qué les gustaría? ¿Qué quieren encontrar o descubrir? Siéntanse libres de tomar un momento para pensar, en una palabra, forma o símbolo que represente lo que quieren y escribirlo en la piedra restante ".
closing_spanish:
Para el cierre, puede darles a las y los participantes la oportunidad de compartir lo que escribieron en sus piedras, todo lo que aprendieron en el proceso creativo o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir.

Por supuesto, esto es puramente opcional y si nadie se siente cómoda o cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien. También puede agradecerles por ser tan creativos y por compartir sobre lo que hicieron. También puede animarlos a deshacerse de la piedra que representa su pasado si así lo desean.

Esto puede ser un ejercicio de curación. Si lo desea, puede sugerir que entierren su piedra pasada en un jardín, la pongan en la basura o la arrojen al océano. "Mientras caminan por la vida, pueden tenerlas consigo, en sus bolsillos o en sus bolsos.

Son suyas para que las lleven como un recordatorio de a dónde se están dirigiendo".
optional_materials:
•  
      Stepping Stones printable worksheet
    Soft instrumental music
  • Stepping Stones printable worksheet
optional_materials_spanish: • Música instrumental suave
introduction:
“Thank you for being here today. Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. It's a time for you to notice your thoughts, needs and feelings. During this time, there is no wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you get to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please ask for what you need. Please remember that all aspects of this workshop are optional, and observing is participating."

"Today, I would like to invite you to create your very own personal stepping stones. The stepping stones give us a chance to reflect on where the path of life has taken us and where we want it to lead us in the future. We are all on a path, always growing." 

"When we practice respecting ourselves, our feelings, our visions, it is very powerful. It has an impact. When we respect ourselves and our feelings, we are not the same person at the end as we were at the beginning, which is why it's so valuable to look at what we are walking away from and what we are walking towards in our path of life."
introduction_spanish:
“Gracias por estar aquí. Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que esta es su ventana de tiempo. Esto significa que este tiempo puede ser un lugar seguro para que noten sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que decidan hacer o decir es voluntario. Durante este tiempo, no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta para participar o crear. Voy a compartir con ustedes unas instrucciones básicas, sin embargo, ustedes deciden cómo quieren participar. Pueden seguir las instrucciones por completo o tal vez quieran hacer algo diferente, depende completamente de ustedes. Durante su ventana de tiempo, tienen completa libertad de decidir. Cómo decidan pasar este tiempo está perfectamente bien. Yo estoy aquí para apoyarles de cualquier forma que pueda, así que siéntanse libres de pedirme lo que necesiten.”

"Hoy, me gustaría invitarles a crear las piedras de su sendero personal. Todas y todos estamos en un camino, cuando hablamos de un sendero de piedras es el camino que estamos recorriendo. Tenemos las piedras que hemos dejado atrás, las piedras que estamos atravesando y las piedras que nos quedan por recorrer. Vamos a crear algunas piedras de nuestro sendero el cual nos da la oportunidad de reflexionar sobre a dónde nos ha llevado el camino de la vida y hacia dónde queremos que nos guíe en el futuro. Todas y todos estamos en un sendero, siempre creciendo." 

"Es muy poderosos cuando nos respetamos y también cuando respetamos nuestros sentimientos y nuestras visiones. Esto tiene un gran impacto en nuestras vidas. Cuando nos respetamos dejamos de ser la persona que éramos al principio y al final somos otra persona, es por esto que es tan valioso observar de qué estamos alejándonos y hacia qué estamos caminando en nuestro camino de la vida."
demonstration:
As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to do a demonstration before inviting participants to create, or create along with them. We have found that generally, doing a demonstration then allowing participants to be on their own during the creation process provides a more focused and "personal" time for them to get in touch with their thoughts and feelings, instead of focusing on trying to follow directions. But please feel free to do what best suits your group. 


Step 1: To start, you can invite the participants to choose at least two colors. If anyone wishes to use only one color, that is perfectly okay too. A pinch of each color will be enough. 

Step 2: Roll each color into a "snake."

Step 3: Wrap the "snakes" around each other like a candy-cane and twist together.

Step 4: Now you may twist each little section of the roll until the colors are blended just the way you want them.

Step 5: Roll the "snakes" into a ball. If you like to create a more marbled effect, you can take your rolled up ball and repeat steps 4 and 5 several times. This blends the colors even more.

Step 6: Finally, you can roll the ball into a rock shape. You can do any shape you wish. A flat surface would be ideal for writing on the stones. You may use the palm of your hand to flatten the ball, a marker, pencil, etc.

   Step 5    Step 6
demonstration_spanish:
Como la persona que facilita el taller, usted tiene total libertad de hacer una demostración antes de invitar a las y los participantes a crear sus piedras o también puede crear una junto con ellas y ellos. Nos hemos dado cuenta que, en general, hacer una demostración y luego permitir que las y los participantes hagan sus piedras individualmente durante el proceso creativo les proporciona un tiempo más personal y les permite "enfocarse" para que puedan ponerse en contacto con sus pensamientos y sentimientos, en lugar de centrarse en tratar de seguir instrucciones. Pero no dude en hacer lo que mejor se adapte a su grupo.

Paso 1:

Para comenzar, puede invitar a las y los participantes a elegir al menos dos colores. Si alguien desea usar un solo color, también está perfectamente bien. Una pizca de cada color será suficiente.

Paso 2:

Enrolle la arcilla hasta formar una "serpiente" de cada color.

Paso 3:

Envuelvan las "serpientes" una con la otra como un bastón de caramelo y gírelas juntas.

Paso 4:

Ahora tomando cada extremo de la “serpiente” y comiencen a torcerlos en dirección opuesta uno del otro hasta que los colores se combinen de la forma que desean.

 

Paso 5:

Formen una bola con las “serpientes” enrolladas. Si desea crear un efecto más veteado, puede tomar su bola enrollada y repetir los pasos 4 y 5 varias veces. Esto mezclará los colores aún más.

Paso 6:

Finalmente, pueden rodar la pelota hasta formar una roca. Pueden hacer cualquier forma que deseen. Una superficie plana sería ideal para escribir sobre las piedras. Pueden usar la palma de su mano para aplanar la pelota, también pueden hacerlo con un marcador, un lápiz, etc.

introduction:
"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."

"Today, I would like to invite you to create your very own personal stepping stones. The stepping stones give us a chance to reflect on where the path of life has taken us and where we want it to lead us in the future. We are all on a path, always growing." 

"When we practice respecting ourselves, our feelings, our visions, it is very powerful. It has an impact. When we respect ourselves and our feelings, we are not the same person at the end as we were at the beginning, which is why it's so valuable to look at what we are walking away from and what we are walking towards in our path of life."
demonstration:
As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to do a demonstration before inviting participants to create, or create along with them. We have found that generally, doing a demonstration then allowing participants to be on their own during the creation process provides a more focused and "personal" time for them to be in tune with their thoughts and feelings, instead of focusing on trying to follow directions. But please feel free to do what best suits your group. 

Depending on the age group, children may still need help creating even after your demonstration. Please feel free to remind them that you are there to help and answer any questions if you see fit.


Step 1: To start, you can invite the children to choose at least two colors. If anyone wishes to use only one color, that is perfectly okay too. A pinch of each color will be enough. 

Step 2: Roll each color into a "snake."

Step 3: Wrap the "snakes" around each other like a candy-cane and twist together.

Step 4: Now you may twist each little section of the roll until the colors are blended just the way you want them.

Step 5: Roll the "snakes" into a ball. If you like to create a more marbled effect, you can take your rolled up ball and repeat steps 4 and 5 several times. This blends the colors even more.

Step 6: Finally, you can roll the ball into a rock shape. You can do any shape you wish. A flat surface would be ideal for writing on the stones. You may use the palm of your hand to flatten the ball, a marker, pencil, etc.

title: Life is Sweet / La Vida es Dulce
objective:
This workshop aims to enhance the family dynamic by reflecting on the bond they share, celebrating positive family moments, both big and small, and looking forward to building a happy future.

 

Note: This workshop can be done with a children's group or a family group.
materials:
• Pennies or a sandbag (for the warm-up)

  • Construction paper or card stock (various colors)

  • Ice cream cone template

  • Ice cream scoop template

  • Pens (for making lists)

  • Markers or crayons

  • Scissors

  • Glue


Material for the Warm-Up:

  • 8 1/2 x 11 Printable Brave/Scared Face Template

  • 8 1/2 x 11 Printable Calm/Mad Face Template

  • 8 1/2 x 11 Printable Happy/Sad Face Template

  • 8 1/2 x 11 Printable Proud/Shy Face Template

  • 8 1/2 x 11 Printable Loving Face Template

  • Paper plates
setup:
Feeling Faces
   
 
   Various colored scoops

Setup for Warm-Up Exercise:
Using the templates provided, you can print the Feeling Faces (see materials). You can cut the faces out and glue them onto paper plates, or you can use them as they are on the page. You can print one of each, but having a couple of each would be ideal. Before the warm-up, you can place the faces together on the floor. Please refer to the Feelings Target Warm-Up workshop for more detailed instructions on how to create the face templates.


Setup for Creation:
On various colored paper, you can out the ice cream scoops and the cones. One cone per child (or family) should be enough, maybe a few extras to account for mistakes. Ideally, each child (family) would have at least 10 scoops. For the scoops, you can use a variety of colors so the finished cones are fun and colorful.

Depending on the age group, you may decide to cut out the individual scoops beforehand. It may be helpful to create an ice cream cone sample to show children and to display throughout the workshop. If you choose to create a sample, we suggest a simple one, so that children aren't intimidated by any "artistic" challenges.
warm_up:
This warm-up aims to helps children notice and express their feelings, and for families, can encourage group bonding. This can be one as one large group with all the children, or you can invite each family to do this separately.

“Today, I'd like to invite you to play a game where you will each have a chance to share your feelings. When we talk about our feelings, whether they are ones we like or ones that are difficult for us, it gives us the freedom to be ourselves and notice what's alive for us. If you don't feel comfortable sharing or even participating, that's perfectly okay. You can use this time any way you like."

You may wish to let the children know that we all have many different feelings, and even sometimes we feel all of these emotions simultaneously. In one day, we can feel joyful, upset, angry, and proud. Remember, that while many of these feelings may seem uncomfortable, strange, challenging, or frustrating, it is useful to acknowledge each and every one of them.

To begin, you can invite the first child to stand a few feet away from the plates (if you have prepared them in advance) and toss a penny/sandbag towards them. If the penny/sandbag lands on a face, the child has an opportunity to share a story about the last time (or any time) they felt that particular feeling. For example, if the penny lands on the “happy” face, the child can share about the last time (or anytime) they felt happy. Depending on the size of the group, you may allow the children to talk for at least one minute. If the penny/sandbag lands between two feelings, the child has the choice to talk about either one of the feelings (you can move the penny/sandbag on top of the feeling the child will be talking about). The other children can practice listening as each person shares. Ideally, each child has had an opportunity to take a turn or pass. If there’s time, you can go around a second or third time. You have complete freedom to adapt or alter any part of this exercise to best suit your needs.

You also have the option to ask who wishes to share, then toss them the bean bag, to avoid selecting the children as opposed to them volunteering.

You can also incorporate more embodied art into the warm-up by giving children the option to make a 'statue' of the feeling instead of sharing verbally. For example, you might say: "Another option is that instead of talking, you can show us an image (statue) of that emotion. For example, here's what I look like when I'm nervous:" you can create a statue with your body, perhaps by hiding your face behind your hands and crouching down. Again, it's entirely up to you.

If it’s feasible, you can also do this warm up outside.

 Two scoops and counting!  

You can now invite the children (or families) to begin creating.

If this is a family workshop, we aim to support a positive family experience and encourage each member of the family to be part of the creation process. You can give the families one minute to assign responsibilities to one another. Assignments may include one person who cuts, one person who writes, one person who glues, etc. Parents and/or caregivers can take on a leadership role, or family members can decide together.

Again, please feel free to facilitate this however way best suits your group.
 

Step 1:
You can invite the children to go in a circle and share an activity they enjoy doing with their family. They can read from their list, or come up with new ideas. If new ideas, you can encourage them to add them to their list. Of course, this is optional, so if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

Step 2:
Each child gets to cut out one ice cream cone (if you haven't done this in advance for them).

Step 3:
Next, children can cut out one ice cream scoop for each activity on their list (if you haven't done this in advance for them).

Step 4:
Now, they may write one activity on each ice cream scoop. They are free to use any and as many color markers as they like. We have suggested providing about 10 scoops per child. You may give them a limit, or print more to allow them to put as many scoops/activities on their ice cream as they like. This is entirely up to you.

Step 5:
Next, you can invite the children to glue the cone and scoops together in a "stacking" fashion.

 

For younger children, you may see the need to help them write. Please feel free to offer assistance where you see fit.
closing:
For the closing, you may give the children (or families) an opportunity to share their ice cream creations, what it means to them, anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share.

You can also invite them to a discussion if you see fit. You can prompt them with questions such as: “How many of you didn't know that you and your family did so much together?" "Where can you display these ice cream cones so we are always reminded of this activity and what it meant for you?" "Did anyone think of some activities that their family hasn't done yet, but would like to try in the future?" "Does anyone have any ideas on how you can plan out how your family is going to do some of these activities?"

Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

You may also encourage children (or families) to display their ice cream cones as a reminder of the positive experiences they’ve shared together, and how much sweeter life is when they are spending time with each other and having fun.
description: To enhance the family dynamic by celebrating positive family moments, both big and small. Families can reflect on the bond they share, and look forward to building a happy future!
notes:
Note about introducing embodied art:

You may wish to share with your participants the benefits of moving their bodies in playful and safe ways. Understanding what’s meaningful about movement and body awareness can help participants feel at ease expanding their comfort zones. For more about embodied art workshops and how to introduce them in your groups, please see Introduction to Embodied Art Workshops.
objective_spanish:
El objetivo de este taller es mejorar la dinámica familiar al reflexionar sobre el vínculo que comparten, celebrar momentos familiares positivos, grandes y pequeños, y esperar construir un futuro feliz.

Este taller se puede hacer con un grupo de niños o un grupo familiar.
materials_spanish:
• Centavos o una bolsa de arena (para el calentamiento)
• Papel de construcción o cartulina (varios colores)
• Plantilla de cono de helado
• Plantilla de cucharada de helado
• Bolígrafos (para hacer listas)
• Marcadores o crayones
• Tijeras
• Pegamento

Materiales para el calentamiento:
• 8 1/2 x 11 plantilla de cara valiente / asustada imprimible
• 8 1/2 x 11 plantilla de cara tranquila / imprimible para imprimir
• 8 1/2 x 11 plantilla de cara feliz / triste para imprimir
• 8 1/2 x 11 plantilla de cara orgullosa / tímida para imprimir 
• 8 1/2 x 11 plantilla de cara amorosa imprimible 
• Platos de papel
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 5 minutos
Demostración: 5 minutos
El Comienzo: 10 minutos
Calentamiento: 15 minutos
Creación: 40 minutos
Cierre: 10 minutos
Total: 1 hora y 25 minutos

(Adapte el período de tiempo para satisfacer sus necesidades.)
setup_spanish:
Configuración para el ejercicio de calentamiento:
Usando las plantillas proporcionadas, puede imprimir las Caras de sentimientos (ver materiales). Puede cortar las caras y pegarlas en platos de papel, o puede usarlas como están en la página. Puedes imprimir uno de cada uno, pero tener un par de cada uno sería ideal. Antes del calentamiento, puedes colocar las caras juntas en el suelo. Consulte el taller Sentimientos Objetivo para obtener instrucciones más detalladas sobre cómo crear las plantillas de cara.

Configuración para la creación:
En varios papeles de colores, puedes sacar las bolas de helado y los conos. Un cono por niño (o familia) debería ser suficiente, tal vez algunos extras por si hay errores. Idealmente, cada niño (familia) tendría al menos 10 cucharadas. Para las cucharadas, puede usar una variedad de colores para que los conos terminados sean divertidos y coloridos.

Dependiendo del grupo de edad, puede decidir recortar las primicias individuales de antemano. Puede ser útil crear una muestra de cono de helado para mostrar a los niños y mostrarlos durante todo el taller. Si elige crear una muestra, sugerimos una simple, para que los niños no se sientan intimidados por ningún desafío "artístico."
warm_up_spanish:
Este calentamiento tiene como objetivo ayudar a los niños a notar y expresar sus sentimientos, y para las familias, pueden alentar la unión grupal. Este puede ser un grupo grande con todos los niños, o puede invitar a cada familia a hacer esto por separado.

“Hoy, me gustaría invitarlos a jugar un juego en el que cada uno tendrá la oportunidad de compartir sus sentimientos. Cuando hablamos de nuestros sentimientos, ya sean los que nos gustan o los que son difíciles para nosotros, nos da la libertad de ser nosotros mismos y notar lo que está vivo para nosotros. Si no es sienten cómodo compartiendo o incluso participando, está perfectamente bien. Pueden usar este tiempo como quieran ".

Quizás desee que los niños sepan que todos tenemos muchos sentimientos diferentes, e incluso a veces sentimos todas estas emociones simultáneamente. En un día, podemos sentirnos alegres, molestos, enojados y orgullosos. Recuerde que muchos de estos sentimientos pueden parecer incómodos, extraños, desafiantes o frustrantes, es útil reconocer a todos y cada uno de ellos.

Para comenzar, puede invitar al primer niño a pararse a unos pocos pies de distancia de los platos (si los ha preparado con anticipación) y arrojar un centavo / bolsa de arena hacia ellos. Si el centavo / bolsa de arena cae sobre una cara, el niño tiene la oportunidad de compartir una historia sobre la última vez (o en cualquier momento) que sintió ese sentimiento particular. Dependiendo del tamaño del grupo, puede permitir que los niños hablen durante al menos un minuto. Si el centavo / bolsa de arena cae entre dos sentimientos, el niño tiene la opción de hablar sobre cualquiera de los sentimientos (puede mover el centavo / bolsa de arena sobre la sensación de la que hablará el niño). Los otros niños pueden practicar escuchar mientras cada persona comparte. Idealmente, cada niño ha tenido la oportunidad de tomar un turno o pasar. Si hay tiempo, puede ir alrededor de una segunda o tercera vez. Tiene total libertad para adaptar o alterar cualquier parte de este ejercicio para adaptarse mejor a sus necesidades.

También tiene la opción de preguntar quién desea compartir y luego tirarles la bolsa de frijoles para evitar seleccionar a los niños en lugar de que se ofrezcan voluntarios. 
También puede incorporar más arte incorporado en el calentamiento dando a los niños la opción de hacer una "estatua" del sentimiento en lugar de compartirlo verbalmente. Por ejemplo, podría decir: "Otra opción es que, en lugar de hablar, nos muestre una imagen (estatua) de esa emoción. Por ejemplo, este es el aspecto que tengo cuando estoy nervioso: "puedes crear una estatua con tu cuerpo, tal vez ocultando tu rostro detrás de tus manos y agachándote. Una vez más, todo depende de ti.

Si es factible, también puede hacer este calentamiento en el exterior/afuera.
creation_spanish:
Ahora puedes invitar a los niños (o familias) a comenzar a crear.

Si este es un taller familiar, nuestro objetivo es apoyar una experiencia familiar positiva y animar a cada miembro de la familia a ser parte del proceso de creación. Puedes darles un minuto a las familias para que se asignen responsabilidades unas a otras.

Las asignaciones pueden incluir una persona que corta, una persona que escribe, una persona que pega, etc. Los padres y / o cuidadores pueden asumir un rol de liderazgo, o los miembros de la familia pueden decidir juntos.

Nuevamente, siéntase libre de facilitar esto de la manera que mejor se adapte a su grupo.

Paso 1:
 Puede invitar a los niños a ir en un círculo y compartir una actividad que disfruten haciendo con su familia. Pueden leer de su lista, o proponer nuevas ideas. Si hay nuevas ideas, puede animarlas a agregarlas a su lista. Por supuesto, esto es opcional, así que si nadie se siente cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.

Paso 2:
Cada niño puede cortar un cono de helado (si no lo ha hecho por adelantado).

Paso 3:
A continuación, los niños pueden cortar una cucharada de helado para cada actividad en su lista (si no lo han hecho por adelantado).

Paso 4:
Ahora, pueden escribir una actividad en cada cucharada de helado. Son libres de usar cualquiera y tantos marcadores de color como deseen. Hemos sugerido proporcionar alrededor de 10 cucharadas por niño. Puede darles un límite o imprimir más para permitirles poner tantas cucharadas / actividades en su helado como deseen. Esto es totalmente de usted.

Paso 5:
A continuación, puede invitar a los niños a pegar el cono y juntarlos de manera "apilada".

Para los niños más pequeños, puede ver la necesidad de ayudarlos a escribir. Por favor, siéntase libre de ofrecer asistencia cuando lo considere oportuno.
closing_spanish:
Para el cierre, puede darles a los niños (o familias) la oportunidad de compartir sus creaciones de helados, lo que significa para ellos, todo lo que aprendieron, sintieron o experimentaron en el proceso de creación, o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir.

También puede invitarlos a una discusión si lo considera conveniente. Puede hacerles preguntas como: “¿Cuántos de ustedes no sabían que ustedes y su familia hicieron tanto juntos?" "¿Dónde pueden exhibir estos conos de helado para que siempre recordemos esta actividad y lo que significó? ¿para ti?" "¿Alguien pensó en algunas actividades que su familia aún no ha hecho, pero que le gustaría probar en el futuro?" "¿Alguien tiene alguna idea sobre cómo puede planificar cómo va a hacer su familia algunas de estas actividades?"

Por supuesto, esto es puramente opcional y si nadie se siente cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.

También puede animar a los niños (o familias) a que muestren sus conos de helado como un recordatorio de las experiencias positivas que compartieron juntos, y cuánta más dulce es la vida cuando pasan el tiempo juntos y se divierten.

introduction:
Sample Life Is Sweet creation

"Today you'll have an opportunity to reflect on the positive things you've done as a family (with your family). Sometimes when we have experienced challenges in our lives, we have a hard time remembering the happy times. We can forget to value the time we spend together and how precious it is. When we take time to think about the happy times we've had, life can be so much sweeter. You will first have the opportunity to do a warm-up exercise together that can help you notice and talk about your feelings. Then you have the chance to create a 'Life is Sweet' ice cream cone (as a family)."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
introduction_spanish:
"Hoy tendrán la oportunidad de reflexionar sobre las cosas positivas que han hecho en familia (con su familia). A veces, cuando hemos experimentado desafíos en nuestras vidas, nos resulta difícil recordar los momentos felices. Podemos olvidar valorar el tiempo que pasamos juntos y lo precioso que es. Cuando nos tomamos el tiempo para pensar en los momentos felices que hemos tenido, la vida puede ser mucho más dulce. Primero tendrán la oportunidad de hacer un ejercicio de calentamiento juntos que puede ayudarlos a notar y hablar sobre sus sentimientos. Entonces tienes la oportunidad de crear un cono de helado 'La Vida es Dulce' (como familia) ".

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que este taller es una ventana de tiempo para ustedes. Esto significa que este puede ser un espacio seguro para notar tu pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es tu ventana de tiempo, todo Lo que digan o hagan es voluntario. Ofreceré una idea sugerida para el taller, compartiré los materiales que tenemos disponibles e invitaré a crear, pero no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de hacerlo. No importa lo que parece. Lo que importa es tomarse este tiempo para honrar verdaderamente los pensamientos y sentimientos, sin embargo, surgen. Si no pueden pensar en nada o dejar en blanco qué crear o escribir, sentasen libre de solo observar. Sin embargo, como ustedes elige pasar este tiempo estará perfectamente bien. Este es el tiempo de ustedes. Soliciten lo que necesiten y sepan que estoy aquí para ayudarlos ".
demonstration: You may wish to familiarize the children with the materials they will be using and share the basic creation steps with them (see Creation). If you've made a sample, you can show it to them, and remind them there is no right or wrong way to create.
demonstration_spanish: Quizás desee familiarizar a los niños con los materiales que usarán y compartir con ellos los pasos básicos de creación (consulte Creación). Si ha realizado una muestra, puede mostrársela y recordarles que no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de crear.
opening_circle:
You can invite the children to take a moment (as a family), and create a list of all the things they enjoy doing together. For example, they can say “My family and I love to have breakfast together on Sunday morning.” Or, “We love to bake cookies together.” Or, “We like to give each other hugs.” They might also choose to use short, or one word responses like "movies," "games," "art" or "Dodger games." Anything they come up with will be perfectly okay.

Depending on the age group, you may need to assist them with the writing. Please feel free to adapt to cater to your specific group's needs.
opening_circle_spanish:
Puede invitar a los niños a tomarse un momento (como familia) y crear una lista de todas las cosas que disfrutan haciendo juntos. Por ejemplo, pueden decir "Mi familia y yo amamos desayunar juntos el domingo por la mañana". O: "Nos encanta hornear galletas juntos". O: "Nos gusta darnos abrazos". También pueden optar por usar respuestas cortas o de una palabra como "películas", "juegos", "arte" o "juegos de los Dodgers.” Cualquier cosa que se les ocurra estará perfectamente bien.

Dependiendo del grupo de edad, es posible que necesite ayudarlos con la escritura. Por favor, siéntase libre de adaptarse para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo específico.

You can now invite the participants to begin creating. Ideally, we aim to support a positive family experience and encourage each member of the family to be part of the creation process. You can give the families one minute to assign responsibilities to one another. Assignments may include one person who cuts, one person who writes, one person who glues, etc. Parents and/or caregivers can take on a leadership role, or family members can decide together.

Again, please feel free to facilitate this however way best suits your group.
 

Step 1:
You can invite the participants to go in a circle and share an activity they enjoy doing together as a family. They can read from their list, or come up with new ideas. If new ideas, you can encourage them to add them to their list. Of course, this is optional, so if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

Step 2:
Each family gets to cut out one ice cream cone (if you haven't done this in advance for them).

Step 3:
Next, participants can cut out one ice cream scoop for each activity on their list (if you haven't done this in advance for them).

Step 4:
Now, they may write one activity on each ice cream scoop. They are free to use any and as many color markers as they like. We have suggested providing about 10 scoops per family. You may give them a limit, or print more to allow them to put as many scoops/activities on their ice cream as they like. This is entirely up to you.

Step 5:
Next, you can invite the participants to glue the cone and scoops together in a "stacking" fashion.
closing:
For the closing, you may give the participants an opportunity to share their ice cream creations, what it means to them, anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share.

You can also invite the participants to a discussion if you see fit. You can prompt them with questions such as: “How many of you didn't know that you and your family did so much together?" "Where can you display these ice cream cones so we are always reminded of this activity and what it meant for you?" "Did anyone think of some activities that their family hasn't done yet, but would like to try in the future?" "Does anyone have any ideas on how you can plan out how your family is going to do some of these activities?"

Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

You may also encourage families to display their ice cream cones as a reminder of the positive experiences they’ve shared together, and how much sweeter life is when they are spending time with each other and having fun.
description: To enhance the family dynamic by celebrating positive family moments, both big and small. Participants and their children can reflect on the bond they share, and look forward to building a happy future!
tips:
Note about introducing embodied art:

You may wish to share with your participants the benefits of moving their bodies in playful and safe ways. Understanding what’s meaningful about movement and body awareness can help participants feel at ease expanding their comfort zones. For more about embodied art workshops and how to introduce them in your groups, please see Introduction to Embodied Art Workshops.

Life is Sweet (English)     Life is Sweet (Spanish)
introduction:
Sample Life Is Sweet creation

"Today you'll have an opportunity to reflect on the positive things you've done as a family. Sometimes when we have experienced challenges in our lives, we have a hard time remembering the happy times. We can forget to value the time we spend together and how precious it is. When we take time to think about the happy times we've had, life can be so much sweeter. You will first have the opportunity to do a warm-up exercise together that can help you notice and talk about your feelings. Then you have the chance to create a 'Life is Sweet' ice cream cone as a family."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. title: The Lotus Flower / La Flor de Loto
objective: To help participants see and believe that even out of a murky and dark environment, something beautiful can be created and they can rise above.
materials:
• Lotus flower templates

    • Small

    • Medium

    • Large

  • Heavy paper (construction paper or cardstock)

  • Watercolor paper

  • Watercolors

  • Paintbrushes

  • Glue
setup:
To facilitate an efficient workshop, we suggest having certain material prepared beforehand. You may start with printing one set of the lotus flower templates (with 3 sizes - large, medium, and small) and cut the 3 shapes out. These are used to trace the shapes onto the watercolor paper.

On the watercolor paper, you can then trace the 3 shapes. Ideally, you would like to prepare and cut out enough shapes so each participant has one set of all 3. If you do not have time to cut the watercolor paper in advance, participants may cut out the shapes as part of the creation. 
 

   Workshop set-up    Cutting the 3 different layers
warm_up:
As with any part of this workshop, you have complete freedom to use any warm-up or relaxation exercise that you feel best suits your group. If you choose this exercise, you may consider speaking in a soft, slow pattern, pausing where you see fit.

"I would like to invite you to join me in a relaxation. For those of you who wish to participate, try to imagine that you are a lotus seed buried beneath a muddy lotus pond. There is mud all around you.  Above you, above this muddy pool, are sunshine and air. You are not disheartened as you begin your journey towards the surface."

"With a determined heart, you begin to wiggle in the earth. You grow roots deep, deep into the mud. Your little stem grows up slowly. Suddenly, 'pop,' you are out of the mud. Your stem grows higher and higher, taller and taller. You rise up slowly, fighting against the muddy water. All of a sudden, you are out of the muddy pond. You reach up towards the warm sun shining down on you."

"Your lotus bud begins to grow on top of your stem. It expands and grows larger and larger, finally bursting into full bloom. You stand beautifully above the muddy water, not dirtied by the mud from which you grow. You are fragrant, alive and beautiful. Everyone who sees you marvels at your beauty." 

"You are a beautiful lotus flower, and you inspire people to rise above their pain and sufferings, just as you are rising above the muddy water and not dirtied by the mud from which you grew."

Adapted from "Lotus Meditation" BuddhaNet's Guided Meditation for Primary Students.
creation:
"Remember, any part of this workshop is voluntary. You can simply observe or do something entirely different. It's entirely up to you. For those of you who wish to participate, I now invite you to create your own lotus flower."

With the three different size cutouts of the lotus flower in front of them, you can invite participants to use the watercolors to paint each layer. You may wish to remind them that it doesn't matter what it looks like. What's important is that they take this personal time to focus on their inner beauty and strength. They can choose any color and paint in any manner they wish. They can paint each layer differently or they can all be the same. They might choose not to paint but to draw or color on the flower pieces instead. Whatever they choose is perfectly okay.

"If you choose to create a lotus flower, here is a suggestion of how to create it. Beginning with the largest shape, use the watercolors with your fingers or a brush to lightly cover the petals. You can then take each petal and roll it gently inwards until it curls (you can use a paintbrush or pencil to help with the rolling method). You can simply follow the same process with the two smaller shapes."

Once all three layers are dry, you can invite the participants to glue them together with a small amount of glue on the bottom/center of each layer.

Depending on your time restraints, you may wish to set a time limit or not. Once the participants have had ample time to create their beautiful masterpieces, you can encourage them to notice that they have created something beautiful, and that they are beautiful too. 
 

   Painting the layers    Rolling the edges    Gluing the layers together    Finished lotus flower
closing:
You may close by inviting participants to share how it felt to create the lotus flower. They can share how they are like a lotus flower, and how it felt to create something beautiful. Sharing, of course, is voluntary, and if no one wishes to share, that is perfectly okay.

If they choose to, participants may keep their lotus flower visible as a memento that something beautiful can come out of a painful situation. You may remind them: "whenever you are feeling sad or frustrated about the muck that you have to work through, you too can grow and rise above."

   Finished Lotus flower    Finished Lotus flower
description: To assist participants in seeing and believing that out of a murky and dark environment, something beautiful can be created and they can rise above.
tips:
If you wish to deepen the participant's experience, you may want to invite participants to spend the last 10 minutes to journal about their creation and its meaning. You may wish to provide paper and pens for journaling. 

If they want to share their writing, you can invite participants to share any discoveries that they made.

Another great tip, from leader Laura Maldonado at South Gate Police Department, is to create a lily pad for the lotus flower to lay on. This creates a beautiful color contrast and brings the flower to life.

objective_spanish: Los participantes podrán aprender a utilizar el simbolismo de la flor de loto y puedan reflexionar sobre su propia y personal experiencia y lograr cierta capacidad de recuperación.
materials_spanish:
• Plantillas de la flor de loto

  • Pequeñas

  • Medianas

  • Grandes

  • Papel pesado o cartulina (Por lo menos de 60 libras)

  • Papel para acuarela

  • Colores para acuarela

  • Tazas con agua

  • Pinceles

  • Pegamento blanco para papel

  • Tijeras (si son necesarias)
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 5 minutos
Calentando: 10 minutos
Circulo para apertura: 10 Minutos
Creación: 25 Minutos
Cierre: 10 Minutos
1 Hora
setup_spanish: En papel grueso, imprima los suficientes juegos de plantilla de la flor de loto para usarlos como patrones. Si tiene tiempo, use los patrones para dibujar y recortar de antemano las tres formas en el papel de acuarela
warm_up_spanish:
Pregunte a los participantes si les gustaría escuchar una meditación Budista sobre la flor de loto, si no desean escuchar esta parte proceda a la parte de apertura del círculo. Si no hay disposición. Recuerde a los participantes que tienen la opción de elegir cómo participaran y les dará la opción de tomar este tiempo para escribir en su diario o escribir sobre la forma en que siente la relación con la historia de la flor de loto.

Imaginen que ustedes son un loto enterrado en un estanque lodoso. Están rodeadas de lodo a su rededor. Encima de ustedes, y sobre este estanque lodoso, hay aire y brilla el sol. Y no están descorazonadas al comenzar este viaje hacia la superficie.

Con el corazón determinado, usted empieza a moverse en la tierra. Usted crece raíces profundas en el lodo. Su pequeño tallo crece lentamente. De repente "pop" esta fuera del lodo! Y su tallo crece más y más alto, Usted se ha levantado lentamente, luchando contra el agua sucia y lodosa. Y de repente, usted está fuera del estanque lodoso! Usted alcanza ese tibio sol, que brilla hacia usted.

Su capullo de loto empieza a crecer arriba del tallo, se expande y crece más y más finalmente estalla en plena floración. Usted se pone de pie muy por encima del agua turbia, sin estar ensucia por el barro donde ha crecido. Usted ahora es fragante y bella.

Todos los que la ven están maravillados por su belleza! Su determinación por crecer fuera del lodo les recuerda del Buddha y su viaje hacia la iluminación.

El Buddha, como el loto, se decidió a crecer afuera del barro que lo rodeaba que son el sufrimiento y el dolor de la vida. El hizo todo lo que hay que hacer y nos muestra que también nosotros podemos lograrlo también. Nosotros podemos tener ese dolor, pero todos tenemos la capacidad y el potencial para crecer fuera de nuestros sufrimientos y lograr la sabiduría, como el Buddha.

Usted es una bella flor de loto, y su papel es recordar a la gente a levantarse de su dolor y sus sufrimientos, así como se ha elevado del agua lodosa y no haberse ensuciado de ese lodo de donde usted creció.

Adaptado de "Lotus Meditation" BuddhaNet's Guided Meditation for Primary Students.
creation_spanish:
Invite a las participantes a crear la flor de loto que tiene significado simbólico o es el recordatorio de cómo cada una de nosotros hemos tenido momentos oscuros, turbios en nuestras vidas pero como podemos crecer y ser extraordinarias.

Al final del taller, invítelas a escribir algunas palabras o hasta la fecha que va con su trabajo artístico. Cuando cada una tome un momento para darse cuenta que han creado algo bello... y recuérdeles que ellas también son bellas!
closing_spanish:
Pregunte a las participantes cómo se siente crear la flor de loto. Ellas pueden compartir como ellas son como una flor de loto y/o como se siente crear algo bello. Anime a las participantes a conservar sus flores de loto visibles, como un recuerdo que algo bello puede salir de una situación dolorosa. Recuérdeles "Cuando sea que nos sintamos tristes o frustradas acerca de la inmundicia con la que hemos tenido que pasar, nosotros podemos crecer y elevarnos por encima de todo.
   
Si usted quiere profundizar en la experiencia de los participantes, pida a las participantes tomar los últimos 10 minutos a que escriban acerca de su creación y su significado, si ellas quieren compartir algún descubrimiento que hayan logrado que ellas hicieran y ofrecerles la oportunidad de exhibir su trabajo y sus palabras. Asegúrese de darles la oportunidad de usar un seudónimo o permanecer anónimas. Para más consejos/claves para exhibir el arte y los beneficios para sus clientes, clic aquí. Otro buen consejo, de la líder Laura Maldonado en South Gate Police Department, Es crear un Lily pad para poner la flor de loto ahí! Esto crea un contraste de color fabuloso y mostrar la representación completa de la flor.

You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • The Lotus Flower Worksheet (Spanish)

   
The Lotus Flower (English)     The Lotus Flower (Spanish)
introduction:
Real lotus flower

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you; a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you do or say is voluntary. I'll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there's no wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this window of time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. Please ask for what you need, and know that I'm here in support of you."

As a facilitator, you have the option to take a moment to share how the lotus flower grows and blooms and what it represents. The lotus flower, which is considered sacred to many Asian cultures, is believed to represent innocence, rebirth, growth and potential.

Rooted firmly in the mud, the lotus flower grows in murky waters. With a long stem and petals sprouting from it, the flower always rises above the water's surface, and opens with the light of the morning sun.

A core Buddhist value says: "Like a lotus flower that grows out of the mud and blossoms above the muddy water surface, we can rise above our defilement and sufferings of life." Just like the lotus flower, we can grow to be strong, beautiful and healthy no matter where we come from or what surrounds us.
introduction_spanish:
Antes de principiar, quiero que sepan que este taller es una ventana de tiempo para ustedes - un espacio seguro para identificar sus pensamientos, sentimientos, necesidades y sus visiones. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que haga o diga es voluntario. Voy a darles cual es la idea sobre e l taller, y vamos a compartir los materiales que tenemos a la mano, yo les invito a crear, y quiere decirles que no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de hacerlo. No importa lo que parezca. Lo que sí importa es aprovechar esta ventana de tiempo para plasmar realmente sus pensamientos y sentimientos, como quieran que salgan. Por favor, pidan lo que necesiten, y recuerden que yo estoy aquí para darles el apoyo que necesiten.

Hoy nosotros haremos flores de loto que puedan representar lo que nosotros queramos. La flor de loto es una flor vibrante y condescendiente que crece del barro y de agua turbia y florece sin manchas en la superficie del agua a la luz del sol.

La flor de loto posee un significado sagrado en algunas culturas asiáticas y conlleva tradicionales lecciones de sabiduría. Hay un núcleo budista de valores que dice:
"Como la flor de loto que crece del barro y florece por encima de la superficie del agua fangosa, también nosotros podemos florecer por encima de nuestras impurezas y los sufrimientos de la vida." Al igual que la flor de loto, que puede llegar a ser fuerte y magnífica a través incluso de nuestras mayores luchas
demonstration: You have the option to have a pre-made sample on hand to show your participants, if you feel it may ease any sense of being overwhelmed by the creation process.
demonstration_spanish:
Primero asegúrese que todos tengan los tres cortes en el papel de acuarela. Y ahora demuestre como usar las acuarelas para pintar cada capa usando los dedos o pincel.

   
Pintar las capas.   Enrolle las orillas.    Engomar las capas juntas

Ellas pueden pintar cada capa diferente o todos ellas pueden ser las mismas. Luego tomar cada pétalo y ruédelo suavemente hacia dentro para que se enrolle. Si se les hace más fácil pueden utilizar un pincel o un lápiz para ayudarse en este paso de laminación. Siga el mismo proceso con cada forma. Una vez que las tres capas están secas, pegarlas juntas usando una pequeña cantidad de pegamento en el centro de las 2 capas de fondo.
opening_circle:
"Now that you know what a lotus flower can do, I invite you to think of one thing that you have gone through or grown out of."

You have the option to invite your participants to share something about how they relate to the lotus flower, or go straight to the next step. It's up to you. If you choose to invite them to share, it may be useful to remind them again that it's voluntary and if they choose to just observe in this or any aspect of the workshop, it's perfectly okay.
opening_circle_spanish:
Invite a las participantes a compartir con el grupo o en pares, sobre como sienten que han crecido en su vida.

Si los participantes no tienen la voluntad de compartir, a veces compartir una anécdota o una historia de como usted creció de ese tiempo tan difícil puede lograr que el grupo se pueda abrir.
