title: I Can: Requiem for I Can't
objective:
This workshop is about confronting the things we feel we cannot do in our lives, allowing us recognize and embrace that we can do anything!  By participating in this workshop you will be part of a movement of survivors coming together and collectively letting go of our I Cant's and embracing our I Cans.

 

   
 
  Completed I can shrinky


 




 

 

   
 
Completed I Can shrinky
   


 

 

 

 
  I Can statement created by an adult
materials:
• White card stock for "I Can't" journaling
  • Colored paper for "I Can" statements
  • Paper shredder machine
  • Shrinky Dink paper
  • Shrinky Dink templates
  • Colored pencils
  • Permanent markers, like Sharpies
  • Hole puncher
  • Scissors
  • Toaster oven
  • Ribbon
  • Beads
  • Timer
creation:
Writing I Can'ts:
We are going to begin by identifying and releasing our I cant's during ten minutes of journaling with an "I Can't" prompt. Provide a piece of white card stock (Note: we chose white paper for our I Cant's as it represents death and burials in Nina Jun's, Installation Artist,  Korean culture) for each of the participants. 

We're going to take about ten minutes to write all the I cant's that come up. Optional: you can use a colored pen to write your I cant's... take a second to think... are your I can'ts yellow, red, green...just pick a color.

Keep in mind that there is no right or wrong way to do this writing exercise. You can write sentences, words, lists or draw symbols, shapes. The most important thing is that you don't censor yourself and that you don't stop writing during the whole ten minutes. Don't worry about spelling or grammar, just allow your thoughts to flow onto your paper without judgment.  What you write is just for you and does not have to make sense to anyone but you!

You can begin by writing the words "I Can't" on the top of your paper.  Try to keep writing until time is up.  Note: If you have a client who has difficulty identifying an I can't you can say, "If you feel powerful today and have no I can'ts to speak of, think of a time when you did and just keep writing."  As you write keep trusting whatever comes to mind; it doesn't have to make sense. It's okay if you repeat one I can't over and over again. Now, I'm going to turn on some music and we are going to take ten minutes to write all the I can'ts that come up...Cue music on.

In the last minute remind them - keep trusting what comes to mind.  We have about one more minute. As you finish up, read over your thoughts and notice what stands out...Cue music off.

Sharing & Shredding:
Now I'm going to ask each of you to come up, one at a time, share your I Can'ts with the group, and destroy them by either shredding or tearing them.  Remember, this is voluntary, and you don't have to share anything you don't want to.  Even if you don't want to share what you wrote, I will ask each of you to come up and shred your I Cant's.  This is your opportunity to let go of your I Can'ts. 

Do I have a brave volunteer who would like to come up here with me and share your I Can'ts and then shred them?  Standing at the front of the room, next to the shredder(s), invite others to come shred. As each person comes up tell them its okay to take their time and notice how brave they are.  Continue until each participant has had an opportunity to share their I Can'ts and shred or tear them.

Note: If this is a bilingual group, do not translate simultaneously while the participant shares as it may be disruptive.  We ask that you wait until after the participant has shared and shredded.

I Can Circle:
Discuss how we are all like Cathy, Barbara, and Nina in that we overcame great challenges and as a result have gained great strength and knowledge.  Now that we have let go of our I Cant's, we're going to take this opportunity to notice and celebrate our strength.  I want us to stand up, gather in a circle, hold hands and each share something significant in your life that you thought you couldn't do, but you did and it made you stronger. There is no right or wrong way to share, and you don't have to share anything you don't want. 

Note: If your client is having a hard time thinking of something you can say, "one thing that you did was come to this group. By coming to group you are saying, I can take care of myself." After each person has shared, have the participants sit back down and begin the I Can statement writing portion of the workshop. 

 

 

 
 I Can statement created by a child  


I Can Statements:
Now that we have let go of our I Can'ts and noticed our strength, we are ready to focus on our I Can's. Think about all of the things that you can do, and choose one that really stands out. Pick a color to represent your I Can...take a second to think... is your I Can purple, green, pink?  Then write your I Can statement on the paper provided by AWBW (cue music on). If they choose, the participants can make more than one colorful I Can statement.  Tell the participants that we are going to gather all of their I Can statements and use them in the exhibit.  Give ten minutes for the I Can statement writing. Cue music off.

 

 

 
  I Can statement created by an adult  


I Can Shrinky Dink:
Now we are going to create an I Can shrinky dink to remind us of the I Cans we chose to embrace today! Don't worry if your I Can seems impossible. Be bold!  Never underestimate the power of putting our I Cans out into the world!  Cathy thought her idea of sharing art with others was crazy too; now look at what she has created as a result! 

Note: Play music during the entire I Can creation portion.

Step 1:
Keeping in mind all of the things you can do, use colored pencils and/or permanent markers, write words, colors, shapes, or scribbles on the Shrinky Dink to help you remember your I Can(s).  You can color with permanent markers on both sides of the Shrinky Dink, but can only use colored pencils on the rough side. 

If you'd like to use a template, choose the one that best represents your I Can (remind participants that using a template is optional). Then trace the template or draw on the Shrinky Dink. Add color to fill in your design.

Step 2:
When you are finished coloring, if you like, cut out your I Can shrinky with scissors.  Make sure to punch a hole in the shrinky dink so it can be hung.  Make sure your don't punch your hole too close to the edge of the shrinky paper, as it may break after cooking.

Step 3:
Now the I Can shrinkys are ready for baking. Bake your shrink with the shiny side facing up. This will prevent it from folding while baking. Place the shrinky dink on either a small piece of a brown paper bag, or a metal tray, or a piece of aluminum foil; then place the paper, tray, or foil in the toaster oven.

Step 4:
Cook the shrinkys at 300 degrees for 1-3 minutes.  Watch as your shrinky dink shrinks!  After the shrinky lies flat, allow an additional 15 seconds of baking time to complete the process.  If you pull the shrinkys out prematurely, it is okay to put them back in the oven.

While the shrinkys are cooking have the participants complete the 2012 Art/Photography Release.  Make sure they leave their contact info so they can be invited to the exhibit.

Step 5:
Remove paper, tray, or foil and let Shrinky Dinks cool.  If you like, you can add ribbon so you can hang your I Can shrinky.  You can also add beads if you choose.
closing:
Have a each participant share anything they want about their experience writing their I Cant's, and the I Can(s) they represented on their I Can statement and shrinky. 

Thank the participants and suggest they use their I Can shrinky as a reminder that they can do anything!
description: This workshop is about confronting the things we feel we cannot do in our lives, allowing us recognize and embrace that we can do anything! By participating in this workshop you will be part of a movement of survivors coming together and collectively letting go of our I Cant's and embracing our I Cans.
optional_materials:
• Pens/Multi-colored pens
  • Music
introduction:
Introduce AWBW and the I Can: Requiem for I Can't video.  Briefly explain who is in the video and what their plans are for the exhibit.  For example, Barbra T. Smith will do a performance art piece at the exhibit and Nina Jun will use video to enhance our creations.  Warn the participants that there is a part of the video that may be disturbing to some viewers.  Play I Can introduction video.

This workshop is about inspiring us to have the courage to release all of the things we think we cannot do.  Confronting the things we feel we cannot do in our lives is the first step towards recognizing that we can. By allowing ourselves to go through this process and sharing it through the exhibit, we are coming together to collectively let go of our I Cant's and embracing our I Cans.

We will begin by writing and then shredding our I Cant's (all the things we think we cannot do).  Next we will focus on all of the things we can do by writing an I Can statement you want to share with the world. Finally you will create an I Can shrinky dink to serve as a reminder that anything is possible and we can do anything we put our minds to!

This workshop is an opportunity for you to practice noticing your feelings and respect what needs to come out. Every part of this is voluntary and everyone in the room supports you.  Notice you are safe and among friends.
opening_circle: Go around the room and invite each person to share their name and how they're feeling right now.

title: Permission Canvas / Lienzo de Permiso
objective: This workshop aims to give participants "permission" to do something they have been longing to do, to change a habit, or let go of something they've been hanging onto.
materials:
•    
      Sample art supply materials
       
     
      Optional printable self-led worksheet

    Canvas or cardstock (6" x 6" pieces work well)

  • Paint

  • Brushes

  • Mod podge

  • Cake doilies

  • Scrapbook paper

  • White glue

  • Magazines (we suggest Oprah, Nat Geo or travel magazines as they tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Pre-cut or pre-typed words (see set up for details)

  • Sponges (to make texture in paint)

  • Foam brushes or Brayers

  • Bubble wrap

  • Sharpies (ultra fine & regular would be ideal)

  • Scissors

  • Stamps & ink pads

  • Writing paper

  • Permission Canvas Handout

  • Journaling Questions

  • Paper Dolls Template

Please note that some of the decoration material are optional and can be used in lieu of others. Please feel free to provide what suits your needs.

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable self-led worksheet. If you are utilizing this sheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print them out beforehand for your participants depending on the setting.
setup:
Completed Permission Canvas
"... Just breathe"
 
  Completed self-led worksheet

You can print words and phrases that can be collaged onto the canvases by the participants. For example: "They gave themselves permission to," "They decided to," "They let ______ go," or any other words or phrases that may be better suited to your specific group.

If applicable to your group, you can print copies of the optional words, statements, women and men silhouettes templates in advance.

Once you print them, you can also cut the words out (see images for reference).

If you're unable to print these, you can write them on a board and invite participants to select the ones that apply to them and write it down instead of collage it.

You can print out the paper doll templates for all the participants, but please be mindful that there is not "one" body shape. If participants wish to draw their own body template, that's great, and it might be empowering for them. 

You can also print the journaling questions (one copy per participant, plus some extras).

You may wish to create a sample in advance to get the feel for the creation process, as well as to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample using only the material you're providing so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Ripping magazine cutouts for a unique collage finish.
   
 
  Using Mod Podge to glue on mixed-media materials

You can now invite participants to dive in and start creating. You can suggest that they paint the background of their canvas first, and then think about their permission phrase while the paint dries. Since this is a "mixed media" project, they can blend a variety of techniques when creating their art: paint, stamping, and/or collage.

"I encourage you to give yourself permission to create your canvas in whatever way that you wish. You can collage, paint, or simply have an abstract background. You might want to add a person as a focal point of your art. You can use the doll template as a guide, and collage to create clothing from different scrapbook patterns. You can also draw your person freehand or find a magazine image that represents the future you want to create. Whatever you wish."

"You can begin by choosing one permission phrase that is most meaningful to you. Are you giving permission to take more time out for yourself in the future? Maybe you are deciding to spend more quality time with your children? Or perhaps you want to finally tackle that dream or goal you have not yet gotten around to. You fill in the blank. Once you've decide, you can collage the statement onto the background or you can paint to write your phrase directly on the canvas. Since the canvas is focusing on the future that you want, I encourage you to keep your wording optimistic and affirmative."

If some of the participants finish earlier than others, you can invite them to look back at their journaling questions. They can answer questions they did not answer previously, or they can journal about their creation. They might also create another canvas, doodle, or draw. Feel free to guide the participants as you see fit.
closing:
You can close by inviting the participants to share their canvases with the group and anything they discovered about themselves while creating. They can also share their permission phrase out loud. If there's time, you have the option to use "echo listening" where other group members repeat the phrase back to the participant. Echo listening is a form of listening which is structured to be completely non-judgmental. After listening to participants read their piece, everyone in the room can simply repeat at least one thing they remember the person saying, word for word, so that they hear the entire room "echo" their words to them, rather than judging them. It is one structured way to use supportive listening and ground the vision of the participant.

You can also invite the participants, if they feel comfortable doing so, to display their canvas somewhere that they will be able to see it everyday, as encouragement and inspiration to look towards the New Year with and hope.

Of course, as with any part of this workshop, sharing is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
 

Completed Permission Canvas Completed Permission Canvas
description: This workshop can give participants permission to do something they have been longing to do, to change a habit, or let go of something.
tips: If a canvas is inaccessible to you, you can also use thick watercolor paper or thick card stock.
objective_spanish: Este taller tiene como objetivo dar a los participantes "permiso" para hacer algo que han estado deseando hacer, para cambiar un hábito o dejar de lado algo a lo que han estado aferrados.
materials_spanish:
• Lona o cartulina (piezas de 6 "x 6" funcionan bien)
• Pintar
• Cepillos
• Mod podge (sellador de base de agua)
• Pastelitos
• Papel de recortes
• pegamento blanco
• Revistas (sugerimos Oprah, Nat Geo o revistas de viajes, ya que tienden a tener palabras e imágenes más inclusivas)
• Palabras precortadas o tecleadas (ver configuración para más detalles)
• Esponjas (para hacer textura en pintura).
• Cepillos de espuma o Brayers
• Plástico de burbujas
• Sharpies/Marcadores (ultra fino y regular sería ideal)
• Tijeras • Sellos y almohadillas de tinta
• Papel para escribir
• Preguntas del diario
• Plantilla de muñecas de papel

Tenga en cuenta que algunos de los materiales de decoración son opcionales y se pueden utilizar en lugar de otros. Por favor, siéntase libre de proporcionar lo que se adapte a sus necesidades.
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción 10 minutos
Demostración 5 minutos
El Comienzo 30 minutos
Creación 60 minutos
Cierre 15 minutos
Total 2 horas
setup_spanish:
Puede imprimir palabras y frases que los participantes puedan colgar en los lienzos. Por ejemplo: "Se dieron permiso para", "Decidieron,” "Dejaron ir ______" o cualquier otra palabra o frase que pueda ser más adecuada para su grupo específico. Si corresponde a su grupo, puede imprimir copias de las plantillas opcionales de siluetas de palabras, declaraciones, mujeres y hombres de antemano.

Una vez que los imprima, también puede recortar las palabras (vea las imágenes como referencia). Si no puede imprimirlos, puede escribirlos en una pizarra e invitar a los participantes a seleccionar los que se aplican a ellos y escribirlos en lugar de hacer un collage.

Puede imprimir las plantillas de muñecas de papel para todos los participantes, pero tenga en cuenta que no hay una forma de "uno". Si los participantes desean dibujar su propia plantilla de cuerpo, eso es genial, y podría ser empoderante. También puede imprimir las preguntas del diario (una copia por participante, más algunos extras). Es posible que desee crear una muestra con anticipación para familiarizarse con el proceso de creación, así como para mostrar a los participantes cómo puede verse la pieza de arte terminada.

Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos que cree una muestra simple utilizando solo el material que está proporcionando para que los participantes no se sientan abrumados por ningún desafío "artístico".

Como facilitador, tiene total libertad para alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento de este taller para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo específico.
warm_up_spanish:
Preguntas del diario: Puede abrir invitando a los participantes a completar las preguntas de la revista. Pueden escribir directamente en la plantilla o en una hoja aparte (si está disponible).

Quizás desee asegurarles a los participantes que su escritura es para ellos mismos y que no leerán sus respuestas en voz alta, a menos que lo deseen. También puede recordarles que pueden saltear las preguntas que no les funcionan, pero aliéntelos a tratar de mirar cada pregunta con curiosidad.

Esta es su "ventana de tiempo" para estar presente en cualquier superficie y dejar de lado cualquier culpa o vergüenza que pueda surgir. También puede animar a los participantes a que tengan especial cuidado al inventar sus frases de permiso y crear un enfoque positivo para el "Año Nuevo".

Esta expresión puede ser algo tan simple como darse permiso para simplemente respirar, o tan importante como cambiar de trabajo o comenzar una nueva relación. Algunas ideas para sus lienzos son: "Se dieron permiso para dejar entrar el amor" o "Decidieron volver a la escuela".

Si lo desea, puede reproducir música suave y relajante en el fondo durante el proceso de creación. Esto es totalmente de usted.

Compartir en grupo: Una vez que los participantes hayan tenido tiempo suficiente para completar las preguntas de la revista, puede invitarlos a elegir una de sus respuestas a las preguntas de la revista y, si se sienten cómodos, compartir con todo el grupo, enfatizando que compartir es voluntario. También pueden compartir lo que se siente al dejar de lado un pensamiento, una persona o un hábito que ya no los respalda.

O pueden compartir una de sus frases de permiso y por qué sería importante abrazar esto. Y si nadie se siente cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien. Puedes saltar a la creación.
creation_spanish:
Ahora puedes invitar a los participantes a bucear y comenzar a crear. Puede sugerir que primero pinten el fondo de su lienzo y luego piensen en su frase de permiso mientras se seca la pintura.

Dado que este es un proyecto de "medios mixtos", pueden combinar una variedad de técnicas al crear su arte: pintura, estampado y / o collage. "Lo aliento a que se dé permiso para crear su lienzo de la forma que desee. Puede hacer un collage, pintar o simplemente tener un fondo abstracto.

Es posible que desee agregar una persona como punto. Puede usar la plantilla de muñeca como guía y el collage para crear ropa a partir de diferentes patrones de bloc de notas.

También puede dibujar a su persona a mano alzada o encontrar una imagen de revista que represente el futuro que desea crear. Lo que quieras."

"Puede comenzar por elegir una frase de permiso que sea más significativa para usted. ¿Está dando permiso para tomarse más tiempo para usted en el futuro? ¿Tal vez esté decidiendo pasar más tiempo de calidad con sus hijos? O quizás quiera finalmente enfrentar ese sueño o meta que aún no ha alcanzado. Llenas el espacio en blanco. Una vez que haya decidido, puede hacer un collage de la declaración en el fondo o puede pintar para escribir su frase directamente en el lienzo. Dado que el lienzo se centra en el futuro que desea, lo aliento a que mantenga su redacción optimista y afirmativa ".

Si algunos de los participantes terminan antes que otros, puede invitarlos a revisar sus preguntas de diario. Pueden responder preguntas que no respondieron anteriormente o pueden escribir un diario sobre su creación.

También pueden crear otro lienzo, garabato o dibujo. Siéntase libre de guiar a los participantes como mejor le parezca.
closing_spanish:
Puede cerrar invitando a los participantes a compartir sus lienzos con el grupo y cualquier cosa que hayan descubierto sobre ellos mismos mientras crean.

También pueden compartir su frase de permiso en voz alta. Si hay tiempo, tiene la opción de usar "escucha de eco" donde otros miembros del grupo le repiten la frase al participante. La escucha de eco es una forma de escucha que está estructurada para ser completamente sin prejuicios.

Después de escuchar a los participantes leer su artículo, todos en la sala pueden simplemente repetir al menos una cosa que recuerden que la persona dijo, palabra por palabra, para que escuchen que toda la sala "haga eco" de sus palabras para ellos, en lugar.

Es una forma estructurada de utilizar la escucha de apoyo y fundamentar la visión del participante. También puede invitar a los participantes, si se sienten cómodos haciéndolo, a mostrar su lienzo en algún lugar donde puedan verlo todos los días, como estímulo e inspiración para mirar hacia el Año Nuevo y la esperanza.

Por supuesto, como con cualquier parte de este taller, compartir es opcional y si nadie se siente cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.
tips_spanish: Si no puede acceder a un lienzo, también puede usar papel de acuarela grueso o cartulina gruesa.
optional_materials:
• Pre-typed Words template

  • Pre-typed Statements template

  • Women's Silhouettes template

  • Men's Silhouettes template
optional_materials_spanish:
• Plantilla de siluetas de mujer
• Plantilla de siluetas de los hombres
introduction:
This workshop was written for the New Year's, but it can be used at any time during the year. The "New Year" doesn't have to be the new calendar year, it could be a "new year" of transition, hope, commitment, or any other "beginning" in a participant's life. Please feel free to alter the wording of the introduction as you see fit.

"New Year's is a time of the year that symbolizes renewal and rebirth. It's also an opportunity for us to invite ourselves to bid farewell to the concerns and problems of the past year, and prepare for a new and healthy beginning. We can focus on the things that we want more of in our lives, and look forward to the coming months with more hope, enthusiasm, and an open heart."

"Today, you'll have an opportunity to transition into the New Year in a positive way. You'll have a chance to notice how it would feel to let go of something or someone who is holding you back in your life or a habit you wish to break."

"Afterwards, if you wish to, you can give yourself permission to think about something you really want to accomplish, or a healthy habit you would like to take on. It could be learning a new instrument, creating stronger bonds with family and friends, or anything else you wish to do that can help redirect your focus from negative things, to positive things. Through journaling and painting, you will have a chance to create a canvas that gives you the affirming permission to do whatever you choose in the future."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
introduction_spanish:
Este taller fue escrito para el Año Nuevo, pero se puede usar en cualquier momento durante el año.

El "Año Nuevo" no tiene que ser el año calendario nuevo, podría ser un "año nuevo" de transición, esperanza, compromiso o cualquier otro "comienzo" en la vida de un participante. Por favor, siéntase libre de alterar la redacción de la introducción como mejor le parezca.

"El Año Nuevo es una época del año que simboliza la renovación y el renacimiento. También es una oportunidad para que nos invitemos a despedirnos de las preocupaciones y problemas del año pasado, y nos preparemos para un comienzo nuevo y saludable. Podemos centrarnos en las cosas que queremos más en nuestras vidas, y esperamos los próximos meses con más esperanza, entusiasmo y un corazón abierto ".

"Hoy, tendrá la oportunidad de hacer la transición al Año Nuevo de una manera positiva. Tendrá la oportunidad de darse cuenta de cómo se sentirá al dejar de lado algo o alguien que lo está reteniendo en su vida o en un hábito. usted desea romper ".

"Luego, si lo desea, puede darse permiso para pensar en algo que realmente desea lograr, o en un hábito saludable que le gustaría adquirir. Podría ser aprender un nuevo instrumento, crear vínculos más fuertes con la familia y los amigos. o cualquier otra cosa que desee hacer que pueda ayudar a redirigir su enfoque de cosas negativas a cosas positivas. A través del diario y la pintura, tendrá la oportunidad de crear un lienzo que le otorga el permiso para hacer lo que elija en el futuro."

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepa que esta es su ventana de tiempo. Esto significa que este puede ser un espacio seguro para notar sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades.

Durante este tiempo, no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de participar. o crear. Voy a compartir algunas instrucciones básicas, pero puedes elegir cómo quieres participar. Puede seguirlo por completo, o puede querer hacer algo diferente, depende completamente de usted. 

Durante tu ventana de tiempo, tienes total libertad para elegir. Estoy aquí para ayudarlo en todo lo que pueda, así que no dude en preguntar por lo que necesita."
demonstration:
You can paint brayer or sponge brush, then roll the paint on the bubble wrap.
Stamp bubble wrap to your canvas to give an artsy background.

You may wish to take a few minutes to explain the material to the participants.

Depending on which materials you're using, you might wish to:

  • Demonstrate how to use the materials to create textures and unique effects. You can show how to use a foam brush, sponge or brayer for blending and layering paint on bubble wrap and then transferring to canvas to create a polka dot effect.

  • Show how to use materials to create textures, shapes and tone on tone effects, by using a light dabbing motion.

  • Explain how Mod Podge can be used as glue for collaging, or as a coating to finish their art.


If you have a sample, this may be a good time to pass it around the room.
demonstration_spanish:
Es posible que desee tomarse unos minutos para explicar el material a los participantes. Dependiendo de qué materiales esté utilizando, es posible que desee: Demuestre cómo usar los materiales para crear texturas y efectos únicos.

Puede mostrar cómo usar un pincel de espuma, una esponja o un rociador para mezclar y aplicar capas de pintura en plástico de burbujas y luego transferirlo al lienzo para crear un efecto de lunares.

Muestre cómo utilizar materiales para crear texturas, formas y efectos de tono sobre tono, utilizando un movimiento ligero. Explica cómo se puede usar Mod Podge como pegamento para collaging, o como un recubrimiento para terminar su arte. Si tiene una muestra, este puede ser un buen momento para pasarla por la sala.
opening_circle:
Journal Questions:
You can open by inviting participants to fill in the journal questions. They can write directly on the template or on a separate sheet (if available). You may wish to reassure participants that their writing is for themselves and they won't be reading their answers out loud, unless they want to. You can also remind them that they can skip questions that don't work for them, but encourage them to try to look at each question with curiosity. This is their "window of time" to be present to whatever surfaces and let go of any blame or shame that may come up.

You may also wish to encourage participants to take special care in coming up with their permission phrase(s) and creating a positive focus for the "New Year." This expression can be something as simple as giving themselves permission to just breathe, or as significant as changing jobs or starting a new relationship. Some ideas for their canvases are: "They gave themselves permission to let love in" or "They decided to go back to school."

If you like, you can play soft relaxing music in the background during the creation process. This is entirely up to you.

Group Sharing:
Once participants have had ample time to fill in the journal questions, you can then invite them to pick one of their answers to the journal questions, and if they feel comfortable, to share with the whole group, emphasizing that sharing is voluntary. They can also share what it would feel like to let go of a thought, a person or a habit that no longer supports them. Or they can share one of their permission phrases and why it would be important to embrace this. And if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay. You can skip to creation.

title: Our Safe Home / Nuestro Hogar Seguro
objective: This workshop gives children an opportunity to explore what a safe home means to them and what elements go inside and around it to make it feel safe through the creation of a "safe home" book.
materials:
•  
    Our Safe Home material and sample set-up  

    Construction paper

  • Markers

  • Colored pens and/or pencils

  • White Elmer's Glue

  • Glue sticks

  • Glitter glue

  • Puffy paint

  • Assorted ribbon, yarn, pipe cleaners (either or all of these work for binding)

  • Assorted flowers

  • Foam shapes

  • Scissors

  • Hole punchers
setup:
Depending on the age group, you may consider cutting out the house templates and even writing the questions on them (see creation) beforehand. Ideally, however, the children would do this as it's part of the creation process. This is up to you.

You can also write the creation questions on the board, or anywhere visible to all so children can copy.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance for children to see what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample so that children aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
"I'd like to invite you to join me in a brief warm-up exercise. Remember, if you prefer to use this time to do something else, that's okay too. This is your time and you get to choose however you want to spend it. For those of you who wish to participate, in a minute, I'm going to ask you a few questions and I invite you to just think about what the questions are asking. There are no right or wrong answers to these questions and whatever pops into your mind, thoughts, feelings, image or anything, will be perfect. Later, you can reflect back on your thoughts as you create your safe home books. Any questions before we get started?"

You can invite the children to get in a comfortable position. They can close their eyes or keep them open. However they're most comfortable. You may consider speaking slowly and in a soft tone and allowing children ample time to reflect on each question.

"For those of you who wish to participate, what does a safe home look like to you? Maybe it is full of pictures from the good and happy times? Maybe it is full of smiling faces? Maybe it is full of people or it just has the people you want there? Maybe it's just you there."

"What does a safe home feel like? Maybe it is a place you are happy to return to at the end of the day. Maybe it is warm and cozy. Maybe you can freely share your feelings, hopes and dreams there. Maybe it is a place where you feel happy, loved, and relaxed."

"What does a safe home sound like? Maybe there are no loud voices or bad words. Maybe people are happy and laughing. Maybe it is quiet and peaceful or maybe music is playing and everyone is singing. Think about what you would like to hear in your safe home."

"How do you want to be treated and treat others in your home? Maybe you'd like a hug when you get home from a long day of school. Maybe it's important to you for everyone to say 'please' and 'thank you.' I encourage you to think about what you could do to help treat others the way they'd like to be treated in your home, too."

"How can you family work together to create a safe home? What small steps can you take to work toward making your home feel safe to you?"
creation:
Once children have had a chance to reflect on their thoughts about what a happy and safe home means to them, you can then invite them to create. You can share the following creation steps with them and pass around your sample at this time and invite them to create. You may also choose to create along with them. Whatever works best for you and your group.

Depending on the age group, we are offering alternate options for creation (see bottom of creation section).

 

      
  Step 2: Cutting the folded lines

Step 1: Creating the House Template
"You can begin by folding a sheet of construction paper, length-wise, in half. You can use any color paper you like. You get to create six of these, each acting as a page for your "safe home" book. You can use same color for all pages, or different colors. It's entirely up to you. Once you have folded the paper in half vertically, you can fold two corners over to the centerfold and cut along these corner fold lines. Now, you have a template to create the rest of the pages in your safe home book."


Step 2: Cutting Out All the Pages
"You can use the template you just created to trace and cut 5 more home shapes, or pages for your book. Again, you are free to use any color paper you like for each of your pages."
 

      
  Step 3: Writing Safe Home Questions

Step 3: Reflecting on Safe Home Questions
"Next, you may write down the following questions, one on each page, at the top of each house shape and leave one house page blank. The blank page will be the front of your book, it can be the house you get to decorate shortly. Take as much time as you need to reflect on these questions and write them down. Remember, there are no right or wrong answers. Only what is right for you."

(You can write these questions on a board for everyone to see, and invite them to write them, or you can read them to the children).

  • "Page 1 - Leave blank to decorate later."

  • "Page 2 - What does a safe home look like?"

  • "Page 3 - What does a safe home feel like?"

  • "Page 4 - What does a safe home sound like?"

  • "Page 5 - How do we treat each other inside our home?"

  • "Page 6 - How are we going to work together to create our Safe Home?"
     

      
  Step 4: Binding the pages

Step 4: Binding the Pages
"When you have your pages written out, you can align these pages with one another and punch holes along the left-hand side. Remember to put your blank page at the front as the cover of your book. Once you've done that, you can lace a ribbon, yarn, pipe cleaner (or any other binding material you've provided) through the holes and tie them to create binding. If you prefer, you can simply staple the pages papers together. It's entirely up to you."


Step 5: Decorating the Cover
"Next, you get a chance to decorate your cover page. If you choose to do so, I'd like to encourage you to have fun. You can use any shapes, images, words, symbols, and design materials that you imagine your safe home to have on the outside. I'd like to remind you that it doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is that you've taken this time to honor your thoughts and feelings."

 

 

    
    Our Safe Home smells like...

Here are the alternate creation activities that may be better suited for your specific group.

Alternative Option For Younger Children:
Depending on the age group, you have the option to invite them to choose a piece of construction paper and draw their safe home with all of the things that make them happy, both inside and outside of the home. You can guide them by asking questions like, "What kinds of things would make you feel safe in your bedroom?" "What people would you like to see in your safe home?" "What can you draw outside of your home to make you feel safe?"

Alternative Option for Teens:
Using graphing paper, pencils, and rulers, you can invite teens to create a floor plan of their safe home and invite them to label all of the different aspects of the home (people, things, sounds, etc.) that make them feel safe. You have the option to invite them journal about "What steps can you take to make your home feel safe?"

Alternative Option for Families:
If you're working with families, one option is to invite each family member to create "My Safe Room." This can be their personal bedroom, the living room, the kitchen, or anywhere else in their house where they like to spend their time.
closing:
Our beautiful Safe Home!  

For the closing, you may give children an opportunity to share their creations and some of the ways they can make their home safe. They can also share anything they felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

If you're working with families, you may wish to remind them that if they work together, they can create this safe home in the future. You can also thank the participants for being here today.
description: Participants will be provided with an opportunity to discuss the meaning of a safe home and what goes inside and around it to make it feel that way. They will be invited to make specific commitments to creating that safety in their own homes.
objective_spanish: Este taller les brinda a las y los niños la oportunidad de explorar qué significa un hogar seguro para ellas y ellos y qué elementos van dentro y alrededor de él para que este se sienta seguro a través de la creación de un libro de "hogar seguro."

setup_spanish:
Dependiendo de la edad del grupo, puede considerar recortar las plantillas de la casa e incluso escribir las preguntas en ellas (ver creación) de antemano. Sin embargo, lo ideal es que las y los niños lo hagan ya que es parte del proceso de creación. Esto depende completamente de usted.

También puede escribir las preguntas de creación en la pizarra o en cualquier lugar visible para que todas y todos puedan copiarlas. Puede ser útil crear una muestra de antemano para que las y los niños vean cómo puede verse la pieza de arte terminada. Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos que cree una muestra simple para que las y los participantes no se sientan abrumadas ni abrumados por ningún desafío "artístico".

Como la persona que facilita este taller, usted tiene total libertad para alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento del mismo para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo específico.
warm_up_spanish:
"Me gustaría invitarles a unirse conmigo en un breve ejercicio de calentamiento. Recuerden, si prefieren usar este tiempo para hacer otra cosa, también está bien. Este es su momento y pueden decidir cómo quieren pasarlo. Para aquellas y aquellos de ustedes que desean participar, en un minuto, les voy a hacer algunas preguntas y les invito a que piensen en lo que se hacen las preguntas a ustedes mismas y mismos.

No hay respuestas correctas o incorrectas a estas preguntas y cualquier cosa que venga a su mente, ya sean pensamientos, sentimientos, imágenes o cualquier otra cosa, será perfecta. Más tarde, podrán reflexionar sobre sus pensamientos mientras crean sus libros de hogar seguro.

¿Alguna pregunta antes de que comencemos? Puede invitar a las y los niños a ponerse en una posición cómoda. Pueden cerrar los ojos o mantenerlos abiertos. Cómo sea que les haga sentir más comodidad. Puede considerar hablar lentamente y en un tono suave y permitir que las y los niños tengan tiempo suficiente para reflexionar sobre cada pregunta.

"Para aquellas y aquellos de ustedes que desean participar, ¿qué es para ustedes un hogar seguro? ¿Tal vez esté lleno de fotos de los buenos y felices momentos? ¿Tal vez esté lleno de caras sonrientes? Tal vez esté lleno de personas o simplemente esté la gente que quieren que esté. Tal vez sólo esté cada una y uno de ustedes ahí".

"¿Cómo se siente un hogar seguro? Tal vez sea un lugar al que les gustaría volver al final del día. Tal vez sea cálido y acogedor. Tal vez puedan compartir libremente sus sentimientos, esperanzas y sueños allí. Tal vez sea un lugar donde se sienten felices, amadas o amados, relajadas y relajados"

"¿Cómo suena un hogar seguro? Tal vez no haya voces fuertes o malas palabras. Tal vez la gente esté feliz y riendo. Tal vez sea tranquilo y pacífico o tal vez la música esté sonando y todo el mundo esté cantando. Piensen en lo que les gustaría escuchar en su hogar seguro ".

"¿Cómo les gustaría que les trataran en su casa? Tal vez les gustaría recibir un abrazo cuando lleguen a casa después de un largo día de clases. Tal vez sea importante para ustedes que todas y todos digan 'por favor' y 'gracias'. ' Les invito a que piensen en lo que podrían hacer para ayudar a tratar a las y los demás de la misma forma en que les gustaría que les traten en su casa".

"¿Cómo pueden trabajar junto con su familia para crear un hogar seguro? ¿Qué pequeños pasos pueden tomar para que su hogar se sienta seguro para ustedes?"
creation_spanish:
Una vez que las y los niños hayan tenido la oportunidad de reflexionar sobre sus pensamientos acerca de lo que significa un hogar feliz y seguro para cada quien, puede invitarles a crear. Puede compartir los siguientes pasos de creación con el grupo y pasar su muestra en este momento e invitarles a crear. También puede optar por crear al mismo tiempo que el grupo.

Lo que sea mejor para usted y su grupo. Dependiendo de la edad del grupo, ofrecemos opciones alternativas para la creación (ver la parte inferior de la sección de creación).

Paso 1:

Creando la Plantilla de la Casa "Pueden comenzar doblando una hoja de papel de construcción, a lo largo, por la mitad. Pueden usar cualquier papel del color que deseen. Pueden crear seis de estos, cada uno de los cuales actúa como una página para su libro de su " hogar seguro ". Pueden usar el mismo color para todas las páginas, o diferentes colores. Depende totalmente de ustedes. Una vez que hayan doblado el papel por la mitad verticalmente, pueden doblar dos esquinas al pliegue central y cortar a lo largo de estas líneas de doblez de la esquina. Ahora, tienen una plantilla para crear el resto de las páginas en su libro de hogar seguro ".

Paso 2:

Cortar todas las páginas "Pueden usar la plantilla que acaban de crear para trazar y cortar 5 formas de hogar, o páginas para su libro. Nuevamente, pueden usar cualquier papel de color que deseen para cada una de sus páginas".

Paso 3:

Reflexionando sobre las preguntas de un hogar seguro "A continuación, pueden anotar las siguientes preguntas, una en cada página, en la parte superior de cada casa y dejar en blanco una página de la casa. La página en blanco será la portada de su libro, puede ser la casa que van a decorar en breve. Tómense todo el tiempo que necesiten para reflexionar sobre estas preguntas y escríbalas. Recuerden que no hay respuestas correctas o incorrectas. Solo lo que es correcto para ustedes". (Puede escribir estas preguntas en una pizarra para que todo el grupo las vea e invitarles a escribirlas, o puede leerlas en voz alta para el grupo).

•    "Página 1 - Dejar en blanco para decorar más tarde".

•    "Página 2 - ¿Cómo se ve un hogar seguro?"

•    "Página 3 - ¿Cómo se siente un hogar seguro?"

•    "Página 4 - ¿Cómo suena un hogar seguro?"

•    "Página 5 - ¿Cómo nos tratamos entre nosotras y nosotros dentro de nuestra casa?"

•    "Página 6 - ¿Cómo vamos a trabajar juntas y juntos para crear nuestro Hogar Seguro?"

Paso 4:

Encuadernando las Páginas "Cuando tengan sus páginas escritas, pueden alinearlas entre sí y hacer agujeros en el lado izquierdo. Recuerden colocar su página en blanco en la parte frontal como la portada de su libro. Una vez que hayan hecho eso, pueden atar una cinta, un hilo, un limpiador de tuberías (o cualquier otro material de enlace que haya proporcionado) a través de los agujeros y atarlos para crear un enlace. Si lo prefieren, puede simplemente engrapar los papeles de las páginas. Todo depende de usted. "

Paso 5:

Decoración de la portada "A continuación, tendrán la oportunidad de decorar su portada. Si deciden hacerlo, me gustaría animarles a que se diviertan. Pueden usar cualquier forma, imagen, palabra, símbolo y material de diseño que imaginen que su hogar seguro tiene en el exterior. Me gustaría recordarles que no importa cómo se vea. Lo que importa es que se han tomado este tiempo para honrar sus pensamientos y sentimientos ".

Aquí están las actividades de creación alternativas que pueden ser más adecuadas para su grupo específico. Opción alternativa para las y los niños más pequeñas y pequeños: Dependiendo del grupo de edad, tiene la opción de invitarles a elegir un pedazo de papel de construcción y dibujar su hogar seguro con todas las cosas que les hacen felices, tanto dentro como fuera del hogar.

Puede guiarles haciendo preguntas como "¿Qué tipo de cosas les harían sentirse seguras y seguros en sus habitaciones?" "¿Qué personas les gustaría ver en su hogar seguro?" "¿Qué pueden dibujar fuera de su casa para que se sientan seguras y seguros?"

Opción alternativa para los adolescentes: Al usar papel cuadriculado, lápices y reglas, puede invitar a las y los adolescentes a crear un plano de su hogar seguro e invitarles a etiquetar todos los diferentes aspectos del hogar (personas, cosas, sonidos, etc.) que les hacen sentir seguras y seguros.

Tiene la opción de invitarles a escribir sobre "¿Qué pasos pueden tomar para que su hogar se sienta seguro?" Opción alternativa para las familias: Si está trabajando con familias, una opción es invitar a cada miembro de la familia a crear "Mi habitación segura".

Puede ser su dormitorio personal, la sala de estar, la cocina o cualquier otro lugar de su casa donde les guste pasar el tiempo.
closing_spanish:
Para el cierre, puede darles a las y los niños la oportunidad de compartir sus creaciones y algunas de las formas en que pueden hacer que su hogar sea seguro.

También pueden compartir todo lo que sintieron o experimentaron en el proceso de creación, o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir. Por supuesto, esto es puramente opcional y si nadie se siente cómoda o cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.

Si está trabajando con familias, puede recordarles que, si trabajan juntas y juntos, pueden crear este hogar seguro en el futuro. También puede agradecer a los participantes por estar aquí hoy.

introduction:
"Today, you have an opportunity to talk about safety and what it means to you. You'll get to reflect on what safety looks like, what it sounds like, and even what it smells like. I'm going to invite you to create a book that shows all of these different things. You'll be able to add words and drawings that say and show all of the things that make up your safe home."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
introduction_spanish:
"Hoy, tendremos la oportunidad de hablar sobre la seguridad y lo qué significa para ustedes. Podrán reflexionar sobre cómo es la seguridad, cómo suena e incluso cómo huele. Les invitaré a que creen un libro que muestre todas estas diferentes cosas. Podrán agregar palabras y dibujos que digan y muestren todas las cosas que conforman su hogar seguro ".

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que este taller es una ventana de tiempo para ustedes. Esto significa que este puede ser un espacio seguro para notar sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que digan o hagan es voluntario. Ofreceré una idea sugerida para el taller, compartiré los materiales que tenemos disponibles y les invitaré a crear, pero no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de hacerlo. No importa cómo se vea. Lo que importa es tomarse este tiempo para honrar verdaderamente sus pensamientos y sentimientos, sin importar cómo surjan. Si no pueden pensar en nada qué crear o escribir, siéntanse libres de solo observar. De cualquier forma estará perfectamente bien. Este es su momento. Por favor, pídanme lo que necesiten y sepan que estoy aquí para ayudarles".

title: Examining Relationships Collage / Examinando Relaciones Collage
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to examine and gain a better understanding of key relationships in their lives, through the creation of a collage art piece that symbolizes those relationship dynamics.
materials:
• Large Head template

  • Small Head template

  • Child Head template

  • Cardstock

  • White paper (at least 2 per participant)

  • Collage material (patterned papers / tissue papers)

  • Scissors

  • Glue sticks

  • Oil pastels (CrayPas or crayons)

  • Markers
setup:
Workshop table setup

 

You are welcome to provide any and as many decoration material you like.

You can print the three head templates on white cardstock and cut them out in advance. Participants will get to use there as stencils during creation. We recommend printing and cutting out enough of each head template for each participant to choose from.

You can lay out the supplies for each participant to have easy access.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
Scribble warm-up exercise in progress

 
     
  Representing feelings with lines and shapes

"Before we start with the creation process, I'd like to invite you to a brief warm-up exercise. If you prefer to just observe, that's perfectly okay. Observing is participating."

"Sometimes it is helpful to move your body because we store many of our emotions there. Sometimes these emotions become so suppressed and repressed that we don't even have access to them anymore because they are so deeply buried."


You can invite participants to pick up any color oil pastel or crayon, and begin making large circular scribbles on their white paper. You can encourage them to experience the simple motion of using their hands and arms by engaging their shoulder to slowly make random circular scribbles. This can help them to try and "get out of their heads" and quiet their internal chatter or self-talk. You can allow participants to do this for half a minute or so until you feel that everyone is focusing on the scribble motion and becoming more present.

Next, you can invite them to add to their scribble by picking up another color and use their non-dominant hand to make fast and angular motions. Then, using both hands together, they can make either angular or circular motions using the two colors next to each other.

Next, you can welcome participants to use lines, shapes and colors to represent their feelings so that the line serves as a metaphor. We recommend that you start with common emotions like "anger" or "sadness," and then transition to more complex feelings like "jealousy."

For example, you can ask participants to select a color that represents 'anger' to them, then show "how I feel when I'm angry." That is, how would my anger look as a line or shape using oil pastels on the paper. You can invite participants to turn their papers over and "doodle" a line or shape that represents how those feelings would look to them.

Some sample feelings you may prompt for this warm-up include: angry; sad; afraid; confused; jealous; nervous/anxious, etc. You can continue to give feelings prompts until you sense they are ready to move onto the creation.
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create to the following creation process. You may wish to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create or participate. They are free to use the art supplies and this time however they wish.

 

     
  Silhouettes representing the relationship dynamic

 
 
  Creating a collage




 
 
  Coloring the collage


 

Step 1:
"For those of you who want to create, you can start by selecting one relationship in your life you'd like to focus on today. Through the collage creating process, we can represent a relationship between ourselves and another person(s) that is in conflict or a relationship that is not the way you want it to be. We all have people in our lives who we would like to change our relationship with. This constantly changes; maybe you were feeling great about your relationship with your daughter last week but today you are really mad at her. This relationship might be one that ebbs and flows. Maybe you think: 'I love my daughter, but whenever we talk about money, we have an argument.' If you like, pick a relationship that comes to mind that you would like to work on examining today."


Step 2:
"Next, you can select two colored or patterned papers; one to represent you in your relationship, and one to represent the other person. Or, you could choose one side of yourself versus the other. You can use your head template(s) to trace profile heads on to colored or patterned papers. After tracing the template, you can cut out each head. Now you have two or more heads representing the roles in the relationships. The head templates are in profile so that you can choose to place them looking at each other or looking away from each other."


You may want to hold up the heads at the same time and demonstrate a few of the variety of ways that the heads can face. The direction they are facing and their placement on the paper can represent the conflict.


Step 3:
"You can then decide how you'd like to glue down your heads in a way that reflects the current relationship. You can place them in a way that represents the relationship dynamic. For instance, facing each other, turning away from each other, one facing the other and the other turning away, etc. The possibilities for where you place these heads are endless. How you choose to demonstrate your relationship is totally unique to the reality of it in your life and completely up to you. There is no right or wrong way to express it."

 

Step 4:
"Finally, you can use any and as many of the art supplies provided to decorate your art piece in any way that you like to represent the conflict relationship. You can draw images, shapes, use colors, write words, or you may want to add symbols of your relationship. I encourage you to work from your instincts and cut, glue, scribble and/or draw anything that feels right at the moment. Remember, there is no right or wrong to create or participate."
closing:
Relationship collage with many heads



 

"Each of you has bravely taken the opportunity to be present in the workshop today. We honor how challenging it can be to try to uncover painful feelings that you may not feel comfortable expressing or sharing. You'll get the opportunity to volunteer and express any feelings that this exercise evoked."


You can invite participants to share if the Examining Relationships Collage helped them to better understand their relationship, anything they noticed or learned from taking a deeper look at their relationship, or anything else they may wish to share.

You can close by thanking the participants for bravely taking this window of time to notice their relationships that have been significant to them and for honoring their choice to share verbally or participate via observing.


Optional Closing Exercise:
If time permits, you can invite participants to think and journal on the back of their creations about their next steps in moving forward.


Optional Closing Discussion:
"Now that we have examined our relationships, we can start to think about what can we do about them. What do we need in order to have a healthy relationship with ourselves and others? How do we advocate for what we need in our relationships? How can we continue to meet these needs in our future relationships? Is it possible that this is a relationship that you need to let go?"

You can generate a discussion with the participants about what the next step is and encourage them to use this "call to action" as homework. To help facilitate this conversation, you can refer to the Relationship Boundaries handouts.
description: The participants will take the time to deeply look at the relationships in their lives and notice what they mean to them, why they look the way they do, and why they are in them. By exploring a strained relationship, the participants will examine the dynamic and how the relationship and roles function.

Participantes podrán usar estas plantillas durante la creación.

"Antes de comenzar con el proceso de creación, me gustaría invitarte a un breve ejercicio de calentamiento. Si prefieres observar, está perfectamente bien. Observar es participar".

"A veces es útil mover tu cuerpo porque almacenamos muchas de nuestras emociones allí. Hay veces que estas emociones se reprimen y reprimen tanto que ya no tenemos acceso a estas porque están profundamente enterradas".

Invitar a todo participante a que escojan cualquier color pastel o crayón al óleo y empiecen a hacer grandes garabatos circulares en su papel blanco. Puede animarles a experimentar el simple movimiento de usar sus manos y brazos haciendo que sus hombros se muevan haciendo garabatos circulares al azar. Esto puede ayudarles a tratar de "salirse de sus cabezas" y acallar su conversación interna o dialogo. Puedes permitir que todos nosotros/nosotras como participantes hagan esto durante aproximadamente medio minuto hasta que sientas que cada participante se están enfocando en el movimiento del garabato y se estén concentrando.

A continuación, ustedes podrán agregar su garabato escogiendo otro color y usar su mano no dominante para hacer movimientos rápidos y angulares. Luego, usando ambas manos juntas, pueden hacer movimientos angulares o circulares usando los dos colores uno al lado del otro.

A continuación, puedes invitar a todo participante a usar líneas, formas y colores para representar sus sentimientos, de modo que la línea sirva de metáfora. Recomendamos comenzar con emociones comunes como "ira" o "tristeza", y luego pasar a sentimientos más complejos como los "celos". Por ejemplo, puede pedirle a cada participante a que seleccionen un color que represente el "enojo" para luego mostrarles "cómo me siento cuando estoy enojado". Es decir, ¿cómo se vería mi enojo como una línea o forma usando pasteles al óleo sobre el papel?

Puede invitar a cada participante a voltear sus papeles y "garabatear" una línea o forma que represente cómo nosotros/nosotras mismas/mismos veríamos esos sentimientos. Algunos ejemplos de sentimientos que puede pedir para este calentamiento incluyen: el enojo; tristeza; temer; confusión; celos; nervios / ansiedad, etc.

Puedes continuar dando indicaciones de sentimientos hasta que sientas que están listos/listas para avanzar hacia la creación.
creation_spanish:
Ahora puede invitarlos/invitarlas a todos si desean pasar al siguiente proceso de creación. Tal vez quiera recordarles que no existe una forma correcta o incorrecta de crear o participar. Son libres de usar los materiales de arte y esta vez como quieran.            

Paso 1:
"Para quienes quieran crear, pueden comenzar por seleccionar una relación en su vida en la que les gustaría centrarse hoy. A través del proceso de creación de collage, podemos representar una relación entre nosotros y otra persona (s) que está en conflicto, o una relación que no es la forma en que usted quiere que sea. Todos tenemos personas en nuestras vidas con quien nos gustaría cambiar nuestra relación. Esto cambia constantemente; tal vez te sentiste bien con la relación con tu hija/hijo la semana pasada, pero hoy estás realmente enojado con ella/él. Esta relación puede ser una que va y viene. Tal vez pienses: 'Amo a mi hija, pero cuando hablamos de dinero, tenemos una discusión'. Si lo desea, elija una relación que le venga a la mente y le gustaría trabajar en la examinación de hoy. "

Paso 2:
"A continuación, puede seleccionar dos papeles de colores o con dibujos; uno para representarte en tu relación y otro para representar a la otra persona. O bien, podría elegir un lado de usted en contra de otro/otra. Puede usar su (s) plantilla (s) de cabeza para trazar las cabezas de perfil en papeles de colores o con dibujos. Después de trazar la plantilla, puede recortar cada cabeza. Ahora tienes dos o más cabezas que representan los roles en las relaciones. Las plantillas de cabezas están en el perfil para que pueda elegir ubicarlas mirándose unas a otras o apartarlas una/uno de otro/otra. " Es posible que desee sostener las cabezas al mismo tiempo y demostrar algunas de las diversas formas en que las cabezas pueden mirarse. La dirección en que se muestran y su ubicación en el papel pueden representar el conflicto.

Paso 3:
"Luego puede decidir cómo desea pegar sus cabezas de una manera que refleje la relación actual. Puedes colocarlos de una manera que represente la relación dinámica. Por ejemplo, uno/una frente al otro/otra, alejándose uno/una del otro, uno/una frente al otro y el otro alejándose, etc. Las posibilidades de dónde coloque estas cabezas son infinitas. La forma en que elija demostrar que su relación es totalmente única a la realidad de la misma en su vida y depende completamente de usted. No hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de expresarlo”.  

Paso 4:
"Finalmente, puede utilizar cualquiera y tanto de los materiales artísticos provistos para decorar su obra de arte de la forma en que desee para representar el conflicto en la relación. Puede dibujar imágenes, formas, usar colores, escribir palabras o puede desear agregar símbolos de su relación. Le doy ánimo a trabajar desde sus instintos y cortar, pegar, garabatear y / o dibujar cualquier cosa que la/lo haga sentir bien en este momento.  Recuerde, no hay bien o mal para crear o participar.”
closing_spanish:
"Cada uno de ustedes ha tomado valientemente la oportunidad de estar presente en el taller de hoy. Honramos que tan difícil pudo haber sido el tratar de descubrir sentimientos dolorosos que quizás no se sienta cómodo al expresando o compartirlo. Tendrá la oportunidad de ser voluntario/a y expresar cualquier sentimiento que evoque este ejercicio”.

Puede invitar a todos los/las participantes a compartir si el Collage de Examinación de Relaciones les ayudó a comprender mejor su relación, cualquier cosa que notaron o aprendieron al profundizar en su relación o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir.

Puede terminar agradeciendo a todos las/los participantes por participar en esta ventana de tiempo valientemente para notar sus relaciones que han sido importantes para ellos y por honrar su elección para compartir verbalmente o participar a través de la observación.

Ejercicio de cierre opcional: si el tiempo lo permite, puede invitarlos a pensar y escribir en el reverso de sus creaciones los pasos a seguir hacia adelante.

Discusión final opcional: "Ahora que hemos examinado nuestras relaciones, podemos empezar a pensar qué podemos hacer acerca de estas. ¿Qué necesitamos para tener una relación saludable con nosotros mismos y con los demás? ¿Cómo podemos abogar por lo que necesitamos en nuestras relaciones? ¿Cómo podemos seguir satisfaciendo estas necesidades en nuestras relaciones futuras? ¿Es posible que esta sea una relación que deba dejar ir? " Usted puede generar una discusión con todo participante sobre cuál es el próximo paso y animarlos para usar este" llamando a la acción "como tarea.

Para ayudar a facilitar esta conversación, Puede consultar los folletos de Límites de relaciones.

introduction:
Examining Relationships Collage with opposite facing heads

 

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

"In life, we encounter countless relationships. Whether the relationship is simply that of acquaintance with our mailman, the deep relationship we share with our family or friends, or the relationship that we have with ourselves. All of these relationships are significant and have a role in our lives. While we may act differently and play different parts in each of our relationships, it is essential that these relationships are healthy."

"Relationships can be challenging and wonderful for various reasons. It is important that we take the time to deeply look at the relationships in our lives and re-examine what they mean to us, why they look the way they do, and why we are in them."

"In domestic violence, an abusive person often uses destructive behaviors that can negatively impact relationships on many levels. Abuse can make trust, communication, joy, safety, and shared dreams with anyone seem impossible and unattainable. Even in non-violent relationships there can be chaos and conflict. Then again, sometimes the most challenging and conflicted relationship in life is the one that we have with ourselves. We all have had at least one relationship, past or current, that is conflicted or painful."

"The idea of looking at these relationships can be intimidating and challenging. It can be difficult to make the time or space to allow ourselves to do this. In this workshop, rather than jumping to 'repair' strained or broken relationships, you'll get a chance to examine them. In doing so, you might find that sometimes the only way to 'fix' a broken relationship is letting it go. You might also notice that there are relationships that are important to mend and heal in order to be happy and healthy. Today, you are invited to take the time to pick one conflicted relationship you would like to work on."
introduction_spanish:
"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepas que ésta es su ventana de tiempo. Esto significa que éste puede ser un espacio seguro para notar sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Puesto que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que dice o hace es voluntario. Durante éste tiempo, no hay ninguna forma correcta o incorrecta de participar o crear.

Voy a compartir algunas instrucciones básicas, pero puedes elegir cómo quieres participar. Puedes seguir por completo éstas o puedes elegir para hacer algo diferente, depende completamente de usted. Durante su ventana de tiempo, usted tiene total libertad para elegir. Sin embargo, la elección de pasar este tiempo estará perfectamente bien. Estoy aquí para apoyarle en cualquier manera en lo que pueda. Así que por favor no dude en preguntar por lo que necesite”.

"En la vida, nos encontramos con innumerables relaciones. Ya sea que la relación sea simplemente una relación con nuestro cartero, la relación profunda que compartimos con nuestra familia o amigos, o la relación que tenemos con nosotros mismos. Todas estas relaciones son significativas y tienen un rol en nuestras vidas. 

Sin embargo podemos actuar de manera diferente y desempeñar diferentes roles en cada una de nuestras relaciones y es esencial que estas relaciones sean saludables”.

"Las relaciones pueden ser maravillosas y desafiantes por varias razones. Es importante que nos tomemos el tiempo para analizar profundamente estas relaciones en nuestras vidas y volver a examinar lo que significan para nosotros/nosotras, por qué se ven así y por qué estamos en ésta."

"En la violencia doméstica, una persona frecuentemente es la abusiva, usa comportamientos destructivos que pueden impactar negativamente las relaciones en varios niveles. El abuso puede hacer que la confianza, la comunicación, la alegría, la seguridad y aunque los sueños compartidos con alguna persona parezcan imposibles e inalcanzables. Incluso en las relaciones no violentas, puede que haya problemas y conflicto. Por otra parte, a veces la relación más desafiante y conflictiva en la vida es la que tenemos con nosotros mismos. Todos hemos tenido al menos una relación, pasada o actual, que es conflictiva o dolorosa”.

"La idea de considerar estas relaciones puede ser intimidante y desafiante. Puede ser difícil hacer el tiempo o el espacio para permitirnos hacer esto. En este taller, en lugar de tratar de" reparar "las relaciones tensas o destrozada, tenga la oportunidad de examinarlas. Al hacerlo, podría encontrar que a veces la única manera de "arreglar" una relación destrozada es dejarla ir. También puede notar que hay relaciones que son importantes para reparar y sanar para poder ser feliz y saludable. Hoy, les invitamos a tomar el tiempo para elegir una relación conflictiva en la que te gustaría trabajar”.

title: Feelings Target Warm-up
objective: This workshop warm-up helps children notice and express their feelings, and encourages group bonding.
materials:
• Feeling face template (multiple expressions)

  • Feeling face template (Black and White)

  • Pennies or small sandbag

 

     
Feeling Face Template (Color)     Feeling Face Template (Black & White)
setup: Using the templates provided, you may wish to print out the feelings faces. You might want to print more than one set. You can cut the circles out and glue them onto paper plates in advance, or you may give the children an opportunity to cut them out themselves and glue them on themselves. You also have the option to just draw and print blank circles and give children a chance to draw their own expressions. This is entirely up to you.
warm_up:
“Today I'd like to invite you to play a game where you will each have a chance to share your feelings. When we talk about our feelings, whether they are ones we like or ones that are difficult for us, it gives us the freedom to be ourselves and notice what's alive for us. If you don't feel comfortable sharing or even participating, that's perfectly okay. You can use this time any way you like."

You may wish to let children know that we all have many different feelings, and even sometimes we feel all of these emotions simultaneously. In one day, we can feel joyful, upset, angry, and proud. Remember, that while many of these feelings may seem uncomfortable, strange, challenging, or frustrating, it is useful to acknowledge each and every one of them.

To begin, you can invite the first participant to stand a few feet away from the plates (if you have prepared them in advance) and toss a penny/sandbag towards them. If the penny/sandbag lands on a face, the participant have an opportunity to share a story about the last time (or any time) they felt that particular feeling. For example, if the penny lands on the “happy” face, the participant can share about the last time (or anytime) they felt happy. Depending on the size of the group, you may allow the children to talk for at least one minute. If the penny/sandbag lands between two feelings, the participant has the choice to talk about either one of the feelings (you can move the penny/sandbag on top of the feeling the participant will be talking about). The other children can practice listening as each person shares. Ideally, each participant has had an opportunity to take a turn or pass. If there’s time, you can go around a second or third time. You have complete freedom to adapt or alter any part of this exercise to best suit your needs.

You also have the option to ask who wishes to share, then toss them the bean bag, to avoid selecting the children as opposed to them volunteering. 

You can also incorporate more embodied art into the warm-up by giving children the option to make a statue of the feeling instead of sharing verbally. For example, you might say, "Another option is that instead of talking, you can show us an image (statue) of that emotion. For example, here's what I look like when I'm nervous:" you can create a statue with your body, perhaps by hiding your face behind your hands and crouching down. Again, it's entirely up to you. 

If it’s feasible, you can also do this warm up outside.
description: This activity is a playful way to allow participants to share about a time they felt a feeling in a group setting. This workshop helps the children to notice the spectrum of feelings and that all children feel all of the different emotions. This warm-up can stand alone as workshop or can be used to support other workshops.
notes: Note: This warm-up can stand alone as a workshop or can be used to support other workshops.
tips: You may consider sharing with the youth the benefits of moving their bodies in playful and safe ways. By sharing this information with them, you empower them to feel a sense of ownership over their bodies expressions. For more about embodied art workshops and how to introduce them in your groups, you can see Introduction to Embodied Art Workshops.
optional_materials:
• Paper plates (as a base to glue the faces on)

  • Timer
