title: Turning Over A New Leaf / Dando la vuelta a una nueva hoja
objective: To give participants an opportunity to reflect on their past and turn it over, transforming it into a new leaf, and a new life.
materials:
Optional printable worksheet

  • Large and medium size cardstock

  • Acrylic iridescent paint

  • Paint brushes

  • Paint Palettes or plates/bowls

  • Puff paints

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print copies out for your participants beforehand depending on the setting.
setup:
Depending on your time restraints, you may wish to cut out leaves for your participants ahead of time, as this can take time out of your workshop. This is entirely up to you. You may also consider creating a sample leaf in advance to show participants. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample using only the material you're providing so that participants won't feel overwhelmed with any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
Completed New Leaf with poem
 

You can use our meditation exercise, or your own. It's entirely up to you. The idea is to give participants a chance to relax and get in touch with their thoughts and feelings in a safe space. If you choose to do one, we suggest speaking in a soft, slow tone and pausing where it feels right.

"I would now like to invite you to join me in a brief mediation. For those of you who wish to participate, I would like to invite you to get in a comfortable position. You can stay seated with your feet flat on the floor and your hands relaxed on your lap, or you can lie down. If you like, you may close your eyes, or keep them open... however you're most comfortable..."

"Now, take in a deep, slow breath, and let it out. Take in another deep breath and imagine you are taking in the fall wind...and as you exhale, try to pretend you are the fall wind blowing away all the old leaves still left on the tree.... Continue to take in deep, soothing, and transforming fall wind breaths... and with each exhale, blow away the old leaves... Now, I invite you to imagine you are a leaf still on the tree... shake your head... your shoulders... your arms... your hips... your legs... and your feet. Shake your old self and your old leaves off the tree. Shake off all the old... all the past. Now, as your old leaf falls to the floor, imagine yourself changing colors... imagine your new color. What color do you see? What does your color mean? What does it represent? As you are turning over your old leaf, what does your new leaf, your new life, look like? Now, try to hang onto this new life, new colors... When you feel relaxed and ready, you can open your eyes and come back to this room."
creation:
Completed "Old Leaf"

"For those of you who wish to create, I'd like to now invite you to start by decorating one side of your leaf to reflect your past, and what you wish to leave behind. After you have completed the old side of your leaf that represents your past, you may then turn over your leaf, and begin to picture, in your mind's eyes, all of the colors, shapes, symbols, words and images that represent your new life. This is the life you choose to live. I'd like to encourage you to be bold and allow your mind to open up to the infinite amount of possibilities that your future holds. You are free to choose any colors, and any of the materials provided to decorate your leaf however you like. Remember, there is no right or wrong way to create, and it doesn't matter what your leaf looks like. What matters is that you're taking this time to acknowledge your past, honor your feelings, and take what you've learned into the future that you will create for yourself. When you are ready, you may begin."
closing: For the closing, you can invite the participants to share something about their leaf and what they experienced during the workshop. You may also invite them to share how it felt to reflect on their past, examine their present life, look to their future, and turn over a new leaf. Of course, this is optional and if no one wants to share, it's perfectly okay.
description: This workshop allows participants to turn over a new leaf when they let go of the power and control their abusive partner had on their past and allow themselves to re-design their life and re-define who they are.
objective_spanish: Dar a las y los participantes la oportunidad de reflexionar sobre su pasado y darle la vuelta, transformándolo en una nueva hoja y una nueva vida.
materials_spanish:
• Cartulina de tamaño grande y mediano.
  • Pintura acrílica 
  • Pinceles
  • Paletas de pintura o platos / copitas
  • Pinturas de relieve
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 5 min
Apertura: 10
Calentamiento: 10 min
Creación: 45 min
Cierre: 10 min
Total: 1:25 hora
setup_spanish:
Dependiendo del tiempo que tenga disponible para el taller, es posible que desee recortar las hojas para sus participantes con anticipación, ya que esto puede quitarle tiempo a su taller.

Esto depende totalmente de usted. También puede considerar crear una hoja de muestra por adelantado para mostrar a las y los participantes como se ve el arte terminado.

Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos que cree una muestra simple y utilizando solo el material que está proporcionando para que las y los participantes no se sientan abrumadas o abrumados con ningún desafío "artístico".

Como la persona que facilita este taller, usted tiene total libertad para alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento de este taller para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo específico.
warm_up_spanish:
Puede usar nuestro ejercicio de meditación, o uno suyo. Depende totalmente de usted. La idea es darles a las y los participantes la oportunidad de relajarse y ponerse en contacto con sus pensamientos y sentimientos en un espacio seguro. Si elige hacer un ejercicio de meditación, le sugerimos hablar en un tono suave y lento y hacer pausas donde lo sienta pertinente.

"Ahora me gustaría invitarles a unirse conmigo en una breve mediación. Para aquellas o aquellos de ustedes que deseen participar, me gustaría invitarles a estar en una posición cómoda. Pueden permanecer sentadas o sentados con los pies apoyados en el piso y sus manos relajadas en sus regazos, o pueden recostarse. Si quieren, pueden cerrar los ojos o mantenerlos abiertos... como sea sientan más comodidad ... "

"Ahora, respiren hondo y lento y dejen salir el aire. Respiren hondo de nuevo e imaginen que están inhalando el viento del otoño... y al exhalar, traten de pretender que son el viento otoñal que sopla todo el aire y tira las hojas viejas de los arboles... Continúen tomando respiraciones profundas, calmadas y transformadoras de viento otoñal... y con cada exhalación, tiran las hojas viejas en los arboles... Ahora, les invito a imaginar que son una hoja aún en el árbol ... sacudan lentamente su cabeza... sus hombros... sus brazos... sus caderas... sus piernas... y sus pies. Sacudan su viejo yo y sus viejas hojas de árbol. Sacudan todo lo viejo... todo el pasado. Ahora, mientras sus hojas viejas caen al piso, imagínense como ustedes van cambiando de color... imaginen su nuevo color. ¿Qué color ven? ¿Qué significa su color? ¿A qué se debe? ¿Cómo se ve su nueva hoja, su nueva vida, ahora? Intenten aferrarse a esta nueva vida, nuevos colores... Cuando se sientan relajadas o relajados y estén listas o listos, pueden abrir sus ojos y regresar conmigo a esta habitación."
creation_spanish:
"Para las personas que desean crear, me gustaría invitarles a comenzar por decorar un lado de su hoja que refleje su pasado y lo que desean dejar atrás.

Después de haber completado el lado antiguo de su hoja que representa su pasado, entonces pueden voltear su hoja y comenzar a imaginar en su mente, todos los colores, formas, símbolos, palabras e imágenes que representan su nueva vida.

Esta es la vida que eligen vivir. Me gustaría animarles a que sean audaces y permitir que sus mentes se abran con infinitas posibilidades de lo que ofrece su futuro. Son libres de elegir cualquier color, y cualquiera de los materiales proporcionados para decorar sus hojas como quieran. Recuerden, no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de crear, y no importa cómo se vean sus hojas.

Lo que importa es que estén tomando este tiempo para reconocer su pasado, honrar sus sentimientos y llevar lo que han aprendido  al futuro que están creando para ustedes. Cuando estén listas o listos, pueden comenzar."
closing_spanish: Para el cierre, puede invitar a las y los participantes a compartir algo sobre sus hojas y lo que experimentaron durante el taller. También puede invitarles a compartir cómo se sintieron al reflexionar sobre su pasado, examinar su vida actual, mirar su futuro y darle la vuelta a una nueva hoja. Por supuesto, esto es opcional y si nadie quiere compartir, está perfectamente bien.
optional_materials:
• Puff paints

  • Glitter glue

  • Scissors

  • Magazine cutouts (for collaging; we recommend Oprah and travel magazines as they tend to have more inclusive words and imagery).

  • Sequins or medallions

  • Fall themed scrapbooking accessories
optional_materials_spanish:
• Pinturas de relieve
  • Pegamento con brillantina
  • Tijeras
  • Recortes de revistas (para hacer collage; recomendamos la revista Oprah y las revistas de viajes, ya que tienden a tener palabras e imágenes más inclusivas).
  • Lentejuelas o medallones
  • Material temático de otoño para hacer scrapbooks
introduction:
Completed New Leaf  

"Each fall, leaves turn breathtaking shades of orange, purple, red, yellow and brown in a fantastic show of nature's glory. But why do leaves change color? Although Jack Frost gets most of the credit, the scientific reason for our beautiful fall foliage is a process called photoperiodism. As the sun moves further south, the hours of daylight shorten and the temperatures fall. This causes leaves to cease production of chlorophyll, the chemical that colors the leaves green. As the chlorophyll disappears, the underlying colors of the leaves are unmasked. The next strongest pigment becomes dominant giving the leaves a 'new' color."

"Often times, because of a traumatic experience, we are not able to be the person we want to be, or spend our time how we want, or design our lives the way we want. It's important to be able to begin a new season in our lives and allow our true colors to shine. As we shed the colors of our past we are able to re-establish who we are, and what we want in our lives. Today you'll have a chance to decorate one side of a leaf to represent your past and then 'turn over a new leaf' and decorate the opposite side to represent your new life, the way you want it to be."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. It's a time for you to focus on your thoughts, needs and feelings. title: Turning Over A New Leaf
objective: To give children an opportunity to reflect on their past and turn it over, transforming it into a new leaf, and a new life.
materials:
Optional printable worksheet

  • Large and medium size cardstock

  • Acrylic iridescent paint

  • Paint brushes

  • Paint Palettes or plates/bowls

  • Puff paints

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print copies out for your participants beforehand depending on the setting.
setup:
Depending on your time restraints, you may wish to cut out leaves for the children ahead of time, as this can take time out of your workshop. This is entirely up to you. You may also consider creating a sample leaf in advance to show them. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample using only the material you're providing so that children won't feel overwhelmed with any "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You can use our meditation exercise, or your own. It's entirely up to you. The idea is to give children a chance to relax and get in touch with their thoughts and feelings in a safe space. If you choose to do one, we suggest speaking in a soft, slow tone and pausing where it feels right.

"I would now like to invite you to join me in a brief mediation. For those of you who wish to participate, I would like to invite you to stand up like a tall tree. If you feel more comfortable seated, that's perfectly okay. However you feel comfortable. Now, try to take in a deep breath and let it out. Take in another deep breath... and imagine you are taking in the fall wind, and as you exhale, pretend you are the fall wind blowing away all the old leaves still left on the tree... Continue to take in deep, soothing fall wind breaths and blow away the old leaves. Now, pretend you are a leaf still on the tree... shake your head... your shoulders... your arms... your hips... your legs... and your feet. Shake your old self and your old leaves off the tree. Shake off all the old, all the past. Now, as your old leaf falls to the floor, imagine yourself changing colors. Imagine your new color... what color do you see? Are there any other images that come to your mind when you think about turning a new leaf? Now, try to hang onto this new life, new colors... when you feel relaxed and ready, you can return to your seat."
creation:
Completed "Old Leaf"

"For those of you who wish to create, I'd like to now invite you to start by decorating one side of your leaf to represent your past, and what you wish to leave behind. After you have completed the old side of your leaf that represents your past, you may then turn over your leaf, and begin to picture, in your mind's eyes, all of the colors, shapes, symbols, words and images that represent your new life. This is the life you choose to live. I'd like to encourage you to be bold and allow your mind to open up to the infinite amount of possibilities that your future holds. You are free to choose any colors, and any of the materials provided to decorate your leaf however you like. Remember, there is no right or wrong way to create, and it doesn't matter what your leaf looks like. What matters is that you're taking this time to acknowledge your past, honor your feelings, and take what you've learned into the future that you will create for yourself. When you are ready, you may begin."
closing: For the closing, you can invite the children to share something about their leaf and what they experienced during the workshop. You may also invite them to share how it felt to reflect on their past, examine their present life, look to their future, and turn over a new leaf. Of course, this is optional and if no one wants to share, it's perfectly okay.
description:
To provide children with the opportunity to think of their old leaves (past) and turn it over, transforming it into a new leaf, and a new life.
 Keep in mind this is a workshop can be done in one or two sessions. Doing this workshop in one session requires prep time.

introduction:
Completed New Leaf  

"Each fall, leaves turn breathtaking shades of orange, purple, red, yellow and brown in a fantastic show of nature's glory. But why do leaves change color? Although Jack Frost gets most of the credit, the scientific reason for our beautiful fall foliage is a process called photoperiodism. As the sun moves further south, the hours of daylight shorten and the temperatures fall. This causes leaves to cease production of chlorophyll, the chemical that colors the leaves green. As the chlorophyll disappears, the underlying colors of the leaves are unmasked. The next strongest pigment becomes dominant giving the leaves a 'new' color."

"Often times, because of a traumatic experience, we are not able to be the person we want to be, or spend our time how we want, or design our lives the way we want. It's important to be able to begin a new season in our lives and allow our true colors to shine. As we shed the colors of our past we are able to re-establish who we are, and what we want in our lives. Today you'll have a chance to decorate one side of a leaf to represent your past and then 'turn over a new leaf' and decorate the opposite side to represent your new life, the way you want it to be."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. It's a time for you to focus on your thoughts, needs and feelings. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

title: Queen of the World
objective: This workshop aims to empower participants to envision a world in which they are in charge, through the creation of a crown that symbolizes their power in that world.
materials:
• Card stock crowns

  • Scissors

  • Glue

  • Magazines (Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Stickers

  • Markers (various colors)

  • Colored pencils

  • Sequins

  • "Queen of the World" poem by Beatrice Schenk de Regniers
setup:
You are welcome to supply your favorite decoration material, in addition to what we have suggested.

You can print one copy of the poem for to read to the group during the meditation, or print a copy for each participant. It's up to you.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You are welcome to use our suggested meditation or use your own. We have found that guided meditations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.
 

"I'd like to invite you to join me in a meditation, to center ourselves in the moment. If you prefer to just observe, or do something else during this time, that's perfectly okay. This is your window of time."

"For those of you who wish to follow along, I invite you to get in a comfortable position. You can put you can close your eyes if you feel safe doing so, or keep them open. However you are most comfortable."

"Now start to notice your breathing. While you are in this moment, I invite you to focus on this poem I will read, and find your own meaning in it..."

(You can read the poem)

"Now try to envision yourself as queen of your world. What would that look like?..."

"Take a deep breath in... now let it out..."

"How does it feel to be in complete control of your world?... What would your world sound like?... Take another deep breath in... and let it out. What words or pictures come to mind?"

"See if you notice how you visualize who you are as the queen of this world... What values, beliefs, responsibilities, are important to you?"

"Breath in... then breathe out... and when you are ready, you can come back to this moment and begin creating your crown."
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create, to begin doing so. You may wish to remind them that it doesn't matter what it looks like. What's important is that they are taking this time to honor their thoughts, feelings, and visions of their ideal world in which they are in charge and decorate their crowns in any way that is expressive, empowering, and meaningful to them.

 

Queen of the World decoration using drawing, collage and stickers
closing:
For the closing, you can give participants a chance to share their crown, what it means to them, what they want in their ideal world, how they plan of working towards that in their lives, or anything else they may wish to share.

If you like, you can invite each participant who wishes to share to open with: "If I were queen of my world...."

Of course, this is optional, and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.
description: This workshop gives women the opportunity to be queen for a day by creating their own crown.
optional_materials: • CrayPas (oil pastels)
introduction:
"Magic Mom" crown decoration
 

"Today, you'll get a chance to imagine that you are the queen of your world. Each one of us has a vision of what our world would be like if we were in charge. During this time each of you will have the opportunity to develop ideas that you can incorporate into your life. These ideas represent the best life for you as you envision it. You will also get an opportunity to create a crown with words, pictures and colors that represent your new world."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
demonstration:
If you see the need, you can take a moment to introduce the material and demonstrate some creation techniques. For instance, you can explain that participants can use scissors to cut words and/or images out of magazines, or use their hands to tear them out for a cool effect. title: A Journey Within
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to explore the power of journaling and the perspective it can provide on fear, negative thinking and the healing process.
materials:
• Journal or sketchbook

  • Pens

  • Intentions quotes handout
setup:
Sample table setup

 

You can print copies of the Tips for Journaling handout for each participant.

You can also print a copy of the Intentions Quote handout and cut the prompts into individual strips and place them in a bowl or basket for the last part of the creation.

You can invite participants to bring their own journals, if they have them, or provide them with new blank ones.

It may be helpful to provide soft, relaxing instrumental music to play in the background during meditation and/or journaling.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
You can invite participants to volunteer and share one word about what they intend to get out of this workshop. It could be peace, comfort, strength, etc.

Next, you can invite participants to begin to journal by taking their one word intention, write it down and allow other words to tumble onto the page. You can encourage them to keep their hand flowing, even if they're writing the same word over and over.

If time permitting, you can invite participants to volunteer and share what they wrote.
creation:
Participants during guided meditation


 

To begin the creative process, you can invite the participants to a guided meditation. We've found that guided meditations are most effective when spoken in a soft, slow tone, pausing where it feels right.

If you're providing candles, you can light one per table to help set a relaxed atmosphere.


Guided Meditation #1: Up a Flight of Stairs
"I now would like to invite you to join me in a guided meditation. If you prefer to just observe, that's perfectly okay. Observing is participating. For those of you who wish to follow along, try to get in a comfortable position. If you feel safe, you can close your eyes, or keep them open. However you're most comfortable."

"Now take in a deep breath... and let it out... continue to breathe, for breath is like magic... Your breath holds the knowledge of your pleasure... It holds the knowledge of your pain."

"It know what you are afraid of, what you dream of. It holds the knowledge of all your identities, all that you would like to be and how you would like to be seen. And, it holds the truth. Your breath goes everywhere… it is part of everything that you are."

"Now try to imagine yourself walking down a hallway, with your most favorite clothing on. At the end of the hall is a set of stairs. Ascend the stairs one step at a time, while watching and feeling yourself step up, up and up, knowing that at the end of the stairs is a door. Notice the energy in your step... is it heavy? Is it light? Are you looking forward, or looking back? Simply notice how you look and feel as you ascend the stairs."

"Open the door and see the entire universe before you... what does this look like to you? This is your journey and your universe, your favorite place to create... it can look and feel any way that you want it to look and feel."

"Imagine taking that first step through the door, into the vast space and being suspended in the most beautiful place you’ve ever seen. You are light, surrounded by light... you can do anything, and you can create anything.  You are completely supported… imagine the freedom of being completely supported by the universe… imagine being supported by your hopes and dreams and all that you want to be. Knowing that you are supported, let’s take a walk, deeper into your universe. What do you see? How do you feel? Describe this experience to yourself."

"See every detail... allow yourself to fly from star to star, if you would like. Take note of everything… even if all you see, feel and hear is silence… as you journey deeper into your universe… what do you see? Now, gently remind yourself to return to the door… walk back through, and descend the stairs one at a time until you reach the bottom. When you're ready, I invite you to open your eyes, pick up your pen and write about your experience, doodle about what you saw and felt and heard."


You can give participants about 10 minutes to journal, then invite any who wish to volunteer to share what they wrote. This may be a good opportunity to thank them for their willingness to share and courage to change.


 

    
  Art from A Woman With Wings


 

Guided Meditation #2: Finding Your Genius Seed
"For those of you who wish to follow along, I now invite you to another guided meditation about our own individual genius seed. We all have one. What is yours? This image and symbol of your brilliance will remind you of the creativity and healing within. This guided meditation allows for discovering and claiming your 'genius seed.' If ever stuck in the writing process, or need motivation to journal, this visualization and journey helps to unlock and guide you."

"Now imagine yourself once again, walking down a long hallway… noticing your dress, your movements… at the end of the hall is your flight of stairs, that takes you directly to your universe, your place of creativity, your place of power. Take each step one at a time, noticing your energy, noticing your feelings, noticing you. You can either go up the stairs or down the stairs, it's completely up to you. You are free to decide where you would like to go today."

"You are now at the end of the stairs about to open the door... take a pause and ask to be greeted by a being that knows and loves you... Open the door; step out into your favorite place where you are greeted by your loving being... this most loving being, and say: 'I want to find my genius seed. Will you take me there? Will you support me in my journey'?"

"Now imagine your loving being saying: 'Yes. Absolutely. Of course'."

"Notice your loving being in great detail… how they move, what they look like… see every step of the journey they take you on. Imagine the smells in the air, how your skin feels. Remember to breathe in and out, and go deeper into your adventure, as you step closer and closer to finding your genius seed."

"Your loving being, your guide, stops and points... 'there it is, you’ve found it!' What do you see? Reach for it, touch it, smell it, feel it. Now ask your genius seed to show you all of your talents and abilities; your gifts… ask it tell you all about you. Take the time to really listen… to hear all that is said about you."

"Your loving being gently reminds you it’s time to return home… this time, with your genius seed in hand. Now that you’ve found it, it will never leave you."

"The journey home is a quick one… back to the flight of stairs, stepping out of your adventure, taking one step at a time, noticing how you feel, what you see. You are at the end of the stairs. When you are ready, I invite you to slowly open your eyes and start to write about your genius seed, the journey to find it, what is it, and what it tells you about you."


You can give participants about 10 minutes to journal, then invite any who wish to volunteer to share what they wrote. This may be a good opportunity to thank them for their willingness to share and courage to change.

You can now invite participants to take an Intentions quote at random out of the basket / bowl and read it to themselves. You can then share the following:

"What does this mean to you? How does it make you feel? When you feel your feelings and emotions, they become the precursor to great insight and personal wisdom. For those of you who wish to follow along, I now invite you to take about 10 minutes to write and doodle."
closing: You can give participants a chance to volunteer and share anything they wrote, discovered, felt or experienced during the workshop, or anything else they may wish to share.
description: This workshop takes the participant on their own journey of creativity, where the product is their own wisdom. The journal or sketchbook becomes a point of reference for their lives, and lends perspective on their fears and challenges, joys and enthusiasm, and every emotion and feeling in between.
tips:
The following is a list of tips for leading journaling workshops provided by Patricia Varga:

1)  Ceremony
Begin the journaling process as you would begin a ceremony, for this is sacred time for self – to connect with the creativity and imagination within. Lighting a candle, saying a few words of inspiration sets up the journey.  

If writing one’s own prayer or words of inspiration is too daunting, too scary, you can develop one together, or give them one and encourage them over time to develop their own.

They can use a poem from a book, a line from a play, a passage from the Bible; whatever they feel a connection to, whatever comforts or inspires them.

2) Write and doodle every day
Creativity is a process, it is a practice. Writing and doodling everyday, even if you write your name a hundred times on a sheet of paper and that’s it, gets the creative muscles in shape. The physical act of picking your favorite pen, putting it to paper and letting the words and doodles tumble onto the page, is meditative. It takes you to another world where possibilities are endless.  

Once you get your rhythm, you never lose it, for you know what it feels like to write, to doodle, to let go. Your creative memory is in place.

3) Creativity only knows how to create
There is no right or wrong, no judgment, only joy. I encourage you and your clients to be “disobedient” during meditation; to know that it’s ok to be different. There are no expectations. If your mind takes you in a different direction, not the one you are being guided to, go with it.  Following your imagination is a beautiful thing - flow with it and feel blessed.  

4) Share your own journey, your humanity.
I tell people about my own fears and criticisms, doubts and challenges and how I use writing and doodling to overcome them.  People want to feel safe and comfortable during the process and that it’s ok to be creative.  Sharing allows for this comfort.  

5) Tell them what you’re going to tell them, tell them, tell them what you told them
Sounds crazy, but illuminating what’s about to take place, can be reassuring and soothing. Allowing the journaling to take place, then giving a quick recap of what took place invites greater participation and helps reinforce the process.

6) A Beginning
Please know that this workshop is a beginning for what could become a life-long journey of creativity. There are more workshops, more techniques, more meditations, but for now, this is a great place to start.

“In this journey of creativity, the product is wisdom… wisdom that reminds you of your talents and abilities, and that all that you dream and hope for is possible.”

Patricia Varga, A Woman with Wings

"Once you trust this connection - some call it 'God,' some call it 'The Divine,' some call it 'Meditation,' some may call it 'Self' - the creativity and ultimate healing is limitless."

    Large Head & Body Template

setup:
Have body and head templates ready, one for each participant. Print journal questions on special paper. Have samples on hand if available. If you are using watercolors, be sure to pre-moisten them with a spray bottle before the participants use them.

It's great to make an example of each medium so the participants get an idea of what they can create.
warm_up:
Paper mosaic Inner Self Portrait

Feel free to adapt this relaxation to work with your group and timeframe. Read slowly, pausing in between sentences to create a relaxing atmosphere. Encourage participants to breath deeply and try the relaxation even if they feel uncomfortable relaxing, if necessary try to reassure them that it may feel uncomfortable relaxing because we are so used to just going and going. Remind them that they are in a safe place and that they deserve a window of time that is their own.  You can just close you eyes and relax. If you fall asleep that is great! Just like the art there is no right or wrong way to do the relaxation.

“Get comfortable in your chair, it is good to sit with your feet flat and your hands just laying loosely in your lap. If it feels safe for you, you can close your eyes. Just notice your in-breath and out-breath. No need to change it, simply notice the breath as it enters your nose and fills your chest.

Start with your toes…and wiggle them in you shoes, feel your calves relaxing and your thighs relaxing, ... keep breathing deeply,  breathe air into your hips and feel any tightness gently relaxing, breath into your back – from the lower back, through the mid-back to your upper back. Feel the healing and calming energy come into your tummy… your lungs… your chest… gently wiggle your fingers and your arms, feel your shoulders relaxing… relax your neck… and gently feel your face muscles, your jaw, your eyes and ears relaxing. Take another few moments and check to see if any part of your body is still carrying tension or stress. Breathe into your body a sense of calmness, breathing out and let any last remaining tension just melt away. 

Move your thoughts to your mind... knowing you can relax your mind just like a muscle ... take a deep breathe and go deep within and begin to meet your inner-self. What colors come to mind for your inner-self? What shapes or images arise as you meet your inner-self, are they large or small, round or heart? Is your inner-self male or female, are they young or old, is your image clear or foggy?

Greet your inner self, and ask him or her what they need from you... maybe a hug?.. maybe they just need you to sit and listen... take a moment and just spend some time getting to know and loving your inner-self.

Take a deep breath in and let it out, continue breathing comfortably and know that you can return to talk and share with your inner-self any time you want, reassure her/him you will be back! Hold onto all the images you saw and felt... now bring yourself back to the room  slowly open your eyes... and begin to create a portrait of your inner-self, selecting one of the techniques.
creation:
Remind participants that it doesn't have to look like anything in particular. Remember that is doesn't matter what it looks like, we offer three technique options to choose from. Ask the participants to follow their intuition and see what comes out.  Have fun! There are so many materials that it is good to give the participants time warnings.

Participants diligently working on their Inner Self Portraits
closing: Ask everyone to share their portrait and what it means to them. What did they discover? Are they pleased to meet their inner self. Were they surprised by who they found? What was most important for them to share about the experience or their art.
description: This workshop will assist the participant in going within and discovering more about their inner-self! This workshop gives us an opportunity to go to a deep level and expose, explore, celebrate and get more in touch with our inner-self... our inner most being. This workshop offers 3 different techniques to allow the participant to fully express their inner-selves. This is also a great project for an exhibit.
introduction: This workshop will assist the women and even teens to look inside and discover more about their inner self. We are used to looking at our outer selves, our looks, our clothes, our appearance, the image we try to portray. This workshop gives us an opportunity to go to a deeper level and get more in touch with our inner-self. You will have 3 options of materials, you can also combine them.
demonstration:
Pre-collage Without a background image
Adding a background image Collaging with layers

Explain to the participants the materials that will be available, especially if you are giving all three options. It is important to demonstrate all of the materials you give to them.

Collage
You may want to show your participants the different effects you can get by layering. You can show them how adding a background image can add hidden meaning and also make a collage "pop"! Another wonderful collage technique is to not use scissors. Tearing the paper creates a cool effect. Finally, encourage participants that while choosing images they should try to follow their intuition. This process can be quite surprising and freeing.

Paper Mosaic
You may not need to show a technical demonstration of how to do a paper mosaic, but it's good to at least show an example of what a mosaic is. Participants may choose to use a pencil to outline the spaces they would like to fill with mosaic pieces. It's also important to remind them that mosaics don't necessarily have to be squares, they can do long strips for hair and use lots of shapes.

   
Notice how the white oil pastel was used in the bubbles of this Inner Self Portrait    

Oil Pastel Resist
Give a demonstration to the participants by drawing a shapes with oil pastel on card stock  then using the watercolor over pastel to show how the pastel resists the watercolor. Remind them to use a lot of water and a lot of paint on their brush to create richer color effects. Using a spray bottle is an easy way to add water to the paper to help the watercolors flow.
opening_circle:
Combination collage and paper mosaic Inner Self Portrait

Remind the group that anything shared in this circle is anonymous and should not be shared with anyone outside of this room.  Have the participants introduce themselves and share one thing that others don't know about them!  Ask the clients to be brave when deciding what to share and remind them that everything that is said in group stays in group.

Journaling & Sharing (optional): 
If you plan to use the journal questions provided, realize it takes a lot more time to write and then share. If you have the time use this step as you may notice participants tend to go to a deeper level when they write and share before they create.

Have participants journal on the questions provided and then share what they feel comfortable sharing. It is sometimes helpful to give participants a time frame and play soft music to get them writing. When it looks like most people are done, ask a volunteer to begin the sharing circle and ask them to share whichever answers they are comfortable sharing.

title: Red Flag Banners / Banderas Rojas
objective: This workshop aims to help participants learn to identify red flags and warning signs of a potentially abusive relationship and utilize their past experiences to create a vision for a healthy relationship in the future.
materials:
Optional printable worksheet
  • Red cardstock (or construction paper)

  • Large flag template

  • Small flag templates

  • Glue sticks

  • Scissors

  • Magazines (Oprah, Nat Geo and travel magazines tend to have more inclusive words and imagery)

  • Permanent markers (dark colors and/or metallics)

  • Ribbon / yarn

  • Journaling handout

  • Pens

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print copies out for your participants beforehand depending on the setting.
setup:
Cutting out your group project template
 
 
  Cutting out your individual project template


 

You can facilitate this workshop as a team project, individual project, or both. You can provide either the small flags, large ones or both. It's entirely up to you.

You can print or copy flag templates onto red cardstock or construction paper. Or, you can hand out multiple templates and allow participants to trace.

To save time during the workshop, you may want to pre-cut the flags. You can give participants an opportunity to create more than one flag, so you may want to print the amount of flags accordingly.

You can print out one copy of the Red Flags of Abusive Relationships handout and Journaling handout for each participant. 

You may want to read through the Red Flag handout and highlight the bullet points you'd like to cover. You may also choose to do this workshop in two sessions, if you see fit.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show participants what it can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.


Note: 
Participants who are living with their abusive partners may not be able to take the flags home with them because of safety issues, in which case, you may want to consider facilitating a group project, which can be hung to serve as a reminder of the red flags of an abusive relationship. This will allow the participants to revisit their red flags every time they come to group.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Part 1: Writing out the red flags
 
     
  Part 3: Collaging
 
 
  Part 4: Placing a ribbon and gluing the inside of the flag
 
 
  Tying a knot between the flags

You can now invite those who wish to do so, to begin creating their red flags banner(s). If time permits, you can give participants a chance to make as many flags as you see fit.

The time you choose to allocate to each part is completely up to you. It may be helpful to give participants gentle time reminders to keep your workshop on track.

You may wish to remind participants that there is no right or wrong way to create or participate. They are free to use this time however they like.

 

Part 1: Writing Down the Red Flags
To begin, participants can cut out a red flag (if not done in advance) and on one side, write down the warning signs they've experienced in any past relationships. They can use any color markers that they like. They can write words, draw symbols, or whatever they like. They can refer to the Red Flags of Abusive Relationships handout in opening circle, if they wish.


Part 2: Journaling
After everyone has completed the first part of the project, you can hand out the Healthy Relationships Journaling page. If you have time, you may want to discuss the characteristics of healthy relationships. Otherwise, you can simply invite participants to fill out their journaling page.


Part 3: Collaging
Once they're done with their journaling, participants can begin decorating the other side of their flag(s). They get to use the collage material and any of the art supplies available to express their vision of a healthy relationship and the most important things they wish to have in their future relationship.


Part 4: Putting It All Together
Participants can place a piece of ribbon on the inside of their completed flag along the center seam, apply glue to the inside and fold the flag in half (over the ribbon). They can then add beads (if available) and/or tie a knot at each end of the ribbon.

If creating more than one personal flag, participants can use a larger piece of ribbon, and apply the above steps to as many flags as they've created. Ideally, they would leave some space in between each flag. They can tie a knot and/or add beads (if available) between each flag, if they choose.

If this is a group project, you can invite participants to attach their flag(s) along the large piece of clothesline or ribbon following the same folding/gluing steps as above. They can then add either a knot or a bead before the next flag, so it can be hung up and displayed (if participants choose to do so).
closing:
You can invite participants to volunteer and share their flags, something about the red flags they missed or ignored in past relationships, something about their future relationship, or anything else they may wish to share. Of course, sharing is optional, and if anyone doesn't feel comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

You can reinforce the importance of paying attention to red flags and remind them that they deserve and are worthy of a healthy relationship.

If this was a group project, you can invite participants to volunteer and help hang the banner.

You can end by thanking them for their resiliency and for their courage to be here today.

       
"Never underestimate a woman's intuition."         "It's a relationship that makes your eyes sparkle."
description: In this workshop participants can learn how to identify red flags, or warning signs of a potentially abusive relationship. Participants will have an opportunity to identify the red flags they missed or ignored in past relationships and to notice the qualities they want in future relationships.
objective_spanish: Este taller aspira ayudar a todas/todos las/los participantes a aprender a identificar las banderas rojas y señales de advertencia en una relación potencialmente abusiva y también a utilizar las experiencias pasadas para crear una visión de una relación saludable para el futuro.
materials_spanish:
•    Papel cartulina roja (o papel de construcción)
•    Plantilla de banderín grande 
•    Plantilla de banderín pequeño 
•    Pegamento en barra
•    Tijeras 
•    Revistas (Oprah, Nat Geo y las revistas de viajes tienden a tener imágenes más inclusivas)
•    Marcadores permanentes (colores oscuros o metálicos)
•    Listón/hilo
•    Folleto “Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva 
•    Hoja de trabajo Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva
•    Bolígrafos
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 10 min
Demostración: 5 min
Apertura: 20 min
Creación: 45 min
Cierre: 15 min
Total: 1:35 hora
setup_spanish:
Puede facilitar este taller como un proyecto grupal, individual o ambos. Puede repartir a cada participante ya sean los banderines pequeños, los grandes o ambos. Depende por completo de usted.

Puede imprimir o copiar las plantillas de los banderines en el papel cartulina o papel de construcción rojo. También, puede repartir múltiples plantillas y permitir que cada participante lo trace.

Para ahorrar tiempo durante el taller, puede ser que quiera cortar previamente los banderines. Puede dar a cada participante la oportunidad de crear más de un banderín, así que usted puede querer tener preparadao el número correspondiente de banderines impresos. 

También puede imprimir una copia del folleto “Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva” y de la hoja de trabajo Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva” para entregar a cada participante.

Puede ser que le interese leer el folleto “Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva” y subrayar los puntos que quiera cubrir en el taller. También puede realizar el taller en dos sesiones, si le parece conveniente.

Puede ser útil crear una muestra antes del taller para mostrar a las/los participantes como puede verse. Si decide hacerlo, le sugerimos crear una muestra de demostración muy básica para que las/los participantes no se sientan abrumadas/ abrumados por cualquier reto “artístico.”

Nota: Las o los participantes que están viviendo con una pareja abusiva puede ser que no puedan llevarse las banderas a casa por cuestiones de seguridad, en tal caso, usted puede considerar facilitar un proyecto en grupo, el cual puede servir como recordatorio de las banderas rojas y señales de advertencia de una relación abusiva.

Esto le permitirá a las/los participantes revisitar estas banderas cada vez que vengan al grupo.

Siéntase con la libertad de alterar o adaptar cualquier parte o elemento de este taller para poder servir las necesidades específicas del grupo.
creation_spanish:
Ahora puede invitar a quienes estén interesados, en crear sus banderines rojos. Si el tiempo lo permite, puede darle la oportunidad a los integrantes de crear tantos banderines como usted sienta apropiado.

El tiempo que decida asignar a cada una de las partes del taller depende por completo de usted. Puede ser útil avisarle al grupo de manera sutil cuánto tiempo les queda para que así usted pueda terminar el taller a tiempo.

Tal vez quiera recordarle al grupo que no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de hacer los banderines o de participar en el taller. Cada quién es libre de usar el tiempo como prefieran.

Parte 1: Escribiendo los banderines rojos
Para comenzar, cada participante puede cortar un banderín rojo (si aún no han sido cortados) y comenzar en uno de los lados. Puede escribir las señales de advertencia que identificaron en sus relaciones pasadas. Pueden usar cualquier marcador de color que deseen. Puede ser que decidan escribir palabras, dibujar símbolos o cualquier cosa que deseen. Puede ser que decidan revisitar sus respuestas que escribieron en el Folleto “Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva” como referencia.

Parte 2: Escritura
Después de que todo el grupo haya terminado la primera parte del proyecto, puede repartir la hoja de trabajo “Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva”. Si tiene tiempo puede discutir las características de una relación saludable. Si no, puede simplemente invitar a los participantes a que completen la hoja de trabajo.

Parte 3: Decoración
Una vez que hayan terminado de escribir en la hoja de trabajo, los participantes pueden comenzar a decorar el otro lado de su banderín o banderines. Pueden utilizar el material para hacer collages y cualquier material que tengan disponible para expresar su visión de una relación saludable y sobre todo lo que desean tener en sus relaciones futuras.

Parte 4: Poniendo todo junto
Los y las participantes pueden colocar una pieza de listón o hilo en el interior de su banderín terminado encima de donde está doblado, pueden aplicar pegamento en el interior y doblar el banderín a la mitad (sobre el listón o hilo). Después pueden agregar cuentas (si has disponibles) y/o hacer un nudo al final de cada listón.

Si han creado más de un banderín, los y las participantes pueden usar un trozo de listón más largo y aplicar los pasos anteriores a cuantos banderines hayan creado. Idealmente, dejarán un espacio entre cada banderín. Pueden hacer un nudo y/o añadir cuentas, para que pueda colgarse a la vista (si las y los participantes así lo desean).
closing_spanish:
Puede invitar a las y los participantes de manera voluntaria para que compartan sus banderines, algo que a lo mejor dejaron pasar desapercibido o ignoraron en sus relaciones anteriores, algo sobre sus futuras relaciones, o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir. Claro que compartir es opcional, y si nadie se siente cómoda o cómodo compartiendo también está bien. 

Puede remarcar la importancia de poner atención a las señales de advertencia y las banderas rojas y recordarles que cada participante se merece estar en relaciones saludables.

Si esto lo hace como un proyecto grupal, usted puede invitar a las y los participantes a que de manera voluntaria ayuden a colgar el estandarte de banderines.

Puede terminar el taller agradeciéndoles por su resiliencia y por el valor de estar aquí hoy.

• Beads

  • Twine / string / clothesline (for group project)

introduction:
"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."

"Have you ever thought: 'I saw all the red flags and looked the other way?' Red flags are intuitive warnings that let us know something is wrong. All too often, we silence that little voice inside of ourselves that warns us of a potential danger."

"Abusive people are skilled at manipulating us into believing them and doubting ourselves. Over time, abusers may convince us to automatically defer to what they think and want and to disregard our own needs, wants and opinions."

"Today, I'm going to invite you to take a look back at the red flags from past abusive relationships, and then, if you wish to, you'll get to create your own red flags to honor and allow your inner voice, needs and desires to be heard."

"We can save ourselves a lot of frustration and pain in the future by practicing identifying our red flags. During this workshop you will also have an opportunity to notice the things your want in your future relationships."
introduction_spanish:
“Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que esta es su ventana de tiempo. Esto significa que este tiempo puede ser un lugar seguro para que noten sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que decidan hacer o decir es voluntario. Durante este tiempo, no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta para participar o crear. Voy a compartir con ustedes unas instrucciones básicas, sin embargo, ustedes deciden cómo quieren participar. Pueden seguir las instrucciones por completo o tal vez quieran hacer algo diferente, depende completamente de ustedes. Durante su ventana de tiempo, tienen completa libertad de decidir. Como decidan pasar este tiempo está perfectamente bien. Yo estoy aquí para apoyarles de cualquier forma que pueda, así que siéntanse libres de pedirme lo que necesiten.”

“Alguna vez han pensado: 'Vi todas las señales de advertencia o banderas rojos y las ignoré?' Las banderas rojas son advertencias intuitivas que nos avisan cuando algo está mal. Sin embargo, demasiado a menudo, callamos esa pequeña voz dentro de nosotras/ nosotros que nos advierte de un posible peligro.”

“Las personas abusivas son muy hábiles en manipularnos para creerles y desconfiar de esta voz interior que nos avisa del peligro. Con el tiempo, las personas abusivas nos pueden convencer a que pongamos como nuestra prioridad lo que piensan y quieren y así ignorar nuestras propias necesidades, deseos y opiniones.”

“Hoy les voy a invitar a que echen un vistazo al pasado y vean las banderas rojas que habían en sus relaciones abusivas del pasado, y después, si así lo desean van a crear sus propios banderines rojos para honrar y permitir que las necesidades, y deseos de su voz interna sean escuchados.”

“Podemos salvarnos mucha frustración y dolor en el futuro si practicamos identificando nuestras propias banderas rojas. Durante este taller le será posible tener la oportunidad de notar las cosas que desea en sus relaciones futuras.”
demonstration:
You can introduce the art supplies and demonstrate any creation elements and/or techniques that you see needed (Ex: how to collage, etc). If you've made a sample, you may want to show it for reference.

A personal Red Flag Banners creation with knots in between each flag
demonstration_spanish: Puede presentar los materiales y hacer una demostración de cualquier técnica que sienta que el grupo necesite (por ejemplo: cómo hacer un collage, etc.). Si hizo una muestra, puede enseñarla como referencia.
opening_circle:
You can open by passing out the Red Flags of Abusive Relationships handout and going over it as a group.

You can invite the participants to share about the red flags they saw in their relationship and how they reacted. 

For example, “I knew something was off when he said that all of his ex-girlfriends were crazy, but I rationalized that he was right because he was such a great guy and convinced myself I was being paranoid."

Of course, sharing is voluntary and up to each person whether or not they share. Observing is participating.
opening_circle_spanish:
Puede abrir pasando el Folleto “Las banderas rojas de una relación abusiva” y repasarlo como grupo. 

Puede invitar a un/una participante a que comparta sobre las banderas rojas que vio en su relación y cómo reaccionó a estas.

Por ejemplo, “Sabía que algo estaba mal cuando me dijo que todas sus exnovias estaban locas, pero lo racionalicé y me dije a mí misma que lo que decía era verdad porque él era un gran tipo y me convencí a mí misma de ser paranoica por dudarlo.”

Claro, que compartir es voluntario y depende de cada participante si desean hacerlo o no. Observar también es participar.
