introduction:
Left to right: AWBW Director of Programs Olivia Piacenza, Olga Phoenix, AWBW Leader Zabie Yamasaki, & AWBW Founder Cathy Salser

As trauma service professionals we must integrate self-care into our lives to be well and to be effective. I have developed a tool designed to help us trauma professionals create a personal comprehensive vicarious trauma prevention plan that encompasses both self-care activities and creating full and meaningful life activities, in order to bring wellness, contentment, and joy into our lives. It's called the Self-Care & Life Balance Wheel.

The Wheel was designed to help trauma workers live full, vicarious trauma-free lives. It is an empowering, affirming, and positive tool, comprised of six dimensions: physical, psychological, emotional, spiritual, personal, and professional. Each dimension represents a part of our lives which requires our daily attention. All six dimensions are equally important: without nurturing and addressing our physical needs, we cannot be effective in our professional lives; without cultivating the physiological and emotional aspects of ourselves, we cannot effectively negate the despair, demoralization, and loss of hope imposed by vicarious trauma.
 

I like to think about the Wheel as a bottom of a chair, with its six dimensions being its six legs. My Life Balance chair is steady and supports me perfectly when I nurture and take care of all six dimensions of my life equally. When, however, my focus on certain parts of my life decreases-if, for example, I forget to take care of physical or emotional needs by working too much- my Life Balance chair becomes wobbly and shaky, just the way my life becomes unbalanced and unhealthy.  This is when I become especially vulnerable to vicarious trauma and burnout.  Today we will explore six dimensions of self-care necessary for life balance through journaling and discussions which will lead into us creating Self-Care Touchstones to serve as tangle reminders to put our personal self-care and life balance plan into practice everyday. 

Welcome and Window of Time:
"This workshop is a window of time for you-a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, needs and visions. Since this space is your window of time, everything you do or say is voluntary. I'll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there's no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. Lastly, Please ask for what you need, and know that we are here in support of you."

Facilitator Tip:
It is helpful to intermittently check in with the participants to see whats coming up for them and encourage dialogue throughout the workshop.
introduction_spanish:
"Este taller es una oportunidad de tiempo para ti, un espacio seguro para notar tus pensamientos, sentimientos, necesidades y visiones, ya que este espacio es tu oportunidad  de tiempo para ti, todo lo que haces o dices es voluntario. Compartir acerca de los materiales que tenemos disponibles, e invitarle a crear, recuerde que no hay manera correcta o incorrecta de hacer esto. No importa el resultado final o lo que parece. Por último, por favor, pregunte si necesita algo, y sepan que estamos Aquí para apoyarlo a Usted.”

Como profesionales de servicios de trauma, debemos integrar el autocuidado en nuestras vidas para estar bien y ser eficaces. He desarrollado una herramienta diseñada para ayudarnos a los profesionales de trauma crear un plan personal de prevención de trauma vicario completo que abarca tanto las actividades de autocuidado y la creación de actividades de vida plena y significativa, con el fin de traer el bienestar, la alegría y la alegría en nuestras vidas. Se llama la rueda Autocuidado & Balance de Vida (Self-Care & Life Balance).

La Rueda fue diseñada para ayudar a los traumatólogos a vivir una vida libre de trauma y vicaria. Es una herramienta potenciadora, afirmativa y positiva, compuesta de seis dimensiones: física, psicológica, emocional, espiritual, personal y profesional. Cada dimensión representa una parte de nuestras vidas que requiere nuestra atención diaria.

Las seis dimensiones son igualmente importantes: sin nutrir y satisfacer nuestras necesidades físicas, no podemos ser eficaces en nuestra vida profesional; Sin cultivar los aspectos fisiológicos y emocionales de nosotros mismos, no podemos negar efectivamente la desesperación, la desmoralización y la pérdida de la esperanza impuesta por el trauma vicario.

Me gusta pensar en la Rueda como el fondo de una silla, con sus seis dimensiones siendo sus seis patas. Mi silla de equilibrio de vida es estable y me apoya perfectamente cuando nutro y cuido de todas las seis dimensiones de mi vida por igual. Cuando, sin embargo, mi enfoque en ciertas partes de mi vida disminuye -si, por ejemplo, me olvido de cuidar de las necesidades físicas o emocionales al trabajar demasiado- mi silla de equilibrio de vida se vuelve vacilante y temblorosa, sólo la forma en que mi vida se vuelve desequilibrada Y no saludable. 

Esto es cuando me vuelvo especialmente vulnerable a trauma vicario y burnout. Hoy vamos a explorar seis dimensiones de auto-cuidado necesario para el equilibrio de la vida a través de diarios y discusiones que nos llevará a crear las piedras de Autocuidado (Self-Care Touchstones) para que nos sirvan como recordatorios de atender nuestro auto-cuidado personal y plan de equilibrio de nuestra vida en la práctica todos los días. Consejo para el Facilitador: Es útil que continuamente Usted pregunte a los participantes para ver lo que está pasando con ellos cuando están creando sus piedras de autocuidado y fomentar el diálogo durante todo el taller.
demonstration:
Draw or write words or images to represent the Touchstone you want to create

 

 

 

Add a pea-sized amount of the glue on top of your drawing/words.

 

 

 

 Place your stone on top of the glue and press down. Wipe off any extra glue and let it dry.

“Before we create our Self-Care Touchstones, we will start with a discussion followed by a journaling exercise to help get us thinking about self-care and life balance. I’ll demonstrate the materials and creation process now, so that at the end of the journaling process, you can dive right in. As I demonstrate the steps, remember that more than anything else, this is your special time to listen to and trust your needs. There is no right or wrong way to create. Whatever emerges is great!

How to Create Touchstones:

  1. Using a writing utensil of your choice, write words, create images, symbols, or use colors on the circular paper to represent the Touchstone(s) you would like to create as a reminder of your self-care and life balance plan.

  2. After you are done creating, add a pea-sized amount of the clear tacky glue on top of each paper circle creation.  Make sure to put the glue directly on top of what you created. If you used markers, give them time to dry before adding the glue, as the glue can cause the creation to smear.

  3. Place the flat side of your stone on top of the glue and press down.

  4. Wipe off any extra glue and let it dry.
demonstration_spanish:
"Antes de crear nuestras tácticas de autocuidado, comenzaremos con una discusión seguida de un ejercicio de registro diario para ayudarnos a pensar en el autocuidado y el equilibrio de la vida.

Voy a demostrar los materiales y el proceso de creación ahora, de modo que al final del proceso de registro en su diario, se puede empezar a crear sus piedras autocuidado.

Como demuestro los pasos, recuerde que más que nada, este es su momento especial para escuchar y confiar en tus necesidades. No hay manera correcta o incorrecta de crear.

Lo que emerge es grande! Cómo crear las Piedras de Autocuidado (Touchstones):

Utilice un utensilio de escritura de su elección, escriba palabras, cree imágenes, símbolos o use colores en el papel circular para representar la (s) Piedra (s) de Autocuidado que desea crear como un recordatorio de su plan de autocuidado y balance de vida.

Una vez que haya terminado de crear, agregue una cantidad pequeña del pegamento transparente en la parte superior de cada creación de círculo de papel.

Asegúrese de colocar el pegamento directamente encima de lo que creó.

Si usó marcadores, dales tiempo para que se sequen antes de agregar el pegamento, ya que el pegamento puede causar que la creación se manche.

Coloque el lado plano de su piedra en la parte superior del pegamento y presione hacia abajo. Limpie cualquier pegamento extra y deje que se seque.
opening_circle:
Self-Care & Life Balance Wheel Discussion:
Pass out copies of the Self-Care & Life Balance Wheel. 

The Life Balance Wheel contains 88 suggestions for a range of vicarious trauma prevention practices, ranging from meeting basic physical needs to finding life's purpose and meaning through the psychological and spiritual dimensions. The goal is to give us trauma professionals a great variety of self-care tools so we can explore, test, and adapt them into a personalized, preventative and sustainable vicarious trauma-free lifestyle. Keep in mind that for these activities to work well for you in a crisis, you must practice them regularly and know for sure they work for you. As the word "preventative" implies, this particular method may prevent you from having to be in a state of crisis in the first place.

Also, your vicarious trauma-free lifestyle needs to be sustainable. It means realistic, ongoing efforts which will keep you healthy continuously through your career. For example, I will never become an early bird, thus I know that making myself wake up at 4 am to go to the gym probably will not work in the long run. This type of unrealistic thinking is not only unsustainable, but self sabotaging. If you pick something you enjoy, it will be so much easier to make it a preventative and sustainable part of your vicarious trauma-free lifestyle.

Time permitting: Invite the participants to share anything that is coming up for them.
opening_circle_spanish:
Distribuya las copias de la Rueda Autocuidado & Balance de Vida (Self Care & Life Balance).

La Rueda del Equilibrio de la Vida contiene 88 sugerencias para una serie de prácticas de prevención de trauma vicario, que van desde satisfacer las necesidades físicas básicas hasta encontrar el propósito y significado de la vida a través de las dimensiones psicológicas y espirituales. 

El objetivo es brindarnos a los profesionales del trauma una gran variedad de herramientas de autocuidado para que podamos explorarlas, probarlas y adaptarlas a un estilo de vida autosuficiente, personalizado, preventivo y sostenible. 

Tenga en cuenta que para que estas actividades funcionen bien para usted en un momento de crisis, debe practicarlas regularmente y saber con certeza que funcionan para usted. Como la palabra "preventivo" implica, este método particular puede impedir que tenga que estar en un estado de crisis en primer lugar.

Además, su estilo de vida vicario sin traumas debe ser sostenible. Significa esfuerzos realistas y continuos que te mantendrán sano continuamente a través de tu carrera. Por ejemplo, nunca llegaré a ser un madrugador (early bird), así que sé que hacerme despertar a las 4 am para ir al gimnasio probablemente no funcionará a largo plazo. 

Este tipo de pensamiento poco realista no sólo es insostenible, sino también es  auto-sabotaje. Si escoges algo que te guste, será mucho más fácil convertirlo en una parte preventiva y sostenible de tu estilo de vida sin trauma vicario.
Si el tiempo lo permite: Invitar a los participantes a compartir cualquier cosa que está en la mente de ellos.

Hojas en blanco del autocuidado y de la rueda del balance de la vida: Invite a los participantes a girar la rueda de Autocuidado y Balance de  la Vida (Self-Care & Life Balance) para revelar la rueda en blanco.

Ahora, tomaremos un cierto tiempo para tomar una mirada a las seis dimensiones de la rueda y evaluar de manera realista y honesta su situación actual, donde usted tiene gusto de ir. Tendrá los siguientes dieciséis minutos para reflexionar sobre / escribir sobre estas necesidades por sí mismo.

Utilice el espacio en blanco en cada dimensión de la rueda para anotar las palabras, formas, colores, imágenes o símbolos que aparecen.
 
No hay manera correcta o incorrecta de hacer este ejercicio de registro diario. Puedes escribir oraciones, palabras, listas, dibujar símbolos, formas o cualquier otra cosa que quieras. Sólo permita que sus pensamientos fluyan en su papel sin juicio. ¡Lo que escribes no tiene que tener sentido para nadie sino para ti! También está bien para sentarse tranquilamente y notar lo que viene.

Recuerde que esta es su ventana de tiempo para conectarse con usted y lo que es significativo para usted.

"Mirando la Dimensión Física de su vida, ¿cuáles son las actividades que funcionan bien para usted en la actualidad? ¿Cuáles son las cosas que le gustaría hacer más de? Menos de? Cualquier actividad específica que le gustaría tratar de la Dimensión Física de su vida Rueda Dale 2 minutos para esto.

Mirando la Dimensión Psicológica de tu vida, ¿cuáles son las actividades que funcionan bien para ti actualmente? ¿Cuáles son las cosas que le gustaría hacer más? ¿Menos de? ¿Alguna actividad específica que le gustaría probar desde la Dimensión Psicológica de la Rueda? Dé 2 minutos para esto.

Mirando la dimensión emocional de su vida, ¿cuáles son las actividades que funcionan bien para usted actualmente? ¿Cuáles son las cosas que le gustaría hacer más? ¿Menos de? ¿Alguna actividad específica que le gustaría probar desde la Dimensión Emocional de la Rueda? Dé 2 minutos para esto.

Mirando la Dimensión Espiritual de tu vida, ¿cuáles son las actividades que funcionan bien para ti actualmente? ¿Cuáles son las cosas que le gustaría hacer más? ¿Menos de? ¿Alguna actividad específica que le gustaría probar desde la Dimensión Espiritual de la Rueda? Dé 2 minutos para esto.

Mirando la dimensión Personal de su vida, ¿cuáles son las actividades que funcionan bien para usted actualmente? ¿Cuáles son las cosas que le gustaría hacer más? ¿Menos de? ¿Alguna actividad específica que le gustaría probar desde la Dimensión Personal de la Rueda? Dé 2 minutos para esto

En cuanto a la dimensión profesional de su vida, ¿cuáles son las actividades que funcionan bien para usted actualmente? ¿Cuáles son las cosas que le gustaría hacer más? ¿Menos de? ¿Alguna actividad específica que le gustaría probar desde la dimensión profesional de la rueda? Dé 2 minutos para esto.”
misc1_spanish:
Actividad opcional

Abordar el miedo: Te invito a echar un vistazo largo y duro a las seis dimensiones de la rueda y evaluar de manera realista y honesta tu situación actual, ¿a dónde te gustaría ir, cómo te imaginas tu vida libre de Trauma Vicario y acciones que tomarás para mantenerla. Las siguientes preguntas le ayudarán con este proceso.

Utilice el espacio en blanco debajo de cada pregunta para anotar sus pensamientos, ideas, comentarios, respuestas a medida que surgen.

1.    Examine la Rueda de cerca, entonces atentamente y sin prejuicios, escuche su cuerpo y mente, y anote los pensamientos que vienen.

2. ¿Cuáles son sus esperanzas y objetivos con respecto a este nuevo Auto-Cuidado y Viaje de Bienestar?

3. ¿Cuáles son sus temores acerca de este nuevo viaje de autocuidado y bienestar?

4. ¿Qué es lo que ya sabes acerca de tu vida y hábitos de trabajo que requieren tu   ¿atención?

5. ¿Cómo se siente tu vida? ¿Qué parece estar funcionando bien? ¿Qué parece ser desafiante?

Haz hecho un trabajo  Fantástico respondiendo al primer juego de preguntas.

A menudo es muy difícil reflexionar sobre nuestros temores, metas y aspiraciones. Una de las razones por las que la psique humana realmente no le gusta el CAMBIO, y con frecuencia escuchamos la voz INTERNA de CRITICA especialmente en voz alta cuando nos estamos preparando para iniciar un NUEVO VIAJE, por excitante o prometedor que sea.

Cualquier SENTIMIENTOS (FEELINGS) que usted esté experimentando en este momento, ¡dale la bienvenida! Diga: "Hola, querida sensación, sé que estás aquí y presente. Le doy la bienvenida, porque usted es importante para mí ".

La resistencia de tu psique al cambio generalmente disminuye, al menos un poco, cuando se valida y se le da la bienvenida. Y eso es todo lo que necesitamos para continuar! Actividad

 

Opcional 2:

Apoyos y Saboteadores:  

1. En un viaje como este, es MUY IMPORTANTE tener un AMIGO DE APOYO. Su terapeuta, su pareja, su mejor amigo, su compañero de trabajo, su supervisor, incluso un amigo interno (INNER FRIEND) puede hacer el truco! Siempre y cuando sientas que no estás solo en este viaje, es todo lo que cuenta! ¿Quién esta en  su grupo de apoyo actual? ¿A quién le gustaría agregar para que sea parte de su grupo de apoyo? Piense en el concepto de amigo interno (INNER FRIEND) y vea si puede encontrar uno dentro.  

2. Después de identificar su GRUPO DE APOYO, es valioso tomar tiempo para reflexionar sobre su Saboteadores (SABOTEURS). Podría ser su crítico interior, o un colega poco apoyado, su horario excesivamente lleno, o incluso un hábito poco saludable. Aquí es importante reflexionar sobre el hecho de que no importa quién o qué sean los saboteadores, USTED y su GRUPO DE APOYO pueden abordarlos y tomar cartas en el asunto!  

3. Ahora, con un GRUPO DE APOYO identificado, y Saboteadores (SABOTUERS)expuestos,  vamos a pensar en las razones detrás de obtener este Kit en el primer lugar? ¿Qué es lo que lo motiva a buscar información sobre la Prevención del Trauma Vicario y las Soluciones para Vivir VIDA COMPLETA, ALEGRE Y SIGNIFICATIVA?  ¡Excelente trabajo en el desmantelamiento de BARRERAS e identificación de SOLUCIONES!

Ahora, estamos preparados para crear nuestra RUEDA de CUIDADO PERSONAL Y balance DE VIDA  EN nuestras SEIS DIMENSIONES DE LA VIDA LIBRE DE TRAUMA!

title: Claiming Who I Am
objective: This workshop gives participants an opportunity to dispose the negative messages they receive, and create an art piece that allows them to claim and celebrate their unique identities.
materials:
Optional printable worksheet

  • People shapes template

  • Construction paper / cardstock (variety of colors)

  • Multi-cultural cardstock

  • Round circles (cut out from construction paper; variety of colors)

  • Markers

  • Scissors

  • Glue

  • Small buckets (or cans; for disposal of negative messages; 1 per table)

You can also facilitate this workshop using this printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send the sheet or print copies out for your participants beforehand depending on the setting.
setup:
Sample table setup

 

You are welcome to provide any and as may decorative material that you like (oil pastels, colored pencils, etc.).

You can print copies of the people shape template onto a diverse range of multi-cultural cardstock (1 per child). You may want to cut the shapes out in advance.

You may also consider cutting out a variety of colors circles in advance, enough for each child to choose their preferred color.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to get a feel for the best supplies and creation process for your group. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a basic demo sample so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

It may be helpful to write the creation steps on a board.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
Sample creation

You can now invite those who wish to create to choose a circle and person outline that they connect with and begin creating their person.

You may wish to remind them that there is no right or wrong way to create. They are free to use this time however they wish and create however it feels right for them.

Feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
closing:
You can invite the participants to volunteer and share their Claiming Who I Am creations, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.

You can also give them a partnered sharing option:

"As we bring this workshop to a close, I'd like to give you a chance to share with a partner about this experience. During this process, I encourage you to make it less of a conversation and more of a time to be heard and to witness. As a speaker, try to think about the questions and how you want to share. As a listener, try to think about some non-verbal ways that you can show your partner that you’re listening. For those of you who wish to follow along, take a moment to find a partner in the group. Among yourselves, you can choose who will speak first. You can take about two minutes each to share."

"Here are a few questions you might want to think about when it’s your turn to speak:"

  • "How was this experience for you?"

  • "How can you continue to transform the negative messages that you receive?"

 

Feel free to close out the workshop however way it best suits you and your group.

         
          Claiming Who I Am Creations
tips: The multi-cultural cardstock can come in various "skin colors," but they can never represent every shade. Feel free to invite participants to draw their own "people shape," or use colorful paper (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, etc) so the shape of their paper person represents each individual in a way that's right for them.
optional_materials:
• Oil pastels (CrayPas)

  • Colored pencils
introduction:
"Today we will have an opportunity to celebrate our community and ourselves by creating artwork that shares our unique identities. We will get to  create artwork to represents person we are and the unique qualities we have. The name of this workshop is called, Claiming Who I Am."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this is your window of time. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. During this time, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create. I'm going to share some basic instructions, but you get to choose how you want to participate. You can follow along completely, or you may want to do something different, it's completely up to you. During your window of time, you have complete freedom to choose. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. I am here to support you in any way that I can, so please feel free to ask for what you need."
demonstration:
You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation steps with the participants. Feel free to demonstrate any creation elements and/or techniques that you see fit.


Step 1:
"First, you will get a chance to get rid of all of the negative messages that you've received, because they no longer serve or support you. You'll get to write down all of those words and phrases you've heard or even told yourself onto a piece of paper. Then, you'll get to rip them up and throw them in the trash."


Step 2:
"Next, you'll get to choose the color of circle that you most relate to. This circle represent your core."


Step 3:
"You can then choose any words, phrases, colors and/or symbols that represent who you are at your core and add them to the circle in any way that you choose."


Step 4:
"Next, you can choose a person outline that you most relate to and add features on them that best represent you. You can use any color construction paper and cut out and glue on clothes, hair, glasses, and/or any other elements you like."


Step 5:
"Finally, you can glue the core circle onto your person. The center might be a good spot for this, but you're welcome to place it anywhere you like. There is no right or wrong way to create. You have complete freedom to decorate your person however way you like to honor and celebrate all your wonderful qualities."
 

               
Writing down negative messages   Ripping them up   Throwing negative messages away
 
   
Adding words, phrases, colors and/or
symbols to a circle of your choice to
represent who you are		   Creating clothes and glue them down   Adding your circle to the center
of your person
opening_circle:
Part 1:

       
        Sample Creations

"On the piece of paper that you have in front of you, I'd like to invite you to take some time to write down all of the words and phrases that you've heard from other people and/or ones you've even told yourself. Remember, there is no right or wrong way to do this, you can write the words and phrases big, small or however you want to write them."


Feel free to give participants as much time as you see fit. It may be helpful to give them gentle time reminder as you're getting ready to proceed to the next step.

If time permitting, you can invite participants to reflect on and share, if any feel comfortable doing so, how they felt when they heard these messages, where the messages came from, and/or how they have proven those messages wrong.


Part 2:
"Thank you for taking the time to write down your thoughts. Holding your papers in your hands, let’s take a moment to let these messages in with a deep breath and let them all out with an exhale."

"You'll now get a chance to release these negative messages because they no longer serve you. With your papers in your hands, I’d like to invite you to just rip those messages right up. You can rip them in half, or into as many pieces as you like. However way it feels right for you. As you’re ripping, I encourage you to envision all of those messages being released from your mind."

"At the center of your tables, you’ll notice a small bucket (bin). When you’re ready, I'd like to invite you to go ahead and throw all of those message into the bin. If you don’t feel comfortable releasing your messages in this way, feel free to take them with you and release them in your own way when you’re ready."

title: Resiliency Rainsticks / Palo de la lluvia y resiliencia
full_name: Susan Schaefer Bernardo and Courtenay Fletcher
objective: This workshop aims to help families focus on healthy ways to express their feelings and work together to create a rainstick that represents their resilience.
materials:
•      

    Rainstick kits

  • The Rhino Who Swallowed a Storm book (by LeVar Burton and Susan Schaefer Bernardo)

    • Video: Reading of The Rhino Who Swallowed a Storm (from space!)

  • Rainstick Kit Instructions handout

  • Small beads

  • Tissue paper

  • Construction paper (variety of colors)

  • ModPodge (or a homemade solution of half white glue/half water)

  • Paint brushes

  • Permanent markers

  • Oil pastels (CrayPas)
setup:
You are welcome to provide any and as many of the decorative material as you like.

You can lay out the supplies so that each participant/family has easy access and ample room to create.

You can print a copy of the Rainstick Instructions handout for each participant.

If you'd like, you can also print the optional Rhino journaling sheet for each participant.

If you choose to not go with the rainstick kit and create your own, you can pre-cut aluminum foil sheets down to a size that fits the cardboard tubing you're providing (see Demonstration). The aluminum sheets will be used to create the coils for the inside of the rainsticks.

A less expensive alternative to ModPodge is to create a homemade solution of half white glue, half water. You may need to provide individual cups of this solution for each participant/family.

It may be helpful to create a sample in advance to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a very basic demo sample and using only the material you're providing, so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges.

While this workshop is focused on families creating one collaborative art piece, you can easily modify it for individual creation.

You have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
If you're providing the journaling sheets option, you can pass them out and invite participants to journal their responses to the following prompts. You may want to pause in between each prompt to allow participants to journal.


"Before we create, I'd like to invite you to take a few minutes to think to yourself and with your family. In the story, Rhino was told by the whale to 'sing his own song.' What do you think this means? How do you sing your own song and express your feelings?"

"When you are going through rough times as a family what are some of the things that you do together to bring comfort and hope? What do you do individually to help the family?"

"Rhino had many friends show up to help him out. Who can you and your family go to for help? Asking for help is a sign of strength, it shows that we are resilient."

"For those of you who wish to create, I'd like to encourage you to think about how you want to decorate your rainstick. What words, pictures, and/or symbols do you want to put on it? Do you want to put reminders about how to safely express your feelings? How about writing down those people in your life that you can call when you need help? What colors will you choose? What materials will you use?"

(For family creations):
"You might also want to think about giving each other roles as you create your rainsticks. You can think about tasks that can make things run more smoothly. For example, older family members (adults and/or older children) can be in charge of cutting and younger family members can be in charge of choosing colors and gluing. However you want to split up jobs is up to you, as long as you're creating together, you are on the right track. Any questions before we begin?"
creation:
You can now invite those who wish to create their rainsticks to begin. You may want to remind the that there is no right or wrong way to create or participate. They can use the art supplies however they like.

You can refer them to the Rainstick Kit Instructions handout for the step-by-step creation process.

Feel free to offer assistance where you see the need.
 

         
Decorating using decoupage   Adding embellishments   Adding words to the rainstick
closing:
You can invite the participants to volunteer and share their rainstick creations, the sound it can make, anything they discovered, felt or experienced during creation, or anything else they may wish to share.

You can also opt to ask those who wish to share one or two of the following questions:

  • "How did if feel for the family to work together?"

  • "Did their different roles help out during the activity?"

  • "What ways could they have been improved?"

  • "What are some ways that you can express your feelings to your family to help them understand you more?"

  • "How can knowing our roles help out when we are going through the storms or rough times in our lives?"

  • "Now that your rainsticks are finished, how will you use them to remind you of your family's strength?"


Rainstick Ceremony Closing Option:
For those who wish to partake, you can invite one participant/family to volunteer and start by playing their rainstick. After about 30 seconds or so, you can invite another participant/family to join, then the next, then the next, etc.

As the sounds get louder, you can ask the participants to look around the people in their family and share:

"Working together as a family to make it through the rough times can be hard. I encourage you to allow these rainsticks to be a reminder that together, you are strong enough to make it through the storm."
 

Participants engaging in Rainstick Ceremony

"Today, we'll have an opportunity to create something special with our families. They are called rainsticks. How many of you have heard of a rainstick? introduction_spanish:
“Antes de comenzar quiero que estén consiente que esto es su ventana de tiempo.  Esto significa que esto es un espacio seguro para estar consiente de sus pensamientos, emociones y necesidades. Ya que esto es su ventana de tiempo todo es voluntario.

En este tiempo no hay manera correcta o incorrecta de participar o crear. Voy a dar instrucciones básicas pero usted puede participar en las manera que desea. Es su opción seguir las instrucciones completamente o hacer algo diferente.

Como sea que escoge usar este tiempo es perfectamente bien. Estoy aquí para apoyar en cualquier manera que se pueda y me pueden pedir ayuda si necesitan. Se puede enseñar el ejemplo de el proyecto en este momento “Hoy tendrán una oportunidad para crear algo especial en familia.

El proyecto se llama Palo de la lluvia y resiliencia. ¿Cuantas personas saben que es un Palo de lluvia? Palo de la lluvia y resiliencia son tubos huecos que contienen perlas y otros materiales artesanales.

Cuando se mueve el tubo se puede oír sonidos similares a sonidos de lluvia. Palos de la lluvia fueron creados por los Aztecas que creían que el sonido llamaba tormentas de lluvia pero hoy lo creamos para recordarnos de nuestra fortaleza.

¿Alguna pregunta antes de empezar?
demonstration:
Step 1
 
  Step 2
 
  Step 3
 
  Step 4 & 5

You can introduce the art supplies and share the following creation steps with the participants. Feel free to demonstrate any creation elements that you see fit (Ex: decoupage techniques, etc.).


 

Rainstick Kit Creation:
If you're using the rainstick kit option, you can pass out the instructions handout and share/demonstrate the following steps with the participants.

 

Step 1:
Using your finger, you can pop up the triangles on a white rectangular paper so the triangles are standing upright at approximately 90 degrees.


Step 2:
Roll the white paper into a cylinder with the triangles pointing inward, then slide the white paper tube into the brown cardboard tube.


Step 3:
Choose a foam end cap and wrap it around one end of the tube, then secure the cap with a rubber band.


Step 4:
Pour beads (about 2 tablespoons should be enough) into the open end of the rainstick.


Step 5:
You can use another rubber band to attach a foam cap to the open end of the tube, then turn your rainstick end over end to hear the simulated sound of falling rain.


Step 6:
You can use any of the art supplies available (markers, oil pastels, tissue paper, and/or any other embellishments) and decorate the rainsticks however way you like.


 

Alternate Rainstick Creation:
If you choose not to go with the rainstick kit option, you can follow these steps to create.

 

     
  Sheet of aluminum

 
 
  Step 1

 
 
  Step 2

 
 
  Step 3


 

Step 1:
Use a piece of aluminum foil and fold it horizontally into about a half-inch strip.


Step 2:
Cut pipe cleaners into about 2" pieces and twist them around the foil.


Step 3:
Make a spiral with the foil using your fingers.


Step 4:
Insert the foil spiral into your cardboard tube. The foil spiral allows the beads to fall slowly, helping create the rain sound.


Step 5:
Close one end of the rainstick to make sure the beads stay inside.


Step 6:
Put in a handful of beads into the tube, and check the sound to make sure it's pleasing to you. If not, you can add or remove beads to get the desired effect.


Step 7:
Seal the tube using paper or another type of seal.


Step 8:
Wrap the tube using decorative paper.


Step 9:
You can use any and as many of the art supplies available and decorate the rainstick however way you like.
demonstration_spanish:
Se puede introducir los materiales de arte y compartir los pasos de la creación.

Se puede demonstrar los pasos si es necesario.

Kit de creación del Palo de la lluvia y resiliencia:

SI esta usando la opción del kit puede repartir las instrucciones y seguir los pasos con los participantes.

Paso #1: Usando el dedo pueden levantar los triángulos y surgir los triángulos del papel blanco para que los triángulos estén parados a 90 grados.

Paso #2: Enrollen el papel blanco adentro del cilindro con los triángulos surgidos hacia adentro.

Paso #3: Escoja un cuadro de papel de espuma y úselo como una tapa para cerrar una apertura del cilindro y seguro la tapa con una liga elástica.

Paso #4: Eche las perlas en la parte abierta del tubo. Dos cucharadas es suficiente.

Paso #5: Use otro cuadro de papel de espuma y otra liga elástica para cerrar la ultima apertura. Gire el tubo para oír el sonido de la lluvia.

Paso #6: Se puede utilizar todos los materiales disponibles y se puede decorar el palo de la lluvia al gusto.

 

Creación alternativa para el palo de lluvia:

Paso #1: Use un pedazo de aluminio y dóblelo horizontalmente en una tira de media pulgada.

Paso #2: Corte limpiapipas en 2 pulgada y gírelos alrededor del aluminio

Paso #3: Haga un espiral con un dedo usando el aluminio

Paso #4: Meta el espiral en su tubo de cartón. El espiral ayuda que las perlas caigan despacio creando el sonido de la lluvia.

Paso #5: Cierre un lado del tubo para que las perlas permanezcan adentro del tubo

Paso #6: Meta las perlas en el tubo y compruebe el sonido para probar si el sonido es agradable. Se puede agregar mas perlas para tener el efecto deciado.

Paso #7: Selle el tubo con papel u otro tipo de sello

Paso #8: Envuelva el tubo usando papel decorativo.

Paso #9: Pueden usar los materiales disponibles al gusto.
opening_circle:
For the opening exercise, you can start by reading The Rhino Who Swallowed A Storm to the group.


"The book I'm going to read is called, The Rhino Who Swallowed A Storm. In the story, we meet Rhino, and he is going through a hard time. As I'm reading, I'd like to invite you to listen very closely and see if you have anything in common with Rhino and his friends. If you prefer to just observe, that's perfectly okay. Observing is participating."


After reading the story, you can follow up with one or more of the following opening activities. Feel free to pick the one(s) that best suits your group.


For Older Participants / Families with Younger Children

Embodied Experience - Be the Storm (Shake, Shimmy and Stomp in the Muck):
You can invite participants to either stand up in front of their chairs or in a circle. You can discuss how Rhino was faced with a storm. You can ask: "What did the storm mean?" Or about the different things they saw in the book and the different sounds that come along with them like wind, rain, lightning and thunder. You can invite those who wish to partake in the exercise to move their bodies in the wind, make sounds of rain and lightning by clapping softly and loudly; make booking sounds and thunder and stomp in the mud that all the rain has created.

Whale Breathing:
You can invite participants to visualize a whale spouting out and then taking in the breath you need to dive deep into the storm, facing it and rising joyfully above the experience. Whale breathing can be good when we are faced with hard times. This kind of breathing can help us calm down when we are feeling stressed.


For Older Participants / Families with Older Children

Full Circle Sharing - Weather Forecast:
You can ask: "If you were the weather, how would you describe how you're feeling today?" For example, some might respond: "I feel sunny and bright today because I'm excited for art." Or, "I feel dark and cloudy because I'm sleepy."

Take A Deeper Look Inside This Book:
On the last page of the book, there are questions you can ask the group. Some include:

  • "At the beginning of the book, Mica Mouse is scared by a thunderstorm. Can you think of a time you have been frightened? What did you do?"

  • "At the beginning of the book, swallowing a storm is a metaphor for holding in your feelings. Have you ever had emotions swirling inside of you like a tornado? What are some ways you let them out?"

  • "Rhino meets many helpers on his journey. Who helps and encourages you and your family? How do you help others?"

  • "Mica feels better after reading a book with her papa. What books or activities comfort you and make you feel better?"
opening_circle_spanish:
Para empezar se puede leer el libro “Rino que se Trago la Tormenta” al grupo. El libro que voy a leer se llame “Rino que se Trago la Tormenta.

En el cuento conocemos a Rino que  esta pasando por un tiempo difícil. Al leer el cuento quiero invitarlos a oír atentamente y reconozcan si tienen algo en común con Rino y sus amigos. Si prefiere solo observar esta bien. Observando es participando.

Después de leer el cuento se puede seguir con una de las siguientes actividades.   Para participantes mayores o familias con niños menores: Experiencia encarnada- Sea la tormenta sacudiendo y pisando el lodo.

Se puede invitar a los participantes que se parren enfrente de su silla en un circulo. Se puede empezar una conversación de como Rino se enfrento con una tormenta. Preguntas para el grupo pueden ser ¿que representa la tormenta? o las diferentes cosas que vieron en el libro y lo sonidos diferentes que vienen como el viento, la lluvia, y truenos. Puedes invitar todo los que desean participar en el ejercicio de movimiento y mover sus cuerpos en el viento, hacer sonidos de lluvia y torneo aplaudiendo las mano suavemente o rápidamente.

Hagan sonidos de torneo y pisen en el lodo. Respirar como ballena Puedes invitar a los participantes a visualizar una ballena expulsando agua y después inhalando antes de sumergirse en la tormenta. Enfrentando la tormenta y superándola con alegría.

Respirando como una ballena nos puede ayudar a calmarnos cuando sentimos estrés. Para participantes mayores/ familias con hijos mayores: Compartiendo con el circulo completo- Reporte de clima

Se puede preguntar ¿si fueras el clima como describirías tus emociones hoy?

Por ejemplo puedes decir “Yo me siento brillante como el sol porque me encanta el arte” o “Yo me siento nublado y gris porque tengo sueno”. Revisando el libro de Rino mas profundamente: En la ultima pagina del Libro hay preguntas para el grupo: Unas incluyen “Al principio del libro Mica la ratoncita le tiene miedo a la tormenta. ¿Puede pensar en un momento cuando usted sintió miedo. Que hizo?”

“Al principio del libro tragando la tormenta es un metáfora que representa reprimiendo sus emociones. ¿En algún momento han tenido diferentes emociones remoliendo adentro de ti y como lo dejaste salir?” “Rino conoce a muchos amigos en el camino. ¿Quien los motiva o ayuda a usted y a su familia? ¿Como ayudan ustedes a otros?”

Mica se siente mejor después de leer el cuento con su papa. ¿Que tipo de libros te ayudan a ti y a tu familia?”

Ejercicio para animar: Si imprime paginas del diario puede repartirlos y invitar a los participantes que escriban sus respuestas en las paginas. Necesitara incluir tiempo entre cada indicación para dar tiempo que los participantes respondan.

“Antes de crear su artesanía quisiera invitarlos a tomar unos minutos a pensar individualmente y con sus familias. En el cuento la ballena le dijo a Rino que cantara su propia canción. ¿Que crees que es el significado de eso? ¿Como cantas tu tu propia canción y como expresas tus sentimientos? ¿Cuando están pasando por tiempos difíciles como familia cuales son algunas de las cosa que hacen juntos o cosas que traen consuelo y esperanza? ¿Que es lo que haces individualmente para ayudar a tu familia? Rino tenia muchos amigos que lo ayudaron. ¿Quien te apoya a ti y a tu familia? Pidiendo ayuda es seña de fuerza, enseña fortaleza. Para todos que quieren crear arte los invito a pensar en maneras que pueden decorar sus Palos de la lluvia.

Pueden agregar palabras fotos o símbolos como recordatorios de maneras que pueden expresar sus sentimientos en una manera segura. Pueden escribir nombres de personas que pueden ayudar. Piensen en colores y materiales que quisieran utilizar.

Para creaciones en familias: Pueden pensar en cada persona de la familia y asigne responsabilidades para que todos puedan contribuir a la creación. Un ejemplo seria dándole a una miembro de la familia la responsabilidad a cortar y niños pequeños pueden escoger los colores o agregando el pegamento. Se puede compartir las responsabilidades. Algunas preguntas?

title: Intention Touchstones
objective:
In this workshop, participants will utilize meditation and the creative process to connect directly with an intention they want to move towards in their life. Through creating Intention Touchstones, the participants will explore who they are, what they want and set an intention or goal for the future.


About this Project:

Mallika Chopra and Cathy Salser

This workshop is the result of a collaboration between Mallika Chopra and A Window Between Worlds. Mallika learned about the power of intentions at a young age from her father, Deepak Chopra. She discovered that starting each day with an intention focusing on love, hope, purpose, passion or inspiration proved to be an anchoring device that led to greater connection, happiness and personal fulfillment.
materials:
• Writing Pens

  • 1-2 clear round glass stones (we use 1 1/4" or 1/2") per participant (Stones are available at craft stores, garden stores and online. Make sure to buy the clear, non-iridized stones.)

  • Cardstock in various colors, cut into circles in the same dimension as the stones (We use 1 1/4" or 1/2" EK Tools Circle hole punchers which are available on Amazon.com).

    • If you don't want to use colored cardstock, you can also create your own designs! One way to do this is to utilize acrylic or watercolor paints and paper. You can paint different colors onto the paper, let it dry, and then punch the circles. We've found painting random colors onto the paper works great and can create fun, unique color mixing designs.

  • Clear tacky glue in bottles with a tip

  • Paper Towels

  • Music for meditation and creative time

 

You can check out our AWBW Durational Art Supplies page to find tips on using touchstones, inspiration, AWBW offerings, and recommended links to all the supplies!
setup:
Table set-up

Pre-workshop prep:
Taking time to practice sharing about and leading the meditation portion of this workshop is very helpful as the language may be something you and the participants are unfamiliar with. Practicing saying the meditation mantra, "ah" "hum" (in breath and out breath) out loud before the workshop is a great way to become comfortable with leading the meditation.

Table Set-up:
Arrange pre-cut paper circles, stones, writing utensils and glue for easy access for each participant.
warm_up:
Invite participants to join you in a meditation and then go right into creating the Intention Touchstones. You can facilitate the meditation in whatever way is comfortable and familiar to you. The following thoughts/suggestions were shared by Mallika in January 2016 with the AWBW community.

Meditation allows us to honor and connect with ourselves, quiet our minds, and go beyond the constant chatter to a place where we can ask ourselves questions. From this quiet space, we can begin to tap into our inspiration, our intuitive thoughts and deepest intentions.

People often say, "I can't meditate. My mind is always racing and I can't get rid of thoughts." In meditation we're not trying to get rid of thoughts. Thoughts are always going to be there; what we're doing is settling our thoughts down.

Today, we will be using a sound, "ah" "hum" as a mantra/point of focus. Note: Let participants know that they will will be invited to say/repeat this sound quietly in their minds, in a slow manner, saying "ah" on the in breath (inhale) and "hum" on the out breath (exhale).

With "ah" "hum," it is similar vibrational energy to sounds like I am, amen, mamma. We call it a primordial sound. Primordial sounds are sounds that are soothing to our physiology like the sound of the wind blowing through the trees, the sound of ocean waves and the sound of a children's' laughter. These are sounds that bring up peace and serenity.

The way our mind normally works is one thought triggers another thought, triggers another thought and so on. What were doing through this is meditation is starting to break the cycle of thought by introducing a sound that really has no meaning, that will not create another thought.

During this meditation when a thought comes up, we'll say "ah" "hum," "ah" "hum," "ah" "hum," 2 or 3 times mentally. And if your mind begins to wander again, just let those thoughts come up. And after you've noticed that your mind has wondered off, just go back to the words "ah" "hum," again. The meditation is this natural flow.

Throughout the meditation process, don't worry if you spend the whole time thinking other thoughts. That is completely normal. But if you trust in the practice of repeating the sound, you will find your mind starts to slow down.

I will then invite you to close your eyes if it feels safe for you and I will ask you two questions. I invite you to experience the answers. You may start thinking thoughts, seeing colors or feeling emotions. During the meditation, you can allow whatever pops up in your mind to come up and then let it go. After we ask the questions, we will open our eyes and go straight into creating our Intention Touchstones.

Any questions?

*Begin playing soft music

Speaking in a slow and confident manner, say, "I invite you to get comfortable in your seat. Take a deep breath, and if it feels safe for you, you can close your eyes. Let's start by repeating "ah" "hum," out loud, together. Repeat after me, "ah" "hum," (pause) "ah" "hum" (pause). Now you can whisper it, "ah" "hum" (pause). Now I invite you to think about it mentally (pause). Remember whenever your thoughts get away from "ah" "hum" just come back and prefer "ah" "hum." (Pause for 30 seconds.)

With your eyes still closed, I invite you to stop repeating the words "ah" "hum." And for the next few minutes I will ask you a few questions. There is no need to answer the questions, just experience the answers in whatever way they come up. "Who am I?" (Pause for 20 seconds). "Who am I?" (Pause for 20 seconds). "What do I want?" (Pause for 20 seconds). What do I want? (Pause for 20 seconds). With your eyes still closed I invite you to take a deep breath in and out and shift your attention to your heart. Take another deep breath in, and out, and whenever you are ready you can slowly open your eyes and begin creating your Intention Touchstones."
creation:
Intention Touchstone

"Throughout the creation process, I invite you to practice trusting your thoughts, feelings, desires and intuition. Trust that you know yourself, your values, and your desires better than anyone else. You are the perfect person to identity your intention and what you want for your life."

Halfway through the creation process, remind participants: "As you create, feel free to keep asking yourself, "Who I am? What do I want? What is my intention?"

Before doing a final closing, invite participants to hold their Intent Touchstones in their hands, and to take a moment to look at their creations and see how it feels to notice who they are, what they want and the intention they choose to embrace.
closing:
"Sharing our intentions with others can support us in fully embracing them and help us move ahead in our journey. This is the actual planting of the seed, and when we express our intention, things begin to happen. We start to notice that people want to support us, that we have a community around that supports our intentions.

Give everyone an opportunity to share their Intention Touchstone(s) or what they discovered in the process of creating them. "I invite you to be bold and proudly claim your intention out loud! All of us in this room support your intention and you!"

Remind participants that today is just the beginning, and their Intention Touchstones can support them in moving towards making their intentions a reality. Let them know that they can carry their stones with them, or keep them in a special place, to nurture themselves as they take steps along the way.

Most importantly, remind participants to be gentle with themselves as they try to find their way. Intention isn't always a straightforward path, just like life, and giving themselves opportunities to try-and fail-is often part of, and even crucial to, the process!

Note: As an additional support for those who want to continue this process after the workshop, you can pass out the Intention Touchstones handout. This will serve as a tool to help participants create new intentions, but also as a reminder of the steps needed to bring their intentions to fruition.

  • Intent handout

  • Permanent markers (Fine and/or Extra Fine)

  • Sharpie Paint Pens with Extra Fine Point

  • Colored pencils - White pencils for dark colored paper

  • Ballpoint pens in various colors

  • 3"x 4" sheer bags (Can be purchased at craft stores or online at Papermart.com)

Note: You can also use any other material for creating “Touchstones” (real stones, polymer clay, shrinky dinks, or even paper. When creating something that symbolically can be carried as a touchstone, it’s fine to use whatever supplies you can.)

   
We Rise Touchstones Worksheet     We Rise Touchstones Worksheet
(English)     (Spanish)
introduction:
"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this is a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn’t matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just play with the materials."

"Today's workshop is called Intention Touchstones. So, what do I mean by intention? Or, what is the benefit of identifying an intention?" Invite a few people to share any thoughts that come to mind.

Intentions come from our soul (or from within/from a place deep inside) - they reflect our purpose, what gives us meaning and what we aspire to in our life. Intentions come from a place of mindfulness, of knowing what will give us happiness and peace. An intention is any goal you plan on accomplishing to achieve that happiness and peace.

"Today we are going to discover and set an intention for ourselves. Keep in mind your intention can be anything. It can be something as large as getting a degree or as simple as slowing down, finding a hobby or taking time to breathe.

"Once we've identified an intention, or even multiple ones, we can't just wait for them to magically manifest; we need to take the practical steps that can make each become a reality. One action we will be taking today is creating Intention Touchstones as a tangible reminder to support us on our journeys."
demonstration:
Share about Art Supplies:
I'm going to take a moment to point out a few things about the art supplies available to create your Intention Touchstones.

Using a writing utensil of your choice, write words, create images, symbols, or use colors on the circular paper to represent the Touchstone you would like to create as a marker to represent the steps in your journey.

After you are done creating, add a pea-sized amount of the clear tacky glue on top of your creation.

Place the flat side of your stone on top of the glue and press down.

Wipe off any extra glue and let it dry.

Draw or write words or images
to represent the intention you 
want to share		 Add a pea-sized amount of glue on top of your drawing/words Place your stone on top of the 
glue and press down. Wipe off any
extra glue and let it dry.

title: Flying Tall / Volando Alto
objective: This workshop aims to give participants an opportunity to explore their own definition of personal strength, reflect on their strengths, and claim the positive aspects about themselves they’d like to honor, recognize and remember.
materials:
•  
       Sample material and layout

    Chopsticks or straws (to use as flag pole)

  • Binder Clips (medium or large; to use as flag stand)

  • Scissors (to cut out shape of flag)

  • Construction paper / specialty paper (to use as the flag)

  • Markers

  • Colored pencils

  • Glue
setup:
Depending on the number of participants in your group and the space you're working with, you may consider distributing the colored markers, pencils, assorted paper, and glue around the table for easy access. Each participant should have 1 chopstick and 1 binder clip.

You may consider creating a Flying Tall flag in advance as a sample to show the participants. If you choose to do so, we recommend creating a simple sample so that participants are not intimidated by "artistic" challenges.

As a facilitator, you have complete freedom to adapt or alter any element or portion of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
creation:
"For those of you who wish to participate, try to imagine that you are a country…and you get to have a flag. This flag can remind you of the ways you are strong, and the special or unique qualities each of you has."

"I'd like to encourage you to think about what colors, images, words, symbols that comes to your mind."

"I invite you to choose a piece of paper, and decorate it in a way that reminds you of your strength. You might use words, colors, or images. Whatever you want your flag to be. Remember, this is just for you, and is something special to help you feel connected to how strong you are and can be."

"When you have finished decorating your paper, you'll have an opportunity to apply the glue, wrap the end of the paper around the chopstick, and glue it in place."

"Then, you have the option to clip the binder-clip onto the bottom end of the chopstick to help your flag stand up."

"You can even use the markers to color your chopstick, too. Wow... you have your own flag."
closing:
Sample Flying Tall strength flag

For the closing, you may give the participants an opportunity to share their amazing flags and anything they learned, felt or experienced in the process of creating, or anything else they wish to share. They may wish to share how it felt to reflect on their strengths, if they noticed different types of strengths they were not aware of before. Of course, this is purely optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, it's perfectly okay.

Another option would be to invite participants to break into pairs and share about their flags with each other.

You can also do a full circle share, giving everyone to reveal their flags and describe and of the words, images or symbols on their flags.

You may wish to remind them that just like countries that display their flags on flag poles, they might want to display theirs in a place that is visible to them (Ex: next to their bed, on their desk, on a bookshelf, or anywhere that they'd like to have a reminder of the beautiful strengths inside them.

You may also wish to congratulate them on their courage to honor their thoughts.
objective_spanish: Este taller tiene como objetivo brindar a las y los niños la oportunidad de explorar su propia definición de fortaleza personal, reflexionar sobre sus fortalezas y afirmar los aspectos positivos sobre sí mismas y mismos que les gustaría honrar, reconocer y recordar.
materials_spanish:
• Palillos o popotes (para usar como asta de bandera)
• Clips de carpetas (mediano o grande; para usar como soporte de bandera)
• Tijeras (para recortar la forma de la bandera)
• Papel de construcción / papel especial (para usar como bandera)
• Marcadores
• Lápices de colores
• Pegamento
timeframe_spanish:
Introducción: 5 min
Demostración: 5 min
Apertura: 10 min
Creación: 30 min
Cierre: 10 min
Total: 1:00 hora
setup_spanish:
Dependiendo de la cantidad de menores en su grupo y del espacio en el que esté trabajando, puede considerar distribuir los marcadores de colores, lápices, papel surtido y pegamento alrededor de la mesa para un fácil acceso. Cada participante debe tener 1 palillo y 1 clip de carpeta.

Puede considerar crear una bandera de Volando Alto por adelantado como ejemplo para mostrar al grupo. Si decide hacerlo, le recomendamos que cree una muestra simple para que las y los niños no se sientan intimidadas o intimidados por los desafíos "artísticos".

Como la persona que facilita este taller, usted tiene total libertad para adaptar o alterar cualquier elemento o parte del mismo para satisfacer las necesidades de su grupo específico.
creation_spanish:
"Para aquellas y aquellos de ustedes que desean participar, traten de imaginar que son un país... y tienen la oportunidad de tener una bandera. Esta bandera puede recordarles las formas en que son fuertes y las cualidades especiales o únicas que cada quien tiene."

"Me gustaría animarles a pensar qué colores, imágenes, palabras, o símbolos se les vienen a la mente".

"Les invito a elegir un pedazo de papel y a decorarlo de una manera que les recuerde su fuerza. Pueden usar palabras, colores o imágenes. Lo que quieran que sea su bandera. Recuerden, esto es solo para ustedes y es algo especial para ayudarles a sentirse en conexión con lo fuerte que son y pueden ser ".

"Cuando hayan terminado de decorar su papel, tendrán la oportunidad de aplicar el pegamento, envolver el extremo del papel alrededor del palillo y pegarlo en la posición que deseen".

"Entonces, tienen la opción de sujetar el clip de carpeta en el extremo inferior del palillo para ayudar a que su bandera se levante".

"También pueden usar los marcadores para colorear sus palillos. Wow... tienen su propia bandera".
closing_spanish: Para el cierre, puede darles a las y los niños la oportunidad de compartir sus increíbles banderas y todo lo que aprendieron, sintieron o experimentaron en el proceso de creación, o cualquier otra cosa que deseen compartir. Por supuesto, esto es puramente opcional y si nadie se siente cómoda o cómodo compartiendo, está perfectamente bien.
optional_materials:
You can also facilitate this workshop using printable worksheets. If you are utilizing the worksheets in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person.

  • Flying Tall Worksheet (English)

  • Flying Tall Worksheet (Spanish)

   
Flying Tall Worksheet (English)     Flying Tall Worksheet (Spanish)
introduction:
"Today, you will have an opportunity to reflect on your strengths and your good qualities. We each have unique strengths. Different people have different strengths, and everyone is strong in their own way. There is no right or wrong way to be strong. Your own personal understanding of strength is what matters here today. Everyone has had times when they felt strong and when they felt weak. You will have a chance to create a personal flag that celebrates and represents how strong you are, so the next time you feel down, you can have something to remind you of all the incredible strength you hold inside you. The name of this workshop is called 'Flying Tall.'"

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
introduction_spanish:
"Hoy, tendrán la oportunidad de reflexionar sobre sus fortalezas y sus cualidades positivas. Cada una y uno de nosotros tiene fortalezas únicas. Diferentes personas tienen fortalezas diferentes, y todas y todos son fuertes a su manera. No hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de ser fuertes. Lo que importa aquí es su propio entendimiento personal de la fuerza. Todas y todos han tenido momentos en que se sintieron fuertes y cuando se sintieron débiles. Tendrán la oportunidad de crear una bandera personal que celebre y represente cuán fuerte es cada quien, por lo que la próxima vez que algo les haga sentir mal, pueden tener algo para recordartes toda la increíble fuerza que tienen dentro de ustedes. El nombre de este taller se llama 'Volando Alto'".

"Antes de comenzar, quiero que sepan que este taller es una ventana de tiempo para ustedes. Esto significa que este puede ser un espacio seguro para notar sus pensamientos, sentimientos y necesidades. Ya que este espacio es su ventana de tiempo, todo lo que digan o hagan es voluntario. Ofreceré una idea sugerida para el taller, compartiré los materiales que tenemos disponibles y les invitaré a crear, pero no hay una forma correcta o incorrecta de hacerlo. No importa cómo se vea. Lo que importa es tomarse este tiempo para honrar verdaderamente sus pensamientos y sentimientos, sin importar cómo surjan. Si no pueden pensar en nada qué crear o escribir, siéntanse libres de solo observar. Cómo sea que decidan participar está perfectamente bien. Este es su momento. Por favor, pídanme lo que necesiten y sepan que estoy aquí para ayudarles".
demonstration: You may wish to take a moment to show your flag sample (if you've created one) and briefly explain the material and how to assemble and mount the flag.
demonstration_spanish: Es posible que desee tomarse un momento para mostrar su bandera muestra (si ha creado una) y explicar brevemente el material y cómo ensamblar y montar la bandera.
opening_circle:
You may open by inviting the participants to a brief discussion on what strength means. Of course, this is optional for both you and them, but sharing their thoughts can help inspire them to be more connected with themselves through the creation process.

If you choose to incorporate a brief discussion, you're welcome to use some of these questions as prompts or any of your own.

"I'd like to invite you to think about what strength means to you. Is it about how many pounds you can lift? Or does it mean something more than that? For example, one kind of strength is being reliable. Another kind of strength is making good decisions. Another kind of strength is integrity."

"As you can see from our discussion, there are all kinds of ways to think about strengths. Remember, there is no right or wrong way to feel strong. Whatever it means to you, is perfect."

"I'd like to encourage you to think of a time when you felt strong. A time when you used your strengths to get through something. Can you think of a time you were strong in a 'big' way? What about a time you were strong in a 'small' way? There are different shapes and sizes of strengths, too."

"If you feel comfortable, I'd like to invite anyone who wishes to share some of the different ways a person can be strong."
opening_circle_spanish:
Puede comenzar invitando a las y los niños a una breve discusión sobre lo que significa la fortaleza. Por supuesto, esto es opcional tanto para usted como para el grupo, pero al compartir sus ideas puede ayudar a inspirarles a estar más conectadas y conectados con ellas y ellos mismos a través del proceso de creación.

Si decide incorporar una breve discusión, puede utilizar algunas de estas preguntas como indicaciones o unas preguntas suyas. 

"Me gustaría invitarles a pensar qué significa la fuerza para cada quien. ¿Se trata de cuántas libras pueden levantar? ¿O significa algo más que eso? Por ejemplo, un tipo de fuerza es ser confiable. Otro tipo de fortaleza es tomar buenas decisiones. Otro tipo de fortaleza es mostrar amabilidad".

"Como puede ver en nuestra discusión, hay todo tipo de formas de pensar acerca de las fortalezas. Recuerden, no hay una manera correcta o incorrecta de sentirse fuertes. Lo que sea para cada quien, es perfecto".

"Me gustaría animarles a pensar en un momento en que se han sentido fuertes. Un momento en el que usaron sus fortalezas para superar algo. ¿Pueden pensar en un momento en el que fueron fuertes de una manera "grande"? ¿Qué tal un momento en el que fueron fuertes de una manera 'pequeña'? También hay diferentes formas y tamaños de fortalezas ".

"Si se sienten cómodas y cómodos, me gustaría invitar a quien desee compartir algunas de las diferentes maneras en que una persona puede ser fuerte".
