opening_circle: "If you were raised in an unstable environment, you may occasionally seek perfection and control. In addition, there may have been times where you have been told you had to be perfect or maybe had unspoken expectations placed on you by life, that made you believe that you must be flawless. However, I remind you that there is no such thing as perfection on earth, and I invite you to embrace imperfection and recognize the beauty in it. Today, all you have to do is create without worrying about how it will turn out and simply relax and have fun."

title: Doors Are Boundaries
objective: This workshop aims to help participants explore what boundaries are and where they may need them in their life.
materials:
• Tag

  • Door templates

  • Doors Are Boundaries journaling handout

  • Writing utensils

  • Colored pencils

  • Markers

  • Glue

  • Scissors

 

       
Door Templates    
           
         
   Doors are Boundaries Journaling Handout
setup:
Possible Setup

Prior to the participants arriving, we encourage you to have the materials set up in order to increase accessibility. It may also be helpful to have a simple sample created in order to demonstrate to participants what the final creation may look like.
warm_up:
Journal Questions:

         
          Door Are Boundaries
           

"To get us started, I would like to invite you all to a journaling session. If you would like to participate, I encourage you to think about your boundaries by answering the questions from your ‘Doors Are Boundaries journaling handout’. You are welcome to answer all the questions, just a few, or even just think about the answers if you so choose. Remember this is a Window of Time for you and you can write as much or as little as you like."

  • What feelings come up for you when you think about boundaries?

  • In what areas in your life do you find it easy to set boundaries?

  • Where might your boundaries be too rigid or too loose? 

  • In what areas of your life do you find it most challenging to have boundaries?

  • Who in your life do you find it most difficult to place boundaries with?

  • What kind of boundary do you want to focus on for this workshop? (e.g., work boundary, people boundary, personal boundary- cutting back on TV or getting organized)

  • What boundaries do you want to grow and nurture? (e.g., practice saying no, allowing yourself time for self-care)

Allow some time for the participants to journal or even just think about the questions presented. You are also welcome to play some calming music during this time.

 

Guided Meditation:

         
          Door Are Boundaries Completed Creations
           

"Now that we have finished journaling, I would like to invite you all to a guided meditation. During this exercise, you’ll be invited to take a few deep breaths; however, if this doesn’t work for you feel free to count, or notice your breath, or just do what works best for your body. For those who would like to join, I invite you to make yourself comfortable. This can include having your eyes closed, sitting with your back straight, your feet flat on the floor and your hands lying loosely in your lap. Now I invite you to take a deep breath in and out. This is a special time just for you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension."

“You can take another deep breath in and exhale softly. Now I invite you to move your awareness down to your feet and gently wiggle your toes. Feel the relaxation moving up your calves. Breathe in slowly and exhale slowly. Feel all your stomach muscles gently relax. I welcome you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension, especially around your shoulders. If there's any tension left in your body, just imagine it sliding down and off your body. Breathing in love and breathing out tension. Feel yourself relaxing more and more deeply."

"Now imagine your mind and body completely relaxing and your heart and mind connecting. You may take a deep breath in and slowly release it. One more breath; breathing in love and then slowly out, breathing out any last tension. Now I encourage you to begin picturing in your mind a door. When you envision a door that lets people into your life, specifically the people that you feel safe with, how do you envision that door? What color is it? What shape is it? How big or small is it? Does it have windows?”

“Now envision a door that would keep people out. What does that door look like for you? What is the door made out of? What color is the door? Does this door have steel bars? Is it a bright color or a dark color? This door may have multiple windows or none at all. You may also be imaging more than one door."

"Now I invite you to picture a work door. What kind of door do you want to have at work? Is it a door with mirrors or glass? What color is it? What is your work door made of?"

"Now I invite you to think about what kind of door you need in your life. What would this door look like? What would it be made of? What color would it be? Does it have a welcome mat? Let your heart decide what door is coming to mind."

"You can bring all those images to the forefront of your mind and gently open your eyes, if they are closed. When you feel ready, you can go ahead and begin creating!"
creation:
'Doors Are Boundaries' Example
           

During this time, you may play some relaxing music and assist the participants as needed. To decrease the urge to rush towards the end, it may be helpful to provide participants with time reminders, one or two times, during the creation process before moving into the closing.

"If you are feeling stuck during the creation process, I encourage you to go back to your journaling questions or remember what came to mind when I asked: What material is the door made out of? Is it wood, metal, glass? Does your door have windows? What colors are your doors, are they open or closed, half open? What words do your doors have on them?"
closing:
Door Are Boundaries Completed Creations

As the workshop comes to an end, invite participants to share their creation or one thing that resonated with them while creating their door. Allow some time for participants to share if they would like to. If nobody wants to share you may add: "If you would like, the ocean is also open for anyone to jump right in and share anything regarding their creation or how they felt throughout the whole process of the workshop."

You are also welcome to invite participants to a group discussion. Questions that can be used to help start the discussion can be: 

  • What surprised you about the doors you drew?

  • What door do you feel needs the most nurturing?

  • What boundary do you have that you wish others around you also had?

Remember, sharing is voluntary. Therefore, if nobody would like to share you may offer to go first or you may invite participants to a sitting exhibit, in which they all hold up their creations so everyone can see and they can see others as well. Once everyone who would like to share has,  you are welcome to thank the participants for being present and in community with you.
tips:
Durational Art Tip:

Boundaries can constantly shift and change and are highly influenced by our relationships, environments, past experiences, and more. Therefore, encourage participants to continue assessing their boundaries and creating new doors as new experiences occur.
optional_materials:
Tag Template

You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable tag template. If you do not have a physical tag, you are welcome to utilize the tag template as a substitute; however, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person. For durability purposes, it may be beneficial to print the template on cardstock paper and once the creation is completed you can attach your tag to a metal ring, which can be used throughout the workshop series.

I'll provide some basic creation steps; however, you're free to follow along completely or choose what works best for you. Remember, there is no right or wrong way to participate or create during this time."

“In just a moment, you'll be invited to participate in a journaling session followed by a guided meditation. Since we’ll be moving straight into the creation after the meditation, I would like to first share the art materials as well as the creation steps.”

opening_circle:
"Does anyone know what boundaries are or what it can look like to have them?"

Allow some time for participants to answer, if they wish.

"Boundaries are a form of self-care and are very similar to limits. Our boundaries tell us what we do accept and don't accept in different relationships, interactions with others, environments and much more. Sometimes our boundaries can be too rigid, where we can become isolated and other times we may not have any at all, which may lead to us being targeted by others. Today's workshop gives us the opportunity to explore both sides and see areas in which our boundaries may need more nurturing. To begin our exploration, I invite you to think about boundaries as doors, they open, they close, their different sizes, different strengths, and some may even be see-through."

title: Catalyst Butterflies
objective: This workshop aims to help participants recognize their inner strengths and explore how specific experiences can act as a catalyst for change in their lives.
materials:
Catalyst Butterflies Journaling Handout

  • Tag 

  • Catalyst Butterflies journaling handout

  • Butterfly template

  • Black cardstock (1 per participant)

  • Blank paper for journaling

  • Scissors

setup:
Possible Setup

In order to increase accessibility, we invite you to set up the materials and supplies prior to the participants arriving. We also invite you to create your own example in order to demonstrate to the participants what the final creation can look like. However, it’s important to make a simple sample in order to not overwhelm participants.
warm_up:
Journaling:

"To get you thinking about your transformation, I would like to invite you to a journaling warm-up. If you would like to participate, I encourage you to think about your experiences, and how that has caused change and transformation for you. You may also look at the ‘Catalyst Butterflies Journaling Handout’ for questions to answer; however, feel free to answer all the questions, just a few, or none at all. This is your time and you choose how you would like to use it.”

  • Thinking about the last year or the last six months or even the last three months. Is there anything you would like to let go of such as an experience, relationship, or feeling?

  • In order for a cocoon to change into a butterfly, the butterfly has to break through the cocoon, stretch its wings, and let them dry before they can fly. What challenges or barriers have you faced and broken through recently?

  • Is there an event that has been a catalyst for your change?

  • Is there a change you want to see in your community that you want to be a catalyst for? For instance, this can be your community, your state, city, neighborhood, culture, career, extended family, household, relationships, yourself and more.  

  • If there was a word that could summarize or remind you that you are a catalyst what would it be?

Allow some time for the participants to journal or even just think about the questions presented. You are also welcome to play some calming music during this time.

 

Guided Meditation:

       
        Butterfly Created on Black Cardstock
         

"To help center your heart and to explore your transformation for the creation later on, I welcome you to join me in a guided meditation. During this exercise, you’ll be invited to take a few deep breaths; however, if this doesn’t work for you feel free to count, or notice your breath, or just do what works best for your body. For those who would like to join, I invite you to make yourself comfortable. This can include having your eyes closed, sitting with your back straight, your feet flat on the floor and your hands lying loosely in your lap. Now I invite you to take a deep breath in and out. This is a special time just for you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension."

“You can take another deep breath in and exhale softly. Now I encourage you to move your awareness down to your feet and gently wiggle your toes. Feel the relaxation moving up your calves. Breathe in slowly and exhale slowly. Feel all your stomach muscles gently relax. I welcome you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension, especially around your shoulders. If there's any tension left in your body, just imagine it sliding down and off your body. Breathing in love and breathing out tension. Feel yourself relaxing more and more deeply."

"Now, I encourage you to bring your attention to your mind and to think about this last year. Is there anything you want to let go of? Anything you don’t need anymore? You may take a deep breath in and slowly let it out. Imagine anything you no longer need dissipating out of your life." 

"I invite you to imagine yourself as a caterpillar in a cocoon. Think about the strength and courage you have to break out. Imagine yourself breaking out, you are so strong and powerful. Now imagine what’s within you is your catalyst. You are a catalyst. Allow those powerful words to resonate throughout your heart and mind. What changes do you see happening? Are they big changes or small changes? Are they changes for you? Are they changes for your family? Are there changes in your career? Are they changes for your community? See yourself strong and powerful, you are now the catalyst for whatever you want to do within your life. When you feel ready, bring yourself back into the room and open your eyes if you have them closed, and jump into the creation!"
creation: While the participants are creating, you may play some calming music and offer assistance when needed. Time reminders may also be helpful to participants in order to decrease their anxiety and the need to rush towards the end.
closing:
Completed Creation

As the workshop comes to an end, invite participants to share their butterflies or the word they used to summarize their transformation. Allow some time for participants to share if they would like to. You are also welcome to invite participants to a group discussion. Questions that can be used to help start the discussion can be:

  • What change would you like to see in yourself or for others in the upcoming year?

  • How did it feel to have the strength to burst out of a cocoon and transform into a butterfly?

  • What did you learn regarding change, transformation, and being a catalyst for change?

Remember, sharing is voluntary. Therefore, if nobody would like to share you may offer to go first or you may invite participants to a sitting exhibit, in which they all hold up their creations so everyone can see and they can see others as well. Once everyone who would like to share has,  you are welcome to thank the participants for being present and in community with you.

Durational Art Tip:

“If possible, I encourage you to continue to add to your creation or to think about the questions asked in this workshop to continue transforming and bringing the change you want to see in yourself and the world.”

Therefore, take this time to listen to what your mind, body, and soul need. "Does anyone know what a catalyst is?" Allow some time for participants to answer if they like.

"A catalyst is a person or thing that brings about an event or change. Similar to how a caterpillar bursts out of its cocoon and transforms into a butterfly. setup:
Possible Setup

In order to increase accessibility, we invite you to set up the materials and supplies prior to the participants arriving. Journaling:

         
          'What Fuels You' Creation
           
           

"To get you thinking about your passions and desires in life, I would like to invite you to a journaling warm-up. This is your time and you choose how you would like to use it.”

Guided Meditation:

         
          Completed Creations
           

"Now, that you have finished journaling, I would like to welcome you to a guided meditation. During this exercise, you’ll be invited to take a few deep breaths; however, if this doesn’t work for you feel free to count, or notice your breath, or just do what works best for your body. For those who would like to join, I encourage you to make yourself comfortable. This can include having your eyes closed, sitting with your back straight, your feet flat on the floor and your hands lying loosely in your lap. Now I invite you to take a deep breath in and out. “You can take another deep breath in and exhale softly. Now I invite you to move your awareness down to your feet and gently wiggle your toes. Feel the relaxation moving up your calves. If there's any tension left in your body, just imagine it sliding down and off your body. Breathing in love and breathing out tension. Feel yourself relaxing more and more deeply. Now, imagine your entire body is now totally relaxed."

"As you’re sitting there totally relaxed, I invite you to picture in your mind a giant movie screen. On the screen you are viewing yourself doing all the things you enjoy. "Now I invite you to look at your face on the movie screen. What facial expression are you showing? What feelings are being expressed to you? Are you smiling? Are you radiating happiness and joy? You may take a deep breath in, absorbing that happiness, and slowly breathe out. Let that happiness wash over you. Now holding onto that happiness and that short film of you enjoying yourself immensely, I invite you to come back to the room.   • Describe a person, place, or thing that you find comfort in?

  • What activities do you participate in that allow you to find comfort? (e.g., meditation)

  • What smells, feelings, or sounds bring you comfort?

  • What are some things that you can do to bring yourself comfort in your everyday life?

Allow some time for the participants to journal or even just think about the questions presented. You are also welcome to play some calming music during this time.

 

Guided Meditation

       
      Completed Comfort Journal  
         

"Now that we have finished journaling, I welcome you to a guided meditation. During this exercise, you’ll be invited to take a few deep breaths; however, if this doesn’t work for you feel free to count, or notice your breath, or just do what works best for your body. For those who would like to join, I invite you to make yourself comfortable. This can include having your eyes closed, sitting with your back straight, your feet flat on the floor and your hands lying loosely in your lap. Now I invite you to take a deep breath in and out. This is a special time just for you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension."

“You can take another deep breath in and exhale softly. Now I invite you to move your awareness down to your feet and gently wiggle your toes. Feel the relaxation moving up your calves. Breathe in slowly and exhale slowly. Feel all your stomach muscles gently relax. I welcome you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension, especially around your shoulders. If there's any tension left in your body, just imagine it sliding down and off your body. Breathing in love and breathing out tension. Feel yourself relaxing more and more deeply. Imagine your entire body is now totally relaxed."

“Now I invite you to move your awareness into a very deep place inside of you and let images of comfort come into your mind. Imagine scenes of peaceful places, bubbles floating through the air or maybe there is a special place that feels safe for you. Are there plants, flowers or perhaps tall grasses to lie in? Maybe there is a particular color that comes to mind. What do you smell? Flowers, rain, coffee? Notice if any fragrance floats in. Are there any sounds? Maybe notes of wind chimes tinkling or notes of music that relax you? Open all your senses and whatever sounds, scents or scenes comfort you, I encourage you to let them wash over you. Let your mind wander."

“Just think about what makes you feel good and when you are ready, start to gently bring yourself back into the room. Remember to hold onto the peace and breathe in love. When you are ready, gently open your eyes and begin to write or draw whatever images of comfort came up for you during the meditation.”
creation: During this time, you may put on some soothing music and assist the participants as needed. In order to reduce the need to rush towards the end, it may also be useful to offer participants time reminders, one or two times, during the creation process before moving into the closing.
closing:
For the closing, you can invite participants to share their Comfort Journal creations. Allow some time for participants to share if they would like to. If nobody wants to share you may add: "If you would like, the ocean is also open for anyone to jump right in and share anything regarding their creation or how they felt throughout the whole process of the workshop."

You can also welcome participants to a group discussion. Some possible questions include:

  • How did it feel to focus on your own comfort?

  • What word, symbol, or image from your journal brings a smile to your face?

  • In what ways do you plan to use your comfort journal moving forward?

Of course, this is optional so if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay. Once everyone who would like to share has gone, you can thank the participants for sharing and being present with you today.
tips:
Durational Art Tip:

You may wish to encourage  participants to use this journal for on-going and future workshops as a way to continue to nurture and comfort themselves. They can even incorporate other workshops into this one in creating pages (Affirmation Hearts, Creating a Safe Place, Creating Joy, Sun Kisses, Moon Hugs, Stories of the Heart, The Reasons We Smile, Heart and Soul Recipes, Thank Me Card, A New Year Journal, What Makes Me Shine, Gratitude Mandalas).

"This journal can continue to be a resource for you to comfort yourselves in the future. I encourage you to read it, add to it... Use this journal in whatever way best supports your comfort."

introduction:
"We can get caught up in moving through the fast pace of life and neglect to take the time for self-care. This workshop provides the opportunity for you to explore what comfort looks and feels like to you and help you incorporate it into your everyday life, by creating a personal Comfort Journal. These journals are a way to comfort yourself when you are feeling blue, lonely, and even when you are feeling good. We all need extra nurturing everyday. I hope you find working and looking through your comfort journal is like giving yourself a warm hug."

"Before we begin, I want you to know that this workshop is a window of time for you. This means that this can be a safe space to notice your thoughts, feelings, and needs. Since this space is your window of time, everything you say or do is voluntary. I’ll offer a suggested workshop idea, share about the materials we have available, and invite you to create, but there’s no right or wrong way to do this. It doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is taking this time to truly honor your thoughts and feelings, however they come out. If you can’t think of anything or draw a blank on what to create or write, feel free to just observe. However you choose to spend this time will be perfectly okay. This is your time. Please ask for what you need, and know that I’m here in support of you."
demonstration:
“In just a moment, you'll be invited to participate in a journaling session, followed by a guided meditation. Since we’ll be moving straight into the creation after the meditation, I would like to first share the art materials as well as the creation steps.”

“At your table, you should see a tag, the 'Comfort Journals Handout', a spiral binder, colorful cardstock paper, colorful construction paper/copy paper, magazines, collage materials, markers, colored pencils, glue, and scissors. All these materials can be used for the creation process, so please feel free to play with them to help you get comfortable.”

Step 1: “For those of you who wish to create your comfort journals, you may want to start with the cover in a way that expresses your unique sense of comfort. You can choose from the colored papers and collage words and images that represent comfort to you and use that as the cover of your journal. You can use any of the material provided in any way that you like. Remember, you can also create a cover on your tag, by decorating one side of it. There is also no right or wrong way to create. And it doesn't matter what it looks like. What matters is that you are taking this time to notice and honor your thoughts and feeling of peace and comfort and creating something that is meaningful to you."

Step 2: "If you complete your cover early, you may explore the first pages of your journal, if you are using a tag you can use the opposite side and fill it with whatever brings you comfort" (see “Future Comfort Ideas” below). If you see fit, you can offer some suggestions or ideas for pages to create (e.g., gratitude list, self-care ideas, intentions for how they can nurture themselves in the future) or anything else that may apply to your specific group.

 

Note: Here are some Comfort Journal content suggestions you can share with your participants: love notes to yourself or from others, comfort letters from friends, affirmations, inspirational sayings, photographs, pressed flowers/leaves, prayers, poetry, pictures of items that comforted you as a child (e.g., toy, teddy bear, or blanket), quotes, song lyrics and more. Whatever is positive, loving, nurturing, and comforting to you, can be included in your Comfort Journal.

 

         

Step 1: Decorate cover of journal and/or tag

      
             
           

Step 2: Fill first page or back of tag with whatever brings you comfort
opening_circle:
"For those who wish to participate, I'd like to invite you to think about how you seek comfort. What does comfort mean to you? What does it look like? Feel like? Smell like? Taste like? What role does comfort take in your life? If you feel comfortable, you are invited to share what comes to mind when you think of the word 'comfort.' If you prefer, you can journal your thoughts on comfort on your own. Feel free to reflect and share in the way that best supports you."

Feel free to give as much time as you see fit for participants to either share or write down their thoughts.

"Thank you for sharing and for taking this important time to consider your self-care. As you may have noticed, we all have a different idea of what comfort is and different ways that we can find it. It might feel like a luxury, but comfort is an essential personal need. Whether it is getting a warm hug, taking a bath, lighting a candle, feeling heard, comfort is necessary to our self-care and our lives. When we nurture ourselves, we feel more alive and more like ourselves. It is important that we foster a sense of comfort that best supports us. The more we are able to nurture ourselves, the easier it becomes to love ourselves."

warm_up:
Journaling:

         
         

"Inner Me" by Rose Curtis
           

"For today's warm-up, I encourage you to join me in a small journaling session to get you thinking about your inner-self. You may look at the ‘Inner Self-Portraits Journaling Handout’ for questions to answer; however, feel free to answer all the questions, just a few, or none at all.   • Are there any secrets your inner self would like to share with you?

Guided Meditation:

         
         

Inner Self-Portrait on a tag

"Now that we have finished journaling, I welcome you to a guided meditation. During this exercise, you’ll be invited to take a few deep breaths; however, if this doesn’t work for you feel free to count, or notice your breath, or just do what works best for your body. For those who would like to join, I invite you to make yourself comfortable. You can sit with your feet flat on the floor and your hands just laying loosely in your lap. If it feels safe for you, you can close your eyes and just notice your in-breath and out-breath. No need to change it, simply notice the breath as it enters your nose and fills your chest."

“You can take another deep breath in and exhale softly. Now I invite you to move your awareness down to your feet and gently wiggle your toes. Feel the relaxation moving up your calves. Breathe in slowly and exhale slowly. Feel all your stomach muscles gently relax. I welcome you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension, especially around your shoulders. If there's any tension left in your body, just imagine it sliding down and off your body. Breathing in love and breathing out tension. Feel yourself relaxing more and more deeply. Imagine your entire body is now totally relaxed."

"I welcome you to move your thoughts to your mind... knowing you can relax your mind just like a muscle ... take a deep breath and go deep within and begin to meet your inner-self. What colors come to mind for your inner-self? What shapes or images arise as you meet your inner-self? Are they large or small, round or a heart shape? Is the image of your inner-self clear or foggy? I invite you to greet your inner self, and ask them what they need from you... maybe a hug? Maybe they just need you to sit and listen. Take a moment and just spend some time getting to know and love your inner-self."

"Take a deep breath in and let it out, continue breathing comfortably and know that you can return to talk and share with your inner-self any time you want, reassure them you will be back! Hold onto all the images you saw and felt, then gently bring yourself back to the room and slowly open your eyes. When you feel ready, you are welcome to jump into the creation!"

Possible Setup

You may wish to create a sample in advance to show participants what the art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample so that participants aren't intimidated by any "artistic" challenges.

This can include having your eyes closed, sitting with your back straight, your feet flat on the floor and your hands lying loosely in your lap. Now I invite you to take a deep breath in and out. This is a special time just for you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension."

“You can take another deep breath in and exhale softly. Now I invite you to move your awareness down to your feet and gently wiggle your toes. Feel the relaxation moving up your calves. Breathe in slowly and exhale slowly. Feel all your stomach muscles gently relax. I welcome you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension, especially around your shoulders. If there's any tension left in your body, just imagine it sliding down and off your body. Breathing in love and breathing out tension. Feel yourself relaxing more and more deeply. Imagine your entire body is now totally relaxed."

“Now, I invite you to imagine yourself sitting on a comfy couch with your feet up and a snuggly blanket around you. You have poured yourself your favorite cup of tea or warm beverage and you begin to feel its warmth. You see the heatwaves rising above it and you begin to smell the delicate flavor scents of your favorite tea. As you sit there you begin to relax by wiggling your toes, then moving your awareness to the calves of your legs and your thighs, you begin to feel safe and cozy under your fluffy, comfy blanket.

“Take another deep breath in allowing the warmth and scent of your favorite tea and breathing out any tension. Now I welcome you to visualize your cup of tea. What kind of cup is it? Is it fine China with a gold rim? Are there flowers on your cup of tea? Maybe a geometric design? Just visualize a beautiful tea cup that you absolutely love and think about the color and the shapes that decorate it as it rests on a saucer. Now in your mind, take a drink of the tea, notice how delicious it is and just how happy it makes you feel... sipping your tea with your fluffy blanket. The tea continues to warm you and you feel totally at peace... a sense of joy surrounds you.”

“As you continue sipping your tea in your mind, think about the words of comfort that you give others and words that are complimentary to you and just let them wash over you ...hold on to those words that make you feel happy, cherish those words .... And know that you can hear them anytime you drink tea... or coffee ... or make a space for them to float into your mind. When you feel ready, slowly and gently bring yourself back to this room... bring those cherished words with you and gently open your eyes and begin to sketch the cup and saucer that you visualize in your mind. You can also jot down any new words that come to mind."

title: Permission Canvas / Lienzo de Permiso
objective: This workshop aims to give participants "permission" to do something they have been longing to do, to change a habit, or let go of something that no longer serves them.
materials:
• Permission Canvas Journaling Handout
     

    Tag

  • Permission Canvas journaling handout

  • Canvas or cardstock (6" x 6" pieces work well)

  • Paint

  • Brushes

  • Cup filled with water

  • Magazines or precut words

  • Glue

  • Scissors

  • Paper for journaling

    

 

Please note that additional materials are optional and can be used in lieu of others. Please feel free to provide what suits your needs.

Additional Materials (optional):

Paper Doll Template
 
Pre-typed Statement Template

  • Paper doll template

  • Pre-typed statement template

  • Pre-typed words template

  • Cake doilies

  • Scrapbook paper

  • Sponges (to make texture in paint)

  • Foam brushes

  • Bubble wrap

  • Sharpies (ultra fine & regular would be ideal)

  • Stamps

  • Ink pads

 

 

 

Pre-typed Words Template
setup:
Possible Setup  
                 

You can print words and phrases that can be collaged onto the canvases by the participants. For example: "I gave myself permission to...," "I decided to...," "I let ____ go," or any other words or phrases that may be better suited to your specific group.

If applicable to your group, you can print copies of the pre-typed statement template, pre-typed words template , and paper doll template in advance. Once you print them, you can also cut the words out (see images for reference). If you're unable to print these, you can write them on a board and invite participants to select the ones that apply to them and write it down instead of collage it. You can print out the paper doll templates for all the participants. If participants wish to draw their own body template, that's great, and it might be empowering for them. You can also print the journaling questions (one copy per participant, plus some extras).

You may wish to create a sample in advance to get the feel for the creation process, as well as to show participants what the finished art piece can look like. If you choose to do so, we suggest creating a simple sample using only the material you're providing so that participants aren't overwhelmed by any "artistic" challenges. Remember, as a facilitator you have complete freedom to alter or adapt any portion or element of this workshop to cater to your specific group's needs.
warm_up:
Journaling:

         
          Completed creation on tag

Participants can write directly on the template or on a separate sheet (if available). You may wish to reassure participants that their writing is for themselves and they won't be reading their answers out loud, unless they want to. You can also remind them that they can skip questions that don't work for them, but encourage them to try to look at each question with curiosity. This is their "window of time" to be present to whatever surfaces and let go of any blame or shame that may come up. If you like, you can play soft relaxing music in the background during the journaling process.

"For today's warm-up, I encourage you to join me in a small journaling session to get you thinking about the thing you would like to give yourself permission to do. You may look at the ‘Permission Canvas Journaling Handout’ for questions to answer; however, feel free to answer all the questions, just a few, or none at all. This is your time and you choose how you would like to use it. Are there any questions before we begin?"

  • Think about something you are ready to let go of... how would this feel and what would your life look like if you let it go?

  • Think about a habit you want to change, how would it feel to overcome this habit?

  • Think about a feeling you want to let go of, how would it feel to be free of this feeling?

  • Think about someone you are ready to let go of, who is it and how would it feel to move on from that relationship?

  • Think about something you really want to do but have been too timid or too afraid to try: what would that be?

  • Start writing out some permission phrases; fill in the blanks for what works for you…

    • I let ________________________ go.

    • I gave myself permission to_____________________.

    • I decided to____________________.

You may also wish to encourage participants to take special care in coming up with their permission phrase(s) and creating a positive focus for this year. This expression can be something as simple as giving themselves permission to just breathe, or as significant as changing jobs or starting a new relationship. Some ideas for their canvases are: "I gave myself permission to let love in" or "I decided to go back to school."

 

Guided Meditation:

         
          Completed self-led worksheet
           

"Now that we have finished journaling, I welcome you to a guided meditation. During this exercise, you’ll be invited to take a few deep breaths; however, if this doesn’t work for you feel free to count, or notice your breath, or just do what works best for your body. For those who would like to join, I invite you to make yourself comfortable. This can include having your eyes closed, sitting with your back straight, your feet flat on the floor and your hands lying loosely in your lap. Now I encourage you to take a deep breath in and out. This is a special time just for you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension."

“You can take another deep breath in and exhale softly. Now I invite you to move your awareness down to your feet and gently wiggle your toes. Feel the relaxation moving up your calves. Breathe in slowly and exhale slowly. Feel all your stomach muscles gently relax. I welcome you to breathe in love and breathe out any tension, especially around your shoulders. If there's any tension left in your body, just imagine it sliding down and off your body. Breathing in love and breathing out tension. Feel yourself relaxing more and more deeply. Imagine your entire body is now totally relaxed."

“Now, I invite you to imagine yourself in a white room. On the walls of this room in big, bold words is the phrase ‘I give myself permission to…’. There is nothing after that, because you decide what you would like to do. In your imagination, I welcome you to think of anything you would like to allow yourself to do. Maybe you want to stay in bed all day or maybe you want to laugh more, or maybe you want to spend more time with family, whatever you like.”

“Imagine the joy of giving your permission to do whatever you like. I welcome you to take one last deep breath in and then out. Keeping those images with you, I invite you to bring yourself back to the room and gently open your eyes if you have them closed. When you feel ready, you may go ahead and jump into the creation."
creation:
Completed Examples: Permission Canvas

During this time, you may put on some soothing music and assist the participants as needed. In order to reduce the need to rush towards the end, it may also be useful to offer participants time reminders, one or two times, during the creation process before moving into the closing.
closing:
"She gave herself permission to be alone."

  
             
           
         

"She gave herself permission to just breathe."

  

You can close by inviting the participants to share their art with the group and anything they discovered about themselves while creating. They can also share their permission phrase out loud. If there's time, you have the option to use "echo listening" where other group members repeat the phrase back to the participant. Echo listening is a form of listening which is structured to be completely non-judgmental. After listening to participants read their piece, everyone in the room can simply repeat at least one thing they remember the person saying. It is one structured way to use supportive listening and help ground the vision of the participant.

If you like, you may also welcome participants to a group discussion. A few closing questions can include:

  • What are  you giving yourself permission to do this year?

  • In what ways can exploring the concept of giving yourself permission be helpful/beneficial?

  • What discoveries did you make from this experience? 

  • Was there anything that stood out to you or surprised you?

Of course, as with any part of this workshop, sharing is optional and if no one feels comfortable sharing, that's perfectly okay.

"I encourage you to give yourself permission to create your canvas/tag in whatever way that you wish. You can collage, paint, or simply have an abstract background. You might want to add a person as a focal point of your art. You can use the doll template as a guide, and collage to create clothing from different scrapbook patterns. Step 2: “Next you choose a permission phrase that is most meaningful to you. Are you giving permission to take more time out for yourself in the future? Maybe you are deciding to spend more quality time with your children? Or perhaps you want to finally tackle that dream or goal you have not yet gotten around to. You fill in the blank. Once you've decided, you can collage the statement onto the background or you can paint to write your phrase directly on the canvas/tag. Since the canvas/tag is focusing on the future that you want, I encourage you to keep your wording optimistic and affirmative."

If some of the participants finish earlier than others, you can invite them to look back at their journaling questions. They can answer questions they did not answer previously, or they can journal about their creation. They might also create another canvas/tag, doodle, or draw. Feel free to guide the participants as you see fit.
opening_circle: "Today, you'll be invited to notice how it would feel to let go of a habit, someone, or something that is no longer serving you in your life. Afterwards, if you wish to, you can give yourself permission to think about something you really want to accomplish, or a healthy habit you would like to take on. It could be learning a new instrument, creating stronger bonds with family and friends, or anything else you wish to do that can help redirect your focus from negative things, to positive things. Through journaling and painting, you will have a chance to create a canvas that gives you the affirming permission to do whatever you choose in the future."

title: Domestic/Sexual Violence Workshop Series
objective:
About the Author: 

         
          Rose Curtis
           

Rose Curtis has been facilitating art workshops for over 20 years for A Window Between Worlds. She has a Masters in Education and has led workshops with a variety of communities; including teens in high schools, women in domestic violence shelters, along with men and women in drug and alcohol rehabilitation. She has also been the Survivors Art Circle Facilitator in the past in Venice, CA, and then virtually during Covid. She passionately believes everyone can benefit from creating and healing from art, regardless of their background and story.

In an effort to help survivors of DV and SV, Rose and AWBW collaborated to develop the Survivors Art Circle Series, which are twelve workshops that facilitators may use once a month for the whole year with DV and SV survivors. Each workshop curriculum is categorized under a certain theme that we hope can set a foundation and be built upon to better support the healing of those who have experienced trauma. For example, the first theme focuses on safety and self-regulation, then comes strengths and a positive self-image, then identifying and honoring feelings, exploring relationships and building support networks, healing and integration, and finally envisioning a brighter future and celebrating joy and gratitude. Although this workshop curriculum series was designed with DV and SV survivors as the forefront of our minds, this series can also be used with survivors of any trauma. If you would like any guidance on how to facilitate these workshops, please do not hesitate to hop into our office hours every first Friday of the month with our Program Coordinator Rachel Price. We also encourage you to email her at rprice@awbw.org with any questions you may have, at any time.

 

Workshop Series Tag Creation:

       
        Multiple workshops on a binder ring.
         

The following workshop series can all be created on tags and later attached to metal binder rings for accessibility and as a physical reminder to participants of their journey through the workshop series. However, we also created a tag template for those who would like to join in the series, but do not necessarily have access or would like a bigger canvas than a physical tag. The Tag Template may be cut out and hole punched, in order to attach to a metal binder ring or it may be left as is, you have the power to decide how you would like to participate and create.

 

Guided Meditations:  

Rose likes to include guided meditation in her workshops so that the participants have a chance to go within and just forget about everything else. She shares, "Joining in a guided meditation can provide participants with a chance to focus on themselves and I often share with participants that it might not be that comfortable the first time or even the 10th time. However, I encourage them to give it a try because it can be a great way to shut out the outside world and get into our hearts and minds and see what we need to hear from ourselves!"

Remember, feel free to adapt this meditation to work with your group and time frame. You are encouraged to read slowly and pause in between sentences to create a relaxing atmosphere. You can remind participants that they are in a safe place and that they deserve a window of time that is their own. Just like art there is no right or wrong way to do this

meditation.

 

Community Agreements:

       
        "What Fuels You" & "My Cup of Tea"
        Creations

The start of a workshop should include the co-creation of community agreements. This can help set the foundation of safety and trust, while also establishing the expectation of the group. You can create a practice to acknowledge when someone new joins the group, by welcoming them to the space, providing folks with a chance to introduce themselves, and then reviewing the community agreements that have been created and inviting modifications/additions. Once the community agreements have been established, we recommend you display the agreements in a visible location and invite edits or changes based on the groups needs. Explore the Adult and Children's community agreements workshop on the dashboard today!

 

Beginning the Workshop Series:

As you start the series, we encourage you to begin with “Comfort Journals,” as it provides participants with the opportunity to find comfort and ground themselves. This process parallels the Arc of Healing and as the series progresses, the foundation of safety and trust is set and continues to build to include grounding, expression, awareness, empowerment, and integration. To learn more about how to facilitate this and other workshop series, check-out the Workshop Series Facilitation Guide.

 

Domestic/Sexual Violence Workshop Series Training Video Part 1:

Check out the Workshop Series Training Video featuring Rose Curtis facilitating the art workshop Embracing Imperfection!

 

Domestic/Sexual Violence Workshop Series Training Video Part 2:

Check out the Workshop Series Training Video featuring Rose Curtis facilitating the art workshop Doors are Boundaries!

 

 

Theme 1: Safety and Self-regulation

Comfort Journals

           
            Comfort Journal

We can sometimes get caught up in moving through the fast pace of life and neglect to take the time for self-care. This workshop provides the opportunity for participants to explore what comfort looks and feels like in order to help incorporate it into their everyday life. Through the creation of a personal comfort journal, participants may be able to comfort themselves when they are feeling blue, lonely, and even when they are feeling good. We all need extra nurturing everyday, so we hope creating and looking through your comfort journal is like giving yourself a warm hug.

 

 

           
            Loving Your Inner Child Creation

Loving Your Inner Child

This workshop provides an opportunity for participants to go back in time to comfort, love, and protect their inner child. Through the creation of a collage, participants are invited to re-parent themselves and provide their inner child with words and affirmations that they may not have received growing up.

To read more about how you can love your inner child, check out this Blog Post by Rose Curtis.

 

 

       
        Intentional Affirmation Cards

Theme 2: Strengths and Positive Self-image

Intentional Affirmation Cards

It’s suggested that by writing affirmations down and placing them somewhere visible such as on your mirror, next to your computer, your refrigerator or using it as your computer screen, can train your subconscious mind to tune into the truth of self-love. Therefore, this workshop invites participants to create their own affirmation cards, which can be used daily to reinforce and teach our mind to think more positively about ourselves, our health, our abilities, and how lovable we are. 

 

       
        Inner Self-Portrait

Inner Self-Portraits

This workshop aims to help participants learn more about themselves by going within and discovering their inner self. Through the creation of a self portrait, participants are invited to imagine themselves in a way that best resonates with them. Participants will have the opportunity to use colors, shapes, words, and much more to discover their inner self.

 

 

 

           
            Embracing Imperfection Creation
             
           
            My Cup of Tea

Theme 3: Identifying and Honoring Feelings

Embracing Imperfection

If you were raised in an unhealthy environment(s), you may occasionally seek perfection and control. There may have been times where you have been told you had to be perfect or maybe had unspoken expectations placed on you by life, that made you believe that you must be flawless. However, I kindly remind you that there is no such thing as perfection on earth, and I gently invite you to embrace imperfection and recognize the beauty in it. In this workshop you will have the opportunity to embrace imperfection and illustrate that perfection is not necessary.

 

My Cup of Tea

Similar to the warmth of a hot cup of tea, compliments and words of encouragement can also provide that comfort and make us feel good. Therefore, today's workshop is all about making ourselves feel our own love by the way we talk to ourselves. We will think about the words of encouragement that we often tell others and embrace these words of encouragement for ourselves through the creation of a cup filled with compliments.

 

 

 

 

 

Theme 4: Exploring Relationships and Building Support Networks

         
          Center of My Universe

Center of My Universe

A circle is a very powerful symbol and when we put ourselves at the center of our universe, we can only expect powerful changes to happen in our lives. In this workshop participants will have the opportunity to think about what exactly they want in their universe and put themselves in the center of it. Participants will have the opportunity to envision their ideal world and put themselves at the center of it, through the process of creating a ‘Center of My Universe’ collage.

 

Doors are Boundaries

         
          Doors are Boundaries

Our boundaries tell us what we do accept and don't accept in different relationships, interactions with others, environments and much more. Sometimes our boundaries are too rigid, where we can become isolated. And other times we may not have any boundaries at all, which may lead to us being targeted by others. This workshop gives us the opportunity to explore both sides and see areas in which our boundaries may need more nurturing. In order to explore our different boundaries, in this workshop you will be invited to think about boundaries as doors; they open, they close, their different sizes, different strengths, and much more.

 

Theme 5: Healing and Integration

Permission Canvas

       
        Permission Canvases
         

In this workshop, participants are encouraged and given "permission" to do something they have been longing to do, to change a habit, or let go of something they've been hanging onto. Participants will have the chance to notice how it would feel like to let go of something or someone who is holding them back in life or a habit they wish to break. Through this process, participants are also welcome to give themselves permission to think about something they really want to accomplish, or a healthy habit they would like to take on. It could be learning a new instrument, creating stronger bonds with family and friends, or anything else they wish to do that can help redirect their focus from negative things, to positive things. 

 

Catalyst Butterflies

       
        Catalyst Butterfly Creation

A catalyst is a person or thing that causes change and we all have experienced an event in our lives that has created the energy in us to make a transformation. That event is a catalyst that propelled us forward, similar to how a caterpillar bursts out of its cocoon and evolves into a butterfly. Within each of us is a power to create a transformation whether it’s within our own body, a relationship, within our family or moving beyond our inner circle to our place of employment, our neighborhood, our community and even further: the state, the country, and the world! This workshop provides participants with an opportunity to recognize their inner strengths and process what event propelled their transformation.

 

         
          'What Fuels You?' Creation
           
         
          Life Clocks

Theme 6: Envisioning a Brighter Future and Celebrating Joy and Gratitude

What Fuels You?

In this workshop participants have the opportunity to explore their wishes and aspirations for themselves, their relationships, career, life, and much more. For some participants, what fuels them can be the people and/or things that motivate and push them forward throughout life, especially during difficult times. During this workshop, participants will have their window of time to focus on them and what their heart desires by creating a collage of the things they love to do, relationships they have, and much more. 

 

Life Clocks- You Decide

Every day we’re faced with deadlines, agendas, and things we have to do; however, it always seems there isn't enough time. Sometimes, it may even feel like we have no choice about how we fill our time. This workshop aims to give participants a chance to reflect and decide how they wish to spend their time, by creating a special clock that represents how they wish to live their lives.

title: Community Agreements
objective: This workshop aims to create a safe and brave environment for participants through the creation of community agreements.
materials:
• Square fabric - includes satin cording

  • Fabric markers

  • Parachute
setup:
Possible Setup

In order to increase accessibility, we invite you to set up the materials and supplies prior to the participants arriving. We also invite you to create your own example in order to demonstrate to the participants what the final creation can look like. However, it’s important to make a simple sample in order to not overwhelm participants. When using the fabric markers, we encourage you to place a barrier (such as a cardboard) underneath the material to keep the pigment from soaking through.
warm_up:
Embodied Movement:

The Wind Takes Away (Community Agreements Edition) 

         
          Game Setup
           

You can provide enough chairs and space for every participant, including the facilitator (you), to sit in a circle around an empty center space. Alternatively, if there aren't enough chairs or space, you can modify this workshop to use post-it notes or tape on the floor to mark spaces to sit or stand. You will also need at least four participants to play, but the game works best with six or more people. 

"I now invite you to join me in playing a game called 'The Wind Takes Away!' It is similar to musical chairs, except that no one ever gets 'out'. Since you may be getting up and switching chairs, you might want to place any personal items under or behind your seats so that they do not get damaged in the movement. The phrase we'll be repeating over and over is, 'The wind takes away anyone who...' 

For those of you who wish to participate, let's practice saying that phrase a few times, until we get comfortable with it." (You may want to support the children in repeating the phrase all together a few times).

"I am going to remove my chair from the circle and whoever is in the center of the circle without a chair, like I am now, will share something that makes them feel safe/brave in a community/group. Let’s do a quick practice run before playing. I’ll go ahead and start as an example.” 

"The wind takes away anyone who loves hearing music during the art workshops."

"So if you identify yourself as someone who loves hearing music during the art workshops, then any of you who are sitting in the circle can go ahead and stand up. Notice that each person gets to decide for themselves if they want to identify with the statement. It's not up to anyone else to say ‘but you love music, stand up!’ The person who is left without a chair, then goes into the center of the circle and has the opportunity to make a statement.”

Participants are also welcome to use the community agreements flashcards if they feel stuck or want to explore different examples such as: 

  •          
             

    Flashcards participants can use for inspiration.
               

    The wind takes away anyone who loves hearing music during the art workshops.

  • The wind takes away anyone who feels being kind in a group is important.

  • The wind takes away anyone who feels sharing is brave.

  • The wind takes away anyone who likes art.

  • The wind takes away anyone who likes being an o.w.l. (Observer/Witness/Listen).

  • The wind takes away anyone who likes to have a window of time for themselves.

 

Parachute Mushroom Activity:

If you have a parachute, you can invite the participants to work as a team to get the parachute to look like a mushroom or a turtle shell. If possible, have the parachute set up on the ground (outside or indoors), and welcome the children to stand around it. 

“Alright! If you would like to join, I welcome you all to get in a wide circle around the parachute on the floor. If you like you can also stand where there is a handle on the parachute. If you all just prefer to just observe and listen for now, that is completely okay as well!”

“Great. Now has anyone ever played the game mushroom?” Allow some time for participants to answer if they like.

“So the point of this game is to work together as a team and to blow up the parachute so it can look like a mushroom. To do that I welcome each of you to grab the parachute and to lift your arms up high into the sky and then bring them down.” 

“Did you all see the parachute fill with air? Let’s try it again! On a count of three we will lift the parachute above our heads and then bring it quickly down towards the ground!”

You are welcome to continue lifting and lowering the parachute and then after you can invite the participants to take turns letting go of the handle and going under the mushroom shell.

“If you like, you can also take turns going under the mushroom shell!”

After a few minutes of this or when your group feels ready, you are welcome to invite them to start creating!
creation: While the participants are creating, you may play some calming music and offer assistance when needed. Time reminders may also be helpful to participants in order to decrease their anxiety and the need to rush towards the end.
closing:
Completed Creation
           
           
           

“Thank you all for being present and expressing what you would like to experience in our group/community. Before we end our workshop, I would like to welcome anyone to share what they created or any thoughts and feelings that came up for them throughout the workshop?

Allow some time for participants to answer. If the group is silent, you can offer other questions that can help inspire the participants to engage in discussion such as: 

  • Is there a new community agreement that you learned today?

  • How did it feel to work as a team to put together our parachute?

  • Describe something interesting that you learned about yourself while creating your community agreements?

Once everyone who would like to share has gone, inform the participants that your agreements will be visible each group session, in order to remind everyone what they want in their community.

Optional: You are also welcome to play a final game of parachute mushroom using the quilt the participants made. However, depending on how many squares are made (e.g., 4 vs. 3 squares) it may be difficult for the parachute to fly up and down.
notes: You can invite the participants to leave their fabric squares in the room and hang it up somewhere visible, so anytime they join the group they can remember their community agreements and how they would like to be treated in this space. We also encourage you to take a picture of the creations/community agreements, just in case all the participants want to take their creations home. If this occurs, have all the community agreements written down on an easel pad for future groups to see when they come in.
tips:
Durational Art Tip:

Remember, community agreements can always shift and change so participants/facilitators are welcome to add or scrap agreements that no longer serve the group. In addition, as new group members join we encourage you to look over your quilt full of community agreements, and see what can be added by the new members.
optional_materials:
You are welcome to print out the community agreement flashcards to use during the warm-up and to demonstrate the variety of community agreements available to your participants. Additionally, the flashcards may also be laminated and saved for future use.  

  • Community agreements flashcards (Small and Jumbo combined)

 

   
Small Community Agreement Flashcards     Jumbo Community Agreements Flashcards
introduction:
“Before we get started, I would like to emphasize that this is a Window of Time for you. During this time, I welcome you to focus on what you need, what you're thinking and what you're feeling.”

“Who in this room likes creating art? You can raise your hand if this fits for you.” Allow some time for participants to raise their hand. “Great now, how many of you feel like creating art is hard or has someone ever told you that your artwork wasn’t good?” Allow some time for participants to raise their hand, if they like. “Thank you, for sharing! I wanted to ask those two questions because, this is not an art classroom meaning, I will not judge you, you wont judge me, and we especially will not be judging our art work. There is no wrong or right way to create; as long as you do what feels right for you, then that is all that matters. Do you have any questions before we begin?”
demonstration:
“In just a moment, you’ll be invited to join in a small warm-up followed by the creation. Since we will be moving straight into the creation after the warm-up I would like to first share the art materials as well as the creation steps. At your table, you should see a square fabric, fabric markers, and yarn.”

Step 1: “With the fabric markers, you are welcome to draw, color, or write on the fabric square how you would like to be treated in this group or what you need in order to feel safe/brave. For instance, no judgment or being kind to everyone.”

Step 2: “Then you can pick out two of your favorite satin cording(s) and loop them through two holes.” 

Step 3: “Finally, we can assemble our squares together by tying each satin to another square and creating our group parachute.”

 

     

Step 1: Decorate your square

       Step 2: Loop the strings through the holes
         

 

 

 

 

Step 3: Assemble the squares together
opening_circle:
“Has anyone here played the game parachute mushroom?” Allow a moment of silence for participants to raise their hand or answer. 

“To play this game you need two important things: supportive team members and a lot of trust! Similarly, when joining an art workshop, it can sometimes feel intimidating or scary, so it’s important to create an environment of safety and trust. However, you may be asking how do we create such an environment? Well, that’s where community agreements come into play!”

“Does anyone know what a community agreement is?” Allow some time for participants to answer the question if they like.

“Community agreements are exactly what it sounds like! Agreements that we all come up with as a group that will help guide how we treat one another, support each other, and will help make this space feel safe/brave and fun. To be in a community together we have to work together as a team! Are there any actions or things that we can do to help us work together?” Allow some time for participants to answer if they like. If nobody in the group says anything, you are welcome to start it off as an example.

“Some actions can include, being kind to each other or not judging ourselves/others.” Feel free to add any other community agreements or actions that can help make the environment/community safer and more welcoming. You may also use the Community Agreement Flashcards to aid in demonstrating more agreements.

“Thank you all for those wonderful responses! Now to help us warm-up, I invite you to play a little game with me.”

title: Community Agreements
objective: This workshop provides participants with an opportunity to explore and establish safety and trust in a group environment by creating community agreements.
materials:
• Square fabric - includes satin cording

  • Fabric markers
setup:
Possible Setup

In order to increase accessibility, we invite you to set up the materials and supplies prior to the participants arriving. We also invite you to create your own example in order to demonstrate to the participants what the final creation can look like. However, it’s important to make a simple sample in order to not overwhelm participants. When using the fabric markers, we encourage you to place a barrier (such as a cardboard) underneath the material to keep the pigment from soaking through.
warm_up:
Journaling:

“For today’s warm-up, I invite you to think about the things that make you feel safe/brave or comfortable with others or in different environments/spaces. Some question that I invite you to explore and answer are: 

  • What is needed to make this space feel safe so that you feel comfortable enough to share?

  • Describe how you show respect to others and how do you like to be treated in return? 

  • How do you like to participate and what does it look like for you?

  • Is there anything the facilitator or your group members can do to make you feel supported, open, and trusting?

  • Think about the best group experience you have been a part of. What happened that made this group satisfying?

  • Think about the worst group you have been a part of. What happened that made this group unsatisfactory?

 

         
          Completed Community Agreements Worksheet

Group Share:

“If you feel comfortable, I welcome anyone to share something that you wrote that really stuck out to you or that you would like the group to know.” Allow some time for participants to journal and share before moving on to the creation portion.

“Alright, now that you have explored your expectations and hopes for the group. I invite you to create your square, with words, colors, and drawings of the community agreements you would like to have in this group.”

 

Worksheet:

Using the Community Agreement Workshop Worksheet participants are welcome to brainstorm and establish agreements for themselves and others to agree on and follow. The left side can be used to gather their thoughts and ideas, and the right side to finalize them. Participants are welcome to use words, shapes, symbols, colors, and images to represent their agreements. You're also welcome to provide some examples of community agreements that work best for you and your group such as:

  • Everything is Voluntary:

    • There is no right or wrong way to participate

  • Confidential Space:

    • What is said here, stays here, what is learned is shared

    • Confidentiality is a tool for participants to exercise autonomy and manage risk: It is especially important to share about confidentiality if anyone in the art workshop is a mandated reporter as we want to model transparency, a fundamental element to co-creating a safe and supportive environment. 

  • Take Care of Yourself

    • You are welcome to doodle, color, take breaks

  • Judgment-Free Zone for ourselves and others

    • Oops, Ouch & What: This is a gentle way to let others know when something does not sit well with you when shared by others (“ouch!”) or from yourself (“oops!”), especially when your feelings are impacting your ability to stay present and connected. “What” is an invitation for participants to ask any questions they may have. The aim is to encourage folks to speak up any time they have a question to help mitigate any concerns participants may have about asking questions.

  • Focus on Yourself

    • Use “I” statements

    • Avoid arguing with others' lived experience: hold space for & sit with it.

    • Practice boundaries and consent

  • Create Space for Everyone

    • Share the air: Move up & move back

    • Acknowledge the intent, attend to the impact: If something is said that negatively impacts a participant, while it is important to acknowledge that it was not the intent of the person who said it, we encourage you to keep the emphasis on the impact it had on the person who was harmed. This can be particularly helpful in supporting participants to be empathetic towards one another.

    • Pronouns honor each person’s truth

    • Minimize distractions (for example: mute when not speaking)

  • Fun and joy are welcome!

    • Play and joy are important components of wellness and healing
creation: During this time you may play some calming music and offer assistance if needed. Time reminders may also be helpful to participants in order to decrease the rush towards the end to finish their creation. You may also encourage participants to continue their creation if they did not finish during the closing, at home, or other times.
closing:
Completed Creation

“Thank you all for honoring all of the ways you choose to participate, including observing. Before we close out, I invite anyone to share what they created or any thoughts/feelings that came up for them throughout the workshop?”

Other questions that can help inspire the participants can include: 

  • Which community agreement(s) resonated with you the most?

  • How did it feel to work as a team to put together your Community Agreement banner?

  • Is there anything new or interesting that you learned about yourself or others while creating your community agreements?

Once everyone who would like to share has gone, inform the participants that your agreements will be visible each group session, in order to remind everyone what they want in their community.

“Thank you again for being in community with one another today. I look forward to growing and nurturing our group as we continue onward.”
notes: You can invite the participants to leave their fabric squares in the room and hang it up somewhere visible, so anytime they join the group they can remember their community agreements and how they would like to be treated in this space. We also encourage you to take a picture of the creations/community agreements, just in case all the participants want to take their creations home. If this occurs, have all the community agreements written down on an easel pad for future groups to see when they come in. You can also find more info about community agreements in the Facilitator Manual.
tips:
Durational Art Tip:

Remember, community agreements can always shift and change so participants/facilitators are welcome to add or scrap agreements that no longer serve the group. In addition, as new group members join we encourage you to look over your banner full of community agreements, and see what can be added by the new members.
optional_materials:
Community Agreements Worksheet

You can also facilitate this workshop using a printable worksheet. If you are utilizing the worksheet in lieu of the regular workshop materials, be sure to send a digital copy or print them out for your participants if you are meeting in person. You may also use the worksheet for the warm-up or coinciding with the journal questions.

“Today we invite and welcome you, to establish a foundation of safety, trust, and more through the creation of community agreements. Before I continue does anyone know what community agreements are?” Allow some time for participants to answer if they like.
